## ED-106

[THEME][TERM] NSColor(white:alpha:) is an sRGB grey. B2's only app sites are App/Views/Terminal/TerminalStore.swift:50-51. In dark the terminal's nativeBackgroundColor is white 0.08 and its nativeForegroundColor white 0.9; in light they are 0.985 and 0.12. The two uses in release/dmg/generate_installer_background.swift are a build script, not the app. AppKit documents init(white:alpha:) as a grey in the generic gamma 2.2 space. The pixels on screen, though, depend on how SwiftTerm 1.20.0 converts and draws nativeBackgroundColor and nativeForegroundColor, and SwiftTerm is not in the pinned tree (project.yml:8-9). So the Swift does not decide the drawn value. The binding spec does. PR-TERM-045 (spec/TERM.json) expected_result says 'The background matches the panel's own fill exactly, so the terminal has no visible seam', and its windows_path says 'Same four values'. The panel fill is the SwiftUI sRGB Color(white: 0.08) / Color(white: 0.985) at App/Views/Terminal/TerminalPanel.swift:107, the same literals. ED-092 files the white/alpha constructor ('Color(white:alpha:)', most plausibly NSColor(white:alpha:)) among the fixed sRGB colours. DECISION: keep ED-092's reading. new SwiftColor(white:, opacity:) serves Color(white:), Color(white:opacity:) and NSColor(white:alpha:) alike, with every channel equal to white in sRGB. There is no separate gamma 2.2 factory. Rejected reading, for the final report: under gamma 2.2 to sRGB, white 0.08 would be 12.54/255 against 20.4 as sRGB, 0.12 would be 24.50 against 30.6, and 0.9 would be 230.23 against 229.5. 0.985 is byte 251 under both (251.30 against 251.175). In dark mode the gamma reading would leave the terminal about 8 levels darker than its own panel, which contradicts PR-TERM-045. Whether a real macOS render through SwiftTerm shows such a seam is UNVERIFIED under OD-0001 and goes on the final report's unverified list with this ED. No oracle id.

## ED-107

[THEME][UI] Where the port's two faces come from, and how they are registered. FACTS. OD-0009 picked the faces: Inter for text and Cascadia Mono for monospaced. The owner's sheet described Cascadia Mono as '(ships with Windows)' (decision_batch_20260922.md:68), and PA-0013 and UNK-0007 say the same. Probe P9 found it is not an inbox font. It is not in C:\Windows\Fonts or the per-user fonts folder, and no Fonts registry key names it. It exists only as a shared font of the Windows Terminal package, so it resolves by name only while Terminal is installed (RESULT.md section 2, lines 58-64). When Avalonia cannot find a family, it silently substitutes Segoe UI and TryGetGlyphTypeface still returns true (section 2, finding 1). A lookup by name would therefore put the 22 `.monospaced` sites and the 2 `NSFont.monospacedSystemFont` sites into a proportional face on any PC without Terminal. P9's control CB1 shows that breaks every column: spread 121.7 to 146.1 DIP at all 22 sites (RESULT.md:204). That is a silent substitution of assets the contract forbids (PORT_CONTRACT.md:173), and a visible compromise the owner has not accepted (:181). So it cannot be the engineering choice. The 22 `design: .monospaced` sites pass no weight, and TerminalFont.swift:15 and LinkParagraphView.swift:117 pass .regular. But MarkdownView.swift:1192-1196 renders inline code (`.code` intent) inside a SwiftUI Text that also carries `.stronglyEmphasized` and `.emphasized`, and inside headings whose font is semibold (MarkdownView.swift:302-304, :376-380; ChatFont.swift:7). So monospaced text at 600 and 700, and italic monospaced text, is reachable at B2. How SwiftUI picks that face is platform knowledge, and its visual parity stays UNVERIFIED under OD-0001. DECISION. (1) Cascadia Mono ships inside the app. The files are the unmodified static TTFs from one official microsoft/cascadia-code GitHub release: CascadiaMono-Regular, -SemiBold, -Bold, -Italic, -SemiBoldItalic and -BoldItalic, or whichever of these the release actually contains; CASCADIA.md records what exists. The Nerd Font 'NF' and Powerline 'PL' variants and the variable file are not used. The variable file is excluded because this stack does not apply the wght axis (RESULT.md section 2, finding 2). Files are not subset or renamed, since the licence's Reserved Font Name applies to modified versions. The files go to src/Marrow.UI/Assets/Fonts/ with the release's OFL text, as AvaloniaResource. porting/probes/p9/CASCADIA.md records the release tag, asset URL and size, each file's path in the zip, byte size, sha256, head.fontRevision and name IDs 1/2/16/17, plus the same fields for the Windows Terminal file P9 measured, so any version difference is visible. If the release has no static italic or semibold file, record that in CASCADIA.md, and those cases fall to Avalonia's simulation as a named deviation for the owner. Do not add another source. (2) Before the unit's Cascadia assertions are trusted, the orchestrator reruns probe P9 with P9_CASCADIA_FILE set to the bundled Regular file. The 22/22 alignment result in RESULT.md section 4 must hold with one advance per size, or this ruling is reopened. It then resolves each bundled file through `fonts:CascadiaMono#Cascadia Mono` at 400, 600 and 700, upright and italic, and records the lines in CASCADIA.md: family, typo, weight, style, sim and fixedPitch, as INTER.md section 5 did for Inter. (3) SwiftFont.cs defines `CascadiaMonoFontCollection`, an EmbeddedFontCollection subclass like the package's InterFontCollection, with key `fonts:CascadiaMono` over `avares://Marrow.UI/Assets/Fonts`. The default design resolves to `new FontFamily("fonts:Inter#Inter")` and the monospaced design to `new FontFamily("fonts:CascadiaMono#Cascadia Mono")`. Resolve keeps passing the requested weight and style unchanged (ED-091), and face selection is Avalonia's. (4) Inter comes from Avalonia.Fonts.Inter 12.1.2 (OD-0009), referenced by Marrow.UI.csproj only (added with this ED; Marrow.App and the test projects get it transitively). (5) There is one registration point: `public static AppBuilder WithSwiftFonts(this AppBuilder builder) => builder.WithInterFont().ConfigureFonts(m => m.AddFontCollection(new CascadiaMonoFontCollection()));`. The headless TestApp and the app shell's AppBuilder (M6) both call it. (6) Tests check the FontFamily key source (`fonts:Inter` or `fonts:CascadiaMono`) and glyph-typeface resolution: the typographic family name, or the family name when that is empty, plus the requested weight and FontSimulations None. Inter is checked at 400, 500, 600 and 700 (measured). Cascadia Mono is checked at 400 with IsFixedPitch true, and at 600, 700 and italic 400 only for the files CASCADIA.md shows present and resolving without simulation. Unmeasured weights are not asserted. (7) The installer's third-party notices list Inter and Cascadia Mono with their OFL texts (PORT_CONTRACT.md:288). (8) Add a dated correction to PA-0013 (platform_adaptations.md:312) and UNK-0007 (unknowns.md:146): Cascadia Mono is not an inbox font (P9 section 2), and the port ships it (ED-107). No new oracle id. Rasterisation stays UNVERIFIED under OD-0001. The download needs the owner's own confirmation in chat (INTER.md section 7). Until the files land, the unit finishes everything except the Cascadia key and glyph assertions. Inter's package has no italic and no 800 face (INTER.md section 1), while B2 asks for italic text (LinkParagraphView.swift:116, `.emphasized` runs through MarkdownView.swift:1192-1196) and for .heavy (HydraGlyph.swift:56, MCPGlyph.swift:49); those fall to Avalonia's nearest face or simulation, unmeasured, and the source for them is an owner question (2026-09-23) that must be answered before the markdown and glyph units run. The 22/22 monospaced alignment of P9 RESULT.md section 4 was measured on Windows Terminal's CascadiaMono.ttf, not on the release file; it carries over only after the rerun in (2).

## ED-109

[CONVENTIONS] Yes. The scan reports a raw non-ASCII character anywhere in a scanned .cs file, under Rules "R-STR-9": in //, /// and /* */ comments, in identifiers, and in every kind of literal. A leading UTF-8 BOM is still excluded, as the unit already pinned. The scan's scope is otherwise unchanged: every file, tests included, Port/ included. Why: the rule 5.2 fingerprints says 'Every non-ASCII character in C# source is an eight-digit escape' (R-STR-9). A comment cannot hold an escape, so the rule already requires ASCII comments, and 2.7 says so directly. The repository's own tool assumes it: porting/tools/escape_nonascii.mjs says 'Comments in these files are ASCII by rule, so every non-ASCII character is inside a literal'. Read that way, 'in a literal' in the 5.2 row qualifies the two escape forms, which only a literal decodes. It does not qualify the raw character. This reading also makes the check simpler: raw non-ASCII needs no lexer context. Cost today: none. Every raw non-ASCII hit on integration is inside a literal (the ED-108 list).

## ED-110

[CONVENTIONS] No. The API-pattern rows of 5.2 (every row except R-STR-9) match code only. Text inside //, /// and /* */ comments is not matched. Code on the same line outside a comment is still matched, so `/* note */ await Task.Delay(250);` is caught. String and char literals are still matched as before; this ruling does not change that. Why: each row is 'a rule's fingerprint', and the rules it fingerprints (R-ISO, R-TASK-3, R-TIME, R-STR-4, R-CODE and the rest) govern calls and constructs. A comment runs nothing. 'As text' in 5.2 describes the method, a text scan instead of an analyzer (ED-076 declines BannedApiAnalyzers), not the scope. Catching comments would force an allowlist entry, which must carry a Swift line, for every comment that explains a rule ('never Task.Delay here'), and no Swift line exists for such a comment. The unit's scanner already knows comment boundaries: it pins that a four-digit escape in a comment is not caught and that `//` inside a string starts no comment. So the cost is nil. Follow-on, settled by the allowlist rule of the F.SourceScan rulings (an entry only for a hit a unit cannot avoid, with its exact trimmed line and its Swift line): JavaScript copied from Swift into a C# literal, such as the `.catch(` at MCPBridgeSource.swift:150 and CommandCodeAPI.swift:400, will hit the R-ERR-1 bare-catch row because literals are still matched. The row is not narrowed; the porting unit adds an allowlist entry for each such line with its Swift line.

## ED-111

[CONVENTIONS] Verbatim literals (@"...", $@"...", @$"...") and raw literals ("""...""", $"""...""") are treated as follows. (1) A four-digit sequence (a backslash, u, then four hex digits) is caught when the run of backslashes right before the u has odd length, exactly as in ordinary literals. So @"\\u2019" (an escaped backslash in regex terms) is not caught. (2) A \x sequence is not caught. (3) A raw non-ASCII character is caught, as ED-109 and the unit's pinned test already say. Why: R-STR-9 gives a separate reason for each ban, and this ruling applies each reason where it holds. - Four-digit escapes are banned because 'the agents' file tools were observed to decode four-digit escapes into raw characters while writing'. That hazard is in the text of the file, whatever the literal kind. It matters most exactly here: a decoded @"\u001B" in an ANSI regex becomes a raw ESC, which is ASCII, so the non-ASCII check can never see it. - \x is banned because 'its length is variable', which is a C# escape property. In a verbatim or raw literal C# decodes no escape, and .NET regex \xHH always takes exactly two hex digits. So a ported regex keeps the natural form (for the Swift pattern cited at Text.cs:51, [GeneratedRegex(@"\x1B\[...")]). A non-ASCII character in a regex is written with a C# eight-digit escape in an ordinary literal.

## ED-112

[CONVENTIONS] The `_ =>` row (R-ENUM-1, R-ENUM-3) reports every `_ =>` not followed by `throw new UnreachableException()`, with one exception: when its nearest unclosed bracket, found with the lexer's literal and comment tracking, is `(` or `[`, it is a lambda parameter and is not reported. That covers R-OBS-1's prescribed didSet (IMPLEMENTING.md:551) and `items.Select(_ => 0)`. A `_ =>` at top level, in a switch-expression block, or in any other `{` block is reported. That includes an arm that starts its own line. There is no exemption by switch subject type. A discard arm the Swift genuinely needs (a `default:` over a String or Int subject) goes to the allowlist with its Swift line. It is not rewritten to avoid the scan.

## ED-113

[GIT][WIN] A working-tree watch whose git directory lies outside the working root holds no stream in the port. DECISION: the port's WorkingTreeWatch init resolves both paths as upstream does (:132-133), using the port's full-path canonicalisation (PR-GIT-072 windows_path). It then tests containment as :143 does (`gitRoot.hasPrefix(root + "/")`), using the port's single path-containment predicate (R-PATH-1; ED-019, ED-026, ED-036, ED-038, ED-039, ED-045) on those canonical forms, never an ordinal prefix on uncanonicalised strings. When the git root lies under the root, the watch starts one FileWatcher.WatchTree over [root], as upstream starts one stream. Otherwise it starts no watcher and leaves `state.stream` nil. That is upstream's branch when FSEventStreamCreate or FSEventStreamStart fails (:144-154, PR-GIT-072 failure_cases). settledGeneration then returns nil at once (:247), and every currentTree captures fresh into its own index (:296, Git.swift:435-437). The streamless watch is still registered in `watches` (:101-105), because upstream registers a two-root watch too. This keeps the 32-slot eviction order identical for every other directory (PR-GIT-078 describes the streamless state). WHY: the cookie proof needs one ordered stream across both roots (:15-18). Two ReadDirectoryChangesW handles are not ordered against each other; the unit saw 30 of 30 reorders with a 1 ms root handler. The source's own rule is that a watch which cannot vouch means a fresh snapshot (:18-21, :89-91). There is no single-handle alternative. The app puts worktrees in Storage.worktreesDirectory (Storage.swift:38; AppModel.swift:1125-1129; AppModel+Hydra.swift:545-551), whose only common ancestor with <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name> is a profile or drive root. A cookie under the working root would enter `git add -A` (Git.swift:459) or bump the generation (:197-205). SCOPE, stated plainly: every app-created worktree thread (worktree and Hydra sessions) takes this path, so each of its snapshots is a full `git add -A` (46 ms at 4k files, 200 ms at 60k, :10-11), off main. Outputs are identical to upstream; only time differs. A faster route with a real global order (for example the NTFS USN journal) would be a separate proposal. The divergence is recorded in PA-0017, the platform adaptation for the FSEvents and vnode-source boundary. For F.FSWatcher: WatchTree keeps IReadOnlyList<string> roots and the arrival-only two-root test. FileWatcher promises no order between roots. Order within one root stays asserted (Changes_under_one_root_are_delivered_in_the_order_they_happened). Spec edits applied with this ED: GIT.json PR-GIT-072 and PR-GIT-076 windows_path, and a note under UNK-0011 item 2.

## ED-114

[GIT][WIN] Buffer sizes and loss for the two file watches. DECISION: (a) FileWatcher.WatchTree's bufferSize defaults to 65536, the largest InternalBufferSize the documented FileSystemWatcher API accepts. The parameter stays so tests can force an overflow at 4096 (P8). The watch exposes `int BufferSize { get; }`, read back from FileSystemWatcher.InternalBufferSize. Every WatchTree Error, overflow or otherwise, maps to Everything = true (P8 Design consequence). (b) FileWatcher.WatchDirectory keeps FileSystemWatcher's 8192 default, is not recursive, and takes no size parameter. Any Error on it, overflow or otherwise, runs the handler once on main through MainActor.Post, merged with a run already pending. WHY (a): FSEvents has no small per-stream buffer that a burst fills. Upstream designs for builds that write thousands of files to cost one walk of their output (:48-52, :82, :214-215). On Windows every overflow becomes changed = nil and a whole-tree `git add -A` (:211-212, :308). So the buffer that overflows least is the closest to upstream. P8: 4 KB overflowed in 6 of 18 bursts of 10,000 creates; 64 KB in 0 of 3 (informational); 8192 was not measured. Correctness does not rest on the size, because every Error means everything. Within what P8 measured (creates), no loss went unsignalled in 0 of 18 trials. P8 did not measure lost Deleted or Renamed events, so no stronger claim is made. Memory: at most 32 registered watches (:87), each with at most one handle under ED-113, so at most 2 MB of nonpaged buffer. WHY (b): a vnode source never drops a directory write, and pending events merge into one handler run (CommandCodeSession.swift:654-657). scanApprovals re-reads the whole directory each time (:670-681), so a run on Error recovers any lost entry event. Without that run, a lost overflow would leave a tool approval unanswered and the agent waiting. A run on a non-overflow Error, such as a deleted directory, is harmless: scanApprovals returns when the directory cannot be read (:672-673). TESTS (Decision trait ED-114): WatchTree with no bufferSize gives BufferSize == 65536. Deleting an EMPTY watched directory runs the WatchDirectory handler at least once, on main, outside any task. The directory must be empty so that only the Error can cause the run. If Windows raises no Error there, report it; do not switch to a populated directory, whose entry removals would run the handler anyway.

## ED-115

[ALL] R-GCD-3 corrected: file watches have no latency and no time-based coalescing. DECISION: delete R-GCD-3's clause "the latency coalescing is the port's own, a `TaskHandle` re-armed by each event (record it as a platform adaptation)". In its place write: "Neither source has a latency. The one FSEvents stream passes latency 0 with kFSEventStreamCreateFlagNoDefer (WorkingTreeWatch.swift:142, :145), and a dispatch source has none (CommandCodeSession.swift:654). The only coalescing is what those APIs do without a clock: events that arrive before the handler runs are handed over together. For the tree watch that is one batch of paths in order, as the FSEvents callback receives count paths (:172-176). For the directory watch it is one handler run, as a vnode source merges pending events. Nothing waits on SwiftClock." No platform adaptation is written for a latency, because the port has none. The FSEvents and vnode-source boundary itself is recorded in PA-0017. WHY: a timer re-armed by each event is a debounce, which FSEvents at latency 0 with NoDefer never does. During a long build it would hold the cookie event past the 1 s wait (:258-261) and tear the watch down for good (:271, PR-GIT-078). Commit 39e23ca stands, with With_zero_latency_a_steady_stream_of_changes_is_delivered_while_it_lasts. The latency tests dropped from 3d5a834 stay dropped. Edits applied with this ED: IMPLEMENTING.md R-GCD-3 and the section 4.3 row, and F.FSWatcher.spec in porting/deps/foundation_units.json and units.json.

## ED-116

[GIT][WIN] Each watch delivers where its source does. DECISION: FileWatcher.WatchTree takes the SerialQueue its batches run on: `WatchTree(IReadOnlyList<string> roots, SerialQueue queue, Action<FileWatcherBatch> onEvents, int bufferSize = 65536)`. This mirrors FSEventStreamSetDispatchQueue(stream, queue) (:147). Each batch runs as one queue.Async item, FIFO, outside any Swift task (R-GCD-1). The WorkingTreeWatch twin passes its own `new SerialQueue("droppy.working-tree-watch")` (:121; QoS is dropped under R-GCD-2). FileWatcher.WatchDirectory keeps MainActor.Post, because its source is `queue: .main` with `MainActor.assumeIsolated` (CommandCodeSession.swift:654-657). R-GCD-3's "with events marshalled by `MainActor.Post`" becomes "with events delivered on the queue the source names: the working-tree watch's SerialQueue (WorkingTreeWatch.swift:121, :147) and main for the approval directory (CommandCodeSession.swift:654)". WHY: the source decides this, and PR-GIT-072's expected_result says so: "on a dedicated serial queue at utility priority". IMPLEMENTING.md :276 already lists FileSystemWatcher events among the places that are off main. Note (:179-226) only touches Mutex state and resumes continuations, so nothing needs main. Routing it through main changes behaviour. A main-actor segment longer than 1 s (the hang watchdog expects stalls: HangWatchdog stallThreshold 4 s) would hold back the cookie's event. The cookie wait would then time out and tear the watch down for good, deleting the scratch index (:258-271, PR-GIT-077/078), where upstream's utility queue keeps counting. It would also put thousands of paths per build callback onto the UI thread. Test impact, without weakening anything: the WatchTree tests keep every assertion. They build the queue as `new SerialQueue("test", runtime.Loop)`, so ManualMainLoop.RunUntil still drives delivery deterministically (R-TEST-5). The handler records `queue.IsCurrent && !SwiftTask.IsInTask` in place of `MainActor.IsIsolated && !SwiftTask.IsInTask`. The WatchDirectory tests stay on main unchanged.

## ED-117

[UI] Frame clock timing (F.FrameClock; ED-083, ED-098 (1), R-VIEW-10, R-TASK-3). The Swift source only calls TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval:paused:)), CADisplayLink.preferredFrameRateRange and 17 or 30 ms sleeps. The cadence rules of SwiftUI and Core Animation are platform behaviour that the pinned source does not contain (O-34, part 7). DECISION: (1) Wake-ups and time. Frames from the IFrameSource are the only wake-ups. Every duration and date is read on SwiftClock and SwiftDate at that frame (ED-068, R-TIME-1). The TimeSpan a frame source passes to its callback is passed on by AvaloniaFrameSource and recorded by ManualFrameSource, but it decides nothing in TrySleep, DisplayLink or AnimationTimeline. Reasons: (i) ED-068 and R-TIME-1 require every stamp, timer and wait to read SwiftClock.Provider. (ii) The Swift callers compare the timeline date and the tick time with stored Date.now stamps (EffortSlider.swift:1042 and :1051, StreamVeil.swift:188-189, FractionChase at AboutUpdateViews.swift:365-370), which only works if both are on one clock. (iii) TrySleep and Appear start outside any frame, and IFrameSource has no 'now' outside a frame, so only SwiftClock can measure from the call. (iv) ED-098 (1) exists so that time never comes from Avalonia's internal animation clock and a headless test can drive it by hand; the manual frame source together with ManualTimeProvider satisfies both. Required tests where only frame time moves (SwiftClock held still): an appeared 1/30 timeline gets no update after its appear draw; a MinimumInterval-null timeline updates at every frame with the same SwiftDate.Now; a 17 ms TrySleep does not resume; a preferred-30 link ticks once, at the first frame, and no more; an unpreferred link ticks at every frame with the same SwiftDate.Now. The existing test with the clock moving and no frame (nothing happens) stays. Binding amendment of ED-098 (1), recorded here without rewriting ED-098: "Frames come from the seam and are the only wake-ups; elapsed time and dates are read on SwiftClock and SwiftDate at those frames; the TimeSpan a frame callback receives decides nothing (ED-117 (1)). This binds F.SwiftAnimation as well." (2) Due rule. A span S measured from an instant s is complete at a frame when (SwiftClock.Now - s) + 1 ms >= S, compared in TimeSpan ticks. A Double interval becomes a span through SwiftTask.Seconds, so 1/60 s is 166 667 ticks. The 1 ms tolerance covers the jitter of 60 Hz frame times (frames 16 or 17 ms apart against 16.667 ms need more than 0.67 ms). A span is never cut short by more than 1 ms. That is under half a frame on every display up to 480 Hz, and at 239 Hz it is under half of 4.18 ms, so the tolerance can bring a wake-up forward by at most the one frame that lands within 1 ms of the due time. Verification item, for the port's state and Windows verification list: once FrameClock ships, measure on the owner's 239 Hz PC the update intervals of a 1/60 and a 1/30 timeline with the chat open. p2 shows irregular frames (median 4.83 to 8.08 ms). Record whether 1 ms covers UI-thread dispatch jitter. Changing the tolerance is an ED amendment, never a test edit. (3) AnimationTimeline. Appear draws at once with SwiftDate.Now, paused or not. While it is appeared and not paused, it asks for every frame. At a frame it updates when MinimumInterval is null, or when the span MinimumInterval since its last draw is complete by (2). The last draw is the appear draw or the last update, measured on SwiftClock. It passes SwiftDate.Now at that frame, never an entry date. Intervals missed without a frame collapse into one update. There is no grid. The cadence is the display rate divided by the smallest whole number of frames that covers the interval: 1/60 updates every frame at 60 Hz and every 4th frame at 239 Hz; 1/30 every 2nd frame at 60 Hz and every 4th at 120 Hz; 1/24 and 1/20 every 3rd frame at 60 Hz and every 10th and 12th at 239 Hz. The source's comments describe the rates this way, as fractions of the display rate (StreamVeil.swift:175-177 'half the display's rate', TimelineRows.swift:496-497 'a quarter of the display's rate', AboutUpdateViews.swift:350). The date is the frame's own time because the callers turn it into motion against Date.now stamps and absolute phases: EffortSlider.swift:1042 and :1051 (startedAt = Date.now; timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(startedAt)), TimelineRows.swift:500, HydraProgressBar.swift:509, AboutUpdateViews.swift:365 and :451. An entry date would lag the drawn frame by up to one frame. A grid anchored at Appear is rejected: Appear falls at an arbitrary point between frames, so frame jitter near a grid point would drop frames at random for 1/60 on a 60 Hz display. A timeline has at most one frame request outstanding. (4) DisplayLink. A display link ticks on main, outside any task. Its first tick comes at the first frame after Add, whatever its preferred rate. Without a Preferred rate it then ticks at every frame. With Preferred p it ticks at a frame when the span SwiftTask.Seconds(1.0 / p) since its last tick is complete by ED-117 (2), the same 1 ms tolerance. So (24, 60, 30) ticks every other frame at 60 Hz, including frames 16, 17, 17 ms apart; every 4th frame at 120 Hz; and every 8th frame at 239 Hz. Minimum and Maximum are stored and not read. Maximum cannot bind, because the rule never ticks faster than Preferred. Minimum would bind only on displays of about 62 to 71 Hz and 93 to 95 Hz, where the rule ticks every 3rd or 4th frame, at 20.7 to 23.9 Hz. That difference is part of O-34. The owner's 239 Hz display ticks every 8th frame (29.9 Hz). Invalidate stops it, also inside its own tick, and afterwards no more frames are asked for. The first tick comes at the next frame because it is the same link and the same selector as the unpreferred link (StreamVeil.swift:359-360), whose first tick is the next frame. VeilClock also sets `now` only in tick (StreamVeil.swift:188), so waiting a whole period after Add would keep a newly veiled chunk on a stale clock for 33 ms. The required test over 4 ms frames with Add at 0 expects ticks at At(4 + 36k) for k = 0..28, which is 29 ticks to 1020 ms; its name says 29. (5) Frame-tick sleep. FrameClock.TrySleep(d) resumes at the first frame at which the span d since the call, on SwiftClock, is complete by ED-117 (2), with the same 1 ms tolerance. It never resumes on time alone and never between frames. From a call made at a frame, a 17 ms beat is therefore one frame at 60 Hz (16.667 + 1 >= 17) and four frames at 239 Hz (16.74 ms), which matches the source's 'beats'. A 30 ms sleep is two frames at 60 Hz. Cancellation works as in SwiftTask.TrySleep: it returns false at once, whether the task was cancelled before or during the sleep, and a task already cancelled asks for no frame. Frame-tick sleeps are exactly ThreadTimeline.swift:1168, :1211, :1223 and HydraFusedPairIcon.swift:40. OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:224 is a detached 30 ms flush delay in Services, not a frame tick, so it keeps SwiftTask.TrySleep (Services cannot reference Marrow.UI). (6) Paused and schedule changes. There is no grid, by ED-117 (3), so there is no anchor to keep or restart. While paused the timeline asks for no frames, and a frame requested before the pause does nothing when it arrives. A change of the schedule never calls update by itself, whether it is a pause, a resume or a new interval: the content holds its last draw through the pause, as the source says of its scroll pauses (StreamVeil.swift:184-186 and :377-379 'holds its last frame through a scroll'; TimelineRows.swift:496-498 'holds still while the reader scrolls anywhere, so the mask pass below never lands on a scrolled frame'). On resume it asks for a frame at once (Pending == 1). At each frame, rule (3) is measured from the last draw before the pause, so the first frame after a pause of at least one interval updates, and the cadence runs from that update. A new MinimumInterval applies from the next frame, measured from the last draw. Redraws for other state the parent reads (HydraProgressBar.swift:132-133 'drawn once per change') belong to the view units and their Tracked updates, not to F.FrameClock. Exact expected dates for the unit's pause test (1/30, frames every 4 ms, pause at 40 ms, resume at 140 ms): [Start, +36, +144, +180, +216] by +240 ms. A timeline, a display link and a frame-tick sleep each have at most one frame request outstanding. A resume while a stale request is still outstanding reuses it and asks for no second one. AnimationTimeline exposes DateTimeOffset? Date (the date of its last draw, null before Appear) and Redraw(), which runs update again at once with that date and changes neither the last-draw instant nor the requests. A view unit calls Redraw when state its parent body reads changes, including state that changes paused. Redraw never passes SwiftDate.Now. Which date SwiftUI gives a redraw caused by the parent is part of O-34. Pause test: [Start, +36, +144, +180, +216] by +240. Pending is 1 just after the pause (the stale request) and 0 after the frame at 44 ms and at every paused frame after it. It is 1 at once on resume and 1 while running. Additional cases: pause at 40 and resume at 40 with no frame between gives Pending == 1 and one update at most per frame thereafter. Redraw while paused calls update with the last-draw date (At(36)) and does not move the next due time. (7) Oracle item. The rules in (2) to (6) choose a port behaviour where SwiftUI and Core Animation behaviour is unverified, so under R-TEST-6 and ED-086 they get an open oracle item. The item is O-34 (Appendix B). Every test whose expected value rests on ED-117 (2) to (6) carries [Trait("Decision", "ED-117")] and [Trait("Oracle", "O-34")], never a Req trait, with a one-line comment that says so. The ManualFrameSource tests, the source-scan test, the cancellation tests and the Avalonia frame-time test do not rest on O-34 and do not carry it. O-34 goes on every test whose expected values rest on ED-117 (2) to (6), including the appear-while-paused, waits-for-a-frame (collapse) and disappear tests. The Appendix B row names the six TimelineView(.animation) sites (HydraProgressBar.swift:142, :507, TimelineRows.swift:499, EffortSlider.swift:1050, AboutUpdateViews.swift:364, :450), StreamVeil.swift:174-178 and the frame-tick sleeps. HydraProgressBar.swift:551 (.periodic, 1 s grid from startedAt) is outside F.FrameClock and outside O-34.

## ED-118

[MCP][PROVAPI][UI] F.HTTP network defaults within one run. URLSession's defaults are what the source relies on, and F.HTTP reproduces them. (1) User-Agent: DEVIATION OD-0012 F1 (ED-088). The source's default is 'Droppy%20Code/<build> CFNetwork/<v> Darwin/<v>' (R-NET-1). The port sends exactly 'Marrow/<AppInfo.Current.Version>', read when each request is built, with no CFNetwork, Darwin or .NET token. The owner named the network User-Agent "Marrow/<version>" (decision_batch_20260922b.md section F), and foundation_units.json ties F.HTTP to it. A User-Agent from HttpAdditionalHeaders or from the request replaces it. (2) Headers added under O-27 (parked): - Accept "*/*" when neither the request nor the configuration sets one. - Accept-Encoding "gzip, deflate, br", with the body decoded. - A body with no Content-Type gets application/x-www-form-urlencoded. - Accept-Language is the constant "en-US,en;q=0.9". The app ships English only (project.pbxproj:107-112, and no localization files), so CFNetwork is believed to send an English tag whatever the system language. The region subtag is part of the O-27 question. Windows' language list is not used. (3) Cookies (O-28): one process-wide RFC 6265 store for URLSession.Shared, and a memory store per URLSessionConfiguration.Ephemeral session that ends with the session. (4) Cache (O-33), for URLSession.Shared under .useProtocolCachePolicy: - Stored: GET responses with status 200-299 that came from the server, carrying explicit freshness (Cache-Control max-age, or Expires), and not marked no-store. These are Apple's documented conditions. A request whose own policy or configuration forbids caching is not stored. - Answered from the store while fresh. Age and freshness are measured with SwiftClock.Provider, never the wall clock. - Parked under O-33: no heuristic freshness, and no size cut-off. - A configuration with UrlCache = null never reads or writes a cache. ReloadIgnoringLocalCacheData never reads one (UpdateChecker.swift:103-104). - URLSessionConfiguration.Ephemeral's default UrlCache is a new memory-only URLCache private to that configuration. Apple documents that ephemeral sessions keep caches in RAM. No source site relies on it. (5) Cookies and cache live in memory for the run until the owner answers item #2b. The in-run behaviour is the same under every option offered. (6) Tests (R-TEST-5): A_cookie_set_by_a_server_goes_back_to_it_on_the_next_request_of_the_shared_session and A_cacheable_answer_to_a_GET_on_the_shared_session_is_served_again_from_the_cache change process-global state. Move them into one xUnit collection with DisableParallelization = true. Their expectations do not change. Edits: - engineering_decisions.md: record ED-118 as above. - HttpSecondTests.cs, A_request_without_Accept_goes_out_with_the_headers_URLSession_adds: assert Assert.Equal(["en-US,en;q=0.9"], exchange.HeaderValues("Accept-Language")), keeping the O-27 trait. Replace 'has no ruling ... stays reported as a STOP' and 'an owner question next to 7.1 item 12' with a citation of ED-118. - HttpSecondTests.cs, the O-33 test: replace 'an owner question next to 7.1 item 12' with ED-118. - Add the non-parallel collection for the two tests named in (6).

## ED-119

[ALL] The F.HTTP surface. (1) ACCEPTED: URLSession.HttpClientTimeout, a public get-only member marked PORT-ONLY in its doc comment. R-NET-1 requires HttpClient.Timeout to be infinite, and the manual clock cannot see .NET's 100 s wall-clock limit (R-TEST-5). The only other way to test it would be an InternalsVisibleTo project edit, which is a forbidden need. (2) ACCEPTED: URLSessionConfiguration (Ephemeral, returning a new object on every read, plus RequestCachePolicy, UrlCache, TimeoutIntervalForRequest, TimeoutIntervalForResource, WaitsForConnectivity and HttpAdditionalHeaders), URLCache (a type whose only value the source uses is null), and URLRequest.CachePolicy (UseProtocolCachePolicy = 0, ReloadIgnoringLocalCacheData = 1). This is the surface of UpdateChecker.swift:101-110, the one URLSession(configuration:) site F.HTTP serves. AppUpdater.swift:459-530 (downloadTask with a delegate) stays out of scope, because PA-0014 replaces that install path. (3) NOT ACCEPTED: URLSessionConfiguration.AppInfo. ED-065 already decides how a test replaces a Swift static: 'statics that tests replace are Ambient<T> seams overridden per async flow'. AppInfo.version is a Swift static (Text.swift:3-9, enum AppInfo { static let version }). The seam therefore belongs on AppInfo, not on a Foundation type. The proposed member would also leave URLSession.Shared's User-Agent, the one 40 of the 41 sites use, untestable with a controlled version. DECISION: in src/Marrow.Core/Support/Text.cs, AppInfo gets `public static Ambient<AppInfo> Running { get; } = new(() => FromAssembly(Assembly.GetEntryAssembly() ?? typeof(AppInfo).Assembly, DevelopmentBuild));`, and `Current` becomes `public static AppInfo Current => Running.Current;`. Nothing in src reads AppInfo.Current yet, so no caller changes. Http.cs reads AppInfo.Current when the request is built, in the caller's flow, not once at construction. Production behaviour is the same, because the value never changes in a run. Because Text.cs belongs to an already-merged Core unit, the orchestrator grants F.HTTP this one edit (with a Core test that an override is scoped to its async flow) rather than scheduling a separate repair.

## ED-120

[SEC][MCP] amends only the chunk paragraph of ED-093, from "A value longer than 2560 bytes" to "delete removes the primary first". The rest of ED-093 stands: target name, UserName, type, persistence, the SecItem status contract, the backend seam and the live test. SOURCE FACTS - MCPKeychain.swift:42-44 updates with one SecItemUpdate. A reader sees the old or the new value. A refusal (any status except errSecItemNotFound) returns false and leaves the item as it was. - APIKeychain.swift:34-39 deletes and then adds, so after a refused add the account holds nothing. - MCPOAuth.swift:712 rewrites the whole OAuth JSON on every token save. That is the one value that can pass 2560 bytes. - ED-093's fixed names `<target>#2..` are overwritten while the live primary still references them. DECISION (1) Encoding. - A value of at most 2560 bytes is one bare primary with no attributes, as in ED-093. - A longer value is split into 2560-byte chunks. The primary holds chunk 1 and exactly one attribute: keyword `Marrow_Chunks` (the <CompanyName>_<Name> form the CREDENTIAL_ATTRIBUTE documentation asks for). Its value is the ASCII bytes of `<count>/<slot>`, in decimal with no leading zeros, where count >= 2 and slot is 1 or 2. - Continuation n (2..count) is `<target>#<slot>.<n>`, with the same UserName, CRED_TYPE_GENERIC, CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE and no attributes. - The keyword and the name forms are a persisted format and never change. (2) Write (Add, Update, and the add half of both helpers). - Read the primary first. For Add, a present primary means DuplicateItem and nothing is written. For Update, an absent primary means ItemNotFound and nothing is written. - The old slot is 0 when the primary is bare. It is also 0 when the primary is absent or its attribute is malformed. - A value that fits one chunk is written as a bare primary. - Otherwise the new slot is 2 if the old slot is 1, and 1 in every other case. Write continuations 2..count of the new slot in ascending order, then the primary last with one CredWrite. That CredWrite replaces the old credential and its attributes in one step. - The new slot never equals the slot the current primary references. So no chunk that a readable value depends on is written or deleted before the primary stops referencing it. - After the primary succeeds, sweep: - For a chunked new value, delete `<target>#<new>.<count+1>` upward until the first not-found. This removes a stale tail from a crashed attempt. - Delete the other slot's continuations from .2 upward until the first not-found. For a bare new value, sweep both slots from .2. - A sweep delete that fails does not change Success. The value was saved, as SecItemUpdate would have saved it. Whatever the sweep left behind is removed by the next write or delete of the item. (3) Refusal (OD-0008 A6: fail closed, store nothing). - If a continuation write is refused, the primary is never written. - If a continuation write or the primary write is refused, delete the new slot's continuations already written and return the refusal status unchanged. It is never mapped to ItemNotFound. - The old primary and its chunks are never touched. Update and SetUpdating keep the old value and report failure/false (MCPKeychain.swift:42-44). SetReplacing already ran its delete (APIKeychain.swift:34), so it leaves nothing. (4) Read (CopyMatching, Read). - A bare primary is its blob. - Otherwise parse the attribute as in (1), read `<target>#<slot>.2..<count>` and join the blobs as bytes before the UTF-8 decode. - A malformed attribute or a missing continuation is ItemNotFound, as ED-093 says for a missing chunk. (5) Delete. - Read the primary and delete it first, so every reader gets ItemNotFound at once, as with SecItemDelete. - Then delete both slots' continuations from .2 upward until the first not-found. Do this even when the primary was absent or malformed, so a user's delete removes every fragment. - The status is the primary delete's status: Success, or ItemNotFound when there was no primary. The one exception: if a continuation delete fails with something other than not-found, return that failure, because stored values remain (OD-0008 A12). (6) One writer. - Every SecretStore operation runs under one process-wide reentrant lock (a C# `lock` on a static object). It must be reentrant because the tests read from inside BeforeWrite and BeforeDelete on the same thread. - ED-002 (engineering_decisions.md:15) gives the app a single-instance lock, so no other Marrow process writes these credentials. - The backend seam gets no enumeration. WHY: two slots are the smallest encoding that gives SecItemUpdate's all-or-nothing replacement under Credential Manager's 2560-byte blob limit. Every leftover stays under a bounded set of names that the next write or delete of the item removes. It keeps ED-093's bare one-chunk items, target names and status contract. Only the continuation names in the chunk tests change.

## ED-121

[STORE] F.FileOps: where the atomic write checks its bytes, and what a mismatch does. Only WriteAtomic verifies. MoveItem, ReplaceItemAt and RemoveItem write no bytes (R-FS-1 lists 'the bytes verified' under .atomic writes). Each attempt: (a) write the bytes to a temporary file beside the destination whose name does not end in .json, and flush it to disk (FileStream.Flush(flushToDisk: true); copied from swift-foundation Data+Writing.swift write(), which calls fsync(fd) before the rename); (b) read the temporary file back and compare it byte for byte with the input; (c) only if they match, go on to the replace (after the ED-124 attribute step). (d) On a mismatch, delete the temporary file and count the attempt as failed; the next attempt starts over with a fresh temporary file. A transient failure of the replace itself keeps the verified temporary file beside the destination through the wait, as FileOpsTests.cs:167 and :547 require. Either way it waits the next RetryDelays entry (ED-122). A sharing violation during the read-back counts as transient. When the last attempt fails, WriteAtomic throws the error from that attempt: the Windows error itself for a replace failure (test :203), or an IOException naming the file for a mismatch. It is a thrown error (SwiftTry.IsThrownError, R-ERR-1). The destination keeps its old bytes and its attributes (ED-124), and no temporary file is left behind. Checking before the replace keeps the .atomic contract 'the new bytes or the old ones', and the rename moves exactly the file that was checked. No text is invented (R-ERR-2). Swift never checks bytes, so parity is unaffected. The mismatch path is tested only if that needs no file-system abstraction or internal seam (R-FS-1: 'never a file-system abstraction'). Otherwise it stays untested, and the happy path's byte-equality tests cover the check.

## ED-122

[STORE] F.FileOps retry schedule. FileOps.RetryDelays = [100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700] ms. That is 8 attempts (the first plus 7 retries, each wait on SwiftClock, ED-068) and a total wait of exactly 2.8 s. The wait comes before each retry, and one attempt follows the last wait. The same schedule applies to WriteAtomic, RemoveItem, MoveItem and ReplaceItemAt. Why: (1) The step is copied, not invented. The only retry values the project records are those of the PA-0015 fix itself, negative_test.mjs:68, which waits 100*(i+1) ms, a linear backoff in 100 ms steps. (2) The count is set by the source. The port cannot keep that fix's 12 attempts (6.6 s total) because the Swift blocks the main actor on the disk writer: DiskWriter.removeSynchronously and waitForQueuedWrites call queue.sync (Storage.swift:367-379), from Storage.swift:74, :93 and AppModel.swift:1325. HangWatchdog reports a main-thread stall at 4 s (HangWatchdog.swift:24) and pings every 0.5 s (:52). A single locked file must never produce a hang report that macOS, which has no sharing violations, would never produce. So the total must stay below 4 s minus one ping interval (3.5 s). The largest linear 100 ms schedule under that is 100..700 ms, total 2.8 s; adding 800 ms would make it 3.6 s. (3) PA-0015 classifies this as an internal engineering decision that changes no observable behaviour ('it does not change any observable product behavior'), so it is not an owner question. Accepted residual: a synchronous bulk remove of several files that all stay locked can still add up past 4 s. That is the inherent PA-0015 situation, and the outcome is the same as on a single failure: the try? at Storage.swift:372 swallows it. The unit's tests assert the exact list and the 2.8 s sum. The current shape-only test (FileOpsTests.cs:44-53) becomes an exact-value test citing ED-122.

## ED-123

[STORE][PROVCLI] F.FileOps ReplaceItemAt with a missing original; new oracle item O-35. Parked choice: FileOps.ReplaceItemAt(original, replacement) with a missing original throws at once. The error is FileNotFoundException, an IOException, and a thrown error, so the catch at CommandCodeSession.swift:759 takes it. Nothing is moved: the replacement file stays where it is with its bytes, and no retry timer is armed, because a missing item is not a sharing violation. At the only call site this means the first reply goes through the fallback at :760, a direct .atomic write of <id>.reply.json, and <id>.reply.json.tmp stays behind until clearApprovalFiles (:766-770) removes it. Why this choice: (1) The open Foundation implementation throws here. swift-corelibs-foundation FileManager+POSIX.swift _replaceItem calls `try attributesOfItem(atPath: originalItemURL.path)` with no existence check before it, so a missing original throws. On Windows, the Win32 ReplaceFileW primitive fails the same way; the unit's probe printed 'replace missing: FileNotFoundException'. (2) macOS's closed Foundation cannot be read or run here (OD-0001), so the answer stays UNVERIFIED as O-35. The Windows toolchain cannot settle it either: that would be swift-corelibs-foundation, and a macOS run is needed. (3) The choice cannot change what the CLI mod reads. Under either Foundation outcome, <id>.reply.json ends up holding the verbatim payload (PR-PROVCLI-249). The only difference is the transient .tmp file, which the mod never reads (it reads <id>.reply.json) and which clearApprovalFiles deletes. The either-or test (FileOpsTests.cs:704-739) becomes a test of the throw branch alone. It carries [Trait("Oracle", "O-35")] and no Req trait (R-TEST-6), with a comment saying the expectation is parked. The call-site behaviour (fallback write, stale .tmp) is tested by the CommandCodeSession unit, not here.

## ED-124

[STORE] F.FileOps: an atomic write keeps the destination's read-only state; new oracle item O-36. Copied from swift-foundation Data+Writing.swift writeToFileAux: fstatat on the destination, mode = st_mode & ~S_IFMT, fchmod(fd, mode) on the temporary file before the rename. The attempt reads the destination's attributes. If the destination exists and has FileAttributes.ReadOnly, then after the bytes are verified (ED-121) the temporary file gets ReadOnly. Then the destination's ReadOnly is cleared and the temporary file is moved over it with a MoveFileEx-style replace (File.Move overwrite). ReplaceFileW refuses read-only files, so it is not used here. The result is read-only from the moment it appears. If the replace fails, the destination's ReadOnly is set again at once, before the retry wait. When the retries run out, the old file keeps its bytes and its ReadOnly exactly as before, and the temporary file has its ReadOnly cleared and is deleted. A destination that did not exist, or was not read-only, gets a new file without ReadOnly. ReadOnly is the only attribute carried over, because it is the only one that stands for a POSIX mode bit. No other attribute is asserted. The result stays UNVERIFIED as O-36: whether swift-foundation's behaviour holds on macOS 26 is open under ED-086, and the Windows toolchain cannot settle it because its Windows branch differs. Tests: An_atomic_write_over_a_read_only_file_... also asserts ReadOnly on the result, with [Trait("Oracle", "O-36")] and no Req trait. A read-only variant of the retries-exhausted test asserts old bytes, ReadOnly still set, and no stray file. A write to a new path, or over a file that was not read-only, asserts the result is not ReadOnly. This matters for NativeFileTools.swift:88 and :118: an agent's edit to a read-only project file leaves it read-only, as on macOS.

## ED-125

[STORE] F.FileOps: which Windows errors are transient. Nothing in porting/ recorded this, yet the reviewed tests need it: the reader that shares everything (FileOpsTests.cs:540-550, 'a plain rename over this holder is refused') and the retries-exhausted tests (:203, :371, which allow UnauthorizedAccessException) require that ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED from a held handle arms a retry, while a missing folder (:114), a missing item (:387), an existing move destination (:419) and a missing replace original (O-35, ED-123) must throw at once. The unit's own probe saw 'move: UnauthorizedAccessException 0x80070005'. DECISION, the smallest one consistent with PA-0015 and those tests: FileOps retries on ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION (0x20), ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION (0x21), and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (0x5) once the read-only attribute has been dealt with (ED-124 for atomic writes; read-only cleared before a delete, R-FS-1). It throws at once, with no retry timer armed, on everything else: file or path not found, already exists, invalid name, disk full and the rest. The cost is that a real permission denial waits the ED-122 schedule (2.8 s) and then throws the real error, which PA-0015's 'bounded, then a real error' already allows. Tests that depend on the classification carry a Decision trait for this ED.

## ED-126

[PROVACP][MCP] For StdioProcess.terminate on Windows, ED-047 (b) governs each step; ED-027 keeps only its intent (all three steps, in order, and the 3 s wait). Step 1 (:120-121): close the stdin write handle on the write queue, whether or not the child is still running. Step 2 (:122-123): if the child is still running, send CTRL_BREAK_EVENT through the AttachConsole helper (the P6 form) to the child's own process group on its own hidden console. The child was created with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, so the app's own group is never signalled. Step 3 (:125-126): at +3 s through GlobalQueue.AsyncAfter, if the child is still running, TerminateProcess on that pid alone, with no job object, so grandchildren survive as on macOS. ED-027's sentence 'Step 2 becomes Node's subprocess.kill(), which on Windows is TerminateProcess with exit code 1; step 3 is then a no-op' is withdrawn. COMPATIBILITY: the graceful step is CTRL_BREAK, not SIGTERM. It reaches the child's process group, meaning the child and any descendant that did not start its own group, where macOS SIGTERM reaches the pid alone. A CLI that ignores CTRL_BREAK is killed at +3 s where a macOS one would have exited on SIGTERM. Edits: add an amendment note to ED-027. Add ED-027 to the IMPLEMENTING.md 1.6 list of Node-term decisions. In R-PROC-1, replace 'ladders of ED-027 and ED-047 ... exit status (ED-027)' with 'ladders of ED-047 (ED-126)'; the exit status is a separate open item, listed in missed. Fix the B1 citations in ED-027 and ED-047 to StdioProcess.swift:119-128. The ladder, signal and spawn tests stay as written. This ED is the recorded amendment of ED-027 (ED-027's text is not rewritten): its step 2 as Node's subprocess.kill() is withdrawn, and only its intent stands. Citation fix for B2: ED-027's StdioProcess.swift:114-122 and ED-047's StdioProcess.swift:115-123 read StdioProcess.swift:119-128; ED-047's Shell.swift:110-118 is unchanged in B2. What exit status a killed or CTRL_BREAK-ended child reports (Swift reports 9 with terminationReason .uncaughtSignal after SIGKILL, and CommandCodeSession.swift:445 treats 130 as interrupted) is not decided here; it is an owner question of 2026-09-23.

## ED-130

[PROVREG] On the path branch, a leading '~' followed by '/' or '\' is replaced by the home folder, which is the `home` seam: null means the user's own profile folder. So '~\bin\tool.exe' resolves exactly as '~/bin/tool.exe' does. A leading '~name' (NSString's other-user form) is left unchanged: there is no user database lookup on Windows, and Foundation also leaves the text unchanged when that user does not exist, so the path simply fails the existence test. Reason: ED-031 (3) makes '\' a separator for the path test on Windows, and expandingTildeInPath (Shell.swift:418) expands a leading '~' path component. With '\' a separator, '~\' is that same component in Windows spelling. Expanding only '~/' would treat two spellings of one path differently.

## ED-132

[FMT] The default of SwiftFormatters.CurrentLocale is the swift-foundation Locale.current of an app with only an English localization. Locale.current is built with bundle matching on (swift-foundation Locale_Cache.swift:165; Locale_ICU.swift:207-214). The app sets no CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations and ships only en (project.yml:6 and the GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE settings; project.pbxproj knownRegions Base, en; no .lproj, .strings or .xcstrings under DroppyCode/). So the user's region is kept and the language becomes en. DECISION: the default is computed each time it is read (so CultureScope drives it). It ports Locale_ICU.swift:229-279 over System32\icu.dll with these inputs. The preferred locale (AppleLocale) is uloc_forLanguageTag(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.Name), never '-' replaced by '_'. The result of that call is used as it is, including when it parses only a prefix. It is always present, possibly as an empty string. The bundle localizations are the constant ["en"], and the matched localization is therefore always "en", so no Windows input stands for AppleLanguages. Then: languageIdentifierWithScriptCodeForLocaleIdentifier (:1639-1655) is applied to both the preferred locale and "en" (uloc_addLikelySubtags, language-script). If they are equal, the preferred locale is kept. Otherwise localeIdentifierByReplacingLanguageCodeAndScriptCode (:1657-1708) runs: maximize the preferred locale, set language en and script Latn, keep the numbering system only if it is valid for en and not its default, keep the other components. Then its step-3 canonicalization (:1704-1705) drops the script only where it is implicit, that is where uloc_addLikelySubtags(language_region) yields the same script. It never minimizes the language or region away. If the preferred locale is empty or a guard returns nil, the result is the canonical preferred locale, and if that is empty, "en_001" (:236-239, :274-279). Pinned results: de-DE gives en_DE, fr-FR gives en_FR, en-GB gives en_GB, en-US gives en_US and the invariant culture gives en_001. Under de-DE, Formatted(12345L) is "12.345" and the .long date of 2021-01-17T22:03:12Z in UTC is "17 January 2021". Under fr-FR it is "12,345". Under the invariant culture it is "12,345". Every test of this derivation carries the new Oracle O-37, allocated here: "Locale.current of the English-only app is the user's region with its language replaced by en (swift-foundation bundle matching)". It is unverified on macOS 26 (ED-086), and _canonicalLocaleIdentifier there is CoreFoundation code outside the open source. Live updates on WM_SETTINGCHANGE (CultureInfo.ClearCachedData) belong to the App layer. This default is Locale.current for the whole port. Other units that consult Locale.current follow this default; SwiftString.LocalizedCaseInsensitiveContains and its siblings, which read CultureInfo.CurrentCulture today, need a Core repair to match. Edits: IMPLEMENTING.md Appendix B gains row O-37, and R-FMT-2 gains the sentence 'Locale.current is SwiftFormatters.CurrentLocale, whose default is the bundle-matched en_<region> id of ED-132 (O-37).'

[FMT] The user's 12/24-hour preference. In swift-foundation, AppleICUForce24HourTime and AppleICUForce12HourTime become LocalePreferences.hourCycle: h23, h12 or nil, with 24 winning (Locale_Preferences.swift:193-198, :327-335). ## ED-135

[FMT] U+202F before the day period. Windows icu.dll 72.1 carries the CLDR alt="ascii" en time patterns, with U+0020 before a. macOS 26 and CLDR 42+ use U+202F: CLDR release-46 en.xml lists each U+202F pattern next to its alt="ascii" U+0020 twin. DECISION: the formatter repairs the pattern udatpg returns, before udat_open, for a locale whose language is en. An unquoted U+0020 directly before an unquoted pattern letter 'a' becomes U+202F. Quoted literals, 'b' and 'B' fields and U+202F already present are left unchanged, so the repair is idempotent. There is one exception, from checking all release-46 en*.xml: for a locale whose region is ID, the pattern of skeleton hmsv ("h.mm.ss. a v") keeps U+0020. No call site reaches it, since no style uses 'v' and ID is a 24-hour region. It is one named constant marked O-23. Other languages pass through icu.dll unchanged (ED-073's named ICU deviation). No app-local ICU and no package. The existing U+202F tests stay and must pass.

## ED-139

[ALL] Option (b). In SwiftPath.Normalize, a leading \\?\UNC\ (with 'UNC' matched ASCII case-insensitively) becomes \\ before backslashes are turned to forward slashes, so \\?\UNC\srv\share\a normalizes to //srv/share/a. ## ED-141

[ALL] SwiftPath.StandardizingPath and SwiftPath.StandardizedFileURLPath are purely lexical on Windows. They never read the file system, never resolve a junction, symbolic link or other reparse point, and give the same result whether or not the path exists. Why: on macOS, standardizingPath resolves links before '..' so that the standardized string names the file the kernel would open, because POSIX applies '..' to the link's real parent. Windows applies '..' lexically before the file system sees the path. Measured on this PC: with J a junction to A\B, opening J\..\x.txt read the x.txt beside J, not A\x.txt, through both cmd and .NET. So the lexical result is the one that names the same file as the original on Windows, which is the parity the Swift's resolution buys. The '/private' removal has no Windows counterpart. ED-037 already dropped the /private spellings for this feature. Where the Swift wants links resolved it asks for it explicitly: ProjectGuidance.swift:66-67 (resolvingSymlinksInPath) and WorkingTreeWatch.swift:125-127 (realpath). Those are separate operations that belong to their own units and are not part of this one. No product surface changes.

[MCP][STORE] JSONValue's writer on a non-finite Double. Oracle item O-47 (Appendix B). Basis: the literal reading of JSONValue.swift:62, where `try?` catches only a thrown error, plus R-CODE-5 (a non-finite JSON Double is an EncodingError, a thrown error under SwiftTry.IsThrownError). Apple's documentation says data(withJSONObject:options:) raises an exception for an object that cannot produce valid JSON, and isValidJSONObject excludes NaN and infinity. The park is "null" and not a trap for this reason: no Swift code builds a non-finite .double (only :32 from a parse and :150 from a float literal), but the port's parse does. Measured on .NET 10, JsonElement.TryGetDouble returns true with +/-infinity for "1e400", "-1e400" and a 400-digit integer. A trap would therefore crash the port on provider JSON that Darwin may reject at parse time (O-09). ## ED-148

[PROVACP][MCP] The PR-PROVACP-150 performance guard is the one sanctioned R-TEST-5 exception. Decided: Sixteen_MiB_unterminated_in_8_byte_chunks_costs_about_as_much_as_complete_lines keeps its Stopwatch. It carries a Decision trait with this ED's assigned number, and a comment calls it the exception. Why: the record's verification_method explicitly asks for "a performance guard", and its windows_path says the same incremental behaviour is required "not just the same result", with no quadratic time. The mutation that rescans from the start of the remainder (search = start + 0 at :23) produces the same messages and the same scanned values at :58, because the no-match branches reset search at :28/:38. So elapsed work is its only observable, and the class has no deterministic probe for it. The guard stays within the spirit of R-TEST-5. It measures no product time and changes no clock the product reads. Its budget is 10x a baseline measured in the same run plus 2 s, with a mid-run check every 1024 appends. The mutation's cost is about 1.76e13 scanned bytes, many orders of magnitude over the budget, so contention from parallel test classes cannot turn a correct port red in practice. The exception covers this test only. R-TIME and the source scan still forbid Stopwatch in src, and no other test may cite this ED. The reviewer's other recorded points are correct and need no ruling. 4(a): a Prepend scalar joined to a colon always stays in the name part under both the Character split and an IndexOf split. ## ED-150

[UI] AppZoom's ZoomLayout under Avalonia's measure clamp. Take option (a). ZoomLayout is a Panel (ED-095). MeasureOverride returns Size(0,0) when there is no child (:35). Otherwise it measures the first child with each dimension of the available size divided by the scale, keeping infinity infinite (:48-50, where a nil SwiftUI dimension is an infinite Avalonia constraint), and returns the child's DesiredSize times the scale (:36-37). ArrangeOverride arranges the first child at Rect(0, 0, finalSize.Width/scale, finalSize.Height/scale) and returns finalSize, doing nothing when there is no child (:40-46, :44 unscaled(bounds.size)). It never arranges from the measured size. Do not override MeasureCore and do not add a clamp of your own. Why: Avalonia 12.1.2's Layoutable.MeasureCore clamps every control's DesiredSize to its own constraint. So the child's DesiredSize is already at most the unscaled proposal, and the size the child really wants above that is lost before ZoomLayout reads it. Overriding the panel's MeasureCore therefore changes nothing. The drafter's throwaway probe against 12.1.2 in %TEMP% gave 'zoom(MeasureCore override) desired 1000, 800, child desired 500, 400'. Reaching the child's real wish would take a layout protocol the port does not have. Where the port differs from Swift: only when the content wants more than the host divided by the scale does the zoom report the host size (1000x800) where Swift reports 1400x1000 at 200 or 1125x900 at 75. When the content wants less, the port and Swift agree exactly. Placement and drawing do not change, because :44 places from the bounds. Why nothing visible changes: every Swift site hosts the zoom in FrameHostingView with `sizingOptions = []` (WindowManager.swift:104, :195-201; RootView.swift:267-270, :276-281). The host's frame defines the size, and the content's fitting size never sizes a window, a minimum window size or a chat column. Condition of this ED: in the port, every host of AppZoomModifier (the window roots and the chat column hosts) must arrange the zoom at the host's own frame and never size anything from the zoom's DesiredSize. That mirrors sizingOptions = []. If a port site ever sizes from it (SizeToContent, an Auto row or column, a StackPanel, a minimum size taken from the content), the deviation becomes visible and that site must STOP for an owner question under PORT_CONTRACT.md:181. Record: (i) append ED-150 to porting/engineering_decisions.md, tagged [UI], citing AppZoom.swift:34-50, WindowManager.swift:104 and :195-201, RootView.swift:267-270, ED-095 and the probe output; (ii) append to PR-WIN-220's windows_path in porting/spec/WIN.json: 'Avalonia clamps every DesiredSize to its constraint (ED-150), so when the content wants more than the host divided by the scale, the layout reports the host size rather than the content's wish times the scale; placement from the arranged bounds is unchanged, and hosts arrange the zoom at their own frame as FrameHostingView (sizingOptions = []) does.' Leave expected_result as the Swift behaviour and add no spec `deviation` field, because every one of those is backed by an OD; (iii) in code, put `// DEVIATION ED-150: Avalonia clamps the child's and this panel's DesiredSize to the constraint; AppZoom.swift:36-37 does not clamp.` on the MeasureOverride return and the same marker on the new test. Do not touch docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, because the port has no such file. Visual parity stays under PR-WIN-219's capture comparison at 75, 100 and 200 and PR-WIN-220's interaction test at 200. Once adopted, this ED is the ruling the unit's PENDING RULING comment waits for.

## ED-151

[THEME][UI] NSSound, which the pilot's FinishChime and SettleChime tests stopped on. SOURCE FACTS: the only NSSound sites at B2 are the two chimes. Each builds one sound lazily in a static (FinishChime.swift:12-16, SettleChime.swift:11-15) from ToneSynth.wave bytes with NSSound(data:), which yields nil when the data cannot be read, and sets a Float volume. FinishChime.play() calls play() only: NSSound declines a play while that sound is already playing (FinishChime.swift:19-21), so several finishes at once make one chime. SettleChime.play() calls stop() and then play(), a replay from the top (SettleChime.swift:17-21). DECISION: a foundation unit F.Sound provides SwiftSound in src/Marrow.UI/Port/SwiftSound.cs: static SwiftSound? Create(byte[] data), which returns null when the data is not a PCM WAV the port can play, as NSSound(data:) returns nil; float Volume; bool Play(), which returns false and does nothing while this sound is playing; bool Stop(); and bool IsPlaying. Output goes through the seam SoundOutput.Current, an Ambient<ISoundOutput> (the MainActor.Executor pattern). Production plays on the default output device through the Windows waveOut API (winmm.dll by P/Invoke, no new package), with Volume applied to the samples. Tests use a fake output that records each play, stop and volume, and completes a playback on demand. The chime units test against the fake: the bytes and volume of the one sound each builds, that it is built once and only on first use, swallow-while-playing (FinishChime), stop-then-play (SettleChime), and silence when Create returns null.

## ED-152

[NET][SAFETY] F.HTTP redirects (blocker 1, 2026-09-23). (1) Redirect limit: `Http.cs` `MaximumRedirects` becomes 20. URLSession follows 20 redirects and the 21st redirect response fails the task with URLError(.httpTooManyRedirects) before another request goes out. The source gives no number (every site leaves redirects to URLSession: MCPHub.swift:455-465, LinkTitles.swift:47, PlanLimits.swift:243-249; no redirect delegate anywhere in the tree). Best evidence: swift-corelibs-foundation swift-6.2-RELEASE FoundationNetworking/URLSession/HTTP/HTTPURLProtocol.swift:459-465, `redirectCount > 20` fails with NSURLErrorHTTPTooManyRedirects, commented "This value mirrors Darwin". CFNetwork's value is undocumented, so it is parked as oracle O-48; its tests carry Oracle O-48 and no Req trait. The loop shape at Http.cs:662 is unchanged. (2) Safety default under O-29: once a redirect chain has changed origin (scheme, host or port), no Authorization is sent again for the rest of the chain, whether it came from the request fields or from the configuration's HttpAdditionalHeaders. The Hop record gains `bool LeftOrigin` (false on the first hop; `hop.LeftOrigin || !sameOrigin` in Redirected), and Build skips a configuration field named Authorization (ordinal ignore case) when LeftOrigin is true. Every other configuration header still goes on every hop, as corelibs does (HTTPURLProtocol.swift:497-499). No user-visible change: the only configuration headers in the source are UpdateChecker.swift:108 (User-Agent, Accept). Port-only guard, not a deviation. Tests: two O-48 tests in HttpTests.cs (20 followed; the 21st fails, no timed negative wait), two O-29 tests in HttpSecondTests.cs whose chain includes a same-origin hop inside the foreign origin (server/a, other/b, other/c, server/d), so the sticky rule is actually exercised. Not adopted from corelibs, recorded so nobody cites it as parity: corelibs also follows 305 and 306 and turns HEAD into GET on a 303; Http.cs does neither and no Swift site depends on it. Open, not decided here: user-configured MCP headers that carry credentials under other names (MCPHub.swift:459, MCPProbe.swift:312, MCPProxy.swift:325-329) still cross origins on a redirect; that is an owner question (work/rulings2/owner_questions.md, Q1) and blocks the MCPHub, MCPProbe and MCPProxy units until answered.

## ED-156

[SET][FS] Production settings store (blocker 5; closes ED-079's "Action: decide the production format"). (1) Format, approved as fcd7934 has it: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Marrow Code\UserDefaults.json (SettingsStore.ProductionPath(localAppData); tests pass a folder under MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR), compact UTF-8 JSON with no BOM, one object with keys in ordinal order, each value a one-member object tagged with the XML property-list element name: bool; integer (Int64); real in shortest round-trip text, -0 kept, non-finite as the strings +infinity, -infinity, nan; string; data (base64); date (round-trip UTC "O"); array; dict (ordinal keys). Read skips exactly one leading UTF-8 BOM and such a file counts as fully read. No oracle item: cfprefsd's plist is not observable by any Swift code. (2) Recovery: a missing file is an empty store and nothing is created until the first write; an existing unreadable file makes the constructor throw. When Load does not take every top-level entry (parse failure, non-object root, or any entry TryRead rejects), the constructor first preserves the original bytes: if an existing <path>.unreadable or <path>.unreadable-N (tested File.Exists || Directory.Exists) already holds the same bytes, nothing is written; otherwise FileOps.WriteAtomic to the first free name, never overwriting an earlier copy; if that write fails, the constructor throws. The main file stays untouched until the first write. (3) Writes use the DiskWriter shape (Storage.swift:337-356; IMPLEMENTING.md:426): Set and RemoveObject update the map under the lock and return; one private SerialQueue writes the newest snapshot, coalesced (one Async per first enqueue), with FileOps.WriteAtomic outside the lock and LastWriteError set or cleared in `catch (Exception e) when (SwiftTry.IsThrownError(e))`. Port-only `bool Synchronize()` (twin of UserDefaults.synchronize(), WebsiteCaptures.swift:109) drains the queue and returns LastWriteError is null; on the writer thread it returns without waiting. ISettingsStore is unchanged. A whole-file snapshot is safe because the app is single-instance (ED-002). Named risk: a process killed within milliseconds of a Set loses that change, where the Mac keeps it in cfprefsd. A string with a lone surrogate is written as U+FFFD, which matches what a Swift String holds after bridging; do not "fix" it with a throw. (4) Test correction: the 7676733 tests that asserted durability at return get Synchronize() before every reopen or disk inspection and at the end of every writing test (so no queued write outlives its folder or TestRuntime); Writes_apply_in_order_and_each_is_on_disk_when_the_call_returns is renamed Writes_apply_in_order_and_are_on_disk_once_Synchronize_returns; no expected value changes. (5) integer(forKey:) and double(forKey:) are not built: no B2 caller (R-SET-1 stands). The constructor read keeps no retry; if start-up reads hit sharing violations, the App binding unit raises a Core FileOps read-with-retry. The Marrow.App start-up unit binds UserDefaults.Standard to this store and calls Synchronize() on normal exit and from the unhandled-exception handler.

## ED-158

[UI] F.StyledText rendering (blocker 7; ED-092 (3)). (1) Image runs: SwiftUI Text(Image) is a Text value, so StyledText gains the constructor `StyledText(IImage image, bool isTemplate)` (MarkdownView.swift:391-403, :491) and two trailing Run fields with defaults, `IImage? Image = null, bool IsTemplateImage = false`; an image run's Text is "". An image run renders as one InlineUIContainer; a non-template image is an Image sized to image.Size in DIPs; a template image is a Border of that size whose OpacityMask is ImageBrush(s) with Stretch.Fill when `image is IImageBrushSource s`, DrawingBrush(d.Drawing) when `image is DrawingImage d`, otherwise NotSupportedException naming ED-158; when run.Color is set, TextElement.SetForeground(border, run.Color.Brush(border)), and in every case Border.Background is bound to the border's own inherited TextElement.Foreground, so an uncoloured template image takes the text's foreground with no subscription on the host. (2) Baseline: the child's baseline is always set locally, TextBlock.SetBaselineOffset(child, h + (run.BaselineOffset ?? 0)), because the property inherits; if h + offset is exactly 0, write 1e-6 (Avalonia's IsZero falls back to the height). A positive offset raises the run; the mention glyph (16 DIP, -3.2, MarkdownView.swift:386, :490-493) gets 12.8. The SwiftUI side is oracle O-49. (3) One Inline per stored run, in order, no coalescing, empty runs kept; `AppendTo(InlineCollection inlines, TextBlock host)` appends this value's inlines only, so VeiledText can interleave them with its own prose (StreamVeil.swift:295-300, :326-331); `Render(TextBlock host)` does `host.Inlines ??= new InlineCollection()`, Clear(), AppendTo. (4) A text run with a non-null, non-zero BaselineOffset makes Render and AppendTo throw NotSupportedException("StyledText: a numeric baseline offset on a text run has no B2 caller (ED-158)"): the only baselineOffset in the tree is on the image (MarkdownView.swift:493). (5) Text-run styles go only through public TextElement and Inline properties: a Font is resolved with the run's weight, italic and monospaced digits and copied into FontFamily, FontSize, FontWeight, FontStyle and FontFeatures (tnum = 1); with no Font only what the run changes is set; weight uses SwiftFont's own mapping through an internal helper; underline and strikethrough are a new TextDecorationCollection with no stroke. Colour brushes come from a private static ConditionalWeakTable<TextBlock, Dictionary<SwiftColor, IBrush>>, calling color.Brush(host) only on a miss, so repeated renders (VeiledText re-renders every fade frame) add at most one theme handler per colour per host. (6) Modifier precedence: a modifier sets its trait only on runs where that trait is still null (inner wins), as SwiftUI resolves Text modifiers outside in; oracle O-50. Test correction: in Applying_a_trait_does_not_erase_the_other_run_styles delete only `Assert.Equal(SwiftFont.Weight.Bold, run.Weight);`, and add An_inner_trait_wins_over_the_same_trait_applied_outside (Oracle O-50). No B2 site applies the same trait at two levels, so no B2 output changes. (7) Links stay with the MarkdownView unit (AttributedString, ED-092 (3)).

The Swift mechanism (WorkingTreeWatch.swift:246-273) writes a cookie and waits for that cookie's event, with no flush, poll or probe, so it counts exactly what the kernel reported before the cookie; the doc comment at :241-243 claims more than the mechanism does. Full fresh captures for in-root watches and a USN-journal proof are rejected for this unit (PA-0017 keeps the USN idea as a separate proposal). ## ED-162

[LAUNCH][WIN] HangWatchdog stack capture (blocker 11; PR-LAUNCH-017; replaces /usr/bin/sample, HangWatchdog.swift:95-112). The port-only src/Marrow.Core/Port/StackSampler.cs runs on the hang-watchdog thread and uses the runtime's documented diagnostics IPC on its own process only (pipe "dotnet-diagnostic-" + Environment.ProcessId; an internal overload takes a pipe name, for tests). Sequence: connect NamedPipeClientStream (Asynchronous); send EventPipe CollectTracing2 (0x02/0x03; circularBufferMB 256, format NetTrace, requestRundown true; providers Microsoft-DotNETCore-SampleProfiler level 4 and Microsoft-Windows-DotNETRuntime level 5, keywords 0x18 Loader|Jit); read the reply and session id; drain the trace stream continuously from then until end of stream (the runtime's session disable waits for its streaming thread, so an undrained pipe deadlocks Stop); wait 2 s on SwiftClock; send StopTracing (0x02/0x01) on a second connection. Bounds, each a CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan, SwiftClock.Provider.Current): connect 2 s, CollectTracing reply 2 s, window 2 s, Stop exchange plus end of stream 10 s; on any bound both pipes are disposed, which abandons the session. Parse the nettrace version the runtime writes; attribute ThreadSample stacks to OS threads; name frames from MethodLoadVerbose and MethodDCEndVerbose ranges. Body layout (the capturer's own, ED-003 (1)): one block per sampled thread, main first then ascending OS id; header "Thread <osid>" plus " (main)" plus ":"; distinct stacks in descending sample count, ties first-seen, as "  <count> samples" then frames innermost first, four-space indent, "Namespace.Type.Method(signature)", "[Native Frames]" or "[unresolved 0x<hex>]"; blank line between blocks. Failure bodies keep ED-003's two cases: never started (pipe missing, connect or reply timeout, IPC error, any exception before a session id) gives exactly "stack capture could not run: " + reason + "\n"; started but ended abnormally gives "stack capture ended early: " + one of "no end of trace within 10 s", "runtime error 0x<8 upper hex>", "malformed trace at byte <n>" + "\n\n" + the stacks parsed so far. No exception leaves the capturer (ED-078).
