## ED-257

[UI][SETTINGS][MCP][GLASS] MCPSettingsPage: the `.glass` action buttons and the editor's Add server / Save (heading ED-257; the lead numbers it at merge). (1) THE SMALL `.glass` PILL IS ACCENT-FILLED UNDER A TINTED WINDOW. SOURCE FACT (reference video 1-settings-tour.mov, stills scene-1-settings-tour-186.00 and -187.00, 2560x1440, pink pixels R>200, G<120, B>90 counted by E:/Droppy/work/scratch/mcpsettingspage/pill_measure.py): the Swift `.buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small)` buttons of the cards and rows (MCPSettingsPage.swift:324-330,345-348,503-507,525-528) draw as a solid accent capsule 20 pt tall (Connect 65 x 20, Sign in 56 x 20, median fill (247,47,121)) with a white label; the cause is the window's `.tint(accent)` (WindowManager.swift:177,191; Popovers.swift:11). The earlier comment "plain .glass takes no tint" (MCPSettingsPage.cs, FollowUpEditor.cs:71-75) is refuted for a tinted window. MCPSettingsPage.ActionButton now reads the inherited Popovers.TintProperty (the one ThemeTint sets, WindowManager.cs:818) and fills the capsule with it at full strength under a SwiftColor.White label, following a later change of the tint; width is the label plus 12 each side. ENGINEERING DECISION: an untinted window (System, Light and Dark themes: the property is null) keeps the neutral interactive glass with the primary label colour, UNVERIFIED (no video of that case; OD-0098 says the source is then the proof, and the source states only `.glass`). The hover and press fills of the pill (catalogue hover.accent-pill-instant, press.accent-pill) are not modelled. (2) THE CONTROL SIZES. A `.controlSize(.small)` button is 20 pt tall with an 11 pt label (measured); the editor's button has no controlSize (MCPSettingsPage.swift:698-702), so it is regular: 22 pt tall (measured for a text-only `.glass` regular button, Providers Login, S 174.50) with a 13 pt label (the regular control's text style, Add pair S 120.50 measures about 13 pt); both replace the former Chrome.CapsuleContentHeight (28) and 11 pt label. (3) `.glassProminent` ("Fix it", Add server, Save) is drawn with the same capsule, always filled: by the window's tint, else by the accent, under a white label, with the glass effect tinted by it. ENGINEERING DECISION, UNVERIFIED: no `.glassProminent` control is in the reference videos; only the size follows (2). (4) THE ARGUMENT EDITOR'S INSET (OD-0032, "Windows argument-editor inset compensation"): the argument box carries Padding (11, 4), the source's 6 plus the 5 a Mac TextEditor's text has inside its padding (SettingsView.swift:829 pads the commit-instruction placeholder by 5 to line up with a TextEditor's text; the video, S 199.50, measures that placeholder 16.7 px in from the card edge, 12 + 5); the vertical 4 is the source's (the same placeholder has no vertical padding). (5) NOT PROVEN, FOUND BY THE REAL-PRESENTER TESTS: with the editor open in the real presenter (overlay host), Escape does not close its popover; nothing in PopoverHost, Presentation or PlainControls handles Escape (NSPopover's transient behaviour closes on it). Outside MCPSettingsPage.

## ED-258

[THEME][UI][SIDEBAR] Port-side choices from the SidebarView parity pass (unit/parity-sidebarview, review passes 1 and 2, pass 2 in rounds 2 and 3, 2026-10-03), each where the Swift names the behaviour but not a Windows or Avalonia mechanism for it. (1) SwiftUI `Color.red`. B3's one sidebar site is SidebarView.swift:927 `Text("Delete").foregroundStyle(.red)`, the archive question's Delete label (PR-SIDEBAR-095). ED-092 sends a system colour with no B3 value to the macOS documented values, and ED-104 records the method for Color.yellow as an appearance pair. DECISION: SwiftColor.Red is an appearance pair, light sRGB #FF383C (255, 56, 60) and dark #FF4245 (255, 66, 69), both opaque. These are the Red entries of the 'System colours Light/Dark' rows of the macOS 27 UI Kit (OD-0045; read into E:\Droppy\work\apple-kit\macos27-uikit-controls.md:57-58), the same table edition whose Yellow entries are exactly ED-104's (255, 204, 0) and (255, 214, 0). Increased contrast is not modelled (as ED-104). UNVERIFIED under OD-0001, no oracle id. Before this the port drew #FF3B30 in both appearances. Not changed: AppTheme.FrameworkRed (#FF3B30), the Chrome.danger fallback of the three system-hue themes, which PR-THEME-031's windows_path fixes as one constant red; whether that constant should follow this pair is a THEME question, not this unit's. (2) Glyphs that leave the Hydra head card (UI-SIDEBAR-038; SidebarView.swift:1466-1516, :1535, :1541; 2-chat-use.mov 5.33-5.40 s, where the glyphs past twelve fade in and out on the chevron's toggle). A SwiftUI view leaving under the default .opacity transition no longer takes part in the layout the others settle into; an Avalonia panel keeps a fading child in its layout until it is removed, so a leaving row would hold the chevron down and let it jump when the fade ends. DECISION: a glyph or chevron that leaves is lifted out of its row onto a canvas layer over the card, at the place it was drawn, and fades there; the layer is the card's own size, clipped to the same rounded shape (:1521), and takes no input. A glyph or chevron that joins fades in where it is placed. On the chevron's own toggle its symbol changes (:1516): the chevron that goes leaves this way, where it stood, and the one that comes joins (review round 2: 2-chat-use.mov 5.340-5.378 s shows the down-chevron still drawn, faint, where it stood 17-27 ms after the press, then gone). The animation is the innermost `.animation` whose value changed: :1535 snappy(0.18) when the card's row count changes, else :1541 Chrome.panelSlide when the head ids change, else the transaction the change came in (the chevron's own withAnimation(.snappy(0.18)), :1515-1516); none for the first build. Still open (OD-0076, not claimed): the surviving glyphs jump to new places where the Mac glides them (UI-SIDEBAR-036), and so does a chevron that keeps its symbol while the card's rows change under it (a head joining or leaving while every head shows); and (review round 3, not this unit's) a glyph or chevron still fading in from the chevron's toggle jumps to full opacity before it fades out when the chevron is pressed again within 0.18 s (HeadCardsRow.Leave places it whole and SwiftTransition.Remove starts from there: ED-159's unruled interruption follow-up, continuing from the presentation value, which OD-0076's 'no single-frame jump' presses). (3) Row state across a new pass of the list, and within a row. SwiftUI keeps a row's @State under its ForEach id (:470-472, :524) and hands the row its new inputs, and keeps the view of a conditional's branch while the branch holds. DECISION: the list hands a surviving ProjectRow its new snapshot and count, a surviving HeadCardsRow its new heads, and (review round 2) a surviving SidebarHelperRow its new snapshot and isLast (its connector drawn again for it), in place (SidebarView.UpdateItemView), so an open Remove-project question (OD-0008 A9, OD-0012 E2), an open ellipsis menu and an expanded head card survive a new thread. Within a row the branch's view is kept while the branch holds: ProjectRow's ellipsis-and-plus HStack and its count Text (:1115-1133), SidebarHelperRow's ellipsis (:1375-1384), so an open menu keeps the button it hangs on when the row's record, count or hover changes; a kept RowActionsButton is handed how to build its actions and builds them as its menu opens (a RowActionsButton overload, UI/Chrome/Popovers.cs; SwiftUI hands the button the body's new actions on every render). Still open (UNRESOLVED, not claimed): SidebarThreadRow, HelperStubRow and the headers still take a new value by a rebuild where they stand, so their own @State may not survive a change of their record; a menu already open keeps the items it opened with where SwiftUI would re-render them under it (a helper's Reveal worktree item and a project's activation items are the ones that can change, and only by a change made elsewhere while it is open); a helper row's status is drawn again, by a cut, when the record's unread mark or last status changes, where ActivityStatus (:2410-2427) would change inside itself; the count Text takes a new number in place with no content transition (how SwiftUI draws a Text's new string under an animation is not settled here). (4) SidebarRow's accessory (UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:731-737; UI-SIDEBAR-058, PR-SIDEBAR-126, PR-WIN-200). SwiftUI keeps `accessory(isHovering)`'s views under their structural identity, and a conditional in it that changes branch runs the default .opacity transition under the transaction in force: the hover's withAnimation(Chrome.hover). The port's SidebarRow takes a closure that returns a control, which says nothing of identity. DECISION: the control is the identity: the control the closure returned last time is the same view and stays where it is, untouched; any other control is another branch, and the old one leaves and the new one joins on SwiftTransition's default opacity under the current transaction (at once with none); the first body places it. A caller whose accessory reads its own state asks again through SidebarRow.RefreshAccessory, with the row's own hover. The EmptyView accessories (the shorthand initializer, Chrome.swift:748-757, and Settings' rows, SettingsView.swift:149) keep one empty control. (5) SidebarRow's selection (review round 3; UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:683, :717-718, :729, :738, :741-745; PR-WIN-200 'with the selection change animated on the 0.1-second hover curve'). SwiftUI hands a row its parent's new `isSelected` under the row's identity, and `.background { shape.fill(fill).animation(Chrome.hover, value: isSelected) }` puts its own curve on the fill for a change of that value whatever the transaction. The one SidebarRow whose selection changes is the Settings sidebar's (SettingsView.swift:148-149, a ForEach over the visible pages); 1-settings-tour.mov 47.765-47.85 s shows the wash leave General and reach Hydra together over about 0.1 s (E:\Droppy\work\parity\evidence\SidebarView\review\round3\settings_selection_measure.txt). ## ED-260

[UI][CHAT][TEST] TimelineRows, the rows of the timeline (records UI-CHAT-024 to -061, -070 to -072, UI-GIT-044 to -050, UI-HYDRAMERGE-002 to -007, UI-RUNTIME-001 to -004), proven from the pinned source under OD-0098 (2026-10-03: where no reference video shows a state, the Swift is the proof). Each reading below is an ENGINEERING DECISION where it relies on a framework's documented behaviour; none changes what the Mac shows. (1) THE CONTINUOUS CORNER. SOURCE FACT: every pill, card and plate of these records is `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:, style: .continuous)` (TimelineRows.swift:313, :464, :579, :691, :1012, :1817, :2137, :2155, :2364, :2398, :2660, :2818; ChatBadge.swift:49, :65; and `.clipShape` of the delegation card's wave, :698). ED-181 says every such site draws through SwiftShapes so that the curve, when it lands, changes only that file. Two sites did not: ChatBadge's pill and its clip (a raw CornerRadius and a RectangleGeometry) and the delegation wave's clip (a RectangleGeometry). DECIDED: both go through SwiftShapes now (`RoundedRectangle`, `RoundedRectangleGeometry`, `.Continuous`), drawing the same circular arcs as before until the curve lands (MARROW_DEFERRED ED-181 still holds). TimelineRowsCdTests pins the radius and the style of every site (a Rule test, no Req: the curve itself is not proven), so a record resting on them lacks nothing but the curve; the working line of ThreadTimeline.cs:1551 still sets a raw CornerRadius and is the ThreadTimeline unit's. (2) THE TURN DURATION. SOURCE FACT: Components.swift:37-40 formats `Duration.seconds(max(0, Int(interval.rounded())))` with `.units(allowed: [.seconds, .minutes, .hours], width: .narrow, maximumUnitCount: 2, fractionalPart: .hide(rounded: .down))`; the reference video shows "5s", "10s", "28s", "38s", "1m 23s" and "Failed after 1s" (2-chat-use.mov 9.0 s and 168.0 s). The port's formatter is swift-foundation's own algorithm (SwiftFormatters.DurationUnits, Oracle O-65, with its boundary tests); the boundaries no frame shows (60 s "1m", 3599 s "59m 59s", 3600 s "1h", 3725 s "1h 2m", rounding to whole seconds first) are what that algorithm gives, in the en_US register of the video. TimelineRowsCdTests holds them. (3) THE LINK STYLE. `.buttonStyle(.link)` on the output's Show full output button draws its label in the view's tint, the theme's accent (OD-0088, ED-253), with the pointing hand; the earlier "no approved link-style adapter" stop (TimelineRowsUiAuditTests #4) is resolved by them. (4) THE DEFAULT ACTION. `.keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)` on Revert (:2791) is Button.IsDefault in the port: Return pressed in the hosted confirmation activates it once and closes the popover first (a Rule test; the small control size of :2796 stays UNRESOLVED, no source or frame gives its metrics). (5) NOT SETTLED, NAMED. The settle glide's soft arrival (Chrome.swift:938-955, .opacity(isVisible ? 1 : 0).offset(y: ...) under .animation(.softAppear)): SwiftTransition.Gather gives a modifier with no animatable data its identity at the start of the transaction (ED-098 (2)), so a finished head's pill, and every other soft appear, shows at once instead of fading up from 4 points low. SwiftUI animates the body's own opacity and offset, so the Mac fades. The fix belongs to Chrome and F.SwiftAnimation (every user of softAppear), not to TimelineRows; UI-CHAT-052 waits for it as well as for the curve.

[UI][CHAT][TEST] HydraMergeTrack duration when the step and the mode change in the same pass (TimelineRows.swift:838-839, UI-HYDRAMERGE-004; reviewer finding 2026-10-04). ENGINEERING DECISION: the body carries two `.animation(_, value:)` modifiers, `.smooth(duration: 0.5)` for `step` closest to the view and `.smooth(duration: 0.45)` for `mode` outside it. SwiftUI hands the transaction down from the outer modifier to the inner one and the one nearest the view has the last word, so a mode alone takes 0.45 s and a step, alone or together with the mode (the outcome note pins the step to the last dot and leaves running in one pass, :962-964), takes 0.5 s. The port picks `step != step ? 0.5 : 0.45`. This precedence is not a recorded reference result (no reference video isolates it), so the record's own clauses (a step alone 0.5 s, a mode alone 0.45 s) are proven by TimelineRowsFinMergeRowTests.A_step_alone_glides_over_half_a_second_and_a_mode_alone_settles_over_0_45_seconds and the combined case carries Rule R-TEST-4, not a Req.

(1) A CLI THAT CANNOT BE LAUNCHED. DEFECT: ProviderRegistry.LoadCommands' catch stored SwiftErrors.LocalizedDescription(error) (ProviderRegistry.swift:855-858 stores error.localizedDescription). A launch failure (the thread's folder is gone, the executable cannot start, the command line is too long) is a Win32Exception, InvalidOperationException or CommandLineTooLongException, none an ILocalizedError or ISwiftErrorIdentity, so that call throws NotSupportedException by design (SwiftErrors.cs:121-125) inside the catch of a non-throwing MainActor task, which ends the process (SwiftTask.cs:188-205). ENGINEERING DECISION (per site, R-ERR-2, O-14, the same decision as PiCLI.StartFailureDescription and ThreadRuntime :1736 and :2599, UI-RUNTIME-042): such an error is stored by its own Message (Windows' text for the failure; macOS has Foundation's), every error that has a Swift description keeps it; the in-flight entry is removed as before, so Retry is not stuck behind it. Evidence (stand-ins only, the fail-closed ClaudeScript and ProviderProbeStandIns; no real CLI): ProviderRegistryCommandErrorTests (the stored text equals the Message of the same handshake failure caught directly, locale-proof; no list invented; the in-flight map empty; the next forced load lists and clears the error; the 33rd key evicts the oldest entry WITH its error, which the existing eviction test only proved vacuously), ComposerViewTests (a folder that is gone shows the launch failure and its Retry row instead of ending the app; a failing retry replaces the note; two composers on one provider and folder, and two spellings of the folder, launch the CLI once; a composer for Copilot, Cursor or DeepSeek launches nothing: one pump after the slash, because LoadCommands registers its load before its first await; it used to wait 1.5 s on the clock, R-TEST-5; mutant: the provider guard removed, killed for Copilot and Cursor, and DeepSeek has no executable to launch). SOURCE FACT: StreamVeil.swift:51-55 a veil's first call adopts its text as the baseline without fading it, so the words of a block that is new are not a veil's chunk; what dissolves a new block in is the block's own insertion: MarkdownView.swift:86-97 is a ForEach over blocks.enumerated() with id: \.offset, every block wears .transition(softAppear) (:92, :51-56), and Chrome.swift:949-961 gives the insertion opacity 0 to 1 with a 4 pt offset to 0 over Animation.softAppear (smooth, 0.32 s, about 0.352 s to settle) with an animation of its own, so it runs without an ambient one and carries on through the evaluations that follow. DEFECT (measured by the review: a flush from "Hello" to "Hello there" and a new second block left " there" veiled and "World begins" at full ink, opacity 1, no offset): the port builds the reply's whole tree again for every flush and never called SwiftTransition.Insert, so a block that a batch opened appeared whole, mid-stream and at the end of the stream (where, with nothing left dissolving, the reply also switched to prose runs at once). The first claim of round 2, "words that arrive together with the completion now fade in too", held only for a batch that extends a block that is there. ENGINEERING DECISION (PORT-ONLY, OD-0076): MarkdownVeils keeps, per markdown view (its path), whether its tree has been built before, and per block place (b{n}) when the block arrived (null for a block that was on screen when the tree first attached, StreamVeil.swift:18-19, and after Reset). MarkdownView.VeiledBlocks asks the scope: a block that is new in a known tree is inserted with SwiftTransition.Insert under :51-56's transition whose insertion half is decomposed into Opacity.Combined(Offset(y: 4)).Animation(Animation.SoftAppear) (Chrome.SoftAppear's modifier carries a Bool alone, which the transition mechanics apply at its identity at once, SwiftAnimation.cs Gather: the reason ThreadTimeline.RowTransition and HydraPanel give); the tree of the next flush, which builds that block's view again, continues the same arrival from where it was (SwiftTransition.Insert takes the time already elapsed), neither starting again nor finishing at once; a block that leaves (the parser re-deriving the reply shorter) arrives afresh if it comes back (TreeBuilt drops the places past the block count); Reset and Release (the end of the stream) forget the arrivals with the places. At the end of a stream the arrival is part of what still dissolves: FadingUntil also counts the blocks that are arriving, so the reply stays its veiled blocks until the later of the chunks and the arrivals has settled (about 0.35 s), then becomes prose runs; and that path is taken for any reply whose tree was built before, not only for one whose places hold text (a reply that so far drew only a table or a delegation card has no text place). Only the veiled views of a streaming reply insert: the prose runs of a settled reply still only attach their blocks' transition (PR-THEME-107, the OD-0076 transition audit). Evidence: MarkdownBlockArrivalTests (UI.Tests, the host path of the rows, manual frame and time sources, frame by frame every 20 ms: opacity and offset follow Animation.SoftAppear's curve, never go back, no frame moves a quarter of the travel, the blocks already there stay whole; an arrival carried on through three rebuilds with a second new block starting on its own; the first build and a Reset adopt; shrink and regrow arrives afresh; at the end of the stream the new block dissolves in before the prose runs, alone, with a chunk still fading (the later of the two is waited for), as a link paragraph, mid-stream too, and after a reply that drew only a table; nothing is kept afterwards, MarkdownVeils.Arrivals is 0) and TimelineRowsStreamVeilTests (App.Tests, the real AssistantMessageRow mid-stream, through the next flush, and at the end, and the narration). 12 mutants of the arrival killed: no arrival; restart on rebuild; snap on rebuild; the end-of-stream check ignoring arrivals; the end-of-stream path only for places that hold text; the first build arriving; Reset keeping arrivals; no prune; no offset; Release keeping arrivals; the tree never marked built; a shorter arrival length (three of them, no arrival, restart and the check ignoring arrivals, also at the real-row level). WindowCornerWedge (Marrow.UI.Chrome) fills the window's rectangle minus the very rounded rectangle the content is clipped to (SwiftShapes.RoundedRectangleGeometry at Chrome.WindowCornerRadius, continuous, so it follows the shape wherever ED-181 takes it) with the scrim the backdrop draws at that moment (WindowBackdrop.Scrim for the setting and the theme, black in dark and white in light; a window at 0.98 or more is solid, so the corners are too); it takes no pointer, follows the setting and the theme in the same frame as the backdrop, and sits BELOW the clip so the glass and its hairline still stop at the curve. RootView keeps its four source layers in order and adds the wedge as a fifth painted first (ZIndex -1; the two tests that counted four layers now count five); SettingsView puts it under its clipped frame and the Rise open (OD-0074, ED-249) fades it with the glass it belongs to. ## ED-261

[UI][SETTINGS][UPDATE][HAPTIC] Settings > About, the update views (AboutUpdateViews.swift; the blitz unit blitz-aboutupdateviews; the lead numbers it at merge). Three decisions, each a necessary internal choice. (1) THE CHECK NOW BUTTON IS THE SMALL ACCENT GLASS CAPSULE OF THE REFERENCE VIDEO (AboutUpdateViews.swift:826-833 `.buttonStyle(.glass).controlSize(.small)`, WindowManager.swift:162,170-191 `.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)` and `.tint(theme.spec.accent)` on every hosted window root; OD-0042 "as the reference videos show them"; supersedes the former untinted ChromeGlassCapsule with a callout label in 9 x 5 padding, about 25 pt tall, drawn the same when disabled). SOURCE FACT (1-settings-tour.mov, S 211.7-213.9, 2560x1440 at 1 px = 1 pt, on the Monokai theme, accent F92672, frames extracted and measured with PIL): the capsule is 20 pt tall and about 78 wide at rest with a white label of about 11 pt, fill (247,46,120) over a (52,59,60) backdrop; the hover frame is (254,68,141) and the press frame (254,79,189) with a violet glow under the pointer; "Checking..." is about 82 wide, a grey translucent capsule (75,84,85) over (53,60,59) with a dim label (123,133,136). DECISION: Marrow.UI.Chrome.SmallAccentGlassButton.Create(title, action, enabled): a 20 pt capsule, 10 pt side padding (Apple kit small row, apple-kit/macos27-uikit-controls.md:68), label 11 pt Medium. Enabled: the port's own material (OD-0005) tinted with Chrome.Accent at full strength and interactive, label white, plus a white wash over the face at 8 % under the pointer and 13 % while held, eased with Chrome.hover (OD-0076: the Mac changes in one frame, the port eases in its hover motion), because the material's own pointer light is a soft spot and the reference lightens the whole capsule; the constants are calibrated to the frames within the tolerances of SmallAccentGlassButtonTests. Disabled: the same material washed with the label colour at 11 %, not interactive, label at 30 % of the label colour (the video's grey fill is white at about 11 % over its backdrop and its label about 30 % of white over the fill). The press frame's violet glow and its 2 px growth per side are NOT reproduced (UNVERIFIED variance, blue is compared only as lighter than hover). Widths are Inter against the reference's SF (ED-059), compared with a tolerance of 8 pt. The row swaps its button and its sentence by a crossfade (OD-0076 T1, built below, review of 2026-10-04). Headless note: Avalonia.Headless composites the glass material only for an owner that is a direct child of the window's panel beside its backdrop, so SmallAccentGlassButtonTests render the button's own effect and parts at that arrangement; AboutUpdateViewsCheckNowLookTests pins the control inside the row (size, label, place, effect). Other pages' `.buttonStyle(.glass)` buttons (the About "Show" button beside it, Edit, Reveal, Choose) are drawn untinted by their own units today and are not changed here; the same recorded frames show Show as the same pink capsule, so they should move to this control. (2) Haptics.Sink (port-only Ambient<Action<HapticPattern>>, default no-op, ShortcutsSettingsPage.cs) is where Haptics.Perform goes, so the three call sites of the celebration sweep (AboutUpdateViews.swift:804,809,812) and their times can be observed on the manual clock; the shipped sink still does nothing (port_impacts X6: no sound or animation substitutes for a haptic). (3) UpdateProgressSlider follows the Reduce Motion environment live (:387,408 read it on every body evaluation), by a property-changed handler on the inherited property, so the sparkles drop and return when the Windows animation-effects setting changes while the slider shows; the pill's own chase response (:687-690) is still read when the face is built (an install that begins after a setting change reads the new value; a change mid-install does not move the already hosted slider's response: UNVERIFIED, rare). OD-0076 TRANSITIONS BUILT (review of 2026-10-04; each was a cut, the Swift's own `.animation(.easeInOut(0.18), value: isReady)` of :671 wraps the `if isReady {...} else {...}` branches of :643-660, whose removal and insertion take SwiftUI's default opacity transition, and OD-0076 rules every swap of content a crossfade): Marrow.App.Views.Settings.CrossfadeSlot is the place where content swaps: the old content fades out where it stood while the new fades in, over 0.18 s on the ease of :671 (easeInOut), on the frame clock, each layer going on from the opacity it has when a second swap meets one in flight (no jump), the slot's size easing from where it is to the new content's size over the same animation (a label whose width changes eases its container's width), the leaving content taking no input and leaving the tree when gone; under Reduce Motion (:671 `nil`; OD-0076's still clause) they cut. T1 the Check now row is built once: its button (label, accent capsule to grey and back) crossfades through a CrossfadeSlot and its detail sentence fades out over the first 0.09 s and the new words in over the second (HydraProgressBar's swap; the sentence keeps ChromeRow's own TextBlock, inside a SentenceHeightGlide box), and the box's height eases over the whole swap on the same curve, from the height it has to the height the new words take at the width given (an invisible measuring TextBlock that carries the new words, accessibility view Raw, hit testing off, in the box only for the swap; the box clips while it eases), so the row and the card ease by the line that a rewrapping sentence adds or takes (at the default 780 pt Settings window the resting sentence takes two lines and "Asking GitLab for the latest release…" one: 13.3 pt) instead of stepping in one frame; Reduce Motion cuts the height with the words. A change that leaves the sentence as it is while a swap runs lets the swap go on to those words (the early return used to cancel it and could leave the old words at full opacity); Reduce Motion switched on meanwhile finishes it at once. T2 and T3 AboutVersionPill hosts its face in a CrossfadeSlot: a change of what it shows between the slider, the ready button and the three standings (Up to date, Check failed, Not checked yet) crossfades, a rebuild that looks the same replaces the face at once unless a swap is running (then it crossfades too, never cutting to the end), the face's own colour ease of :671 (wash, symbol tint, title) is kept inside the new face. ## ED-262

[UI][COMPOSER] The effortslider-a parity pass's own engineering decisions (heading ED-262; the lead numbers it at merge). Each is a necessary internal choice made against the contract's section 8, about EffortSlider.swift's chip, popover panel, model list header, effort card and slider; none changes what the Mac shows except where a decision says it makes the port match it. (1) The model chip's label (EffortSlider.swift:65-117; PR-COMPOSER-106/107/108): SwiftUI's HStack(spacing: 5) centred in `.frame(width: lockedWidth)` is a DockPanel centred in the held box. The marks dock left, the chevron and the effort dock right (the chevron outermost), and the name, the one flexible item and the last child, takes what is left and is what gets cut (:89-94); every item after the first carries the 5 point gap as a leading margin of its own, so an icon alone is 14 wide (a one-child HStack has no spacing: the earlier trailing gap made the compact chip 19 and put the icon off centre), and a content shorter than the held box sits in the middle of it (the earlier `*` name column pushed the effort and the chevron to the box's right edge). A name cut by the box takes the whole width it is offered (TruncationFill: SwiftUI sizes a truncated Text to its proposal, whereas Avalonia's TextBlock reports the width of the last whole character), so the content spans the box. The old text of the chip's cross-fade (ED-238, FadeLead) overlays the fresh text's own cell, where it overlaid a Grid column. Alternatives rejected: a Grid with a star column (the two defects above), a custom Panel (more code for the same layout). (2) The model list's section headers are pinned to 22 points (:273 `sectionHeaderHeight`, the literal the height arithmetic of :287 reserves): the shared PopoverSectionHeader (Popovers.swift:117-132, a 6 + line + 3 padded 11 point Text) lays out 23 tall here (Inter's line at 11 points is 14 after layout rounding where SF's is 13), which would put the content two points over the frame it was sized to (the source's own arithmetic leaves it one point over with a pairs section: 7 children, 6 gaps against the 5 reserved). (3) The pair caption's soft appear (:650, Chrome.swift:949-961): the insertion half of `softAppear` is a modifier transition whose Bool modifier has no animatable data (SwiftUI animates the `.opacity` and `.offset` inside it; SwiftTransition snaps it, ED-098), so the card animates the caption's layer properties directly on Animation.softAppear (opacity 0 to 1 and a 4 point rise, smooth 0.32) and fades a leaving caption over easeOut(0.12), as the earlier code did at construction. SwiftUI runs a transition only for a view that joins or leaves a card already on screen, and the reference runtime shows the caption whole in the popover's first frames (2-chat-use.mov 43.665-43.757 s, frames 000506 and 000508 of 2-chat-use_033.500-051.000): the card now places the caption at first paint and animates it only when the pair comes or goes while the card stays. (4) The card takes the pair live (EffortSliderCard.UpdatePair, an observed ViewState like the card's other inputs): ModelEffortPanel hands the card that stays the new EffortPairLook (the chat entering or leaving a pair, or the heads effort resolving differently, :191-197, :510) instead of rebuilding it, so the caption can join or leave a card on screen as in SwiftUI; the title's colours, the line under the title and the track's look follow in place (the colour change on smooth 0.3, OD-0076: never a cut), and the reset action reads the pair the chat leads with when it is tapped (:219-224), not the one the card was made with. A change of provider, model or catalogue entry still rebuilds the card (and crossfades the maker's colours, OD-0090). (5) The single-level note (:620-624; PR-COMPOSER-117, UI-COMPOSER-036) is a 48 point slot (EffortSlider.ThumbSize, OD-0090) with the line centred in it: `.frame(height:)` centres its Text, while an Avalonia TextBlock given that height draws its line at the top. (6) The back chevron's 20 by 20 frame (:290-299) carries a transparent background and the slider's canvas too (:294, :800 `.contentShape(.rect)`): without one Avalonia hit-tests only painted pixels, so a press at the frame's corner, on the 7 px of the knob that stand proud of the track or on the track's rounded ends was ignored.
[UI][COMPOSER] The effortslider-b parity pass's own engineering decisions (the same heading, ED-262; the lead numbers them at merge). They concern EffortSlider.swift's model list, its rows, the chip's mark and the card's round buttons. (1) The model row's HStack (EffortSlider.swift:435-461): SwiftUI puts HStack(spacing: 10) between every two neighbours, a Spacer included, so the name column is followed by 10 + Spacer(minLength: 12) + 10 before the bolt (a model with a fast tier) or the checkmark, and the checkmark sits 10 after the bolt; the row's grid now has exactly the columns of the children it has (no bolt, no bolt column and no gap for it). The pair row (:386-405) already did this (PR-COMPOSER-147); the one rule is applied to both. ENGINEERING DECISION: the HStack spacing rule is SwiftUI's documented layout and the pair row's precedent, not read off a frame (the video shows the 46 pt pitch and the bolt at the right, not the gap behind the name). (2) A pair row's title and detail (:393, :397 `.lineLimit(1)`): the line is cut with an ellipsis at the tail (the default truncation mode) and never wraps; the model row's Text carries no lineLimit in the source (a long model name wraps there), while the port still lays a model row's name and detail on one line (EffortView.Text, MaxLines 1): UNRESOLVED edge, no catalogue name is long enough to reach it on the 318 point list and the row is a fixed 34 or 46 high either way. (3) ProviderRegistry.Models(_:) reads the observed Catalogs property (ProviderRegistry.swift:34, an @Observable var) and not its backing field: a view that lists a provider's models (the model list's "Loading models…" line, the chip, the slider card) tracks that read, so it is drawn again when the catalogue arrives (PR-COMPOSER-145: the list gave way to the rows only when it was opened again, so the placeholder stayed for good). (4) The model chip keeps its fused pair mark while the pair, its lead and its heads' provider stay the same (:73 `.id(pair.id)`; HydraFusedPairIcon.swift:37-42 plays the fuse-in from its own `.task(id: "\(lead)/\(heads)")`): the track callback rebuilds the row without detaching the kept mark, so a change of effort or of fast mode does not play the fuse-in again; another pair, another heads provider, or leaving the pair makes a new mark, as the Mac's task id does. (5) UI-COMPOSER-045 `scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize)` (:350): Windows has no rubber-band overscroll, so the list's ScrollViewer clamps at its ends; what the clause's "bounces only when the content exceeds the frame" can mean here is that the list scrolls only when its rows exceed the frame (the fixed row heights make the rows fit the frame in one pass), which the record's test proves; the elastic bounce itself is a macOS scroll-view behaviour with no counterpart in the toolkit (the reference runtime's Select model list scrolls with "hard clamp at both ends, no bounce", reference-video map/CATALOGUE.md:918, so the clamp is what the Mac shows there too). (6) The popover's placement: UI-COMPOSER-012 and UI-COMPOSER-030 say the popover hangs below the model chip; the source is `.popover(isPresented:arrowEdge: .bottom)` (:120), the arrow on the card's bottom edge, which puts the card above the chip, as the reference video shows (2-chat-use.mov 33.74-33.94 s: the chip sits at the window's bottom); the port places it on top (PlacementMode.Top, flipping below when there is no room above, FlipY). The two records' wording is the error, not the code: the amendment to "above" (made by the effortslider2 unit, ED-286 (4)) is accepted by the lead as a SOURCE FACT from the reference runtime, on the video stills (study/effort-title-2026-10-03/full_22.2.png: arrowEdge .bottom opens the card above the chip), no longer waiting for the owner (lead ruling R2) (the card's geometry and cross-fade are proven under PR-COMPOSER-109 and 118, the chip's parts under PR-COMPOSER-106 to 108).
[UI][COMPOSER] The effortslider-fix pass's own engineering decisions (the same heading, ED-262; the lead numbers them at merge). They concern how the composer keeps the model chip and its popover while the thread is written. (1) ComposerView.swift:161-173 re-evaluates ComposerControls with the new thread, and SwiftUI keeps the views and their @State (the chip's isPresented, lockedWidth and popover) through it. The port drew ComposerControls again for every change of the thread record, and the old chip's detach dismissed its popover, so the first stop the slider crossed closed it (EffortChipInComposerReviewTests). ComposerView.ShowControls now hands the drawn ComposerControls its new inputs (Update: the attach button's recentDownloadsPicker, ModelEffortSlot's thread, ContextMeter's provider and heads provider, SendButton's two routing flags) and draws it again only when it had no thread to draw; the chip takes the thread and hasHistory as observed inputs (ModelEffortButton.Update), the open panel takes the new hasHistory (ModelEffortPanel.SetHasHistory, ComposerView.swift:688 hands it down live), and the chip's catalogue task follows the thread's provider. Alternatives rejected: reparenting the chip into the new row (it still detaches and dismisses), a popover owned outside the chip (a second owner of the presented state). (2) EffortPairBrand compares by its colours (:942 `struct EffortPairBrand: Hashable`). SwiftColor is a class with no value equality, so two brands made from one pair were unequal, ModelEffortPanel hands the card that stays a new brand on every write, and the track effect's identity (:1020-1026) changed on every write with a pair, restarting the clock the record says is kept; the colours are compared as resolved in both appearances, and the track's look cache compares the pair by value instead of by reference.

## ED-264

[UI][MOTION][ACCESSIBILITY] Reduce Motion stills only what OD-0076 added beyond the Mac; the Mac's own animations follow the Mac's own Reduce Motion behaviour (the lead's decision of 2026-10-04; builds on ED-084, IMPLEMENTING.md section 7, R-VIEW-6). SOURCE FACT: the Swift reads the setting at 30 sites in 19 files (`accessibilityReduceMotion` or `NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`: App/Views/Chat/ChatBadge.swift:19,57, HydraButton.swift:350, HydraProgressBar.swift:128-194,501, TimelineMinimap.swift:185,197,230, TimelineRows.swift:487,828,836; App/Views/Composer/AttachmentFlight.swift:55, ComposerWorkingDots.swift:13,16,26,30, EffortSlider.swift:1041,1049, HydraFusedPairIcon.swift:14,41; App/Views/Settings/AboutUpdateViews.swift:387,408,579,671,688,718,797-806, MCPSettingsPage.swift:9,65,236,372, MCPSetupPanel.swift:61,205, ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:430,464; App/Views/Sidebar/RowGlide.swift:76; UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:101,113,976, WindowChrome.swift:223,280; UI/Common/Genie.swift:64,84, HydraGlyph.swift:192, WorkingIndicators.swift:65). What each site does under Reduce Motion is its own: most return or drop the motion, but not all (ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:464 `reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.12) : .spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.8)`; AboutUpdateViews.swift:688 `if reduceMotion { return 0.15 }`; WindowChrome.swift:280 `slideRun` 220 against 420 ms; HydraFusedPairIcon.swift:41 `withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : ...)`). ENGINEERING DECISION, the rule: (1) an animation the Mac has and gates stays gated in the port exactly as the Swift gates it, with the Swift's own alternative (the shorter run, the easeOut, the nothing), read from `\.accessibilityReduceMotion`, which follows the Windows animation-effects setting (ED-084); (2) an animation the Mac has and does not gate (for example the turn fold's `.snappy(duration: 0.24)`, ED-263) is not gated in the port either, because it is the Mac's own motion and no source line stills it; (3) a transition OD-0076 adds where the Mac snaps (the owner-ruled deviation of its second sentence) is stilled by the setting: it cuts to its end state in one frame, nothing else changes. This reading is consistent with OD-0076's first sentences ("Where the Mac animates, the port matches the Mac's motion") and with ED-084; OD-0076's last sentence says "the system's reduce-motion setting stills them", and `them` can be read as every transition including the Mac-matching ones, which would be wider than rule (2). UNRESOLVED (carried into work/design/open-questions-2026-10-04.md as Q-RM): whether the owner wants rule (2) widened so that the Mac-matching, ungated animations also still under Windows animation effects off. Not evidence either way: no reference capture was made with Reduce Motion on (OD-0001, no macOS), so what macOS itself does to an explicit SwiftUI animation that the code does not gate is not a recorded result; the rule takes the code as written.

## ED-265

[CHAT][PERSISTENCE] PR-CHAT-107 follows the Mac exactly, including the save that is skipped (the lead's decision of 2026-10-04; resolves STOP opencode-App.Views.Chat.TimelineRows #3, TimelineRowsPrSourceConflictTests.cs:28). SOURCE FACT: `storeLegacyChanges` sets `summary.changes`, replaces the turn-end entry's content and calls `scheduleSave()` (ThreadRuntime.swift:3797-3803) without `saveRevision += 1`; at an idle phase `scheduleSave` arms an 800 ms task that calls `saveNow` (:3623-3632), and `saveNow` returns at `guard saveRevision != lastSavedRevision` (:3663) when no other mutation has moved the revision since the last save. So the worked-out summary is kept in memory at once and reaches the thread document only when something else bumps the revision (any later mutation that saves; the quit write through `unsavedSnapshot` has the same guard, :3670-3672); on the idle, just-loaded old thread the record has in mind it can be dropped on restart and the diff is parsed again. The doc comment above the function (:3795-3796 "kept on the turn-end entry, so the thread's next open reads it instead of running git for every historical card again") states the intent, not the behaviour. The record's persistence line ("Written back through runtime.storeLegacyChanges, so it survives into the thread document") is therefore true only to that extent. ENGINEERING DECISION, under PORT_CONTRACT section 8 ("Do not silently repair unrelated behavior during a parity port. Record it.") and the upstream-defects register's rule that a parity port reproduces such a defect: the port keeps the same shape, the in-memory store plus `ScheduleSave`, no revision bump, the same guard in `SaveNow`; the existing test An_idle_loaded_legacy_summary_is_updated_in_memory_but_the_pinned_revision_guard_drops_it_on_restart pins it and stays as it is. No owner decision touches it (porting/owner_decisions.md has no entry on legacy summaries or on `storeLegacyChanges`), and nothing about it exposes credentials or destroys data, so section 8's escalation does not apply. Follow-ups, not made here: an entry for it in porting/upstream_defects.md, and the record's persistence clause read as "as the Swift does".
