## ED-270

[WIN][KEYBOARD] The zoom chords are key equivalents of the character typed, not US key positions (Q-ZOOM). SOURCE FACT: Zoom In is `.keyboardShortcut("+", modifiers: .command)`, Zoom Out `"-"`, Actual Size `"0"`, plus a hidden second Zoom In on `"="` "because US keyboards produce '=' for Command-plus without Shift" (AppCommands.swift:53-62); SwiftUI matches `keyboardShortcut` by the character the key types on the active layout. The records already say so: PR-WIN-222 "The chord is a character key equivalent (+), not a US key position" and PR-WIN-225 (Ctrl+= is a second zoom-in chord). The build reads a key event as a US key position (Port/MenuKeyEquivalents.cs, ED-099), with ED-230's reading of Shift with the "=" key and the keypad plus as "+" (MenuKeyEquivalents.cs:66-82; AppCommands.cs:23-25), so on a layout whose "+" key is not Shift with the US "=" position (a German keyboard, where "+" has its own key) the key that types "+" is not read as "+", and the keys are read by where they sit instead of what they type (the build question's example, Ctrl+ß, needs re-checking against this mapping: ß sits at the US "-" position). ENGINEERING DECISION: the port matches Ctrl with whichever key types "+", "=" or "-" on the active layout, and the keypad plus and minus, and Ctrl+0; the build is changed to the records, not the records to the build. It is a defect against PR-WIN-222 and PR-WIN-225, not a new rule.

## ED-271

[UPDATE][NOTIFICATIONS] The update toast is silent (Q "Toast sound"; amends PR-UPDATE-025's reading and the build's `Sound: true`). SOURCE FACT: the update notification's content has a title, a body and `userInfo` and no `sound` (UpdateChecker.swift:249-253), while a chat's notification takes a `sound` argument that defaults to `.default` (AppModel.swift:1258-1263); `willPresent` returns `[.banner, .sound]` for every notification that is not the open chat (AppDelegate.swift:63-75). OD-0028 (and ED-220 (3), engineering_decisions.md line 1627): "Toasts carry the title, the body and the default sound, or none when the source passes nil". The source passes nil for the update notification, so the toast carries no sound; `.sound` in the presentation options only applies the notification's own sound, which is the framework's documented behaviour, labelled ENGINEERING DECISION because no capture on a Mac was made. PR-UPDATE-025's expected_result ("shown with sound ... an audible alert") and its comment in WindowsToastNotifications.cs:132 ("update banners retain default sound") read `[.banner, .sound]` as a sound, and the build passes `true` (WindowsToastNotifications.cs:133-135, `new ToastRequest(identifier, title, body, true, ...)`). DECISION: the update toast posts `<audio silent="true"/>`; the chat toast keeps the default sound. PR-UPDATE-025's and UI-LAUNCH-005's record text is amended to match (porting/spec/UPDATE.json, LAUNCH.json; unit small-fixes), so the records and this entry now agree.

## ED-272

[SETTINGS][CREDITS] The Terminal row of About > Credits (Q "Terminal credit"). SOURCE FACT: the Swift's row is `ChromeRow(title: "Terminal", detail: "SwiftTerm by Miguel de Icaza, MIT License.") { CreditLink(title: "SwiftTerm", url: ...) }` (SettingsView.swift:954-955) and the licence line names it again (:997). The port ships no SwiftTerm, so the row cannot say that. OD-0012 H: "the terminal credit names the component the Windows build ships", and the licence line is settled in OD-0072's list as "the terminal is Marrow's own, built on Windows ConPTY". ENGINEERING DECISION: the row reads "Marrow's own terminal, built on Windows ConPTY." with no link, as built (SettingsView.cs:927), the same words as the settled licence line, because a link would point at a component the app does not credit as third-party code (ConPTY is a Windows API, not shipped code). If a third-party terminal component ever ships, its credit and link are added then.

## ED-273

[TEST][UI] Decisions of the tail blitz (units RootView, CommandPalette, ComposerWorkingDots, HydraPanel, SubagentPanel, UpdateChecker, TourView and the smaller ones). ENGINEERING DECISIONS, none a deviation.

(1) A missing forge CLI is tested over an empty login PATH (PR-GIT-051). `LoginEnvironment.PathForTesting` (Marrow.Core, internal, an `Ambient<string>` that is null in production) makes `LoginEnvironment.Which`, and so `Shell.RunTool`, search a PATH of the test's choosing for the calling async flow; it changes what is SEARCHED only, never the environment a child process is given (so `git push` in the same test still runs normally). Marrow.Core.Tests reaches it directly; the other test projects through `Marrow.Testing.EmptyLoginPath.Begin()` (reflection, as AppModelHarness reaches `HomeForTesting`). Reason: the Services and App test projects put scripted gh, glab and tea first on the process PATH and Marrow.Core.Tests runs on a machine that may have a real gh, so a missing-tool test could not otherwise name the three real forge CLIs hermetically.

(2) The finish-wipe comparison against the reference video is made on numbers (PR-HYDRA-169, DotFieldSweepProfileTests). SOURCE FACT for the measurements is the catalogue item hydra.card-finish-grain-wipe (E:\Droppy\work\reference-video\map\CATALOGUE.md, frames/gap-R3-04: per-column opacity table, 365 px/s front, 0.71-0.75 s band, 1.83 s to clear, 400 x 280 card with 50 x 35 dots). The port's sample of the same field (DotFieldCompositionFrame over the source's keyframes) is compared with it within 0.06 per point: the catalogue's own spread between its two events is 0.04 and one 8-bit step of a 2 px dot is about 0.02. The port's CA ease-in/ease-out are the cubic readings recorded under OD-0001 (UNVERIFIED against a Mac); the largest difference is 0.05 on the falling side (the port's wave falls slightly earlier than the measured one).

(3) The auto-clear delay of a finished head is `HydraPanel.FinishHold + 0.2` seconds (AppModel+Hydra.cs), as the Swift reads it (AppModel+Hydra.swift:604), instead of the literal 2_200 ms: the same value, now coupled to the hold so that one cannot change without the other.

(4) The command palette's search row is a two-column Grid ("Auto,*"), the palette panel has a transparent fill, and the stage capsule of the head panel is the shared chrome glass capsule (UI-WIN-030, UI-WIN-029, UI-HYDRA-019). A horizontal StackPanel never stretches a main-axis child, so the search text box was as wide as its placeholder and a long query grew it past the 600-point panel; the SwiftUI TextField fills the room the magnifier leaves, so the field takes the star column and the 10-point gap is its left margin. A Border with no fill is not hit-testable in Avalonia, so a press on the panel's blank bands (the side and top insets of the search row, the gaps between rows) fell through to the scrim and closed the palette; the record says clicks inside never dismiss, so the panel border carries `Brushes.Transparent`. The head panel's stage capsule was a flat tint at 0.22 where the source applies `.chromeGlassCapsule()` (HydraPanel.swift:158); it now wears the same surface as the heads button beside it (a hit-test-free continuous capsule of glass, flat on a glass panel). Popover edges that the Swift names (`arrowEdge: .bottom` on the close confirmation and the project picker) are passed explicitly as PlacementMode.Bottom, the default made visible, so a test can break them.

(5) The usage floating panel follows `runtime.usage` (UI-USAGE-040). The Swift body re-runs when the usage changes, so the placeholder gives way to the usage panel on the first usage (and back); the port read it once at construction. The panel now tracks `runtime.Usage`: while the scroll view stays (only the figures change) the usage panel inside it is replaced and the scroll offset kept, as SwiftUI keeps the ScrollView's identity; a change of branch swaps the content and the height reported to the pane (the placeholder's 94 or the content's own) follows it.

(6) Copy Link writes through the window the link is in (UI-THEME-045). The real presenter hosts the popover's content in a popup's own root, whose `Clipboard` the port's other menus deliberately avoid (TimelineRows.CopyMessageText), and a null clipboard made the write a silent no-op; LinkPopoverContent is handed the anchor the popover opened from, takes the pasteboard from that window (the content's own root only as the fallback), and clears it before writing as the Swift does (`clearContents()`, LinkPopover.swift:92). `LinkPopover.MeasureContent` is a test seam over the hosted view's intrinsic size, so the 220 by 110 fallback of :36 can be driven.

(7) The head panel's stage capsule is one view across a head change (UI-HYDRA-019; the review of unit/blitz-tail). SOURCE FACT: HydraPanel.swift:136-165 builds the capsule inside `if let selected, let info = selected.hydra { ... .transition(.softAppear) }` with no `.id`, so a head change from one head to another keeps the same view and its contents change under :199 `.animation(liveResize.isActive ? nil : Chrome.panelSlide, value: selected?.id)`; the soft appear is the capsule's insertion and removal only (no head on stage, or one with no record). The port had replaced the capsule on every head change (two capsules on screen, the new one at opacity 0 over the smooth 0.32 s); HydraPanel.StageCapsule now keeps the glass shell, its padding and the drag handle and takes the new head's contents in place. ENGINEERING DECISION (OD-0076, the way the working line's clock does it, HydraElapsedTime.Update): the contents dip out over the first half of Chrome.panelSlide on its ease-in, the new head's come in over the second half on its ease-out, and the shell's width glides from the old width to the new contents' over the second half (the new contents' width is known once they are attached: the clock has no words before). The Mac's own motion for the contents (a text cross-fade and a frame interpolation inside the one view) is UNRESOLVED without a Mac; the structure (one view) and the transaction (panelSlide, none during a live resize or under reduce motion) are the source's. A change of the same head's record (its status) still lands at once, as before. Tests: HydraPanelStageCapsuleTests.A_head_change_keeps_the_one_capsule_and_changes_its_contents_on_the_panel_slide_and_a_live_resize_does_it_at_once and the review's HydraPanelStageCapsuleReviewTests.

(8) The command palette's row keeps the chord at least 8 points from the text (UI-WIN-032, UI-WIN-033). The record says "at least 8 points of space" (CommandPalette.swift:132 `Spacer(minLength: 8)`); the port puts 20 points (the HStack's 12 plus the Spacer's 8) ahead of the chord. UNRESOLVED: whether SwiftUI also adds the HStack's 12 points after the Spacer (32 in all); no Mac and no reference capture shows a row whose title fills its room, so the 20 stays and is not claimed as the Mac's. CommandPaletteChordTests.The_chord_is_the_trailing_item_with_at_least_8_points_between_it_and_the_text_at_the_narrowest_the_row_asks_for proves the floor of 8 and the trailing edge at the narrowest width the row asks for (a title that has to truncate cannot be shaped by the headless backend: no Inter glyph typeface); mutant "margin ahead of the chord 20 to 0" is killed. SUPERSEDED by ED-279: the Spacer is outside `if let shortcut`, so 12 + 8 stays after the text on every row and a chord adds a further 12 (32 before a chord).

(9) A test whose name contains "native" is skipped by the mandatory gate filter `FullyQualifiedName!~Native`, which matches case-insensitively (PR-HYDRA-060, PR-HYDRA-071). The four proofs of a lead that runs its own heads (ThreadRuntimeHydraPromptOrderTests, ThreadRuntimeHydraPolicyPlacementTests) are named "A_lead_running_its_own_heads_..." and "A_lead_whose_heads_run_elsewhere_..." so that the gate runs them. A test name never contains "native" while that filter stands.

## ED-274

[WIN][LAUNCH][TEST] Two decisions from the blitz review of the AppDelegate launch records (PR-LAUNCH-046, UI-LAUNCH-005).
(1) THE MAIN WINDOW'S PROCEDURE HOOK IS A SEAM. AppShell.FinishLaunching put the WM_ACTIVATEAPP / WM_ENDSESSION hook on the main window with a direct Win32Properties.AddWndProcHookCallback, which no headless test could observe: deleting the line left every test green, so "a catch-up check runs whenever the app becomes active" (UpdateChecker.swift:141-149, and the launch activation under OD-0040) rested on tests that called shell.WndProc by hand. The call now goes through the internal Ambient AppShell.AddWindowProcedureHook (default: Avalonia's own AddWndProcHookCallback). Tests record the hook and the window it was put on (the main window, not yet shown when the boot stage is up, so the boot's first activation cannot be missed) and call the recorded hook as Windows would. Behaviour in the app is unchanged. What stays outside the tests: Windows' sending of WM_ACTIVATEAPP to a window of the app (winuser.h) and Avalonia's call of a window's hooks. ENGINEERING DECISION.
(2) THE UPDATE TOAST IS SILENT. UpdateChecker.swift:249-252 builds the content with a title, a body and userInfo and no content.sound, so on the Mac the update banner makes no sound (willPresent's .sound, AppDelegate.swift:74, plays only a content sound; AppModel.swift:1224 likewise passes no sound when the chime already played). WindowsToastCenter.Show posted it with the default Windows sound (a reading of PR-UPDATE-025's "audible alert", a RECORD != SWIFT conflict). It now posts with `<audio silent="true"/>`, as ED-227 (3) already does when the source passes no sound. SOURCE FACT for the content; the willPresent table [] or [.banner, .sound] is unchanged. PR-UPDATE-025 and UI-LAUNCH-005 word the update banner as audible and need the lead's correction (STOP App.AppDelegate #8).

## ED-275

[UI][SHAPES][GLASS] The continuous corner (ED-181 closed; build spec E:/Droppy/work/design/build-specs/continuous-corners/SPEC.md, written 2026-10-03, built 2026-10-04 on unit/blitz-corners; the lead numbers this heading at merge). Each item is an ENGINEERING DECISION unless it says SOURCE FACT; the video is the oracle, the pinned Swift decides which shapes are `.continuous` (OD-0098: where no video frame shows a shape, the Swift source and the documented framework behaviour are the proof).

(1) THE CURVE (SOURCE FACT for the numbers, from a third-party measurement of Apple's runtime that the reference video confirms on macOS 26). One corner is three cubic Beziers; in units of the radius, with `u` along the edge from the vertex and `v` into the shape: C1 (1.528665, 0) (1.08849296, 0) (0.86840694, 0) (0.63149379, 0.07491139); C2 (0.63149379, 0.07491139) (0.37282383, 0.16905956) (0.16905956, 0.37282383) (0.07491139, 0.63149379); C3 the mirror of C1 ((u, v) -> (v, u), backwards). The extent 1.528665 r (CALayer.cornerCurveExpansionFactor(.continuous), NativeScript #11452) is one constant at both ends (the measurement differs by 2e-7 r). The pinned source and Apple's documentation do not state the curve (the original ED-181 fact). Largest gap from the circle of the same radius 0.0138 r at (0.869, 0.0225) r; on the diagonal the curve is 0.0020 r nearer the vertex. Marrow.UI/Port/ContinuousCorner.cs, SwiftShapes.Outline.

(2) THE REGIME (backed by the oracle for capsules and large radii; UNRESOLVED as a source fact in the band below). A `.continuous` corner is Apple's while `2 * 1.528665 * r <= min(w, h)` (its run-in and its neighbour's fit along each side they share; per corner for an UnevenRoundedRectangle), else a circular arc of the requested radius held to half the shorter side. The reference video fits circular ends for the composer (r 22 on 46 pt), the 28 pt glass capsule and the system glass button (circular ends 0.10-0.19 px rms, PaintCode's clamped continuous corner 0.65-1.15 px rms, SPEC.md 2.3); it fits Apple's corner at r 22-26 on the Settings window and Hydra's card (8 of 8 corners better than the circle, rms 0.084-0.226 against 0.137-0.287) and cannot tell the curves apart at r 9 (the models differ by 0.124 px at most). UNRESOLVED: a shape with `h / (2 * 1.528665) < r < h / 2` (the Edited-files card: 40 pt, r 18, band 13.1 < r < 20; a two-line notice pill: 46 pt in the mounted test at 380 pt wide (first recorded here as about 48 pt, corrected 2026-10-04 by the blitz-cornerband review; 50 pt since the callout line box of 17, ED-290 (1) SETTLED 2026-10-04: 16 + 2 x 17, still in the band 16.4 < 18 < 25), r 18, band 15.05 < r < 23; the composer growing past one line) keeps its circular arc here; UIKit rounds such ends to about half the side. SwiftUI on macOS 26 is not documented for it and the Swift source states `.continuous` and nothing more. Corrected 2026-10-04 (adversarial review): the one measurement inside the band is the composer (r 22 on 46, r / h = 0.478): the circle fits it at 0.156 px rms, the iOS 7 shape_2 at 0.212, the clamped continuous corner at 1.148, so the clamped corner is rejected there and the circle cannot be told from shape_2, whose ends differ by one point of radius. Nothing is measured at lower r / h: the video's Edited card (C 9.0) and two-line error banner (C 10.6-12.0) have no extractable edge (a 0.32 quaternary and a 0.1 danger tint over the blurred wallpaper, compression blocks of 4 luma; the same failure as the one-line notice), and no recording shows a multi-line composer. The records whose only shape in the band is such a card or notice (UI-GIT-044, PR-CHAT-108, UI-RUNTIME-002, UI-RUNTIME-003) are therefore not proven on their corner, and no test claims a video fit for it; OD-0098 does not reach it (the Swift source states no regime). The earlier text calling the card "the circular arc the video shows" was wrong.

AMENDED 2026-10-04 (unit blitz-cornerband): OD-0102 settles the band. The owner chose "corner-band: A" on the Corner Band page: a `.continuous` shape with `h / (2 * 1.528665) < r < h / 2` is drawn as Apple's continuous corner at the largest radius that fits, `ContinuousCorner.LargestRadius = min(w, h) / (2 * 1.528665)` (PaintCode's clamped corner), not as a circular arc; the Edited-files card, the two-line notice, the one-step steps card and the one-head delegation card (UI-CHAT-034, -036, -037, -054) take it. The UNRESOLVED above is closed by that ruling, not by evidence; its one measurement stands and is kept: the composer (r 22 on 46 pt) is measured as the circular arc, so it is the one shape exempted (ED-297 (2)). The capsule regime (r at least half the shorter side) and the full-corner regime (`2 * 1.528665 * r <= min(w, h)`) are unchanged. See ED-297 for the mechanism.

(3) THE MECHANISM. Avalonia's Border draws circular corners and its Render is sealed, so a continuous shape cannot be a Border that draws itself. Two mechanisms, chosen by what the shape draws: (a) SwiftShapeBorder (Marrow.UI/Port/SwiftShapeBorder.cs), a Decorator that owns Border's properties (AddOwner, so styles and bindings naming Border.BackgroundProperty apply), draws the fill and the hit shape as the cached path, strokes SwiftUI's `strokeBorder` (the shape inset by half the width, stroked, so the outer edge is the shape; Apple's InsettableShape.strokeBorder documentation) and clips its children to the path with Visual.Clip. Where the corners are circular it calls what a Border calls (DrawRectangle on the inset rounded rect), pixel for pixel (tested). Used where the curve is seen: the window backdrop's layers and hairline (Chrome.swift:218-271), the Settings and main window frames (SettingsView.swift:118-122, RootView.swift:66), the choice-tile ring (ChromeVisualPicker.swift:96-102, whose outer edge the video fits at r 9.0) and the script outline (ChatView.swift:1686-1691). (b) Every other `.RoundedRectangle(r, .continuous)` call on a plain Border (about 60 sites) keeps its Border and its CornerRadius (what every test and the glass read) and is cut by Visual.Clip (ContinuousClip in SwiftShapes.cs), set only while the Border draws a fill, a border or a clip and has no box shadow (a clip would cut it), never over a clip a site set. Measured on a 780 x 580 r 26 shape against the analytic path (headless Skia, the spec's rays): SwiftShapeBorder 0.063 px rms / 0.247 px at worst (the measurement's own bias along slanted edges; identical to the path drawn alone), a clipped Border 0.105 px rms / 0.487 px, the circle 0.135 px rms / 0.562 px. The clipped Border draws its fill with its own circular corner and the clip anti-aliases a second edge, so the two edges multiply coverage where they are within a pixel: that is why a Border cannot reach the exact shape and why the shapes whose stroke or window edge is seen use (a). Replacing the Border at the other sites would have changed the type of about 60 call sites and of 286 `IsType<Border>` and the Border queries in the tests of every parallel unit; sites that want the exact shape change `new Border` to `new SwiftShapeBorder` and nothing else. The clip variant runs 4,096 pt outside the bounds along the straight sides and at every corner that is not Apple's (ClipSlack), so it never doubles the anti-aliasing of a straight edge and never clips what a child draws beyond a side between the corners' run-ins (SwiftUI's `.background(shape)` does not clip its content: the effort title's letters leaving past the chevron, EffortTitleMorphTests; found by the first full run, with a 2 pt slack). Corrected 2026-10-04 (adversarial review): that holds only between the run-ins. Within `Extent * r` (1.528665 r) of an Apple-regime corner the clip path runs in to the curve's ends, so the whole quadrant beyond the bounds there is cut with the sliver: on a 26 pt row of radius 6 a child drawing past a side survives only for 9.2 < y < 16.8. No site is known to draw there (none was found in the records of this unit); one that is found is a defect to route to the shape's owner. Also corrected: a plain Border that strokes (a BorderBrush) in Apple's regime keeps its circular inner stroke edge while the clip cuts the outer edge, so its stroke thins by up to 0.0138 r near each corner (0.19 pt at r 14); the strokes that are seen use SwiftShapeBorder, and any other stroked continuous Border is a defect to route there.

(4) SHADOWS. A SwiftShapeBorder's box shadow is drawn from the circular rounded rectangle of the same radius, before the fill (outer) and after it (inset): the blur hides a gap of at most 0.0138 r.

(5) THE GLASS. The shader's shape distance for a `.continuous` rounded rectangle is the circular corner's plus the offset of Apple's curve from the circle along the circle's normal, a smooth function of the position along the corner (a polynomial on the run-in, two on the arc), faded to nothing inside a corner's centre where the polar angle is undefined; the zero level lies on the path to 2e-5 r (fits: run-in max error 5e-7 r, arc 1.7e-5 r and 5.6e-7 r; Marrow.UI/Port/ContinuousCorner.cs, scratch derive.py). A capsule, a radius past the limit and `.circular` keep the plain circle distance. The shader text is generated from the same constants as the C# mirror ContinuousCorner.Distance; GlassContinuousCornerTests run the shader on Skia's CPU rasteriser and compare it with the mirror (1e-3 px) and the mirror with the path (0.05 px). The fourth-power corner it replaces was 0.187 r (4.1 px at r 22) from Apple's curve.

(5b) COST (recorded, SwiftShapesCostTests; headless Skia on the CPU, 300 shapes of 110 x 60 at r 12, 120 frames, each captured): circular Border median 5.38 ms a frame, continuous Border cut by the clip 7.49 ms (1.39x, +2.1 ms: over the spec's 1.3x and +1 ms budget in this stress; a screen with 30 clipped Borders costs about +0.2 ms), continuous SwiftShapeBorder 5.40 ms (1.00x). A colour-only animation over 300 shapes of either kind builds no geometry (gating test). If the clip proves costly on a low-end GPU, the lever is a minimum radius for a fill-only Border or a cached clip layer.

(6) THE CACHE. SwiftShapes caches one StreamGeometry per (rect, radii, style, clip) (1,024 entries, cleared when full): identical rows share one geometry, a resize builds one, a colour change none (SwiftShapes.GeometryBuildCount, tested).

(7) NOT DONE, tracked here (no marker in the code, the sites are other units' files): raw `CornerRadius = new CornerRadius(r)` Borders whose Swift is `.continuous` and that do not call `.RoundedRectangle(...)` (about 55 lines: HydraPanel, SubagentPanel, FloatingSidebarPanel, MCPKeyPanel/MCPSetupPanel, TourView, UsageFloatingPanel, DiffInspector, HydraProgressBar, the Hydra popovers, ChromeSegmentedPicker, TokenActivitySection and others) stay circular arcs until their unit adds the one call (a plain Border takes the clip, a stroking one becomes a SwiftShapeBorder); and the custom renders RowGlide (r 7), TokenActivitySection cells, AttachmentFlightPlatform and ComposerLightRenderer's mask still draw a circular rounded rectangle (each at most 0.0138 r from the curve: 0.10 px at r 7). UnevenRoundedRectangle's clamping when a side is shorter than the run-ins is not known (the Apple documentation does not say); the per-corner rule in (2) applies.

## ED-276

[UI][ICON][OD-0015] Every place upstream shows its own app icon or logo shows the Marrow icon (the lead numbers it at merge). WHAT WAS WRONG: `SwiftImage.Named("droppy-logo")` loaded `src/Marrow.UI/Assets/Images/droppy-logo.png` and `droppy-logo@2x.png`, byte-identical to the Droppy Code PNGs of the reference (`DroppyCode/Resources/Assets.xcassets/droppy-logo.imageset`, SHA-256 307aca65... and 467897a0...), so the Welcome page (RootView.cs, 104 pt), the new-thread prompt (NewThreadPrompt.cs, 72 pt) and the Settings > About "Made by" row (SettingsView.cs MadeByDroppyRow, 40 pt) drew the Droppy Code droplet. Only the last of those is an `Image("droppy-logo")` in the Swift (SettingsView.swift:1067); RootView.swift:307 and NewThreadPrompt.swift:17 draw `NSApp.applicationIconImage`, like AboutUpdateViews.swift:554 and SettingsView.swift:971, so the port had them on the wrong asset as well as the wrong artwork instead of the Marrow icon that OD-0015 (reaffirmed by OD-0033 for the About pill) rules for "every place upstream shows its own app icon or logo". Those three were the only callers of the asset (the About identity pill, the About app card and the toast already used `Assets/icon.png`). WHAT CHANGED (lead's ruling, follow the Swift): (0) the two `applicationIconImage` sites (Welcome 104 pt, new-thread prompt 72 pt) now draw the packaged app icon `Assets/icon.png` with its margin, as the About identity pill does: a plain `Image`, `Stretch.Uniform`, high interpolation, built by the new `Views/AppIconImage.Make(size)` over one shared bitmap `AppIconImage.Bitmap`, which the About identity pill and the About app card now use too (the pill's private Lazy bitmap is gone); the prompt's icon stays hidden from accessibility (:21). They no longer use the `droppy-logo` asset at all. The rest of this entry therefore applies to the one remaining `Image("droppy-logo")` site, the "Made by Droppy" row (SettingsView.swift:1067, 40 pt). (1) `src/Marrow.UI/Assets/Images/marrow-icon.png` (256 px) and `marrow-icon@2x.png` (512 px) are `src/Marrow.App/Assets/icon.svg` rendered with its viewBox cropped to the tile (`72 72 880 880`, headless Edge, transparent background), so the artwork fills the frame as the full-bleed Droppy PNG did and the row keeps its source size and placement; they sit under Marrow.UI because Marrow.UI cannot reference Marrow.App; the PNGs are a render, not a vector, so the artwork is exactly what icon.svg draws (gradients, clip and keyline). The 24 px and below `icon-small.svg` is not needed: the smallest logo place is 40 pt. (2) The Swift asset name stays the lookup key: `SwiftImage.Assets["droppy-logo"]` now loads the two Marrow PNGs, with a comment citing OD-0015, so the row keeps the Swift name and its `AssetName == "droppy-logo"` assertions still describe the call site. Rejected: renaming the key at the single call site (an edit and test churn for no behaviour). (3) The two Droppy Code PNGs are deleted, not shipped unused. (4) `tests/Marrow.UI.Tests/Port/AssetCatalogueManifest.json` records the droppy-logo entry as a deviation: `deviation: OD-0015`, the shipped Marrow files and hashes in `files`, and the upstream filenames and hashes in `upstreamFiles` (plus `upstreamContentsSha256`); AssetCatalogueTests requires that the deviation is OD-0015, that no upstream hash appears among the shipped hashes and that no upstream file is in the assembly, so the substitution cannot be silent. SwiftImageTests no longer pins the Droppy PNG hashes (it pins the two Marrow renders instead). TESTS: MarrowLogoArtworkTests (Marrow.UI.Tests) and MarrowLogoSettingsRowTests (Marrow.App.Tests, with MarrowLogoCheck) sample pixels that only the Marrow artwork satisfies (transparent corner, white core, the three arm gradient starts, the dark navy tile) on the bitmap the About row holds, and SettingsRestAboutTests and SettingsViewTests assert the same on the attribution row's logo; MarrowLogoPlacesTests, RootViewWelcomeTests and NewThreadPromptTests assert that the Welcome and new-thread icons are a plain `Image` over the packaged `icon.png` (asset hash and pixels equal the approved bitmap, 104 / 72 pt, uniform stretch, high interpolation, hidden from accessibility on the prompt) and that no `droppy-logo` image is on either view. They carry `Decision ED-215` or `ED-179` because the meta-test (Traceability) accepts only ED-nnn, Req and Rule ids, and cite OD-0015 in a comment. Not changed and still open: the "Made by Droppy" row's wording and its link are upstream attribution (OD-0002 and the credits), not the app logo. Design pages `welcome-voice` and `getting-ready` drew the Droppy logo in their window mock; they now draw the Marrow icon inline, whole (icon.svg's own 1024 box with its margin, as the Welcome page's `applicationIconImage` draws icon.png).

## ED-277

[TERM] The terminal panel's tab chip, Escape and live-resize records (TerminalPanel.swift; the blitz unit blitz-terminalpanel; the lead numbers it at merge). Five decisions, each a necessary internal choice. (1) A TAB SELECTS WHEN THE POINTER IS RELEASED INSIDE ITS CAPSULE (TerminalPanel.swift:178 `.onTapGesture(perform: select)`, :177 `.contentShape(.capsule)`; ENGINEERING DECISION, SwiftUI's TapGesture completes on the release inside the shape, OD-0098: no video shows a tab click). TerminalTab arms on a left press, disarms on pointer exit and capture loss, and calls select on the release, the same port of a tap as the Hydra capsule; it selected on the press before. Avalonia's Border already hit-tests its rounded corners, so the capsule needs no clip: a press at the bounding-box corner misses the chip (the test fails with a square corner). (2) A LONG TITLE WIDENS ITS CHIP; THE RECORD'S FAILURE CASE "the chip does not grow unbounded" IS NOT WHAT THE SWIFT DOES (RECORD != SWIFT). The chips sit in `ScrollView(.horizontal)` (:21), which gives its content no width limit along the scroll axis, so `Text(session.title).lineLimit(1)` (:146) is laid out at its ideal width and is not truncated; the port's StackPanel in a ScrollViewer does the same and no width cap was added (ENGINEERING DECISION, SwiftUI layout semantics). (3) THE FOREGROUND-JOB ANSWER IS THREE-VALUED SO "CANNOT TELL" PASSES ESCAPE THROUGH (OD-0031, ED-046 "default to FALSE on any error, empty result, or enumeration timeout"; TerminalStore.swift:70-75 answers false when it cannot ask). ProcessDescendants.HasLiveDescendant returns true, false or null (a non-positive pid, a failed snapshot, a shell pid absent from the snapshot, an enumeration over 500 ms: null) and TerminalSession.ForegroundJobIsTheShell is true only for an explicit false; before, every failure answered "no live child" and so closed the drawer and swallowed the Escape. The 500 ms bound is the port's (ED-046 names a timeout and no value), and the process table reader and the bound are internal seams so a test can force each failure; the default reads the real Toolhelp snapshot. (4) THE TAB CHIP'S REFERENCE COMPARISON IS NUMERIC, ON THE ONE FRAME THE VIDEO HAS (work/reference-video/frames/w-2-chat-use-132.0/termL_132.15-134.95/000040.png, the dark selected chip: panel luminance 19, capsule fill 36, chip 113 x 27 px, title ink 56 px wide and peak 222, cross ink 8 px wide and peak 166). The port renders the same chip headless at 114 x 25, fill 36, title 56 px and peak 222, cross 8 px: the two points of height are UNRESOLVED, NOT A MEASURED FACE DIFFERENCE (the guess that Inter's callout line is 15 px against SF's 16, OD-0009, would explain one point, not the two: 16 would give a 26 px chip against the frame's 27; the record's windows_path leaves visual size parity UNVERIFIED under OD-0001 and the test accepts 25 to 28 px) and the glyph art is OD-0010's Lucide, so the glyph ink peaks are not compared. The unselected chip, the light theme and the exited chip have no frame (OD-0098): their rendered pixels are compared against the source's colours composited by hand (:175 secondary on clear, :176 primary at 0.08, :180 0.55). (5) A LUCIDE GLYPH DRAWN IN A TRANSLUCENT COLOUR BLENDS EACH OVERLAPPING STROKE ON ITS OWN, so its strongest pixel can sit above the single-stroke value (the restart arrow at the chip's 0.55 reads 130 where one stroke would read 97); the restart glyph test bounds the peak by the opaque primary at the same dimming instead of equating it. Not a change of the source's value, only of how the art is rasterised.

## ED-278

[UI][CHAT][TERM][MOTION] The ChatView parity unit's own engineering decisions (heading ED-278; the lead numbers it at merge; amended by the adversarial review of 2026-10-03, round 1). Each is a necessary internal choice made against the contract's section 8; none changes what the Mac shows except where OD-0076 is named. (1) THE CHROME ROW'S STACK (Port/ChatChromeRowStack.cs, PORT-ONLY, R-FILE-2). SOURCE FACT: the row is `HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 10)` whose title is `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` (ChatView.swift:1124,1238), and `.animation(Chrome.panelSlide, value: sidebarVisible)` is on the whole row (:1179). An Avalonia StackPanel gives a control only its own width and animates no layout, so the row is a StackPanel subclass: the title takes the leftover width (the trailing capsules sit at the row's end); when the sidebar takes or gives back the window buttons (the one value :1179 keys) the stack lays out at the final places at once and each control it had already drawn is arranged at its old place plus its offset times (1 - the panelSlide progress), from the clock and the frame source of the context that asked (Glide), so the row closes up or opens by gliding, starting at once; a control is known by its kind and its place among controls of that kind, because the row rebuilds most of its controls on every refresh (a SwiftUI body re-evaluates and a view's identity is its position). A removed control (the Threads button on its softAppear removal) gives up its slot at once and fades where it stood (Departing), as a removed view keeps no slot in an HStack; a control that arrives has no old place and comes in at its own. ENGINEERING DECISION, not generalised: the other structural changes of the row (the Hydra button on its setting, the Branch menu with a repository) snap at once, as the Mac's HStack does without an animation transaction; an OD-0076 transition for them belongs to the app-wide audit. (2) THE TWO SOFT APPEARS (ChatChromeRow.SoftAppear). SOURCE FACT: Chrome.swift:938-960 arrives on `.smooth(duration: 0.32)` fading in from 4 points low and leaves on `.easeOut(duration: 0.12)` as a plain fade. The shared SwiftTransition.SoftAppear (Chrome.cs:196-202) uses SoftAppearModifier, whose animatable data is empty, so it switches opacity and offset at once, a cut; the row decomposes the transition into opacity combined with offset(y: 4) under Animation.SoftAppear, as ThreadTimeline.SoftAppearTransition does. FOLLOW-UP outside this unit (shared code): ComposerView.cs:267,281,1145 and MarkdownView.cs:274,276 still use the cutting shared transition; split it in Chrome.cs the same way, then drop the private copy here. Proof: ChatViewParityAppearTests (the four mutants of the review, each killed: the 4 point rise, the Hydra button on the shared cut, a 0.5 s removal fade, an ease-out insertion). (3) THE TERMINAL'S PUSH (ChatView.PushTerminal). SOURCE FACT: the drawer joins the column's VStack under `.animation(_, value: isTerminalVisible)` (:96,276-279,290), so the thread view above it (timeline, chat box, panels) rises and sinks in step with the drawer's move, and `paneSize` (:241-249) takes the layout's final value once, the panels re-placing under the same panelSlide (2-chat-use.mov C 132.297-132.543: the head panels' bottom rows sit level with the chat box on every frame). The drawer's row takes its height at once, so the port animates the pane's bottom margin from minus a drawer's height to zero (the pane reaches under the drawer by the part still below its resting place) and back; that margin makes the pane's measured size pass through every value between (and layout rounding makes each a fraction off the last), so the scene never reads it: while a push runs it reads the size the push heads for (the column less the drawer's height when it opens; SettledPaneSize), at once when the push starts, so the panels' settle starts with it, and by the same formula on every layout; once an opened drawer's row is the layout the pane's own size is read again (a later drag of the drawer's height reaches the scene). The panels re-place under one panelSlide that starts with the push, so a bottom-docked one rises with the chat box and a top-docked one stays. A push that starts while another runs (the drawer reopened while it is still closing, closed while it is still opening) goes on from the margin the pane has now: a fresh opening starts a full drawer below, a drawer that still holds its row (the one leaving) has already given the pane its reach (OD-0076: the thread view never jumps). ## ED-279

[PALETTE][UI-WIN-032, UI-WIN-033] The spacing after a palette row's text block (supersedes the "UNRESOLVED (ED-273)" note in CommandPalette.cs, whose 20 points before a chord and none without one the review of unit/blitz-tail refuted). SOURCE FACT: the row is `HStack(spacing: 12) { icon (18); VStack(text); Spacer(minLength: 8); if let shortcut { chord } }` with the Spacer outside the `if let` (CommandPalette.swift:110-137, :132). ENGINEERING DECISION (Apple documents an HStack's spacing as the distance between adjacent subviews, and a Spacer is a subview): the text block is followed by 12 (text to Spacer), the Spacer (at least 8) and, only when a chord is shown, another 12 (Spacer to chord). So every row keeps 12 + 8 = 20 points after the text block, a title that fills its room included, and a row with a chord keeps 12 + 8 + 12 = 32 between the text block and the chord. Built as the text stack's trailing margin of 20 (kept when the chord is hidden) and the chord's left margin of 12 (CommandPalette.cs, CommandPaletteRow); the flexible part of the Spacer is the Grid's star column. The 8 is a floor and the 32 the space the row has when the title fills its room; a wider row lets the star column take the rest, as the Spacer does. Tests: CommandPaletteChordReviewTests (no chord, title fills its room, at least 8) and CommandPaletteChordTests (20 without a chord, 32 before one).

## ED-281

[UI][TEXT][OD-0099] Q-TEXT A: all text is drawn greyscale antialiased (no subpixel/ClearType), on every surface, with no hinting. The lead numbers it at merge. SOURCE FACT: the macOS app draws all its text greyscale (OD-0099, owner pick 2026-10-04: "text is drawn greyscale everywhere (no subpixel/ClearType), on every surface"). WHAT WAS WRONG (found by the look-picks designer, confirmed by the failing test of this unit): Avalonia 12.1.2 resolves `TextRenderingMode.Unspecified` to subpixel antialiasing with the platform's default hinting, and Skia draws the LCD colour fringe wherever the layer under the text is opaque (a window's own layer), grey inside an opacity or glass layer, so the same face looked different from surface to surface. A headless render of a sidebar row title, a chat paragraph and a glass-pill label over an opaque neutral backdrop showed pixels with R, G and B unequal before the change. WHAT CHANGED: (1) `Marrow.UI/Port/GreyscaleText.cs`: in 12.1.2 `TextOptions` is not a styled property (a Visual holds a plain `TextOptions` struct set by `TextOptions.SetTextRenderingMode` and `SetTextHintingMode`, and the compositor merges each visual's value with its parent's, unspecified inheriting), so the mode is set on every TopLevel, which reaches every Avalonia-drawn text below it: TextBlock, `FormattedText` through `DrawingContext.DrawText` (the composer text view, the message editor, the terminal surface), `DrawGlyphRun` (MorphingTextBlock) and the glass pill labels. It is applied the moment the application's styles reach a TopLevel, before its first frame: `PortControlThemes.Register` (the one point the app builder and both headless TestApps share) adds a style on `TopLevel` that sets the attached marker `GreyscaleText.AppliedProperty`, and the marker's change calls `GreyscaleText.Apply`. Windows, popup roots and any other TopLevel get it. (2) `TextRenderingMode.Antialias` (Avalonia's own name for greyscale antialiasing). (3) Hinting `TextHintingMode.None`, chosen over Slight: CoreText applies no grid fitting, so macOS draws the outlines scaled only, with linear advances; Slight (vertical-only snapping) would still pull the cap and x-height tops to whole pixels, which the reference frames do not show, and full hinting, which the platform default may resolve to, alters stems as well. At 96 dpi None reads a little softer than Windows' own text, which is the macOS non-Retina look the owner asked for. (4) The text the port draws itself through SkiaSharp is `TaskbarBadge`'s digit (an `SKFont` with `Edging = SKFontEdging.Antialias`, greyscale; its `Subpixel = true` is subpixel glyph positioning, not LCD edging) and the Skia shaders and lights draw no text; a source test keeps it that way. Nothing else in `src` creates an `SKFont`, `SKPaint` text or an `SKSurfaceProperties`. WHAT PROVES IT: `GreyscaleTextRenderTests` (a sidebar row title, a chat paragraph and a glass-pill label render with R == G == B in every pixel over a neutral backdrop; every TopLevel carries Antialias and None; the hinting mode changes the rasterized pixels; and the same render with a window asking for SubpixelAntialias does show fringes, so the check can fail) and `GreyscaleTextSourceTests` (no source file names SubpixelAntialias, LcdRenderText or an RGB/BGR pixel geometry, and every `new SKFont` states `Edging = SKFontEdging.Antialias`). WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: fonts, sizes, colours and layout code; only the rasterizer's request changed.

## ED-282

ED-282-1 [UI][FOUNDATION] AnimatedColor keeps a running fade when its control's appearance is re-evaluated (PR-COMPOSER-055).
FOUND: the slash list's hover fade (Chrome.hover, 0.1 s ease-out, ComposerView.swift:1096-1099) never played: hovering a row selects it, which shows the list again, and each show moves the hosted menu into a new frame (ComposerTextView.showSuggestions, SetFixedContent). The re-parented row gets ActualThemeVariantChanged, whose handler stopped the fade and wrote its end colour. Probe (SwiftClock ticks 0 throughout): right after the pointer-enter the fill alpha was 0, at the end of the same turn it was the target. DECISION: while a fade is running the handler only retargets it (the colour the new appearance resolves) and lets it go on; a fade not running still takes the colour at once, and AppearanceTurn's eased path is unchanged. Evidence: The_hovered_rows_fill_fades_in_over_a_tenth_of_a_second_on_an_ease_out (alpha 0 at the start, the ease-out curve at 0.05 s, the target at 0.11 s); mutation 055-retarget (the old Stop()) killed.

ED-282-2 [UI][COMPOSER] ComposerController.ReplaceCharacters is one edit for the undo stack and reports didChangeText at once (PR-COMPOSER-049).
FOUND (probe, Avalonia 12.1.2): assigning TextBox.Text clears the undo history (CanUndo false after a pick), while replacing the selection (SelectedText) keeps it and one Undo brings the typed run back. DECISION: ReplaceCharacters selects the range, sets SelectedText, puts the caret after it, then calls the text view's OnDidChangeText, the same method TextChanged reaches, because the Swift calls didChangeText() inside replaceCharacters (ComposerTextView.swift:46) and the dispatcher's own TextChanged comes a turn later: without the immediate report, the command pick's draft write (chip) carried the old text and the draft-to-text-view sync restored the typed "/word". Evidence: Picking_a_file_is_one_edit_for_the_undo_stack_..., Picking_a_command_is_one_edit_..., A_range_that_no_longer_fits_the_text_replaces_nothing; mutations 049-undo, 049-sync, 049-guard killed. Not changed (outside the record): paste (InsertPlainText) and Shift/Alt-Return newlines still assign Text and so clear undo.

ED-282-3 [UI][COMPOSER] DraftChips keeps one row, one scroller and its chips from one draft to the next (PR-COMPOSER-088).
The row was rebuilt whole on every chip change and, written under the writers' panelSlide, replayed its collapse arrival each time (a pulse), and reset the scroll offset. DECISION: the scroller and its HStack(spacing 6) are kept; chips are a keyed ForEach (identities "command" and the quote id); the whole-row ChipRowCollapse arrival and departure remain for empty to non-empty and back; a change of the ChipKey (ids, command name) applies the chips under Chrome.panelSlide, any other change (text edits, a command's detail) applies them with no animation and asks for no frame (:941). KNOWN LIMITS, foundation (ED-218) and not clauses of the record: a chip that leaves lingers in layout while it fades, so the chips after it move when it is gone, not with it (closed by ED-282-12); and the glide of the chips that stay is off under reduce motion (ForEach.CanGlide) although Chrome.panelSlide has a 0.18 s ease-out there.

ED-282-4 [UI][COMPOSER] The composer's text box has a control template: a text presenter inside the container inset (PR-COMPOSER-015).
FOUND: the app carries no theme package (PlainControls.PlainTextField's note), and ComposerNSTextView had no template, so a TextBox drew nothing but its placeholder: a headless render of a typed three-line draft was blank (scratch/composerview/render.png before), the box's visual tree held only the TextBox itself, and no text could scroll or keep its caret in view. DECISION: the template is the TextPresenter alone (Text, TextWrapping, selection and caret bound to the box, PlainControls.FieldBrushes for the accent caret and the selection colour) in a Border carrying the box's 0 and 2 point padding; the placeholder stays drawn by ComposerNSTextView.Render (:198-211); the box takes the text's height in the ScrollViewer ComposerTextView already wraps it in (:273), which scrolls past the fixed height and brings the caret into view. Evidence: The_text_view_draws_its_text_and_past_five_lines_it_scrolls_... (red before, with the presenter missing); render after: the three lines and the caret drawn. UNVERIFIED natively (OD-0001): selection and caret appearance, the scroll bar (the outer ScrollViewer theme).

ED-282-5 [UI][COMPOSER] The context ring leaves and returns through the opacity transition, and its track sits on the arc's circle (UI-COMPOSER-013, UI-USAGE-001).
FOUND: the ring was cut in and out (Child = null / Child = button) where Swift's `if !isPoppedOut, ...` (ComposerView.swift:713) is an if-branch with the default opacity transition. VIDEO (settings.usage-panel-switch-live, S 36.340-38.950; usage.pop-out, C 56.915-57.307): the ring fades in 3-4 frames as the column moves, on a Settings switch and on the pop-out button alike. The switch writes with no transaction of its own (a native Toggle brings one on the Mac). Second finding: the track was an Avalonia Ellipse, which insets its outline by half the stroke, so it drew 1.25 inside the arc (radius 6.25 against 7.5); VIDEO static.composer-context-ring fits the track's centre line at 7.53, the arc's circle. DECISION: the ring lives in a slot and arrives and leaves through SwiftTransition.Insert/Remove under `Transaction.Current ?? Chrome.PanelSlide` (the pop-out writes inside panelSlide; a write with no animation takes panelSlide too, as OD-0076 has nothing change by a cut); the first showing places the ring with no transition; a leaving ring takes no click, and its popover closes at once, not when the fade ends; a ring that returns while one is leaving takes the same button back. The track is a Path over the same 15 by 15 EllipseGeometry as the arc. Evidence: The_ring_fades_out_when_the_usage_panel_pops_out_and_back_in_... (both writers), A_ring_that_leaves_with_its_popover_open_..., The_arc_sweeps_clockwise_... (pixels at eight angles over a white ground: the track is under every one, so it is on the arc's circle). Two older B3 ring tests now run the fade on a ManualFrameSource before they read the ring's absence (they asserted the cut).

ED-282-6 [UI][FOUNDATION] A palette symbol with two styles draws its two layers (UI-COMPOSER-010).
FOUND: ED-182 (Q6) drew `.symbolRenderingMode(.palette)` monochrome, so `xmark.circle.fill` with `.foregroundStyle(.white, .black.opacity(0.6))` (ComposerView.swift:1008-1010, EditorAttachments.swift:30) was a white disc with a see-through x, the inverse of the Mac's white x on a black 0.6 disc (the record's colour clause). DECISION: in palette mode with two styles, a .fill symbol that has a container (ED-182 Q4) paints the container (inside and its own stroke) in the second style and draws the other elements over it in the first; every other mode and a palette symbol with one style stay monochrome. SwiftImage.SecondaryForeground is now drawn. Evidence: A_palette_fill_symbol_draws_the_container_in_the_second_style_..., The_remove_badge_is_a_white_cross_on_a_black_60_percent_disc_... (pixels in the composer's strip); symbolRenderingMode_draws_monochrome_in_the_foreground_colour keeps its monochrome half and asserts the palette now differs.

ED-282-7 [UI][COMPOSER] A draft cell claims the armed flight once, when it is first laid out (UI-COMPOSER-009).
FOUND (probe): the screen-frame reader also reports when the cell joins the window, before its first arrange, with an empty rectangle; the armed ghost was taken and flew to the cell's origin, 0 by 0. And a cell that stayed kept isNew true for good (the port has no re-evaluation where Swift's onAppear changes `drawn`), so when another cell was removed beside it and it moved, it took the next picker's drop. DECISION: AttachmentArrival.Report ignores an empty rectangle and sets isNew false after the first laid-out report, with or without a drop (Swift: the strip's next evaluation hands the cell isNew false). Evidence: A_picked_attachments_cell_claims_the_armed_flight_once_and_a_cell_that_stays_does_not_claim_the_next_one (the flight lands on the new cell's laid-out frame; a later drop stays armed when the first cell moves).

ED-282-8 [UI][COMPOSER] The attachment notice's row folds open and shut under the change's transaction (UI-COMPOSER-004; OD-0076).
FOUND: the notice's own transition runs but moves no sibling, so the pill's height jumped by the line and its 6 point margin on arrival and again when the leaving wrapper was dropped; Swift makes both changes inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) (ComposerView.swift:523, :224), which eases the text view's place and the pill's height (documented SwiftUI behaviour, UNVERIFIED under OD-0001). DECISION: NoticeSlot holds the line top-aligned in a clip and folds its height 0 to the line's (and back) along the transaction's animation, with the line keeping its own transition (the 0.12 s ease-out fade on the way out); the slot leaves the column when the fade and the fold are both over. Evidence: The_notice_row_opens_under_panelSlide_so_the_pill_eases_to_its_new_height, After_5_s_the_notice_fades_out_over_0_12_s_while_the_pill_eases_back_and_nothing_is_left_behind. FOUND (foundation, outside this record): the foundation's SoftAppear carries no animatable data, so its insertion snaps to the identity state (SwiftAnimation.cs Gather: a modifier with zero-length data is `to.Update(body)`) where SwiftUI animates the opacity and offset inside the modifier's body, so every SoftAppear site arrives at full opacity at once. NOT changed there (shared by every site). The notice plays its own arrival instead: NoticeSlot.Arrive runs the opacity 0 to 1 and the 4 point rise on Animation.SoftAppear (smooth 0.32) and keeps the transition's removal half; evidence: the arrival is sampled at 0.2 s in The_notice_row_opens_under_panelSlide_so_the_pill_eases_to_its_new_height_while_the_line_comes_in_as_softAppear.

ED-282-9 [UI][COMPOSER] A disabled send button dims its label to half and its fill eases between states (UI-COMPOSER-016; OD-0076).
FOUND: VIDEO content.composer-send-states (C 81.640, C 90.5): an empty composer's send disc is a faint translucent grey with an arrow that is about half white; the port drew a full-white arrow on the quaternary disc. Measured on the extracted frames over the disc: the arrow peak is white at 0.48, 0.51 and 0.50 (R, G, B) of the way from the disc to white, the enabled arrow peak is 0.98 of white (anti-aliasing), the disc adds +11 over the pill where a full quaternary would add +18 to +27. DECISION: a disabled button (empty draft, or a take-back in flight) draws its disc fill and its glyph at 0.5 of their colours (SendDraftState.DisabledLabelOpacity); a change of state moves the fill and the ink along the transaction's animation, else Animation.EaseOut(0.12) (the Mac changes the fill in one frame; OD-0076). NOT CHANGED, measured and recorded: the stop to arrow morph (C 125.762-126.250): the square holds about 0.04 s, shrinks from 10 to 4 pixels over about 0.2 s, the arrow grows from the bottom over about 0.23 s (11 pixels by 126.222); SymbolReplace uses the arrow to stop timings (0.19 s out, 0.18 s in, about the centre) for both directions. Evidence: The_send_button_reads_its_state_from_the_run_the_draft_and_the_revert_in_glyph_fill_ink_name_and_help, An_idle_click_sends_the_draft_once_and_never_interrupts.
