## ED-309

[SKILLS][PROCESS][BUILD][TEST] Unit SK-6 / DL-6 (OD-0103). Authority: first-release/BUILD-PLAN.md 2.5 SK-6 and the Marrow.sln ownership row; first-release/skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN.md 3.1, 3.4, 3.6, 4.2, 7 DL-6 and 8's W0-4 replacement; first-release/skills-PLAN.md 2.6's Store-alias and child-environment rules. ORIGINALS-PLAN.md itself is not present in this checkout; its cited W0-4 replacement is explicitly described in ONDEMAND section 8. These are engineering choices, not new source facts or product defaults.

1. Build ownership: add the authorized BCL-only net10.0 NativeAOT console project `src/Marrow.Shim` to Marrow.sln. Link the same one-type-per-file Services/Shims sources into it instead of referencing the Windows Services assembly (which would drag voice/runtime packages into the small launcher). No production package or layer reference is added. Add build-only fixture/launcher references and output-copy targets to Services.Tests; add a standalone offline test project linking the identical acceptance tests and Services shim sources, since this worker's cache lacks the newer voice and NativeAOT packages. This is a recorded exception to IMPLEMENTING/WORKER_BRIEF protected-project rules, authorized by the owner's SK-6 assignment; the guard itself is unchanged.
2. Sidecar: `<executable basename>.shim` is UTF-8 JSON with a source-generated System.Text.Json context, so NativeAOT needs no reflection. Internal fields are Target (required explicit path), Environment (explicit child overrides), PrefixArguments (e.g. Python `-m pip` or Node's upstream CLI script), PythonPathFile, PackagePaths, NodePath, LibreOffice and WorkDirectory. Absent overrides/prefixes are identity operations; no vendor version, target path, package list or product-facing text is guessed. Installer units supply the pinned paths and lock the files; updates/removal/leases are SK-8/SK-5. ShimFiles writes real `.exe` names; npm/npx `.cmd` wrappers forward `%*` directly (no CALL) to copies under `bin/.launchers/<name>.exe`, whose sidecars target Node plus the upstream CLI script, avoiding shell execution of a batch target by Process.Start.
3. Streams and arguments: inherit the native standard handles and working directory, use ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList and return the target's integer exit code. There is no stream decoding, line buffering or pipe pump. The only added arguments are the explicit installer-supplied prefixes and the plan's LibreOffice profile argument.
4. Windows tree lifetime: IShimLifetime.Arm runs before any child spawn. WindowsShimLifetime puts the shim itself in a non-breakaway Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so children and grandchildren join at creation without a post-start assignment race. The job handle is non-inheritable and intentionally owned until OS process teardown: closing it in a managed Dispose would also kill the shim. External pid-only termination closes the last handle and kills the tree. Non-Windows Arm does no Windows work; this is not a claim of Linux Job Object equivalence. Windows-only acceptance is explicitly skipped with a reason on non-Windows, as the owner requires (overrides IMPLEMENTING's no-skip rule).
5. Python: ONDEMAND 3.4 states `._pth` ignores PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME, while 3.4/3.6 require per-call sets without changing the locked Python folder. Use `work/python-run-<random>` per call: copy the interpreter and adjacent DLL companions, retain adjacent runtime JSON companions (also permits the offline .NET fake interpreter), copy pip.ini so its agent-install target survives relocation, and write the same-named `._pth` with original relative entries resolved absolutely into the locked runtime plus explicit installed package/agent paths, then import site. Clear the copied files' ReadOnly flag so Windows can delete the private run; leave source bytes/attributes unchanged. The large standard-library zip and all packages stay at their absolute original paths. Set PYTHONUTF8=1 in this child only; never mutate process-global/provider/user-tool variables. This copies interpreter/DLL bytes per invocation, trading some local I/O for no mutation/race in the locked runtime and no Python argv emulation. Actual CPython/pip behavior is still the plan's DL-20 live check, not established by fake targets.
6. LibreOffice: make a fresh `addons/work/lo-profile-<random>` for each call, append `-env:UserInstallation=` with an escaped absolute file URI, and delete on normal or nonzero child exit and launch failure. Python's private run also deletes in finally. An externally killed shim cannot run managed cleanup; leftover private Python/profile directories need startup/GC collection by the store lifecycle unit (SK-5), which is not wired here. Do not claim synchronous directory deletion after external termination.
7. PATH: the caller passes the already-resolved isolated data root. ForChild creates addons/bin even if empty and copies the environment; Insert preserves the existing entries and places bin before the first complete Microsoft/WindowsApps suffix (ordinal case-insensitive Windows spelling, quoted entry and trailing slash accepted), otherwise at the end. Windows uses semicolon; explicit separator makes Windows logic executable on Linux; ForChild uses the host separator. No global PATH or actual provider session is edited; SK-11 owns the provider/native run_command wiring and calls this helper.
8. Tests build only the tiny local .NET fake target, and run copied launchers with disposable paths containing spaces and Unicode. MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR is fresh /tmp data for worker commands and set to the fixture root for children. Windows cmd /c needs a raw command line rather than CRT ArgumentList quoting; PowerShell Start-Process -NoNewWindow passes raw native arguments/inherited handles without pipeline transcoding. Git Bash is explicitly Git for Windows at ProgramFiles/Git/bin/bash.exe or the test-only MARROW_SK6_GIT_BASH path, never the WSL alias. No shell/tool downloads or real python/node/soffice targets are used. Wall-clock bounds/polling apply only to real subprocess integration/cleanup, not ported scheduling.
9. Evidence/limits: see `porting/evidence/f-sk-6/REPORT.md` and authentic logs. Linux runs use a JIT apphost (PublishAot=false) because cached NativeAOT toolchain packs are absent. Windows shell/batch/Job Object tests and the NativeAOT publish are delivered/unverified; full-solution build is blocked by missing cached voice packages and Setup assets. Independent adversarial review caught pip.ini, batch dispatch and ordering-test gaps; these were repaired, and an additional read-only-copy regression was reproduced then repaired. No existing acceptance test was weakened/deleted and no ledger status was changed.
10. Windows integration review (unit/integ-sk6). Marrow.sln builds (0 warnings, 0 errors). `dotnet publish src/Marrow.Shim -c Release -r win-x64 -p:PublishAot=true` succeeds when vswhere.exe is on PATH (add "%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer"; without it the ILCompiler link step fails with exit code 123): one standalone Marrow.Shim.exe of 2,924,544 bytes (about 2.8 MiB, no managed DLL beside it; about 41 MB for the 14 shim names of 3.6), and the 21 SK-6 tests pass with that AOT exe as the launcher, including cmd, PowerShell 5.1, Git Bash and the Job Object tree kill. Defects found on Windows and repaired test-first: (a) a sidecar with only "Target" crashed the launcher (the source-generated reader leaves Environment, PrefixArguments and PackagePaths null for fields the file does not name, bypassing their defaults; ShimDefinition.Read restores them; the unit's tests always wrote every field); (b) a per-call profile or Python run folder that cannot be deleted because a worker the target left behind holds it replaced the target's exit code with an unhandled IOException (cleanup is now best effort and the folder is left for the store's collection, item 6); (c) the job killed every descendant at a NORMAL exit, so a background helper a tool starts on purpose died when the tool finished, unlike a direct run; the kill-on-close flag is now cleared at ProcessExit, and a kill or crash of the shim (which never raises ProcessExit) still ends the tree; (d) the soffice tests compared a path containing non-ASCII letters after Windows had re-encoded it to the OEM page, so their folder-deleted checks could pass on a path that never existed: the fake target now writes UTF-8 and the fixture reads UTF-8; empty argument lines are kept on Windows; the fixture's delete retries while an exited image is still mapped; the tree-kill test also ends the direct target, so a launcher that does not own the tree fails it instead of hanging the run; (e) every SK-6 test now carries Rule R-TEST-4 (the Traceability check refuses a test without Req, Rule or Decision). OPEN, a lead decision: Core.Tests ProcessLauncherTests.The_child_joins_its_job_through_the_attribute_list_at_creation_and_is_never_assigned_afterwards (ED-047, R-PROC-1) fails because it forbids the text AssignProcessToJobObject anywhere under src, and WindowsShimLifetime.cs uses it to put the SHIM ITSELF in its job before it starts any child (so no child ever runs outside the job, the window that guard exists for). The guard was not edited. Either exempt that one file in the guard with this reason, or start the target with CreateProcessW and PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST instead. Not established by fake targets and left to DL-20: the real CPython behaviour with the private ._pth copy (the copy of python.exe and the DLLs per call, and a sys.executable that names the private copy, which a console script written by pip would remember). porting/evidence/f-sk-6/source-sha256.txt holds the Linux-time hashes and is not refreshed. Verification: Core.Tests 4057 of 4058 (the one failure is the guard above), Services.Tests 3664 of 3666 on the full run (Traceability, repaired by item (e); MCPOAuthTests.A_failed_shared_refresh_reaches_every_waiter_and_a_later_caller_starts_a_new_request, which passed alone twice: a load flake outside this unit); Feature=SK-6 21 passed, 0 skipped on Windows. Hand mutations, each killed: PATH inserted after the WindowsApps entry, the shim not joining its job, PYTHONUTF8 not set.

LEAD RULING (2026-10-04, Windows verification of SK-6): ProcessLauncherTests' R-PROC-1 / ED-047 scan forbids AssignProcessToJobObject anywhere under src because a child assigned after CreateProcessW runs outside its job for a moment. WindowsShimLifetime.cs is the one exemption: the shim assigns ITSELF (Process.GetCurrentProcess()) to its kill-on-close job before it starts any child, so every descendant is created inside the job and the guarded window cannot exist. The scan keeps forbidding the call everywhere else, and for that file asserts it assigns only the current process and creates no process. ## ED-310

[VOICE][ENGINEERING] Voice typing unit VT-6 (engine, VAD, hardware probe; branch cloud/f-vt-6, built on cloud/f-vt-7; the lead numbers it at merge). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where voice-SPEC.md, voice-pins.json and the OD-0099 picks are silent; none changes an owner ruling. The code is `src/Marrow.Services/Port/Voice/{Engine,Probe}/`, the tests `tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Port/Voice/{Engine,Probe}/` (`Feature` VT-6, `Decision` ED-267 as the stand-in), the gate tool `tools/voice-evidence/VoiceEvidence.cs`. 1. Layering of the engine (V-7.1, V-2.4). `WhisperNetEngine : ISpeechEngine` sits on a seam `IWhisperBackend` (load a model to an `IWhisperModel`, decode to `BackendSegment`s of `BackendToken`s) so everything the adapter decides (decode settings, word assembly, one model at a time, residency, cancellation, load failure) is contract-tested on Linux with a scripted backend, as the ScriptedEngine shape. `WhisperNetBackend` and `WhisperNetModel` are the only types that touch Whisper.net (the members they use are listed in `WhisperNetBackend.UsedMembers` and held to VT-0's `apiMembers` and to the 1.9.1 assembly by reflection: V-T2). Their real loads are Windows-only tests. Ambient fail-closed defaults: `EngineSeams.Backend`, `EngineSeams.VadNative`, `HardwareProbeSeams.Probe` (a test overrides them for its flow; the defaults throw `SeamNotBoundException`).
2. Decode settings (V-7.1). Live: greedy, best-of 1. Final: beam search, beam 5 (`WhisperNetEngine.FinalBeamSize`). Threads: `EngineLoadOptions.Threads` or `max(1, physicalCores - 2)` (V-2.2) read at load. Language: "auto" = `WithLanguageDetection()`, a code = `WithLanguage(code)`. The prompt is set only when it is not empty. Token timestamps on; `WithTemperature(0f)` and the library's own temperature fallback left alone (the spec's "default fallback"). The detected language is returned in `Hypothesis.Language` only when the request was "auto" (V-12.10 says "when it reports one"; a forced language is not a detection). Empty audio returns `Hypothesis.Empty` without touching the backend.
3. Words (V-7.2). A token whose text starts with a space starts a word; spaces-only tokens make no word; a word runs from its first token's start to its last token's end (never before its start); special tokens (`[_BEG_]`, `[_TT_n]`, `<|...|>`; the backend flags them by text, UNVERIFIED against the real token stream) belong to no word and do not split one; for scripts without spaces a segment boundary starts a new word, so a segment's token run is one word ("one word per token run"). `WhisperToken.Start` and `End` are read as whisper.cpp's t0 and t1 in 10 ms units (UNVERIFIED; the voice-evidence tool prints the words with their times).
4. One model, residency (V-7.1, V-7.9). Loading releases the model before it, then loads (so two models are never resident); asking for the model and options already loaded shares it (the hover then the click load once; two loads in flight run the backend once). A failed or cancelled load leaves nothing loaded and forgets the remembered model. "Process-wide" is held by binding ONE `WhisperNetEngine` for the process (there is no static). Passes and loads run one at a time (a `SemaphoreSlim`; a cancelled wait never reaches the backend). V-7.9's "5 minutes without a session" is defined as 5 minutes on the injected clock (`SwiftClock.Provider`) after the last load, the last shared load or the end of the last pass (the engine sees calls, not sessions; a timer is re-armed at each); a pass in flight is never unloaded under (the timer is stopped while it runs and re-armed when it ends). `Unload()` releases at once and waits for a pass in flight. After an idle release a pass loads the remembered model again (a decision the spec does not state; without it a session whose model the hub still believes loaded would fail); a pass before any model was ever loaded throws `InvalidOperationException`.
5. Runtime order (V-7.1, Q-V-9 C, voice-pins.json cuda). `RuntimeOrder.For(facts, useGpu)`: Cuda12 only when the folder is complete and the GPU is NVIDIA, then Vulkan, then Cpu, each only when installed, all kept as the fallback chain; `UseGpu = false` gives the processor only. `FileRuntimeInventory` finds Cpu and Vulkan beside the app (`runtimes\win-x64`, `runtimes\vulkan\win-x64`) and offers Cuda12 only when the pack's five files AND the three NVIDIA libraries the pack does not carry (`cudart64_12.dll`, `cublas64_12.dll`, `cublasLt64_12.dll`, VT-0's `packDoesNotCarry`) are all in `<data root>\runtimes\cuda12\win-x64`; presence only (VT-7 verified sizes and hashes), because VT-0 probe case 15 showed a half-installed CUDA folder aborts the process. `WhisperNativeRuntimes.Configure` sets `RuntimeOptions.RuntimeLibraryOrder`; with Cuda12 in the order it sets `LibraryPath` to `<data root>\runtime.dll` (the loader reads the directory of the path: VT-0 `libraryPathSemantics`) and puts the CUDA folder on this process's PATH (VT-0 probe cases 14 and 17: cudart is found by its bare name). Whisper.net loads a native library once per process, so the order given at the first load is the one that counts. UNVERIFIED until the Windows run: that with `LibraryPath` set the loader still finds the app folder's Vulkan and CPU runtimes as the fallback. Nothing in this unit puts the NVIDIA libraries on disk (that is the NVIDIA companion download, OD-0104); until it does, `FileRuntimeInventory` never offers Cuda12 and the engine runs on Vulkan or the processor.
6. `SileroVad` (V-6.1, V-6.2). Whisper.net 1.9.1 gives segments only (VT-0), so the five whisper.cpp exports are P/Invoked (`WhisperVadImports`, `WhisperVadContextParams` = `{ int n_threads; byte use_gpu; int gpu_device; }` as in whisper.h; `whisper_vad_default_context_params` is not among the five exports, so the struct is filled here). The "whisper" library name is bound to ONE whisper.dll per process by a `NativeLibrary` resolver (a DllImport is resolved once); a second `Open` with another path throws. `whisper_vad_detect_speech` starts Silero's recurrent state afresh on every call (from the whisper.cpp source; UNVERIFIED here), so a frame cannot be answered on its own: `SileroVad` keeps the last `windowFrames` frames (default 8 = 256 ms, `DefaultWindowFrames`) and answers each new frame with the LAST probability of one native call over that window; `Reset()` empties the window. The window length is a cost/accuracy choice (8 frames per 32 ms); the voice-evidence tool compares the rolling answers with one call over the whole clip (max difference, agreement about 0.5) and with Whisper.net's own VAD segments, and prints the cost per frame. The speech-state hysteresis of V-6.2 is the session's (VT-3), not this class's. UNVERIFIED: the struct layout, the export signatures (`bool` as one byte, `float*` read after `whisper_vad_n_probs`), the number of probabilities per call, and the DLL choice: `SileroVad.Open` is given the whisper.dll of the runtime Whisper.net loaded (two different whisper.dll copies in one process may share dependent DLLs by name on Windows).
7. `HardwareProbe` (V-10.1, V-T45). Four steps in the table's order (Processor, Memory, Graphics, GPU backend), each read on a pool thread and reported to the caller's `Action<ProbeRow>` before the next read starts; no timer, no delay (the tests run it on the manual clock without advancing it). The raw reads are the seam `IHardwareSource` (`ProcessorName`, `PhysicalCores`, `TotalPhysicalBytes`, `Adapters`, `DriverVersion`), the backend step the seam `IGpuBackendCheck`. Row texts exactly as V-10.1: `{name}, {cores} cores` (no singular form), `{floor GB} GB`, `{description}, {round GB} GB` or `{description}, shared memory` under 512 MiB dedicated (512 MiB = 2^29 bytes; round = half away from zero, so exactly 0.5 GB reads "1 GB"), `Vulkan, working` / `CUDA, working` / `None working, runs on the processor`. The processor name is trimmed (the registry pads it). The adapter is the non-software one with the most dedicated memory, the first listed on a tie; the vendor comes from the PCI vendor id (0x10DE NVIDIA, 0x1002 AMD, 0x8086 Intel, anything else Other; 0x1022 is not mapped). With no usable adapter the profile has empty description and driver, vendor Other, 0 VRAM, the backend step loads nothing and reads None, and the Graphics row says `No graphics adapter`: UNRESOLVED wording, a proposal (`ProbeText.NoGraphicsAdapter`), for the lead to settle with the Q-V-4 wording. ## ED-311

Unit VT-16, the OpenAI cloud engine, service part (voice-SPEC V-17.2, V-18.1 to V-18.5). The key row on the Voice typing page is VT-13/VT-14's file and is not in this unit. Code: `src/Marrow.Services/Port/Voice/Cloud/`; tests: `tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Port/Voice/Cloud/` (Feature VT-16), all on an in-process handler or a loopback server, never the real API; no test touches the real Credential Manager, so there is no WINDOWS-ONLY test.

1. Seam. `OpenAiTranscriber(VoiceKeyStore, HttpMessageHandler, TimeSpan? timeout = 60 s, Uri? endpoint = the V-18.1 URL)`. The handler has no default, so nothing here can reach the network until a caller binds one (V-18.5, fail closed). The spec gives no way to hand deltas to the session through `ISpeechEngine`; the engine raises `OpsProduced` (word operations, the same `WordOp`s as V-7.5) during the call, on the thread reading the reply, and still returns the `Hypothesis` at the end. Wiring it into the session's Processing is the integrating unit's.
2. Notes, not words. `CloudNote` is KeyMissing, KeyRefused (401), QuotaOrRate (429), NetworkFailure, EngineFailure; the wording is D-VN's pick, built by VT-17 (Q-V-7), so no string is invented here. 5xx and every other status, an unreadable reply and a file over 25 MB (V-18.3) are EngineFailure; a refused or dropped connection and the 60 s timeout are NetworkFailure (the timeout also sets `TimedOut`; V-17.6 lists no separate timeout note). One request per call: no retry and no fallback to the local engine (V-18.4). The user's own cancel stays an `OperationCanceledException`. The exception message carries the note and status only, never the key or what OpenAI wrote back.
3. No key. `LoadAsync` and `TranscribeAsync` both throw KeyMissing before any request (a session without a key stops before it records). The key is read from `VoiceKeyStore` on every call and from nowhere else (not the environment).
4. `VoiceKeyStore` saves with `SecretStore.SetReplacing` (the Providers key pattern: trimmed, empty removes the item), reads blank as no key, and has no logging at all.
5. Request. `file` is `audio.wav` (`audio/wav`), then `model`, `language`, `response_format` = `json`, `stream` = `true`, in that order; no other field (V-18.1 lists no `prompt`, so the request's prompt is not sent). `language` only when the request's language is not `auto` (V-7.13), sent as the code. The model is `gpt-transcribe` until `LoadAsync` is given another id. `stream` is sent for models whose id starts `gpt-` and not for others (whisper-1): V-18.1 says "where the model supports it" without a list. A reply with `Content-Type: text/event-stream` is read as events whatever was asked; any other is read as JSON `{"text": ...}`.
6. Samples are converted at full scale 32767, clipped to [-1, 1], halves rounding away from zero (V-18.1 gives only "16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV").
7. Events. Only `transcript.text.delta` (`delta`) and `transcript.text.done` (`text`) count; other events and unreadable data are skipped. A stream that ends without `done` takes the deltas' text as final. The done text is the result even if it differs from the deltas (it revises and confirms). A word is tentative until whitespace follows it; the done event makes every word solid (V-8.4).
8. Word times. A reply has none, and `StreamingTranscriber.ApplyFinal` drops words wholly in silent spans (V-7.8), so the words are spread evenly over the audio's length. `Hypothesis.Language` is null (the `json` format does not report one).
9. Live passes (V-18.2): the engine treats every call alike, one request. The integrating unit must run only the final pass for this engine; it is not stopped here.
10. WINDOWS REVIEW (2026-10-04, unit/integ-vt6-vt16): ONE DEFECT FIXED test-first. `HttpClient.Timeout` ends at the reply's headers (the reply is read with `ResponseHeadersRead`), so a server that sent its headers and a first event and then went quiet held `TranscribeAsync`, and the orb in Processing, for ever (only the user's Esc ended it). A linked token now carries the same 60 s over the body: it is set when the request is sent and renewed at every event of a stream (a stream that keeps sending is never cut; a JSON body has the 60 s from the send), and its expiry is the same timed-out `NetworkFailure`. `VoiceKeyStoreWindowsTests` runs the key through the app's `SecretStore` on the REAL Windows Credential Manager (generic, CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE, user name `voice-openai`, read back, replaced, removed, ERROR_NOT_FOUND afterwards) under a throwaway service name `Marrow VT-16 test <guid>` through `RenamedTargetCredentialBackend`, which refuses any target outside "Marrow Code" and renames the rest, so the user's own credentials are never touched; the test deletes its item. Not verifiable without the network: that `gpt-transcribe` (Q-V-15, the owner's pick) is a model id OpenAI's endpoint accepts, and the real reply shapes (the loopback fakes follow V-18.1).

## ED-312

CZ-1 “Controls and text”, branch `codex/f-cz-1`, 2026-10-04. Scope: BUILD-PLAN section 2 CZ-1; customization-SPEC CZ-5..8, CZ-12, CZ-4.5.4 and the control portion of CZ-15. No page, settings persistence, manifest, ledger status or locked design source was changed by this feature.

1. **Control composition and ownership.** Put reusable controls in Marrow.UI/Port/Settings/CzControls, one top-level type per file. Options, selected IDs, values, row formatters and dependent visuals come from the caller; an empty option set, missing selected ID or duplicate ID is a programming error and throws rather than inventing a pick. The CZ-12.3 switch adapter takes the actual App SettingsSwitch and delegates its existing toggle provider; it does not recreate its small-switch drawing. Orb tiles require actual Control instances from the voice renderer, and colour wells require the real picker callback from CZ-2. Neither boundary supplies a placeholder or touches voice/picker state. Pages own pair spacing (14 for wells), row wiring and persistence. All these signatures are internal integration choices where the design only gives browser view models.

2. **Fixture provenance and text.** tests/fixtures/customization/generate.cjs executes the unmodified cz.js in Node. Its row/section rendering seams capture every text branch from the real beamRows, auraRows, resetRow and sections methods, its snap cases evaluate the actual slider setter expression, and its czTone fixtures execute the real function. The locked copies omit the external composer-lights hex2, mixHex, fmt and clamp helpers, so the harness supplies the exact CZ-12.10/11 operations. For the unspecified algebraic evaluation order of linear sRGB mixing, use `from * (1 - t) + to * t` in the harness and port; keep the design's binary `t += .05` accumulation and half-up channel rounding. The full CZ-5..8 literal-token inventory is also retained in CzText.TableText (including the tables' keys/format templates), with named style, palette and shape maps and the dynamic AuraColours helper. Markdown line wrapping inside the Off note is removed: cz.js:673 has the single-line text. Tests check the inventory bytes, actual Node row text and the named maps.

3. **Maker data.** The lead supplied liquid-palettes.json on staging at 22902480a; merged that staging update. Its SHA256 is a600baefbcf22aca861392456ff4d9c05088c37627fe30e95cd5142d5c441f15. The committed Node generator follows gen.py's order, nice names, model cleanup and five high stops per theme, and emits MakerLiquids.cs as a read-only ordered dictionary catalogue. This avoids editing a protected project manifest to add a resource. The fixture includes all 30 makers × two themes × four input stops, plus threshold/fallback cases; no generated maker value is a placeholder.

4. **Motion and colour tokens.** Use the existing FrameClock, SwiftClock, Animation.TimingCurve and SwiftColor.PremultipliedMix contracts, following LookMotion's ED-250 lifecycle: retarget from the visible value, settle on detach, and land immediately with Reduce Motion or no bound frame source. LookCard's token properties and motion types are internal in Marrow.App, which Marrow.UI cannot reference; keep the same locked numeric tokens in a UI-local resolver and use the existing Chrome.Accent for focus. Style glyphs request frames only while visible and in their viewport. Theme-dependent brushes are refreshed when ActualThemeVariant changes after attachment; a light-window regression test covers this lifecycle. The caller supplies each row's specified formatter; the optional bare-number fallback uses fmt(v,4), retaining slider snap precision instead of introducing a unit or losing a stored decimal.

5. **Shared menu presentation.** Use Presentation and WindowTransients so Escape consumes the transient before Settings-window closing. Set the presenter's existing IsSheet opt-out on the Popup solely to suppress its OD-0095 tip; the control still exposes button expand/collapse/invoke and menu-item selection peers, not dialog semantics. An owned transform keeps the presenter from installing a second appear animation. Explicitly choose above/below from the enclosing window's bounds (native popup collision normally uses screen bounds), preserve the six-pixel gap and the row's left/right alignment, and place the animation origin on the button-facing edge. Menu width comes from the actual text measurements. Tests use the repository's existing ReviewOverlayPresenter because Avalonia headless cannot create a native PopupRoot; they exercise the real presentation path, pointer light dismissal, window-bound flip, keyboard focus, checked peers and timed transitions.

6. **Verification limits.** The CZ-1 tests use fresh /tmp MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR directories, the headless UI session and scripted frame/runtime seams; they invoke no network, real CLI or user data directory. Native Windows UI Automation traversal, native popup rendering and pixel comparison on Windows remain Windows-only verification, outside what the Linux headless checks can prove. No existing test was weakened or deleted.

CZ-1 acceptance tests are in CzTextTests (CZ-T6, T7, T8, T30), MakerLiquidsTests (CZ-T29) and CzControlsTests (CZ-T9, T13, T25, T42, T43 control part, T92). Additional tests cover pointer capture, Auto, initial card selection, light-theme attachment, fold/divider/text transitions and picker delegation. The Linux test commands filter only those three classes; the environment install script restores and builds Marrow.sln.

Final Linux verification: environment install script restore/build succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors; filtered CzTextTests and MakerLiquidsTests: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; filtered CzControlsTests: 34 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Fixture/catalogue regeneration is byte-identical; git diff --check and one-type-per-file checks pass. Native Windows checks above were not run.
Integration correction (unit/integ-cz1-cz2, Windows review, 2026-10-04). Item 2's choice of `from * (1 - t) + to * t` for the mix is withdrawn: the page's `mixHex` is the playground's (composer-lights playground logic.js:44, `Math.round(x + (b - x) * t)`), and Core already ports it as `BorderBeamMath.MixHex`. The two orders differ in 6306 of the 18 x 256 x 256 channel cases `czTone` can reach and gave `#97b827` for NVIDIA's light `highlight` where the design gives `#97b828`. `CzText.Tone` now calls `BorderBeamMath.MixHex`, the Node harness uses the logic.js formula, and the fixture holds three more tone inputs where the orders differ. Hue: Left / Right (or Down / Up) one degree, Shift ten, Home 0, End 359.9. Opacity: a hundredth, Shift a tenth, Home 0, End 1. Recent: Left / Right move a cursor, Enter or Space picks it. (2) PR-CHAT-104, THE FOLD AND THE TURN-END SWAP (OD-0076; the lead's ruling of 2026-10-04; ENGINEERING DECISION for the mechanism). TRANSITION AUDIT ENTRIES (no separate audit file exists; these are the entries): (a) the finished turn's header fold: the Mac animates it (TimelineRows.swift:2609-2616 `.snappy(duration: 0.24)`, the chevron :2623, the branches :2631/:2661 inside the transaction), the port gives it the same: the body's height glides on snappy(0.24) in both directions, the chevron turns on the same clock, the incoming branch's rows fade in one by one, the outgoing branch is removed at once; no opacity lies on the body or on a branch's root. Reduce Motion: not gated, as the Mac (nothing in TurnFinishedBlock reads it). (b) the turn-end swap (running block to finished block): the Mac cuts it in one frame (2-chat-use.mov 125.743 s "Weaving 37s" -> 125.762 s "Worked for 38s >" plus the answer; ThreadTimeline.swift:1907-1926 `.transition(.identity)`); the port transitions it by OD-0076: the finished block takes the running block's height (its last laid-out height) and eases to its own in 0.3 s (`Animation.Smooth(0.3)`, the size-change language), its header, body, heads and file card fade in over 0.2 s (`EaseOut(0.2)`), the prompt rows (on screen already) do not blink, and the running block's rows are gone at once, so the two are never drawn together. Reduce Motion shows the end state at once (Q-RM A, OD-0099). No exception is listed: the swap is overlap-free. MECHANISM: HeightEase / HeightFoldHost (TimelineRows.cs) lay the content out at its natural height and present the height the animation has got to, clipping only while it runs (a height reveal, not an opacity); a change made under an animation is noted before the layout pass that reads it, one made with no animation is followed at once, and one made while an ease runs continues on the same animation. The body (rule and branch) is one HeightFoldHost; the swap uses the block's own measure. Tests: TimelineRowsTurnFoldMotionTests, ThreadTimelineFoldTests (a frame-by-frame comparison with the curves; the frame-timing check on a long turn that the lead's fold entry of 2026-10-04 names is NOT added here). STOP ThreadTimeline #6 is closed; the record's windows_path and deviation (CHAT.json) are amended.

(3) PR-GIT-137, THE DELAYED CLOSE OF A REOPEN (SOURCE FACT: upstream defect 67, DiffInspector.swift:627-657; PORT_CONTRACT section 8 and ED-196: reproduce, do not fix; the lead's ruling of 2026-10-04). DiffPopoverCoordinator.CompletePopoverClose lost its stale-session early return: it always stops the monitors, clears desiredVisible and drops shownRuntime, and gates only the flag and content clear on session == pendingSession (:640-658). ENGINEERING DECISION: the mirror `isShown` of NSPopover.isShown is cleared by the newest close (session == pendingSession) and by the Popup's own Closed event when the popup really is closed, never by a stale callback, so a popup that a reopen took over is not marked closed. SAFETY CHECK (ruling step 3), measured natively: the port's diff Popup has IsLightDismissEnabled = false (Avalonia's default; there is no counterpart of NSPopover's .semitransient self-close), so the monitors are its only outside dismissal; after the Swift's stale close has stopped them the popover is NOT undismissable: its flag (the inspector's X button, the changes tab, the changes shortcut, a thread switch) closes it on a real popup, and a fresh show starts the monitors again. No minimal closer was added; nothing goes to the owner. FINDING: the usual route to the defect on the Mac and here is not a tap: a press outside the popover reaches the press monitor first and closes it (Close), so a tap on another turn's Review button is a close followed by a plain show with fresh monitors (native: Escape closes it afterwards); the stale close arises only from a Reopen while the popover is shown with no press in between (a keyboard or programmatic bump). Order-dependent test noted, not from this change: DiffPopoverCoordinatorTests.Escape_closes_the_popover_and_is_swallowed_while_other_keys_pass fails in a run with ComposerViewBlitzAreaTests alone, on the unchanged code too (a leaked global key monitor of that class).

## ED-316

[UI][TEXT] How ED-290 (1)'s line boxes are built (unit rec-linebox, 2026-10-04; records PR-MCP-199 and PR-CHAT-115; the lead numbers this heading at merge). ED-290 (1) says what the Mac draws; these items say how, and are ENGINEERING DECISIONS unless they say SOURCE FACT.

(1) THE VALUE. SwiftFont.LineBox is 18 for Body, 17 for Callout and 16 for Subheadline when the font is a text style in the default design with no family of its own, and null (the face's own box) for everything else: a fixed size (System(size:), the NSFont factories, Named), the monospaced design, the unmeasured styles (ED-290 (1)'s TODO) and SwiftFont.Default. It is an absolute line height, never natural + 2 and never a size change; the glyphs stay 13 / 12 / 11 (ED-059).

(2) HOW IT TRAVELS. Avalonia's TextBlock.LineHeight is not inherited, so the box is an inherited attached property, SwiftFont.LineBoxProperty (NaN = the face's own box). SwiftFont.Apply(TextBlock), Apply(TemplatedControl) and PlainControls.Font (the inherited `.font()`) set it with the rest of the font, so a container's `.font(.chat(.callout))` reaches its texts (the notice, TimelineRows.swift:2397) and a nearer font replaces it. A class handler makes every TextBlock (subclasses included: MorphingTextBlock, MiddleTruncatingTextBlock, SelectableTextBlock and the port's own) take the property as its LineHeight at style priority, so a LineHeight a control sets on itself still wins (SystemButtons' 16). Renderers that draw no TextBlock take the box explicitly: ParagraphTextPresenter passes its paragraph font's LineBox to TextFormatter (an NSFont has none, so prose is unchanged) and MiddleTruncatingTextBlock's wrap layout passes its LineHeight; SentenceHeightGlide's measuring probe copies the sentence's LineHeight with its font (it copied only the font, so a glide aimed at Inter's box: a regression this unit caught in AboutUpdateViewsSentenceGlideTests).

(3) WHAT KEEPS THE FACE'S BOX. A text input (Apply on a TextBox, and the plain field's prompt TextBlock) is not measured, so it is NaN under any style; the tooltip's presenter keeps its fixed 13-point line; SF Symbol images (SwiftImage) are not TextBlocks and keep their glyph-based size.

(4) THE IMPLICIT DEFAULT. SwiftFont.Default is the body size and weight with the face's own box, for every port site whose Swift Text has no `.font` above it: ChatView's commit placeholder (:1563) and ScriptsEditor root (:1660), CommandPalette's title (:122), MarkdownView's ordered-list marker (:513-515) and MCPSetupPanel's glass button labels (:83-88, :98-102). The sent bubble (TimelineRowsCaptureTests, C 102.0 = 34) is the guard and is unchanged.

(5) PORT SITES THAT HAD WRITTEN A TEXT STYLE AS A FIXED SIZE (corrected, each against its Swift line). MCPSettingsPage.Text maps 13 / 12 / 11 in the default design to body / callout / subheadline (MCPSettingsPage.swift has no fixed 11, 12 or 13; its fixed sizes are 10.5, 11.5, 14 and 34), except the glass button's own label (fixedSize). SettingsView: the About paragraph (:991-995 body), licence and version (:978, :997 callout), title (:976 title3), a ChromeRow detail set later (Chrome.swift:1068 subheadline), the zoom label (:484), the licence file titles (:1029), Made by Droppy (:1074, :1077, :1086) and CreditLink (:1115). NOT AUDITED: other helpers that take a point size; the remaining fixed 11 / 12 / 13 sites in src were checked (ModelsSettingsPage and the Providers rows are fixed in Swift, S 168.0 and S 190.0-194.0; LookCard's fonts are SPEC's own; SystemButtons and the glass buttons are control labels).

(6) LOOKCARD. LEAD RULING (2026-10-04): the LookCard's rows are Swift ChromeRows, and the Mac draws a ChromeRow 58 tall (1-settings-tour.mov S 23.5, S 194.0), so the rows are 58 and the card follows its content (245 shut, 281 open, SPEC 2.1's 237 / 273); the owner-approved board was drawn with the port's old 54-point rows, so the board's other geometry (paddings, gaps, radii, each control's position relative to its row) is kept and only the row height changes. Built: each row's control keeps the board's offset from its own row top (the segments 13, SPEC 2.3; the Classic line 15, SPEC 2.5; LookCard.SegmentsTop / LineTop), the 4 extra points fall below it, and the Signature line opens at the fold's top (19 below the Classic line, the board's 15 + 4). LookCardRenderTests crops the card at its new height and compares the board still row by row, each row read from its own top in both (mean abs 3.0-3.8 over the card, the mini window 0.3; the dots, landmarks and offsets asserted). OWNER FYI: Appearance look cards are 8 px taller (rows 58, as the Mac).

(7) UNRESOLVED, for the corner-band owner: ContinuousCornerReproofTests.REVIEW_the_four_band_elements_render_Apples_corner_at_the_largest_radius_not_the_circle_of_18 fails on this branch alone (twice) and passes on its base: the one-step steps card is now 45 pt (14 + the callout's 17 + 14) instead of 43, and at 700 x 45 the rendered corner is 64 of 255 off the reference at one edge pixel against the test's 60. A plain 380 x 45 Border cut the same way renders within 1 (probe, not committed), so the gap is the slack clip that a Border with a child takes (ED-297 (9) records 49 to 102 of 255 for it), not the line box; the 45 is what the Swift and the boxes give. Not changed here; the test is unchanged.

(8) REVIEW FIXES (2026-10-04, the reviewer's SwiftFontLineHeightReviewTests). StyledText.Render sets its host's line box from the concatenated Text's font (the tallest run's box; the face's own for a fixed size, which cuts an outer style's box off): the Hydra finished pill (TimelineRows.swift:454-455) draws in 17 and HydraNameText (HydraGlyph.swift:239-241) keeps 15.73 under a callout. LinkTextView (a link paragraph, an NSTextView with an NSFont) takes no box and its own font is the base NSFont (LinkParagraphView.swift:114), so under the .font(.system(.callout)) hosts (TimelineRows.swift:625-631, HydraHeadPopovers.swift:82-93 and :154-160, HydraReportsPopover.swift:640-647) it keeps its own line and height. The ChatDialogControls.TextEditor prompt keeps the face's box as the plain field's does. NOT CHANGED, NOTED: the markdown ordered-list marker (MarkdownView.swift:512-515, Text with .monospacedDigit().fontWeight(.medium) and no font) inherits the environment's font in Swift, so under a .font(.callout) host (the report popover) it is 12 pt in a 17 box; the port draws it SwiftFont.Default (13, plain box) everywhere, because the port has no app-wide default font for it to inherit where SwiftUI's environment has none (the timeline). Making it inherit needs that default first; the size and box differ only under a callout host.

## ED-317

[UI][SHAPES][OD-0102] The clip of a plain `.continuous` Border WITH CONTENT (unit rec-cornerclip, 2026-10-04, from unit/rec-linebox d128af285; the lead numbers it at merge). Each item is an ENGINEERING DECISION unless it says MEASURED.

(1) THE CAUSE (MEASURED, headless Skia). On unit/rec-linebox the one-step steps card is 45 pt (callout line box 17, ED-290 (1)); at 700 x 45 its corner was 64 of 255 off a SwiftShapeBorder's path fill (ContinuousCornerReproofTests.REVIEW_the_four_band_elements_..., tolerance 60). The card is a Border with a child, so ED-297 (9) cut it with the slack clip of ED-275 (3), which is not convex; Skia anti-aliases a non-convex path with its coarser walker, a convex one exactly. A childless Border of the same size takes the exact outline and is within 1. Per corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left), mounted, content transparent, against the path fill: notice two lines 380 x 50 33/29/27/53, steps card 700 x 45 64/56/22/86, Edited-files card 241 x 40 23/20/39/49, delegation card (unsent) 151 x 55 27/29/42/57; bare Borders with content 700 x 45 and 380 x 45 64/56/22/86, 380 x 50 33/29/26/53, 380 x 40 22/20/38/49, 700 x 54 15/13/24/12.

(2) THE RULE. No clip that runs past a straight side can be convex (a convex region whose boundary holds Apple's curve lies inside the tangent line at the curve's end, which is the side itself), and Border.Render is sealed, so a Border's fill cannot be cut apart from its children. `ContinuousClip` now cuts EVERY Border whose rounded corners are Apple's (`ExactClipFits`) by the exact outline, with or without content. The one exception is a Border whose site marks its content as drawn beyond its sides, `SwiftShapes.ContentBeyondSidesProperty` (`.ContentBeyondSides()`), while it has a child not clipped to its bounds: it keeps the slack clip. Marked: the effort title plate (EffortSlider.swift:589, `.buttonStyle(.plain)` draws its label unclipped, the leaving letters of EffortTitleMorphTests). A corner that is an arc keeps the slack clip as before. The band's own corner radius rule (ED-297 (8): CornerRadius 0 under this tracker's clip without a ring, else the drawn radius) is unchanged, so in the band the clip alone draws the corner. The four band elements have no ring (TimelineRows.cs: fills only), so their stroke question does not arise; a ringed plain Border keeps ED-297 (8)'s circle of the drawn radius under the same exact clip.

(3) CONSEQUENCES, taken. (a) SwiftUI's `.background(shape)` does not clip its content; an unmarked Border with content now cuts what a child draws beyond a straight side (the slack clip already cut it within the run-ins of each corner). A site whose source draws past its shape's sides must mark it; none other was found by Marrow.UI.Tests and App Views.Chat, Sidebar, Settings and Composer (below). (b) The hit shape is the clip (the compositor hit-tests Visual.Clip): inside the circle but outside Apple's curve misses, beyond a side misses, unless the Border is marked (SwiftShapesContentClipTests). (c) ED-297 (9)'s consequence now covers Borders with content: the exact outline's straight sides lie on the Border's own edge, so at a position that is not pixel aligned (a fractional transform while it moves) a straight edge pixel's coverage is the fill's times the clip's; a settled Border is aligned by layout rounding. (d) Cost: the exact clip is the same cached geometry per (size, radii, flag); a colour, a move and a child coming or going build nothing, a resize builds one (tested).

(4) AFTER (MEASURED, same reads as (1)). Mounted band elements, all four corners: notice 1/1/1/1, steps card 1/1/1/1, Edited-files card 1/1/1/1, delegation card 1/1/1/1. Bare Borders with content at 700 x 45, 380 x 45, 380 x 50, 380 x 40 and 700 x 54 (r 18): 1 at every corner against the path fill, 0 against the childless Border. The REVIEW test (top-left 8 x 8, sent cards): notice 1, steps card 1 (64 before), Edited-files card 1 (22), delegation card 54 (40): the sent delegation card's 54 is ED-314 (11)'s headless redraw of its DotFieldSweep over the capture; with the sweep removed from the same test it measures 1 (scratch run, not committed). NOT FIXED, outside this unit, stated: a plain Border in Apple's regime at the STATED radius (a tall card: 380 x 120 and 700 x 200 at r 18, 300 x 90 at r 12) keeps CornerRadius r, what the sites read and what the tests assert (164 `Assert.Equal(new CornerRadius(...), x.CornerRadius)` lines in tests, not all on such Borders; ED-275 (3)), and so fills the circle of r under the clip; against the path fill its corners measure 64/61/111/122 (r 18) and 64/66/68/64 (r 12), childless or with content alike (with content on the slack clip before: 64/64/122/138 and 71/76/76/68). Making that corner the clip's alone means a CornerRadius of 0 there too (as ED-297 (8) did for the band) and moving those test reads to StatedCornerRadius; it is the lead's call.

(5) TESTS. New: SwiftShapesContentClipTests (Marrow.UI.Tests: every corner of a Border with content against the childless Border and, in the band, the path fill, at the sizes above; the exact clip, its hit shape and its cache; only a marked Border keeps the slack) and ContinuousCornerBandCornersTests (Marrow.App.Tests: the four mounted band elements, all four corners, at most 8 of 255; the delegation card is the unsent one for the reason in (4)). Changed, none weakened: SwiftShapesBandTests.A_Border_that_cannot_draw_beyond_its_sides_... and SwiftShapesContinuousTests.A_child_that_draws_beyond_a_side_... now mark their Border (the slack is the marked case; the unmarked case is asserted exact first), and ContinuousCornerChecks.ExpectedClip follows the rule.

(6) Review fix: ChromeCard (Chrome.cs:1847) is marked .ContentBeyondSides(): the Swift card is a filled shape, not a clip (Chrome.swift:1012), and a held pinned model row draws its lift fill, shadow (radius 10, y 4) and 1.02 scale past the card's sides (ModelsSettingsPage.swift:255-262); unmarked, the head cut them flat (1263 px, worst 52/255 at scale 1). Found by the review's 44-site audit (ModelsSettingsPageLiftClipReviewTests).

## ED-318

[VOICE][ENGINEERING] Voice typing unit VT-8 (orb renderer; branch cloud/f-vt-8, built on claude/verify-terminal-20261001 at 5b26e94f; the lead numbers it at merge). ENGINEERING DECISIONS where voice-SPEC.md V-11 and voice-orbs.js are silent; none changes an owner ruling. Code: `src/Marrow.UI/Port/Voice/Orb/` (the plan's `Orb*`, as a folder; one type per file), `src/Marrow.App/Port/Voice/VoiceWarmup.cs`; tests `tests/Marrow.UI.Tests/Port/Voice/` (`Feature` VT-8, `Decision` ED-267 as the stand-in), `tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Port/Voice/VoiceWarmupTests.cs` (Decision ED-252); the fixture script `tests/fixtures/voice/ref-orbs.js`.
1. The shader (V-11.1). `OrbShaders.Source` is voice-orbs.js `FRAG` carried function by function with the same names (17 functions, `mfEdgeD` to `orbGlassLiquidAnim`, then `main`). Only mechanical changes: `vecN` to `floatN`; the std140 block member `u.name` to its place in `u[]`; `mrw` to `u[34]`; `main()` to `main(float2 coords)` returning the colour; `gl_FragCoord` (bottom-left origin) to `float2(coords.x, u[0].xy.y - coords.y)` (Skia's coords are top-left; the flip is the shader's own `1.0 - inUv.y` read the Skia way). `OrbShaderSourceTests` re-applies those changes to the design file and requires the result to be in the SkSL character for character, so the carried text cannot drift. Both presets are one program (the style member picks the branch, 9 or 19); GpuWarmup gets two entries, one per preset, each drawing that preset's own frame (the program is compiled once; the entries are the warm-up steps the Getting ready screen shows).
2. The uniform block (V-11.3 left the choice). `uniform float4 u[35]`: `u[0]` to `u[33]` are the export's 136 floats (the WGSL `Uniforms` struct, 544 bytes), `u[34]` is `mrw` (lift, desat, dark, 0). Measured on SkiaSharp 3.119.4: every uniform set copies into a new array (about 48 bytes each), so 64 named members cost 3.1 KB a frame and one array 48 B. `OrbUniformLayout.Members` names where each WGSL member sits (`Access`: `u.time` is `u[0].z`, `u.size` `u[0].xy`, `u.colorA` `u[10]`), and a test holds the table to the struct parsed from the design file and to the compiled program (`Uniforms` is exactly `["u"]`, 560 bytes).
3. Orientation and fidelity (V-11.3 "settled by the fidelity test"). The flip above was derived (GLSL's `inUv.y = 1 - fragCoord.y / size.y` with a bottom-left `fragCoord` is `coords.y / size.y` top-left) and then confirmed by running `ref-orbs.js` in headless Chrome here (WebGL2 on SwiftShader, Playwright's Chromium, 72 frames) and comparing: all 72 frames within 2/255 at 99.5 % of pixels, with the committed test (`MARROW_REF_ORBS_DIR` pointing at the local frames). Mutations: with no flip all 72 fail; with nearest instead of linear filtering all 72 fail; with no 2x below 128 px 82 tests fail. THAT RUN IS EVIDENCE ONLY: the committed reference PNGs must come from the lead's Windows run (ANGLE D3D11). Until `tests/fixtures/voice/ref-orbs/*.png` exists `OrbFidelityTests` is reported SKIPPED with "reference PNGs pending (lead's Windows run)" (a `TheoryAttribute` that sets `Skip` at discovery), never passed; with any PNG present all 72 rows run and a row whose PNG is missing fails. The folder is found from the build folder up, or from `MARROW_REF_ORBS_DIR`.
4. The matrix of V-T50 ("x {32, 26}"). Read as the slot diameter D (the ball) in the fixed 72 px view (V-11.3), at device scale 1, so the shader runs into a 144 px surface and the browser filters it down (`context: 'own'`). States are the STEADY rows of V-11.4's table (the integrators landed): Rest at t 0, 1.3, 4.0; Hover; Listening with three band sets (quiet 0.1/0.08/0.04/0.1, speech 0.5/0.6/0.35/0.5, loud 0.95/0.9/0.8/0.9; low/mid/high/all; the voice follower rests on `all`); Processing; Blocked (not hovered). Every state that is not a Rest time is rendered at t = 2.0. The motion phase is `t * speed * the preset's resting speed` (what a constant speed integrates to), set on the orb before its first frame, so the two sides agree without replaying frames. The C# side takes its targets from Core's `OrbMotion.TargetsFor`; the script has the table's numbers of its own, and `OrbReferenceScriptTests` holds the script's matrix arrays and constants to the test's. Background: the composer card colours (#1c1c1c dark, #f4f4f4 light), as the light fixtures use. The script loads voice-orbs.js as it is: only `export const orbs =` becomes `window.__orbs =` and `export default orbs;` is dropped (each anchor must occur once).
5. Rendering (V-11.3). `OrbRenderer.Draw`: below 128 device px the shader runs into ONE reused offscreen surface (made on the window's GPU context when there is one; remade only when the render size or the context changes: `SurfaceCreations`) cleared and drawn with `Src`, and drawn onto the canvas through a snapshot with linear sampling (`SKSurface.Draw` has no sampling argument and would sample nearest); from 128 px it draws straight onto the canvas. At exactly 2x a linear sample between texels is the 2 x 2 box average (a test compares it with a manual box filter of the 1x frame of twice the size, within 2/255). Opacity (the crossfade's mix times the lease opacity) modulates the paint.
6. Allocation (V-T51 says "0 B per frame"). What the port owns allocates nothing: `VoiceOrbRuntime.Frame` (VT-4) 0 B in Rest, Hover, Processing and Blocked; the uniform copy goes into one reused array. NOT MET: (a) while Listening `VoiceOrbRuntime.Frame` allocates 32 B a frame: VT-4's `OrbExportRuntime.ApplyAudioUniforms` does `foreach (var rule in AudioRules)` over an `IReadOnlyList`, which boxes an enumerator (not this unit's file; a `for` loop over an array fixes it; a test pins the 32 B so it cannot grow and must be updated when fixed); (b) SkiaSharp's own wrappers: the uniform set copies the array (48 B), the frame's shader and the surface's snapshot are managed objects: a drawn 2x frame measured 360 B/frame, asserted under 1536 B. Nothing the size of a surface, bitmap or buffer is made per frame.
7. Scene and handler. `OrbScene` holds ONE `OrbMotion` (the state is the composer's, not the preset's) and a `VoiceOrbRuntime` per orb; the handler steps and draws on the render thread (after `ComposerLightHandler`), with the scene advanced inside `OnRender` so the device ratio is the canvas matrix's. The ball is the motion's slot diameter (the slot spring, V-11.4) in the 72 px view; a changed ratio or diameter lays the orb out again (`Resize`). Crossfade (V-11.5): each orb's mix follows 1 for the chosen orb and 0 for the other with tau 0.12 s and lands within 0.004 (`OrbCrossfade`; the two mixes are complementary, so the picture never dims); an orb is drawn while its mix is above 0 and stepped only while drawn; on a change the new orb's runtime is MADE with the old one's phase (a fresh runtime, because `VoiceOrbRuntime` has no way to reset its last-frame time; its first frame adds no delta). Reduce motion lands the swap at once and stops the phase. Frames (V-11.3): a drawn orb asks for a frame after each frame; a view nobody draws (hidden) asks for none and resumes when drawn; with no GPU or under reduce motion it draws one still (`VoiceOrbHandler.AnimateWithoutGpu` lets a test turn the motion on, as for the composer light). NOT TESTED headless: a MINIMISED window: Avalonia's headless platform keeps drawing it (37 frames in ten ticks), so the "none when minimised" clause rests on the same mechanism as hidden (no `OnRender`, no request) and is for the gate on a real window.
8. Warm-up (V-11.3, GR-1). `VoiceWarmup.Register()` (idempotent; `Unregister()` for tests) adds `voice-orb-siri` and `voice-orb-membrane` under a NEW first-run step `orbs` / "Voice orbs" / order 55, between the strike (50) and the voice hardware check (60); W1 names no step for the orbs, and the Getting ready screen shows the name. Each draws one real frame through `OrbWarm.Draw` (the real renderer into a 16 px surface made by the window's GPU context). NOTHING CALLS `Register()` yet: it belongs in the app's start-up composition (VT-15 or the lead). That the program compiles on ANGLE/D3D11 (V-T54) is native, at the gate; if it fails there, V-11.3 says to split it into passes as the jewel orb was.
