8. UI-SIDEBAR-036, an interrupted glide (HeadCardsRow). The share of an earlier glide still to run, `1 - progress`, is deliberately not clamped at 0: a spring overshoots, its progress passes 1, and the glyph is then drawn past its slot by start * (1 - progress); clamping would put an interrupted glyph back at its slot in one frame. HeadCardGlideTests.A_glide_interrupted_while_the_spring_overshoots_continues_from_where_the_glyph_is_drawn cuts a glide off on a frame where panelSlide is past its end and asserts the glyph is drawn where it was (0.01 pt); it fails with the clamp.

## ED-330

[SKILLS][OPENCODE] SK-11d (WU-9, DL-11 for OpenCode). 1. WHERE IT HOOKS IN. New overload `ProviderRegistry.Environment(provider, OpenCodeSkillLaunch?)`: a null launch, or any provider other than OpenCode/OpenCode Go, returns exactly `Environment(provider)` (test: every ProviderKind, sorted key/value equal). `ThreadRuntime` (App, out of this unit's scope) still calls the one-argument method; the App wiring that passes a launch for a chat with a generation is a follow-up for whoever owns ThreadRuntime. The unit also does not start a generation itself (SK-9 owns that). 2. PATH. With a launch, `ShimPath.ForChild` (SK-6) puts `addons\bin` on PATH; without one PATH is untouched (the plan's "with nothing installed ... equal today's" is read as: no generation = no launch = today's environment; PATH insertion is DL-6's rule and applies when wiring is active). 3. ORDER OF SOURCES, as the plan lists them: global config.json, opencode.json, opencode.jsonc; OPENCODE_CONFIG (relative names against the session folder); project opencode.jsonc/opencode.json outermost folder inward (skipped when OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG is non-empty: the plan says "is set", so any non-empty value counts); `.opencode` folders; `~\.opencode`; OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR (each directory: opencode.json then opencode.jsonc); a user-exported OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT last, but only when Marrow's MCP JSON did not replace it (the Mac behaviour stays, so its paths are then not a source). 4. UNRESOLVED ORDERS FAIL CLOSED. The plan gives no order for (a) opencode.jsonc vs opencode.json in one project folder and (b) several `.opencode` folders walking up. If two such sources both set `skills.paths` with different values the bundle is left out for that session; equal values are fine. 5. LOCATIONS. opencode's `<config>` is `<XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~\.config>\opencode` and its auth file is `<XDG_DATA_HOME or ~\.local\share>\opencode\auth.json` (the plan names `~\.config\opencode` and `auth.json` but not the data folder; xdg-basedir behaviour assumed, UNRESOLVED until WU-11's live check). 6. WORKTREE. When the caller gives none, it is the nearest ancestor of the session folder holding a `.git` file or folder, else the filesystem root (UNRESOLVED against opencode's non-git case). 7. THE VARIABLE. The skills key is appended to the base JSON text by string surgery when the base has no `skills` key, so the MCP JSON (and an inherited one) stays byte-for-byte; a base that already has `skills` is re-serialised with only `paths` replaced. A base with no content at all becomes `{"skills":{"paths":[...]}}`; no `$schema` is added. 8. UNREADABLE = LEFT OUT. A source that exists but cannot be read or parsed, a non-object root, a malformed `skills`/`paths`, a non-string entry, `{env:`/`{file:` in an entry, a corrupt auth.json, or a legacy TOML `<config>\config` leaves the bundle out and the variable as today; exception messages are fixed text and never carry a path value or file content. 9. AUTH. `OpenCodeAuthReader` is a static Utf8JsonReader pass that compares only each top-level entry's `type` string to `wellknown`, skips every other value, and zeroes its read buffer; no field. 10. NOT DONE HERE: DL-12 taps and DL-14 are not in the SK-11d row of BUILD-PLAN 2.5 (the row says only WU-9), so no ACP event adapter was written; no fixture transcripts were needed. The test run was on Linux with .NET 10.0.112 from apt and `-p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true`; 67 other ProviderRegistry/MCP/Skills tests fail on Linux for reasons that predate this unit (stand-in CLI sources found by Windows paths, a Windows cmd.exe test).

## ED-331

[VOICE][ENGINEERING] VT-5 Capture (Windows): voice-SPEC section 4, V-2.2 items 1 and 2, V-4.5, OD-0099 Q-V-19 B. SOURCE FACT: voice typing is an owner-ruled addition with no Swift twin (OD-0091); the rows below are the unit's own choices where the spec is silent, each one place in the code. (1) The endpoint seam. `IAudioCapture` (VT-3) takes no device id and is unchanged. The Windows endpoints sit behind a new Services seam `ICaptureHost` (list the active capture endpoints, the default id, `Open(id or null)` in the device's own mix format, `Watch` for changes), with `ICaptureDevice` for one open stream. Production is `NAudioCaptureHost` and `NAudioCaptureDevice` (NAudio 3.1.0: `MMDeviceEnumerator`, `WasapiRecorderBuilder` with `WithSharedMode().WithEventSync().WithMmcssThreadPriority("Audio")` and no `WithFormat`, which NAudio documents as "uses the device's mix format"; `MMDeviceNotificationClient` for IMMNotificationClient). The ambient is `CaptureSeams.Host` (a Services type, like `HardwareProbeSeams`, so not in Core's `VoiceSeams.All`); its default `FailClosedCaptureHost` throws `SeamNotBoundException` on every member; the double is `ScriptedCaptureHost` with `ScriptedCaptureDevice` (the Microphone row's "scripted enumerator"; VT-13 binds it). Listing, watching and resolving open nothing; only `Open` does. (2) The Microphone pick. `MicrophoneChoices.Items(host)` is `Windows default` first (value null, label `VoiceTypingSettings.WindowsDefaultMicrophone`), then the active endpoints in the system's order; `Resolve(host, mic)` maps a stored `mic` (absent, empty or the literal "Windows default" is the default; an id is matched ignoring case and returned in the system's spelling; an id that is not an active endpoint falls back to the default with `FellBack` true). `WasapiCapture` reads the pick at each Start through a `Func<string?>` (VT-14 passes the settings), and when the pick was listed but `Open` says NotFound (unplugged between the two calls) it opens the default; InUse or any other failure is not retried on another device, it throws, and the session shows its capture-failed note (V-4.4). A missing default is NotFound and throws the same way. (3) Device events. A capture on a chosen endpoint is not ended by the Windows default changing; a capture following the default is (V-4.4), unless the new default is the device already open. Removal of the open endpoint is `DeviceRemoved`; a mix-format change of it (`PKEY_AudioEngine_DeviceFormat`) is `FormatChanged`; the stream stopping by itself is `InUse` (AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_IN_USE, `AudioDeviceInUseException`) or otherwise `DeviceRemoved`; closing the device ourselves raises nothing. The same loss noticed twice (the notice and the stream's end) is one event per kind. (4) The pipeline. `CapturePipeline` is the capture thread's callback (`OnBuffer`: convert to float into a preallocated scratch, write to a `SampleRing` of 2 s at the device's rate and channels; no allocation, no lock, measured 0 B per call for all four encodings), the processing step (`Pump`, run by one dedicated background thread every 10 ms, or by hand when built with `runThread: false`) and the delivery. Conversion to float is done on the capture thread, not the processing thread as V-4.2 words it: it is a few multiplications per sample, allocation-free, and it keeps the ring in float as V-2.2 item 1 says. The processing thread does not downmix, resample or run the VAD: VT-3 put those in `VoiceSession.OnAudio` on the main executor (the contract of `IAudioCaptureSink`), so the pipeline only moves interleaved float in the device's format; each Pump posts at most one delivery to `MainActor`, with the audio in one batch per Pump (rented from the shared pool and zeroed when returned, V-4.7). A device event is ordered after the audio written before it (the ring position at the time it was raised), so the final pass in V-4.4 runs on everything captured. A full ring refuses the whole write and counts it in `DroppedSamples`; a trailing partial frame is dropped. A step that throws on the processing thread is swallowed (a lost batch) so the thread never takes the app down. (5) Stopping. `WasapiCapture.Stop()` (main thread) stops the device, unsubscribes, then `Flush()`es: the ring and every undelivered batch and event reach the sink synchronously before Stop returns, because VT-3's `VoiceSession.Stop` calls `StopCapture()` and then `FlushPending()` while still Listening, and audio posted later would be ignored (V-7.6 "the last 30 ms flushed"). Stop from inside a delivered device event (the session does that) is safe: the queue is drained item by item. Dispose discards what is undelivered. (6) The all-zero check (V-4.5, V-T41) is VT-3's (`VoiceSession.Ingest`: the first 1.0 s of exact 0.0 means Blocked); VT-5 delivers faithfully and turns WASAPI's `AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT` into zeros whatever the bytes hold, and V-T41 runs the real session over the production capture to prove both. (7) `MicrophoneAccess` (App, `IMicrophoneAccess`) reads Windows' answer through `IMicrophonePrivacySource` (production `WinRtMicrophonePrivacySource`: `DeviceAccessInformation.CreateFromDeviceClass(DeviceClass.AudioCapture).CurrentStatus`, which opens no device and shows no prompt). No active capture endpoint is `NoDevice` and is checked first, so the note names the real problem; DeniedByUser and DeniedBySystem are `Denied`; Allowed and Unspecified are `Allowed` (a desktop app has no declared capability, so Windows can say Unspecified, and a block that says nothing is what the all-zero second catches); a reader that throws means Unspecified; an endpoint list that throws means `NoDevice`, but `SeamNotBoundException` is not swallowed. (8) Accepted formats (V-4.2): float32 and PCM of a 16, 24 or 32 bit container at any positive rate and 1 to 8 channels; `NAudioFormats.TryMap` uses the container size, not the valid bits (24 valid bits in a 32-bit container is PCM32, left-justified, scaled by 2^31); anything else makes `Open` throw `CaptureDeviceException(Other)`. (9) Tests. V-T40 is the 64-case matrix (4 encodings x 48000 / 44100 x 1 to 8 channels) through `WasapiCapture`: every channel carries the tone at its own gain so a swapped or merged channel shows, then the session's downmix and the real `PolyphaseResampler` give a 16 kHz mono tone of the expected amplitude (Goertzel within 3 %), plus the allocation probe. V-T41 and V-T42 run the real `VoiceSession`. The microphone is always the scripted host; the three native tests (`CaptureNativeEnumerationTests`, `MicrophoneAccessNativeTests`) only list endpoints, watch and ask for an id that does not exist, and read the WinRT privacy value: none opens a stream. (10) Not done here: nothing constructs `WasapiCapture`, `MicrophoneAccess` or `NAudioCaptureHost` in the app yet (the start-up composition is VT-14's, with the Microphone row of VT-13); real capture on the owner's microphone, a real Windows privacy denial, a real unplug, and the real 100 ms WASAPI buffer cadence are for the supervised native session (a test never opens a real device).

Review follow-up (VT-5, Sonnet review MERGE with two non-blocking items). (11) `WasapiCapture`'s close order is now: stop the device, dispose it (NAudio joins the capture thread, so its last buffer is in the ring), then flush the ring into the sink, then dispose the pipeline (which clears the ring); `NAudioCaptureDevice.Dispose` disposes the recorder before it removes its handlers, for the same reason. Tests: a scripted device delivers a buffer during Stop and another while it is disposed, and both reach the sink. (12) `NAudioFailures.Wrap` turns `AudioDeviceInUseException`, COM errors and anything else from opening or `StartRecording` into a `CaptureDeviceException` of its kind (a `CaptureDeviceException` passes through); `WasapiCapture.Start` already closes the device and unsubscribes when the device's start throws (tested with a scripted device that throws). (13) V-T40 is also run through the real session (`CaptureSessionDownmixTests`, 64 cases): the audio handed to the engine in the final pass is measured, so the session's own downmix weight is tested; with `sum / (channels + 1)` in `VoiceSession.Ingest` 56 of the 64 fail (the 8 with one channel have no sum) while `CaptureFormatMatrixTests` stays green, which is why it is not enough alone. (14) The allocation probe waits for the runtime's tiered-JIT bookkeeping to settle (three consecutive 100-call rounds of 0 B within ten seconds) instead of fixed rounds, because a promotion landed in a measured round once.

MEASURED through the real OLE drop target of the real main HWND (RootViewDropNativeTests, a managed IDataObject holding CF_HDROP called through the IDropTarget Avalonia registered with RegisterDragDrop, window property OleDropTargetInterface): a Drop that sets no effect reports to the drag source the effects it offered (7, copy | move | link), and one that sets Copy reports 1. ## ED-334

(1) [TEST][MARKDOWN] A SEAM TO SEE WHERE AND WHEN A REPORT'S MARKDOWN IS PARSED (PR-CHAT-145; TimelineRows.swift:317-324, :1030-1033; MarkdownView.swift:135-148, :204-255). PORT-ONLY, no Swift twin. The record says the markdown is parsed off the main thread as the pill appears, once per head for a batch; the earlier tests proved only that the parse cache holds the text afterwards, and the native test only that a warmed heads report's tap frame stays within one frame of an empty popover's. `MarkdownView.ParseObserver` (an `Ambient<Action<string>>`, ED-065, default a no-op) is told each text the parser is asked to parse for the block cache, on the thread that parses it: parseWarm's worker (read from the caller's flow in `ParseWarm(texts)` and told from inside `Task.Run`, so a test's override reaches the worker) and the cold parse inside `Blocks(for:)`. Streaming parses are not reported (not this record). Nothing in production acts on it. Fixtures/MarkdownParseLog records the parses with their thread ids and can park a worker parse until released (never the UI thread), so a test decides what has happened before a warm lands.

(2) [PARITY][CHAT] THE PRODUCTION CODE ALREADY DID WHAT THE SWIFT DOES; NO PRODUCT CHANGE. Read against TimelineRows.swift:317-324 and :1030-1033 and MarkdownView.swift:204-255: the pill's `.task(id: body)` (the port's `ViewLifetime.Task`, started on attach, cancelled on detach, restarted when the body changes) returns for a pill with no details, warms [body] for a note and `HydraReportDigest.Parse(body).Heads.Select(Body)` for a batch (that parse is on the main actor in the Swift too), and `MarkdownView.Warm` skips what the cache holds, dedupes by text, keeps the four limits (96 candidates, 262144 bytes a text, 1048576 bytes, 24 texts) and parses the missing texts in one `Task.Run`. The tests (TimelineRowsReportWarmTests, Req PR-CHAT-145) prove, through the seam: a note and each head of a batch are parsed on a worker thread that is not the UI thread, and the UI thread parses none of them; nothing is parsed before the pill is on the screen; a batch is parsed head by head in reading order and never as one text; a body two heads share, a pill that leaves the screen and returns, and a second pill of the same report are parsed once in all; a pill with only an address parses nothing; the merge pill (windows_path) warms the same way; the tap on a warmed pill (a note, and a batch) parses nothing on any thread; a tap before the warm has landed parses on the UI thread (:598-601 'a cold tap parses now'), and the warm that lands afterwards adds no second UI parse. The same is proved on a real window by TimelineRowsNativeReportTests (the second test, real click on the real pills): every head and the note parsed once, none on the UI thread, none again at the tap.

(3) [PARITY][CHAT] THE POPOVER IS NOT MADE LAZY (the lead's 'lazy HydraReportPopover'). The Swift gives two statements: the doc comment at :593-596 says the blocks 'are built lazily, so opening costs the blocks on screen', and the code at :619-639 builds every block at once in a plain VStack, with the comment at :621-622: 'Every block at once: the body is laid out whole to size the panel before it opens, and a lazy stack measured differently once shown (see PopoverScroll)'. The code and its own reason win over the doc comment: PopoverScroll sizes the panel from the whole body, which a lazily built body would not give (the port's `PopoverScroll` does the same, and PR-CHAT-146 pins that it opens at its final height). What IS lazy in the Swift, and in the port, is the popover itself: `.popover(isPresented:)` calls its content closure at the tap, and the port's `BadgePopover(detail)` calls the factory only when shown; its initializer then reads `MarkdownView.blocks(for:)` (:612-617), the cache the pill's warm filled. The test The_popover_is_not_built_before_the_tap_and_a_tap_before_the_warm_has_landed_parses_now_on_the_UI_thread proves that. ED-314 (13) stays as measured: a 30000-character note's tap costs its per-block control construction (270 to 360 ms), which SwiftUI does not pay for value-type views; making that cheap in the port would need the blocks built after the panel is sized, which is a deviation from :621-622 and is not made here. It is an owner decision if a smooth first tap of a very long note is wanted more than a panel that opens at its final size.

(4) [TEST][COMPOSER] WHAT 'COULD NOT BE TESTED AS WRITTEN' WAS IN PR-COMPOSER-211, AND WHAT TESTS IT NOW. The record's verification_method is 'capture comparison of an expanded image-reading tool row and of an expanded command row whose text names a written screenshot, each while loading and after the image lands, plus an interaction test of Open'. Two things in it were not met by the rec-tlr unit's tests (commits 06259ffd8, 85f692c94): (a) the capture comparison cannot be made against the Mac: no frame in the reference videos shows a tool row with a picture in it (CATALOG.md names tool rows only as text rows, e.g. :80, :150), so by OD-0098 the Swift is the proof, and the earlier tests (TimelineRowsBlitzAbHeadTests.An_expanded_row_that_names_an_image_shows_a_spinner_..., ContinuousCornerReproofTests, TimelineRowsFinToolDetailTests) mount both rows, read the spinner, the fitted picture, the plate and the caption from the mounted controls and pixels in both themes; (b) the interaction test of Open pressed a button on a row whose picture was an empty file named .png, which never loads, and the test that loaded a real picture never pressed Open (its `opened` list was never read). TimelineRowsToolImageOpenTests.Open_pressed_on_a_row_whose_real_picture_has_landed_opens_that_file_and_the_plate_around_the_picture_is_measured does both at once on real PNG files written by the TestPng fixture (wide 300 x 150, square 200 x 200, tall 100 x 400; a read for two and a command that wrote the screenshot for the third): the plate is measured as wide as the row (480) and 240, 420 and 420 tall, the picture is aspect-fitted (480 x 240, 420 x 420, 105 x 420) and centred in it, the spinner is gone, the name sits 6 points below at the leading edge and Open ends at the trailing edge; Open is pressed with a real click and hands ShellWorkspace.OpenWithDefaultApp the path of that very file, which `ShellWorkspace.ShouldAttemptShellExecute` accepts, so the real opener would launch it. Still UNVERIFIED and not a test gap: the record's windows_path states visual size parity of the caption row (10 point Inter) stays UNVERIFIED under OD-0001. Nothing in the record needs the owner.

4. The layers, in the stylesheet's order (filter, then clip, then mask, then opacity; z 1 the inner light and its warp mirror, z 2 the stroke ring, z 3 the bloom and its mirror, z 4 the band and the epicentre), inside the composer's rounded shape (corner 22). Three SkSL programs: the seven lobes as seven `radial-gradient(ellipse ...)` with the first on top and premultiplied stops; one ellipse gradient of up to four stops (the wash, the epicentre and every mask); and the layer program (a layer's picture through its mask: the `ie()` ellipse, for the inner light the union of the two edge gradients, `mask-composite: intersect, add`, and the warp's displacement). The soft layers (inner, bloom, epicentre) are rastered at half size in ONE reused surface (the stylesheet's `data-voice-halfres`, `--vb-z` 0.5: every length rides the layer factor, a box-shadow's 1 px spread and the displacement do not) and scaled back up with linear filtering; the 1 px stroke ring and the band stay full size. The bloom is the lobes clipped to the layer's own rounded box (radius P) and then blurred (CSS blur(r): sigma r, decal edges), the inner light's inset shadow a blurred rounded-rect difference (sigma = blur / 2), hue-rotate, brightness and saturate three Skia colour filters composed in the stylesheet's order (each clamps, as a CSS filter chain does). Where the band line splits the base layers (distortion on and not processing) the base is clipped to the area above the line and the warp mirror to the area below, both antialiased polygons (`yn`); the epicentre is clipped below the line before its blur.
5. The displacement (V-13.2: "the SVG displacement replaced by an equivalent noise-offset in the same shader"). feTurbulence (fractalNoise, baseFrequency (0.012 x detail, 0.05 x detail) to 4 digits, 2 octaves, seed 7), feOffset (the driver's dx, dy), feColorMatrix (R kept, G 0.5, B 0, A 1) and feDisplacementMap (R, G) become: Skia's own Perlin fractal noise (the shader browsers use for feTurbulence) read as a child shader in the layer program, the picture sampled at x + scale x (R / A - 0.5) (the green channel is 0.5, so there is no vertical shift). One difference: Skia's displacement filter takes the nearest pixel, this samples linearly. The filter-region cropping `Mn` (an optimisation of the page) is not carried: the rows it cuts are under the band-line clip anyway.
6. The band canvas `Sn` has two ways to be drawn (`VoiceGlowBandMode`). Strokes: as the canvas does, seventeen strokes of the 57-point polyline (a halo, then four widths in each of four colours at four offsets), each with its gradient `I()` and its own blur: exact, but 2.0 ms a frame on the GPU (seventeen layers) and the reference for the CPU. Analytic (one pass, what Auto picks when the canvas has a GPU context): for each pixel the distance to the polyline at each of the four offsets (the polyline is a function of x at an even step, so only segments near the pixel's x count), each stroke's coverage after its blur as a Gaussian edge on each side of its line width (Phi((w/2 - d)/s) - Phi((-w/2 - d)/s), Phi as the logistic form of the normal CDF, error under 2e-4), composited in the canvas's order in floating point; exact for a straight line and good where the line bends slowly against the blur. It is the closer to the browser on the frames (item 2), costs 0.12 ms on the GPU (native, RTX 4080) and 330 ms on the CPU raster (which is why Auto strokes there: the glow is a still without a GPU, item 10). Tests: `VoiceGlowBandTests` (the Gaussian edge of a straight stroke against an independent erf oracle, the fade at both ends, the offsets, the compositing order, the two modes against each other in three states) and a second fidelity theory for the analytic mode over all 28 frames. The shader writes the band at the polyline's x, round caps are the distance clamp; the canvas's `ctx.filter` blur lengths are in bitmap pixels, so the port uses the CSS-pixel value `3.5 x bandWidth / 2` (and three times that for the halo) whatever the device scale.

## ED-337

CZ-4 "Page and light sections (C1)", branch `unit/f-cz-4` (from `unit/f-cz-3` 0af1f96fa), 2026-10-05. Scope: BUILD-PLAN CZ-4; customization-SPEC CZ-2.2, CZ-3.2, CZ-3.3, CZ-4.6, CZ-5, CZ-6, CZ-7, CZ-8, CZ-12.1 to CZ-12.9 as used, CZ-13.1, CZ-13.2, CZ-13.5 (the page's side), CZ-14.1, CZ-15, CZ-16; tests CZ-T5, T10 to T24, T26, T39, T40, T41, T44 (and T11, T14, T17 to T19 for their texts). OD-0085, OD-0089 (and its amendment), OD-0095 (Q-CZ-5), OD-0099 (Q-CZ-3 B, Q-RM A), OD-0076.

1. **What was built.** In `src\Marrow.App\Port\Settings\`: `CustomizationSettingsPage` (IsReady is now true; the chrome row's Preview state control, `CustomizationStage` mounted, the Style cards, the three styles' sections), `BeamSections` (Look, Pace and strength, the Advanced card, Reset), `AuraSections` (Look with the two Custom wells, Motion, Brightness by moment, Advanced, Reset), `CzWellPicker` (the glass picker of CZ-2 in a tipped popover below the open well), and the page's parts: `CzRow` (the port's ChromeRow metrics, a crossfading detail, a dimmed state), `CzRowSlot` / `CzRowStack` (a row in a fold with its divider; the divider rule), `CzSection`, `CzCaptionRow`, `CzNoteRow`, `CzSliderRow`, `CzToggleRow`, `CzSegmentRow`, `CzLightEditor` (reads and edits `AppSettings.ComposerLight`), `CzAdvancedState`. In Core: `CzRowText` (every setting-dependent detail, the value formats `x2 deg s px pc`, the Colour drift format, the dimmed rules, the "is it the default" tests). Every row reads and edits the app's composer light, so a change reaches every composer at once (CZ-13.1); the page follows the settings live through one tracked read (`Apply`).

2. **The expected texts come from the locked cz.js.** `tests/fixtures/customization/page.generate.cjs` runs the real `beamRows()`, `auraRows()`, `resetRow()` and `sections()` of cz.js (the rendering seams stubbed, as generate.cjs does) over 28 Border beam and 17 Uiverse cases and writes `page.json` (rows: title, detail, formatted value, dimmed, folded; and each style's outline of sections, rows, folds and dividers). The tests put every case into the app's settings and read the page's rows; the section outline is compared with the design's line by line (`PageOutline`). The Voice orb and Working dots sections of the design's outline are left out of the fixture (CZ-5, CZ-7).

3. **ENGINEERING DECISION: the page's top inset.** CZ-3's pinned block carries the 60 above its heading (its 372), and `SettingsView` gives a page with chrome controls 60 above its content, so the page takes one back with a margin of -60 (a test holds the heading at 60 below the sheet's edge in a real `SettingsView`). CZ-6 needs the block at the top of the scroll content to pin it.

4. **ENGINEERING DECISION: hooks for the next units.** The page keeps two containers: `Sticky` (the pinned block, Style, the style sections; CZ-5 and CZ-7 add the Voice orb and Working dots sections at its end, CZ-6 makes it sticky) and `Rest` (after the point where the block lets go: the Speech section, CZ-11). Touching Working dots calls `PreviewSession.WorkingDotsTouched()` (CZ-3), which moves the chrome control to Running a turn (tested).

5. **ENGINEERING DECISION: rows, folds and dimming.** A row is the port's `ChromeRow` geometry (padding 16 / 11 / 10 / 11, Body title, Subheadline detail in its 16 point line) with the detail a `CzCrossfadeText` (CZ-12.9); a dimmed row fades its text to 0.5 over 0.3 s and its control goes inert and unfocusable through the control's own Dimmed (so a slider is not dimmed twice). Sections and rows fold with `CzFoldRow` (0.34 s ease, fade 0.24 s after 0.08 s opening, 0.14 s shutting); a section keeps its 20 below inside the fold, so a folded section leaves no gap. The dividers follow the design's rule (none above the first shown row, none around a caption, none after a shown caption) and fade 0.3 s; a row put in place starts with the divider the rule gives it, and the Reset buttons start at their idle look, so building the page fades nothing in.

6. **ENGINEERING DECISION: programmatic display in CZ-1's controls.** `CzRadioGroup.Show(id)` and `CzColorWell.Display(hex)` show a pick/colour that a setting changed (also while the control is folded shut or dimmed, where `Select` and `SetColor` refuse); `CzCapsuleButton.SetAtDefaults(…, animate: false)` places the first look. Without them a Uiverse Reset (which folds the Custom wells shut as it returns their colours) left the wells stale.

12. **T40 and T41.** `FrameCurves` solves the CSS cubic-bezier itself and holds each sampled transition (60 Hz frames after the action, on the manual frame clock) to its curve within 0.02 of the travel, monotonic, never stepping further in a frame than the curve itself (and not more than 15 % of the travel where the curve can keep to that): the dimmed row 0.3 s ease; the detail crossfade; a section's fold and fade; the Advanced chevron 0.3 s ez and nest fold; Reset's idle 0.25 s; and CZ-3's preview rows: the chip's width 0.3 s ez, name crossfade, dot 0.35 s; the typing placeholder 0.15 s / 0.12 s and back 0.25 s; the ring arc 0.6 s; the dots 0.4 s ease-in-out; the ring's spin against its analytic eased integral (330 degrees a second, time constant 0.35 s). Reduce motion: each lands at once and nothing waits for a frame. ENGINEERING DECISION: the working dots' 0.4 s fade is the Mac's own un-gated `.transition` (ComposerView.swift:672), so Reduce Motion leaves it (OD-0099 Q-RM A); the test says so. CZ-T40's rows owned by CZ-1's controls (segmented pill, slider knob, Auto capsule, swatch ring, style card fill) are CZ-1's tests and are not repeated.

Now `CzStyleGlyph` takes its operation back from Avalonia (the pattern of `JewelKnobOperation`) and `CzStyleGlyphPainter` keeps its paint, path and clip, shares the two sweep shaders and two blurs, and turns the CANVAS (the sweep is made once at the origin; the geometry is put in turned back through a kept path) instead of making a shader with a matrix. The light itself draws on the composition thread, its renderer bound stays ED-251's.

## ED-338

**Window corners: the glass is extended to the window's rectangle, so the corner outside the 26 pt curve is the body beside it (main window, Settings, the two guide panels, the tour card).**

1. **Rule.** OD-0075 (owner, 2026-10-02, on the choices canvas): "Window corner: the wedge is filled with the window's scrim." The owner's intent, 2026-10-05: Windows rounds window corners less than the app's 26 pt glass shape, so the glass must be EXTENDED to the window's edge; it should read as one glass surface out to the OS edge.
2. **What caused the seam (SOURCE FACT of the port, measured on a real window).** A window of this app is the system's Acrylic in a rectangle that DWM rounds by 8 px; its content clipped everything to the source's 26 pt continuous shape (RootView.swift:66, SettingsView.swift:119-120, MCPKeyPanel.swift:57, MCPSetupPanel.swift:130), and OD-0075's first build painted a fifth layer, `WindowCornerWedge`, in the wedge between them: the scrim alone. The body inside the curve wears more than the scrim: the legibility tint (`Chrome.glassTint` at 0.12, WindowBackdrop :263-265) and, over the detail column, the detail sheet's wash and tint (`DetailSheetModifier`, Chrome.swift:195-196; `Chrome.SheetInset` is 0, so the sheet reaches the window's edge). So a band followed the curve, lighter or darker with the theme, and the glass seemed to stop before the window's edge. Measured over a (240,200,40) backdrop at the default glass (0.5), the wedge pixel against the body pixel in its column just inside the shape: main window dark (178,148,30) against (105,89,27), light (220,190,71) against (244,227,161) (an earlier capture read (243,210,78) against (249,232,165): the Acrylic itself differs with the window's active state); Settings window over blurred black and white stripes dark 62 against 67 at the top left and 64 against 47 at the top right, light 108 against 128 and 112 against 182; the guide panels headless over grey 128 dark 95 against 89, light 151 against 161. The tour window had no wedge layer at all: its square Acrylic window showed unscrimmed blur outside the 20 pt card, (234,195,39) over the backdrop's (240,200,40), and beside the card's own colour (bottom corners over stripes, dark 80 against 36, light 83 against 243).
3. **Decision (ENGINEERING DECISION).** Not a second, look-alike paint but the body's own layers, extended: every layer of `WindowBackdrop` that fills (the scrim, the solid fill, the tint, the wallpaper and its glass material) fills the backdrop's RECTANGLE, and each window clips its composition with its own rectangle, which DWM then rounds. `RootView.windowClip` and `SettingsView.frame` have no corner radius (their `ClipToBounds` stays); `MCPSetupPanel`'s clip likewise; `TourView`'s scrim, glass and clip are the window's rectangle. The detail sheet, its veils and whatever else the body has reach the corner too, so the corner is the body by construction and the wedge cannot drift from it. `WindowCornerWedge` (UI/Chrome), `RootView.CornerWedge`, `SettingsView.RiseWedge` and `FloatingGuidePanelView`'s own wedge painting are removed; nothing else drew the corner. The Rise open (OD-0074) fades the corners with the glass because the backdrop is the glass; the appearance turnover (OD-0088, ED-254) eases them with the scrim for the same reason.
4. **The hairline.** The source's inner hairline (WindowBackdrop :266-271, the tour's `strokeBorder`) is the glass's edge. At 26 pt it ran as an arc a few pixels inside the window's own edge through the extended glass, which read as a second edge and the glass again stopping before the OS edge (seen on real pixels). So it is the rectangle's inner stroke too: along the straight edges it is where it always was (the outermost pixel), and DWM's rounding cuts it at the corner, where the OS's own border continues the line. The task allowed keeping the 26 pt curve for a hairline; this keeps nothing at 26 pt, and it is a one-line change in `WindowBackdrop` (`Shape()` back for `Fill()` on the hairline) if the owner wants the arc back.
5. **What the 26 pt clip no longer does.** Content in the corner is cut by DWM's 8 px rounding instead of the 26 pt shape. Nothing the windows draw sits in that corner (the sidebar rows, the chrome row and the chat's composer are inset; the veils and the sheet are the glass itself). RootViewTests, WindowManagerSettingsSurfaceTests (ED-181's Settings frame geometry), SettingsViewTests, MCPSetupPanelUiTests, ChromeThirdTests, ChromeFourthTests and the tour tests that pinned the 26 pt and 20 pt clips now pin the rectangle; ED-181's continuous geometry is untouched for every other shape. Census (ContinuousCornerSitesTests): the raw `CornerRadius` sites of MCPKeyPanel (1), MCPSetupPanel (1) and TourView (4 sites, the scrim, the glass fill, the clip and the hairline) are gone; no raw site was added.
6. **Tour (decision).** The tour's Swift draws WINDOW-shaped glass: `TourWindowController.swift:60-90` makes a clear borderless window the size of the card, and `TourView.swift:62-96` takes one 20 pt continuous shape for the glass, the tint, the clip, the hairline and the scrim, so on the Mac the card IS the window and the corner outside the shape is clear. The port's window is a rectangle of Acrylic, so the tour is the same case as the main window and is filled the same way (item 3). The card's material (an app-drawn glass over the scrim) shades a strip about 10 px wide along each edge and lights a rim about 3 px along the bottom; those are the glass's edge and now run along the window's edge, so the tour's test compares a wedge pixel with the pixel in its column deep in the card, clear of that rim and of the line where the strip and the rim meet. The top corners are the page's artwork (a picture that differs from row to row) and are not compared; the artwork now reaches the window's edge too.
7. **Proof.** The wedge pixel is the colour of the body pixel in its column just inside the shape, within 3 of 255 on each channel (`CornerSeam`, tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Fixtures): headless in RootViewCornerWedgeTests (both themes over grey and stripes, and at 0.25, 0.75 and solid), WindowManagerCornerWedgeTests (Settings, including the 0.32 s turnover), FloatingGuidePanelCornerTests (both guide panels) and TourWindowCornerTests; and on real screen pixels in MainWindowCornerWedgeNativeTests and GlassWindowNativeTests (Settings and the tour), over a solid backdrop, stripes and bands of four colours, in both themes. Each was shown red on the seam first (commit "Corner seam tests, red on the seam"). After: the main window's wedge and body read the same pixel at all four corners in both themes ((104,88,25) both, dark; (249,232,165) both, light; a gap of 0 on every pair, also over the bands), Settings at most 3, the tour 0.
8. **UNRESOLVED / not done here.** (a) The pane's top veil (`PaneTopVeil`, Chrome.swift:579-628) is part of the body and now reaches the corner too, so a scrolled page's top corners are the veil's colour like the rest of the top edge; not separately measured. (b) The Mac-corner comparison (the 26 pt cut-away) is not a goal here: the owner's intent is the opposite. (c) Windows 10 and a maximized window have square corners: the glass is square there too, which is the OS's shape. (d) Sheets inside a window that clip a `WindowBackdrop` to their own rounded Border (the scripts editor, `WindowSheetLayer`, ED-333) keep their 26 pt shape: their Border clips the rectangular layers, and the backdrop's `roundedHairline` option gives them the source's hairline on the curve (a review finding of the first version, whose hairline stopped where the curve began).

## ED-339

[SKILLS][TERMS][UNINSTALL][HOST][TEST] SK-13 (`unit/f-sk-13` from `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` bb48c8012), 2026-10-05. BUILD-PLAN row SK-13, skills-ONDEMAND-PLAN DL-15 and DL-16 with 2.5, 3.5, 3.8 and 7, skills-PLAN 2.1, 3.1 (footer) and WU-18, the OD-0099 skills amendments (the vendors' proprietary sets are offered, each under its source's terms with its licence kept beside it), ED-321 (1) and (7), ED-325, ED-326 (1) and (6). The lead numbers this at merge. Nothing here ran an installer, an uninstaller, Velopack or a packaging step; every test uses a fresh folder under MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR, no network and no CLI.
1. **Terms step (DL-15), `Marrow.Services.Port.Skills.Terms`.** `TermsStep(catalogue, state, accept, licenceText, clock)`: `Offer(id)` is null for an open item or an accepted licence hash, otherwise a `TermsOffer` (row label, licence name and link, the catalogue's licence hash, the words of the separate control); `LicenceTextAsync(id)`; `Accept(id, readControlChecked)`. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: (a) the row label is one pattern over the catalogue's vendor field, `Under <vendor>'s terms`, so the two strings the plan prints ("Under Anthropic's terms", "Under OpenAI's terms") are exact and no vendor is special-cased. (b) The plan wants the licence text shown BEFORE any byte of the item is fetched, so the text comes from the item's own pinned licence file through the `ILicenceText` seam (unbound it fails closed; tests script it) and is checked against the catalogue's size and SHA-256 and decoded as strict UTF-8 before it is returned; what the user reads is the file whose hash is stored. No other file of the item is requested until the terms are accepted. (c) `Accept` is refused, storing nothing, unless the read control was used, the item owes terms and the catalogue holds the licence hash (`TermsOffer.CanAccept`). Today every catalogue item is Unpinned (no licence hash), so the owed terms of A2, A6, O5 and O6 are real and cannot be accepted until SK-2's pin run fills them: fail closed (ED-295). (d) The acceptance is stored by the pipeline's `AcceptTerms` (state.json: date, item and licence hash, SK-7), so there is one record; a changed licence file has a new hash and asks again, also after a restart. (e) `TermsGate.Guard(state, download)` wraps the download seam: when `ItemTerms.Required` holds the inner seam is never called and `PipelineTermsRequiredException` is thrown, so no byte is requested. `SkillsHost.GuardedDownloads` is this guarded seam; the pipeline's update and repair use it, and a first install must go through it.
2. **Words (`Marrow.Core.Port.Skills.Terms.SkillsNotices`).** `Footer` is the skills-PLAN 3.1 not-affiliated line word for word, `ReadControl` is "I have read these terms", `UnderTerms(vendor)`. The Skills and Plugins pages are still hidden shells (SA-1's `IsReady` false), so nothing draws them yet: SK-15 must use these constants. NoVendorImageTests is the text test: no image extension, icon or logo field, `avares://` or bitmap type in the skills sources of Core, Services and App, the two page shells and the embedded catalogue (comments excluded from the source scan), and no image among the assemblies' skills resources.
3. **Uninstall hook (DL-16), `SkillsUninstall.BeforeUninstall(dataRoot, ...)`.** It unlocks everything under `addons\` and `skills\` entry by entry (the deny entry and read-only flags; one entry that will not unlock does not stop the rest), and only then deletes `addons\` whole and every child of `skills\` except `enabled.json`. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: (a) the budget is 20 s, so the hook ends well inside Velopack's 30 s; after it no new delete starts and everything is already unlocked; the plan's 10 s on a fake root is asserted on the real NTFS deny entry with 7 locked folders, about 1,050 files and one file held open. (b) A delete that fails (a held handle) falls back to the folder's children one by one, so a held file costs only its own ancestors; the report (`UninstallReport`) lists the deepest paths left and whether time ran out; the held tree is left unlocked, so a plain delete works once the handle closes (tested). (c) Every child of `skills\` but `enabled.json` goes (the condemned list, the reset marker, `chat-paths.json`, `generation-launches.jsonl`, the store, the views): each describes a tree this hook deletes; the switches stay as the plan says. (d) Provider homes and every other Marrow data file are never touched (tested with a sibling provider home and `UserDefaults.json`). (e) `SkillsUninstallHook.Register(register, dataRoot, body)` (Marrow.App) hands Velopack a callback that never throws; `Program.RunVelopackHook` registers it with `app.OnBeforeUninstallFastCallback` before `app.Run()`; the data root is `SkillsDataRoot.Resolve()` = `DevDataRoot.LocalApplicationData()\Marrow Code`, resolved on its own because the hook runs before any app binding exists. The dev and test hosts still never call Velopack (the existing ED-235 tests pass unchanged).
4. **One pipeline per data root (ED-326 (6)(a)), `SkillsHost`.** `SkillsHost.Open(dataRoot, SkillsHostOptions)` builds ONE `SkillsPipeline` for the root, the root's only owner, and `SkillGenerations` bound to it through `IGenerationStore`, plus the terms step. At most one host is open per root in a process: a second `Open` of the same root (also with a trailing separator) throws; `Dispose` frees the root; two roots own two pipelines. `SkillsStartup.Bind(dataRoot)` (Marrow.App) is called from `Program.Main` right after the storage bindings and before the Avalonia application is built; it publishes the host on `SkillsSeams.Host` (an `Ambient<SkillsHost>` that traps until bound, like `StoragePaths.Locations`). A host that cannot open (state.json that does not parse, a catalogue error) is logged, leaves the seam unbound and does not stop the app; a state.json that does not parse is left alone, never replaced. `SkillsHostOptions.Production()` binds the embedded catalogue, the Windows ACL protection and lock, and a process runner with an EMPTY executable allow-list; the download seam, the binding seam and the licence-text seam are unbound, so updates, repairs and installs refuse ("Pipeline seams are not bound") until SK-16 binds them.
5. **Startup settling (review fix: off the launch path).** The pipeline's GC (the `tmp-` residue of an install that stopped, ended chats and spares, and a reset a held handle cut short: the `skills\reset-pending` marker, ED-326 (6)(d)) no longer runs inside `SkillsHost.Open`. `SkillsHost.CollectInBackground()` runs it once on the pool (one task, a failure is logged, `Dispose` waits up to 10 s for it); `Program.Main`'s `lifetime.Startup` handler calls it right after `shell.FinishLaunching()` (the main window set-up), after the single-instance lock is held, so a second instance never runs it. Tested: Open leaves residue, the background task removes it, one task, disposal waits, and the IL of Main/Startup.
6. **Restart trust and orphans (ED-325 "Restart trust"; review fix).** The pipeline refuses an installed record without a trusted descriptor, and no descriptor may be read from an installed folder (ED-321 (3)). ENGINEERING DECISION: `CatalogueTrust.Restore` rebuilds descriptors from the embedded catalogue for skill sets and plugins installed at the pin the catalogue holds now (the inventory is exactly the catalogue's files; the folder is the one the immutable route sidecar names, which the pipeline cross-checks). Every other installed record (a tool or package set, whose installed-tree hashes are derived from the archives at install time and persisted nowhere trusted, and a set installed at an older pin, whose catalogue is gone) has no descriptor: before its record is dropped from state.json, its folder and spares (read from the route sidecar) are written to `addons\orphans.json` (`SkillsPipeline.MarkOrphans`, atomic, `PipelineOrphan`, its own JSON context because `PipelineJsonContext` is compiled into the NativeAOT shim). The pipeline reads that file at construction and every GC of every launch (startup, update, remove, reset-pending, generations) retains those folders; `SkillsPipeline.Orphans` lists the ids and `SkillsHost.Unrestored` the ids dropped at this open. An explicit `RemoveAsync(id)` releases that item's orphan to the GC, and `ResetAsync` clears every orphan. If the sidecar is missing or invalid the folders are unknown, so the entry has an empty folder list and every tool and store tree is retained; a corrupt `orphans.json` does the same (fail closed). Nothing is deleted behind the user's back, on any launch. Nothing can install a tool through the app yet, so no user data is affected today. After an app update with a new catalogue pin, such a set is kept but not shown installed (no "Update available" yet): persisting trusted descriptors so it can be is SK-16's and is UNRESOLVED here.
7. **Reset.** `SkillsHost.ResetAsync` is the pipeline's reset (SK-8): it removes everything under `addons\` and the store and views, keeps `enabled.json` and the accepted terms. Tested through the composed host, including that the terms survive a restart. It does not end the generations' own spare leases; a leased tree is deleted when its lease ends (SK-8's existing behaviour).
8. **UNRESOLVED / not done.** (a) WU-18 r3 (b), the built app started in a child process from a fake Velopack layout with `--veloapp-uninstall`, is NOT run: it goes through Velopack's own dispatch, and the lead's rule is that no installer, uninstaller or Velopack step runs; what is proved instead is the callback, its registration order in `RunVelopackHook` (IL of the method) and the real-ACL hook body. NOT CLOSED until the owner allows that step. (b) First installs are still not in the pipeline (ED-326 (6)(a)): only the terms gate and its seam exist, the orchestrator that installs a new item is SK-16's. (c) The download and binding seams, descriptors for tools after a restart (item 6) and the Settings rows, the terms control and the footer line on the pages are SK-15/SK-16's (the pages are hidden shells). (d) ED-326 (6)(d) stays: a reset whose residue is held keeps `skills\reset-pending`, and while it stands a GC with nothing installed deletes all of `addons\` except `state.json`, which would include a later first download's `.part`. (e) DL-20's live checks, the 150 ms spare budget and a real Velopack uninstall on a real install are not measured.
9. **Tests.** Services: `Skills.Terms` (TermsStepTests 11, TermsGateTests 5, SkillsNoticesTests 2, NoVendorImageTests 3, LicenceBesideItemTests 5), `Skills.Uninstall` (SkillsUninstallTests 8, SkillsUninstallWindowsTests 2 on the real NTFS deny entry with a held handle, REVIEW_SkillsUninstallLinkTests 12: a junction anywhere in the tree is unlinked, never followed), `Skills.Host` (SkillsHostCompositionTests 9, SkillsHostTermsTests 2, SkillsHostProductionTests 3, SkillsHostOrphanTests 6, REVIEW_SkillsHostGcTests 1: the red test of the SK-13 review, kept with its name). App: `SkillsUninstallHookTests` 4 (Decision ED-321), `SkillsStartupTests` 6 (Decision ED-326: includes "launch fails soft for any non-fatal exception", `SkillsStartup.Bind` now catches everything except OutOfMemory, StackOverflow, AccessViolation and AppDomainUnloaded). Fixtures: `TermsRig`, `StubLicenceText`, `FixedClock`, `UninstallTree`, `RefusingUnlockProtection`, `SkillsHostRig` (Services), `MethodCalls` (App, reads a method's IL for what it calls). LicenceBesideItemTests (OD-0099): for the zip, skill set and msi-admin installs the pinned licence file sits in the installed folder byte for byte and is in the trusted inventory, a changed licence is damage to the whole-tree check (the per-launch seal hashes only binaries, ED-321 (4)), and an update installs the new pin's licence beside the new version.

## ED-340

[VOICE][FIRST-RUN] VT-15, the voice preparation service (`src/Marrow.App/Port/Voice/VoicePreparation.cs` and its seams). Where voice-SPEC V-10.3, V-10.7, V-16.4, V-7.7, V-2.6 and V-14.3 are silent, these are the minimal choices made (porting/first-release/BUILD-PLAN.md row VT-15; V-T100 to V-T104).

1. API shape. V-10.7 names `InstallAndTimeAsync(id, progress, ct)`; the ladder, the key and the record need the probed profile, so it is `InstallAndTimeAsync(id, profile, progress, ct)`. `RecommendAsync()` is the synchronous `Recommend(profile)` (BUILD-PLAN: "Recommend"): it reads no PC. One addition: `PrepareAsync(progress, ct)` = a current stored result is given back, else probe (if no profile is known yet), recommend, install and time; it is what Welcome's yes and the orb click call. The language for V-10.2 is `VoiceLanguage.Resolve(voiceTyping.lang, voiceOrb.langMode, Windows display language)`; Auto-detect and "ask" read as multilingual.
2. Consent (OD-0098 D3 with consent). `GrantConsent()` is the one switch (Welcome's yes, or an orb click). Without it `InstallAndTimeAsync` returns `AwaitingConsent` and touches nothing: no source, no engine, no settings write, no item. `ProbeAsync` is always allowed (V-10.7: "always on the Getting ready screen"). Consent is held in memory by the service; storing Welcome's answer is WV-1's. The "Voice hardware" step (`voice-hardware`, GR-1 work step under `FirstRunSteps.Voice`, id hw, order 60) runs only the probe and caches the profile; nothing downloads on the Getting ready screen.
3. A second call while a run is going joins it (an orb click after Welcome's yes): it is replayed the latest item and gets the same result object; the model is fetched once. The run uses the first caller's cancellation token; each caller's own token only stops that caller's wait.
4. Progress items `(Id, Label, Fraction?, State)`. Ids `voice.probe`, `voice.download`, `voice.verify`, `voice.selftest` (V-10.7). The labels V-10.7 leaves to the Words board (pending) are the words already in the tree: "Voice hardware" (FirstRunSteps.Voice.Name) for the probe, "Voice model" for download and verify, "Voice speed test" for the self-test (the two W1 names recorded in FirstRunSteps' note); nothing new is worded. Fractions are real: rows done of four for the probe; bytes received over the total (VT-7's fraction) for the download, Running 0 first and Done 1 last; the verify and the speed test have none while running (null) and 1.0 when done. A model already installed reports only its download item as Done. No timer or clock moves any item.
5. Self-test (V-10.3): the candidate is installed and verified (VT-7's `VerifyForLoad` through the source), loaded (the warm-up load; `UseGpu` true only on a working GPU backend), then one timed decode of the bundled clip with `DecodeRequest("en", "", Live, 0)`; the clip is English (voice-pins.json selfTestClip.language en_us), so the language is "en" whatever the user's. RTF = seconds / 10 from the service's `TimeProvider` (`SelfTestPlan.Rtf`). The ladder is `SelfTestPlan.Decide` unchanged (R1 to R3), with `AnsweredFor` and `AnswerFor` from the stored `liveWordsChoice` and its key (R5); an unanswered slow processor keeps the model with live words off and reports `AskSlowQuestion` (R8). A stored "live" answer installs the smaller rung (not timed again, R6); `rtf` in the record is then the last timing made, of the model before it.
6. Record (V-16.4): `origin` always `auto` (Check my hardware, V-10.6, is the page's `manual`); `vramGB` and `freeVramGB` are bytes / 2^30 rounded to one decimal (the example's 16 and 14 are the owner's 15.99 and 14.0); `at` is UTC to the whole second; `candidate` is the id asked for and `model` the id kept; `app` and the Whisper.net runtime version for the key (V-10.5) are constructor values (the app's version and build as stored; the wiring supplies them). `IsPrepared(out record)` is true when the stored record's key equals today's, from the last probe or, before any, the optional `currentKey` source (startup); `record` is the stored one, current or stale, or null. The result also selects the model: `voiceTyping.model` is set to the kept model only when none was picked; a model the user picked stays.
7. `LiveWords` (V-7.7) is `VoicePreparation.LiveWordsOf(record)` = the stored record's `liveWords`; with no record it is true (OD-0091's live), the answer for a caller that asks before the first run, since no session starts before one.
8. Failure. A download that is not Installed (Failed, Corrupt, Cancelled), a file that verifies Corrupt or Missing, a model not in the catalogue, or any engine exception (an unbound seam throws and so fails closed) ends the run `Failed` with a plain internal message and stores nothing; a cancelled token throws. These messages are diagnostics, not UI words ("The voice model download failed.", "The voice model did not verify (corrupt).", "{id} is not a voice model of the catalogue.", the exception's own text).
9. `VoiceFeature.Enabled` (V-2.6) is an internal static, off by default, turned on by `VoiceFeature.SwitchOn()`, which the start-up composition calls once the orb is in every composer (VT-12, not merged here); `Reset()` is for tests. So no build shows the orb before VT-12. NOT DONE here: V-T104's second half (the orb appears in every composer, V-14.3) needs VT-12's composer pill; the local lead writes it with the wiring. Also not done here: calling `RegisterStep()` and `SwitchOn()` at start-up, the `app` and runtime version strings, and the production `StoreModelSource` composition (the store and downloader on the data root); Welcome's use of `AwaitingConsent` (WV-1).
10. The self-test clip is read by `SelfTestClip.Load` (16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM WAV, chunks scanned, refused otherwise) from `Port\Voice\Assets\selftest-clip.wav` beside the app.

A row shows the variant the user picked in it; until they pick, the in-use variant, else the recommended one, else Compact, following the settings and the recommendation (when it changes by itself the version control is replaced, not animated, because a control in a folded row is disabled). ## ED-343

[UPDATES][SETTINGS][UI][MOTION][GLASS][TEST] Unit UE-4, the Updates page (place A) of OD-0100 (BUILD-PLAN.md 2.4 UE-4; OD-0100 and its pick "Q1 A and D both, Q2 U1 Plain"; OD-0075's Tools page grown into Updates; OD-0076 every change transitioned; ED-320 GlassMaterial; the lead numbers this at merge). Design source (read-only): work/design/decisions-2026-10-04/update-everything (variant A, words U1). Code: src/Marrow.App/Port/Settings/Updates*.cs (page, controller, projector, runner seam, controls); the one Core addition is UpdateOrchestrator.UpdateOne. Nothing was run, installed, published or sent: every source is a seam and the tests use scripted items.
1. WHAT THE PAGE IS. SA-1's shell UpdatesSettingsPage now holds the page and `IsReady` is true (it is listed, searchable and opened by a request). Header: a state line (19 pt, crossfading), a detail line, and the one button; a banner that offers "Restart Marrow" after Marrow's own update (Marrow icon, two lines, "Later"); then sections of rows with Installed and Latest columns. Each row: mark, name and the line under it, Installed, Latest (bold), status, the row's own Update. Under a running row a bar folds open; under a failed row a line with the command to run by hand and Retry folds open. The words are U1's (the design's ue-page.js WORDS.U1) unchanged where they apply.
2. ONE SERVICE, UE-5's. The page reads and drives `IUpdatesRunner` (rows, IsBusy, Changed, CheckNow, UpdateEverything, UpdateOne, Retry, Restart). UE-5's `UpdateEverythingService` (the app's one orchestrator, the one the sidebar pill reads) now implements it (an event `Changed` raised from the orchestrator's, and the four actions as explicit interface members; its pill code is untouched), and `UpdatesRunnerSource.Shared` is `UpdateEverythingService.Shared` unless a test replaces it for its flow. I had first written my own default (an empty orchestrator behind an Ambient with a `Bind` the lead was to call); after the coordinator's note and the merge of unit/f-ue-5 that was dropped, so there is ONE service and no second orchestrator. `OrchestratorUpdatesRunner(UpdateOrchestrator, restart)` stays, as the adapter the page's tests use over scripted items. Tests with the real service: UpdatesSharedServiceTests (a run started from the pill's `Perform` shows on the page and the page's Restart Marrow is the service's restart; a check from the page reaches the pill's state).
2a. WHAT UE-5 LEFT FOR UE-4, AND WHERE IT IS. The Check now and Update everything controls are the page's one button (item 1). The failure command: `UpdateRowCommand.For(row)` (Core, 2 tests) gives "claude update" / "codex update" for the two provider items that have an updater and null for every other item; the page's failure line uses it, and so does the pill's banner fallback in `UpdatePillProjector` ("<Name> is still <v> after its updater ran. Retry, or run <cmd> in a terminal."; an item with no command reads as before; UE-5's own test, whose row id has no command, is unchanged). The Skills and tools hook is `UpdateEverythingProduction.ExtraItems` (a `Func<IEnumerable<IUpdateItem>>`, empty by default, appended before Marrow when the service is configured): SK-13/SK-16 set it to the pipeline's `SkillUpdateItem`s (kind SkillsAndTools, the page's "Skills and tools" section) and UE-3 to its developer-tool items (kind DevTool, "Developer tools"); both sections show on the page and the pill as soon as the orchestrator has such rows. Nothing sets it yet (STATE.md).
3. UE-2 ADDITION (additive, 3 tests, Feature UE-4 in Core.Tests). `UpdateOrchestrator.UpdateOne(id)` runs one due item alone (UpdateAvailable, ChecksWhenUpdated or Failed; anything else, an unknown id, or a run in progress is refused like Retry). UE-2's Retry could run one item alone only when it had failed, and BUILD-PLAN UE-4 asks for a per-row Update.
4. PROJECTION (UpdatesProjector, pure, 15 tests). Phase order Restarting, Checking, Running, Failed, Done, Available, Unsure, Current, as the design's phase(); a failure is shown before a finished run; the button follows the phase (Check now quiet; Update everything; Retry; Restart Marrow; busy "Checking...", "Updating...", "Restarting..."). Names in the detail lines are in PAGE order (Marrow, Provider tools, Developer tools, Skills and tools), as the design lists them, while the orchestrator runs Marrow last. Versions shown are the first dotted number of each text (VersionText.Number), so "codex-cli 0.157.1" shows 0.157.1. Rows of items that are not installed are not listed (nothing to update; BUILD-PLAN UE-3 "rows only for installed tools"). "Up to date" etc. per row as U1 st. A row with no listing shows "Checks when updated" in its status and a dash in Latest. Words NOT in U1, all labelled ENGINEERING DECISION: (a) "1 update available" singular for one (OD-0076's count rule); (b) the section titles "Developer tools" and "Skills and tools" (BUILD-PLAN names the groups; "Marrow" and "Provider tools" are U1's); (c) "Versions are checked when updated" for the page where nothing is known to be available but some versions are only known when their updater runs (offline, or no listing), with the button "Update everything"; (d) the failure line when the item has no command to name: the item's own reason as a sentence ("Winget exited with code 1."), or "<Title> didn't update." when it gave none; (e) several failures are named together ("Codex and Git didn't update"). LEFT OUT: U1's "Marrow's skills and tools come with it." and the footnote "Skills and their tools change only with a Marrow release. A running chat keeps the versions it started with.", because OD-0100's pick says the skills and their tools are separate optional-download rows, not part of Marrow's package. The design's "Marrow skills / Skill tools: Comes with Marrow" rows are therefore not drawn; the Skills and tools group has whatever rows SK-8's items give it.
5. CONTROLLER (UpdatesController, 10 tests). Opening a page where nothing was ever checked runs one Check now (the same listings the button reads, through the seam; nothing when the orchestrator has no items). It remembers when ("Checked just now / 5 minutes ago / 2 hours ago / 3 days ago", singular for one; the sentence is left out when nothing was checked from this page) and a 30 s tick keeps the age current. Changes from the runner (the pill's background check, anything) reach the page as ONE refresh per turn of the main loop however many arrive, and a detached page hears none. A press while anything runs does nothing; the main button's Retry retries every failed row one at a time in run order. "Later" puts the banner away and moves its sentence to the detail line until the next run. Restart Marrow hands over to the runner's restart and shows "Restarting..."; should the process still be here after 25 s (the update engine's own give-up, ED-319 (4)) the button is given back.
6. LAYOUT. The design's columns (84/84/150 in a 960 pt window) do not fit the Settings window (780 pt, 212 sidebar, 24 pt either side = a 520 pt page). Columns: mark 24, name (the rest, 98 pt), Installed 64, Latest 64, status 152, the row's own Update 66; gaps 6; row padding 12/10. Measured with the real fonts in the tests: the widest status ("Checks when updated") needs 148 pt, a calendar version such as 2026.09.25 fits 64, the Update capsule needs 65. ## ED-345

CZ-5 (Customization C2, the working dots), branch `cloud/f-cz-5` from `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` (e6b4656c3). Source: customization-SPEC CZ-10.1 to CZ-10.4, CZ-13.3, CZ-4.6, CZ-T50 to CZ-T55, Q-CZ-7; OD-0085, OD-0089, OD-0099, OD-0076.

1. **CZ-T50 was already built.** `WorkingDotsSettings` (exact bytes `{"mode":"accent","custom":"blue"}`, lenient read), its `AppSettings` property and key, and their tests came with SA-1 (`WorkingDotsSettingsTests`, `AppSettingsVoiceKeysTests`); CZ-5 changes none of it and ran them.
2. **ENGINEERING DECISION: the colour rule is `WorkingDotsColor` (`src/Marrow.App/Port/Settings/`).** `Of(settings, maker)` gives a `SwiftColor` that follows the appearance, one cached object per answer (a field handed the colour it already wears starts no blend); `Resolve(settings, maker, theme)` is that colour drawn in a theme; `For(model, threadID)` reads the setting and the thread's provider inside a tracked read; `MakerOf(brand)` is `JewelPalettes.For(brand).Maker`. Accent is `Chrome.Accent` as it is: the slot does not track the accent, because the field already follows a pick and eases it through `ThemeManager.DidChange`, and a second retarget from the slot would restart that blend. Model is `CzText.Tone(mid, dark, title)` of the maker. The Purple rule (no maker, or a name `MakerLiquids` does not hold) uses `JewelPalettes` Purple's mid `#8C57F7` with no title colour: `Tone`'s own fallback target (white on dark, `#1C1C1E` on light) is passed as the title, which is what `Tone` would pick for an illegible title, and `#8C57F7` is legible in both themes so it comes back unchanged. Custom is the swatch's hex for the theme; `windows` is `SwiftColor.ControlAccentColor`, the lifted system accent the accent picker draws (SPEC CZ-10.1 item 2); an id the palette does not hold reads as the default pick, blue.
3. **The oracle is the design's own code.** `tests/fixtures/customization/dots.generate.cjs` runs the real `wdColour()` and `dotsSec()` of the locked cz.js on a stubbed board (as `page.generate.cjs` does) and writes `dots.json`: 104 colours (30 makers x 2 themes for model, 22 swatches x 2 for custom) and 48 section cases (3 modes x 4 makers x 4 picks). Two inputs come from outside cz.js: the makers are built from `design-src/orb/liquid-palettes.json` exactly as `stage.generate.cjs` does, and `CZ_ACC` (gen.py:93-94 reads `E:/Droppy/work/design/accent-palette-locked.json`, which a cloud session cannot see) is read back from the port's own `AccentPalette.cs`, whose 22 rows were made from that file (the design's `win` is the port's `windows`). `MakerLiquids` is the high-effort table, as the design's `wdColour` reads `.high`.
4. **ENGINEERING DECISION: `ComposerWorkingDots.Tint` and `DotFieldControl.UpdateColor(color, ease)`.** `Tint` is a plain property, not a styled one: its default is `Chrome.AccentNSColor`, an instance `ThemeManager` replaces on every pick, so a styled default would go stale. Setting it calls `UpdateColor(value, ease: true)`, which goes to `Retarget(ease: true)`: the animated field blends on the render server over the existing 0.32 s ease (Q-CZ-7: one curve for every dot colour change, not the design's 0.4 s), a second change eases on from what is shown, and the still dots (Reduce Motion) take it at once because `Retarget` eases only an animated field. `DotFieldSweep` keeps its `UpdateColor(color)` (ease off).
5. **The slot.** `ComposerWorkingDotsSlot` (one `Track` hook before the run flag's hook, so dots that arrive wear the colour from the start; `Dots()` became an instance method; two fields) passes `WorkingDotsColor.For(app, thread)` to its dots. The edit is inside that class only, with no `using` added, to stay clear of VT-12's edits to `ComposerView`. A change of the setting, of the thread's provider or of the theme reaches every composer (CZ-T55, two composers).
6. **The preview.** `ComposerPreview.WorkingDots` (set by `CustomizationStage`'s new optional constructor argument, which the page fills from `AppSettings.WorkingDots`) gives `PreviewWorkingDots.Tint` the colour for the preview maker; the maker switch retargets it.
7. **The section** (`WorkingDotsSections`, `WorkingDotsSwatches`, texts in the new Core `CzDotsText`): after the style's sections and before `Aura.Picker` in `Sticky` (CZ-7a's Voice orb section goes before it). The Custom row is a `CzRowSlot` that folds open only for Custom. Its row padding is the design's (`.row.accsw` top 2, `.stack` bottom 11) with the port's leading 16 and trailing `Chrome.RowControlTrailingPadding`; the lines are 6 apart, the label column 62 (11.5, secondary), 10 between a label and its swatches, swatches 24 with a 2 gap. A pick of the mode writes `Mode`; a pick of a swatch writes `Custom` (the mode stays); both call `PreviewSession.WorkingDotsTouched`. A change of the setting from elsewhere shows in the rows without touching the preview.
8. **ENGINEERING DECISION: a radio group may hold no pick (`CzRadioGroup`).** Classic and Signature are two radio groups with at most one pick between them, so the constructor takes a null pick; `ShowNone()` takes a pick away without raising an event; a group with none has its first button as the tab stop; an arrow key from none goes to the first (Right) or the last (Left); the peer requires a selection only while one is held. A pick that is not an option is still refused (tested).

## ED-346

CZ-6 "Sticky stage (C3)", branch `unit/f-cz-6` (from `unit/f-cz-4` 8f2123579, merged again at a4ec6be88), 2026-10-05. Scope: BUILD-PLAN CZ-6; customization-SPEC CZ-3.5.1 to CZ-3.5.7 (pin, compaction, release, clip, hairline, focus scroll, frame cost); tests CZ-T60 to T68 (T69 is native, at the gate). OD-0089 amendment, OD-0076.

1. **What was built.** Core: `StickyStage` (the arithmetic: target, pin top, block and stage heights, the text's opacity and lift, the hairline's rule, the focus rule and offset) and `Compaction` (the applied value and whether it is easing). App, in `src\Marrow.App\Port\Settings\`: `StickyStageController` (finds the page's ancestor `ScrollViewer` on attach, follows its offset through `ScrollChanged` and the `Offset` property so the block moves in the same turn as the content, runs the one frame request for the ease and the focus scroll), and in `CustomizationStage` the three things it drives: `PinTo` (a `TranslateTransform` on the block, no layout), `Compact` (the stage's height and the text's opacity and lift) and `ShowHairline`; `CustomizationSettingsPage` builds the controller after the sections (`Stickiness`). The block has `ZIndex` 1000.

2. **ENGINEERING DECISION: the slot stays 372, the stage's own layout changes.** `CustomizationStage` asks the page for its rest height whatever the compaction (its `MeasureOverride` adds the compaction back to its content's height, its `ArrangeOverride` takes it off), so folding the stage re-lays out the stage's own subtree only: no ancestor and no section is invalidated or measured (CZ-3.5.2 "the layout keeps the block's rest height", CZ-3.5.7). The preview composer is kept at the stage's rest height and bottom-aligned inside the clipped stage, so it keeps its 12 above the stage's bottom edge, is not re-measured, and the light's bottom edge (its fade) stays put.

3. **ENGINEERING DECISION: an eased jump goes on easing to its end.** CZ-3.5.2 and the design (cz.js `stageTick`) test `|target - col| <= 72` again on every frame, so a jump eases for one frame (22.3 points at 60 Hz) and then snaps the rest (up to 72 points): a cut, against OD-0076, and not "eases with tau 0.06 s" (CZ-T61). The port decides per step: a step the compaction can follow exactly (within 72 of where it is, with no jump in flight) is followed exactly, as the design does; anything else starts an ease that runs on, whatever the next steps are, until it is within 0.05 of the target. Tested against the design's own `stageTick` run by node (`tests/fixtures/customization/sticky.generate.cjs`, `sticky.json`: wheel traces and the first eased frame are identical, the design's snap frame is the one difference) and by sampling the page at 60 Hz.

4. **ENGINEERING DECISION: what a "clip" is.** Every child of `Sticky` but the block gets a `RectangleGeometry` clip from the block's visual bottom edge down, in its own coordinates, clamped to 64 above its top (nothing wholly below the block is clipped: `Clip` is null, and nothing a section draws outside its bounds is cut) and to 64 below its bottom (a section wholly under the block is clipped away). It is recomputed from layout positions on each offset step and each layout pass, and a clip is replaced only when its edge changed (so only the section straddling the block's edge is touched in a scroll). Content added later to `Sticky` (CZ-5, CZ-7) is picked up with no hook. The `Rest` container is never clipped (the block's bottom is never below the sticky container's). Clipped content is not hit: tested with the compositor's hit test and by pixels (the page with every section hidden draws the same under the block).

5. **ENGINEERING DECISION: positions come from layout, not from the transform.** The controller computes where the sticky container and a focus target lie in the viewer's content from the arranged bounds up to the viewer's content and that content's top margin, never from `TranslatePoint`: the viewer arranges its content at a new offset only in the next layout pass, so a transform-based position would be one step stale in the same turn the offset changes (the block would shake). The container's top is 0 in the Settings window (the page's -60 margin takes back the 60 the window gives it, CZ-4 item 3).

6. **Keyboard focus (CZ-3.5.6).** The viewer's answer to a Tab is a bring-into-view request that scrolls at once and leaves the control under the block's edge. The page handles every such request from its own controls (`RequestBringIntoView`) and answers it itself: no scroll for a pointer focus; otherwise, when the control's top is above the block's bottom + 8 (within 0.5 for layout rounding) or the control is not wholly above the viewer's bottom, the page scrolls over 0.3 s ease (at once under reduce motion) to `y' = top - (372 - 92) - 8` (the compaction the new offset will produce), clamped to what can scroll and never under 92 (a control no offset can clear takes the full compaction). The scroll follows the frame clock; the user's own scroll during it takes it over. ENGINEERING DECISION: the spec says "(or below the viewport)"; a control cut by the viewer's bottom edge counts too (a browser's focus scroll would reveal it). A control inside the block itself is left alone while the block is in view; if the block has been carried away with the page, the page scrolls to the point it is let go at. Controls of the later sections (and `Rest`) are handled the same way.

7. **The hairline** is a 1 point `Border` in the row divider's colour (`Chrome.Overlay(0.12)` through `AnimatedColor`) at the bottom of the block's laid-out content, so it lies on the block's visual bottom edge at every compaction with no transform; it is not hit and fades with a `CzNumber` (0.25 s ease; at once under reduce motion), shown while `y > 4`.

8. **Tests.** Core `StickyStageTests` (CZ-T60, T61, T62, T66 and T67's arithmetic against the design's `sticky.json`); App `StickyStagePinTests` (T60, T63, T64, T65 incl. the pixel test), `StickyStageCompactionTests` (T61, T62: wheel steps exact, the 300 point jump sampled per frame against the exponential, a jump back, reduce motion, a scroll in the middle of an ease, the four k values with the composer's 12 inset and the foot following), `StickyStageHairlineTests` (T66: fade in and out sampled per frame against the 0.25 s ease, geometry, colour), `StickyStageFocusTests` (T67: the animated scroll sampled per frame against the 0.3 s ease, pointer focus, an already clear control, reduce motion, back up, the user taking over, a control in the block), `StickyStageLayoutTests` (T68: counting probes and validity flags through wheel steps, an eased jump and a focus scroll). Fixtures: `CustomizationPageRig` gains `scroll` and `height` (the page in a viewer as the Settings window holds it), `StickyStageProbes` (stand-ins for Working dots and Speech), `MeasureProbe`. The test-first red steps seen: the Core tests (compile failure, then green) and all of the App tests against stubs (22 of 28 failed at run time; the six that passed before the implementation are guards that must stay green, such as the layout counters and the sections' unchanged places). Two test-side corrections after the first green run, neither an expectation changed to match output: the compositor's hit test needs two render ticks before it sees the layout of the moment (`StickyStageProbes.HitAt`), and the jump test's expected frames use the clock's own 100 ns rounding of 1000 / 60 ms; one expectation was wrong by my derivation (the clip edge 40 further on is 240, not 160, since the probe moves up the viewer and the block does not) and was corrected from the geometry.

9. **New raw `CornerRadius` sites:** none (the census in `ContinuousCornerSitesTests` is unchanged).

10. **Not done, and why.** CZ-T69, the native frame test (scrolling the page at 60 Hz on a real window against the frame-gap gate): it needs a quiet PC and the native lock, and is the gate's (BUILD-PLAN CZ-6, STATE). No native look at the compaction on a real window. The Working dots section (CZ-5), the Voice orb section (CZ-7) and the Speech section (CZ-11) are not there; the tests stand in for the first and last with probes, and the controller needs nothing from them.

11. **Runs.** New tests: Core 12 (`StickyStageTests`: 8 facts and two theories of 2 rows, with the traces of the design's `stageTick`), App 28 (`StickyStagePinTests` 5, `StickyStageCompactionTests` 9, `StickyStageHairlineTests` 3, `StickyStageFocusTests` 7, `StickyStageLayoutTests` 4). Slices (filter `&FullyQualifiedName!~Native`): Core (Settings, ComposerLight, Cz, Preview, Traceability, Layering, Maker) 161/161; App (Settings, Customization, CzControls, Preview, ComposerLight, Traceability, ContinuousCorner, ComposerPreview, ReviewCz3, StickyStage) 1611/1611 with no failure to rerun. No native run (CZ-T69 is the gate's) and no UI-project run (nothing in Marrow.UI changed). Merged `unit/f-cz-4` at a4ec6be88 (its review cleanups) with no conflict.
