## ED-406

[ACCOUNTS][USAGE] MA-2, OD-0114, 2026-10-05. User-assigned usage-limits foundation on `codex/ma-2`, based on `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` at `7a4cfad3ef57459faf2f593368412fd44d54de06`. The user's unit scope takes precedence over the different proposed MA numbering in the feasibility study. No UI, automatic account switching, Handshake execution, installer, or live provider calls are added.

1. Identity and reads. `UsageAccountKey` is provider plus stable non-secret account-store ID; `default` identifies the legacy account. Account reader overloads copy the selected environment or use the selected API key. Explicit Claude/Codex/Pi accounts require a fully qualified CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CODEX_HOME/PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR; Command Code requires the selected key or HOME. Claude login reads fail closed for explicit accounts, including refresh re-reads; existing single-account readers retain their global-home fallback. Copilot and Antigravity remain single-account because their Windows sign-ins use OS vaults. No new credential store, token collection, or login flow is introduced. The MA-1 store/MA-3 runtime composition can supply these identities and readers.
2. Service data. Window durations are service/window-schema metadata, never inferred from a plan list. Account snapshots keep the reported windows, percentages, reset dates, details and reset credits. Exact foundation status strings are `no 5-hour window` and `limits not shared` as assigned; the future UI can render its finalized wording. Empty windows with only a plan name do not imply shared limits. Explicit Z.ai reads do not apply the legacy guessed five-hour/weekly title fallback. Command Code duration metadata is added through the account reader only, preserving legacy window-record equality.
3. Polling. `AccountLimitsScheduler` uses an injected TimeProvider and account reader; sign-in requests a read, active accounts poll every three minutes, accounts within five percentage points of their Handshake threshold every minute. Inactive accounts receive no recurring polls. Limit and plan-change requests use the earliest allowed deadline and coalesce with an in-flight read; plan changes invalidate the old snapshot/generation. Every start rechecks a one-minute minimum and the service embargo, including after waiting for the global two-read concurrency bound. Production jitter is 0-10 seconds. Missing/error reports replace old data with unknown limits and back off at 3/6/12/24/30 minutes; Retry-After on scoped HTTP quota reads is preserved across sign-out/re-sign-in and late generations. Cancellation/sign-out/disposal stop timers and cancel readers; late completions never publish into a successor generation. Readers hold their concurrency slot until they actually finish, including if they ignore cancellation.
4. Limit attribution. UsageLimitSignal can produce an account-tagged detection; ProviderEvent.UsageLimit accepts account identity. ThreadRuntime.Observe captures the source session's identity and existing session-epoch checks reject old session events. AutoContinue records the limited account, resolves reset data only from that account, uses the composed scheduler even for the default account, and refuses to resume after a provider/account change. When no scheduler is composed, existing single-account reset-read behavior is retained. Missing/rejected/throttled reads produce the existing unknown-reset behavior; port traps still propagate. Account-store/runtime binding and sign-in/in-use/plan-change hooks are composition surfaces, not a new account UI.
5. Rates. UsageRateEstimator keeps observations independently by thread/account/window, in percentage points per minute. Duplicate/out-of-order samples are ignored; missing/removed/expired windows, reset epochs, plan/duration changes and decreases establish a new baseline. These are observed allowance changes during the caller's thread activity; another client sharing the allowance can affect them, so they are not exact billing or guaranteed next-step predictions. No measured data defaults: $20/Pro/Plus and unknown plans 95%; reported 5x/10x/20x tiers 98%. No quota windows are created by these defaults. Smart Handshake cost/margin selection remains a later unit.
6. Evidence. Test-first compilation failures and behavioral regression failures are recorded in `/workspace/ma2-evidence/`. All new tests carry byte-exact Decision `ED-406`; Traceability recognizes that exact ID alongside its existing numeric ED format. Existing ledger bytes are preserved. The task report records the final build, 39 MA-2 tests plus 12 Traceability checks, baseline comparison, independent adversarial review and remaining Linux limitations. No parity/task ledger status is advanced and no Windows/live-provider verification is claimed.


## ED-407

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][ENGINEERING][TEST] MA-4, Marrow's own handoff summary (2026-10-05). Authority: OD-0114 and multi-account-NOTES' "Marrow's own digest" / "Nothing missed"; native transfer boundaries from multi-account-FEASIBILITY section 4. This is an owner-authorized addition with no Swift twin and no UI. Base: claude/verify-terminal-20261001 at 7a4cfad3ef57459faf2f593368412fd44d54de06; implementation branch codex/ma-4.

1. Core/Port/MultiAccount/HandoffSummary mechanically selects recorded history; no model, prompt, network or quota operation is involved. Every user message and assistant reply retains its original text, whitespace and Unicode. Plans/todos, task, file edits and supplied full current diff, command status/exit codes, last error, approvals and queued instructions are retained. The last three recorded turns keep complete output by default. Older successful Read/Search output keeps 512 Unicode scalars as head/tail; other long recorded output keeps 8192, with an item ID and archive path. These are internal selection bounds, not new Settings defaults. A failed read/search is treated as an error, never as safely re-readable output. The last error remains complete. Nothing is irretrievably discarded by this builder.

2. HandoffStore writes an immutable UTF-8 JSON conversation checkpoint atomically into the thread's folder, threads/<thread UUID>/handoff-<checkpoint UUID>.json. HandoffSummary names that absolute path. FullBytes and SummaryBytes count actual UTF-8, without BOM; a small history can have a larger summary. The archive includes the complete ThreadDocument, explicit state and raw event journal. ThreadRuntime.SaveHandoff takes the caller's current diff snapshot; it bypasses ApiTranscript's message/character clipping. The caller must supply a current, unshortened worktree diff. No git command or file contents are guessed by the builder.

3. HandoffJournal records full provider tool output before Timeline's existing 60 KB cap, original assistant deltas/completions before display cleanup, and approval/question requests and chosen answers in an append-only per-thread sidecar. SaveHandoff restores original recorded assistant text and tool output before building. The sidecar survives runtime eviction/restart; it preserves approval scopes as historical records and grants no new permission. Output already discarded by a provider or by legacy storage before this foundation was installed cannot be recovered; existing recorded history is archived as available. The archive contains everything the foundation received, rather than claiming access to hidden provider state.

4. Handoffs require a quiescent checkpoint: no running turn/tool, pending approval/question, queued send, revert, working Hydra head or outstanding head result. AccountHandoff checks this checkpoint and its saved file before creating a destination session. It preserves RuntimeMode/InteractionMode and destination configuration. Cross-service transfer, and same-service transfer without a matching verified capability, start a new session with the summary as the first user message and clear stale resume IDs/anchors/paths and ApiTranscript replay. There is no automatic account selection, retry loop or mid-tool restart.

5. Same-service transcript transfer is gated by an explicit provider/version/mode capability supplied by the caller; no installed version is enabled by default. A manifest copies only listed Claude projects/*.jsonl or Codex sessions/archived_sessions *.jsonl or *.jsonl.zst artifacts into the destination's separately configured account root. It refuses credentials, databases, traversal, symlinks/junctions, missing artifacts, duplicate paths and overwrites. Claude retains --resume UUID and message anchor; CodexSession additionally passes the copied rollout path to thread/resume when the capability supplies it. Source artifacts remain untouched; failure stops the destination and removes transaction-owned copies. A successful launch returns NativeResumePendingAcknowledgement, never a claim of verified cross-account continuity. Real Windows identity/resume/sidecar compatibility remains subject to the study's experiment. Callers must drain/stop the source before launching this foundation; account bindings and destination continuity acknowledgement belong to the account-switch transaction.

6. Tests were written before implementation: missing MA-4 APIs produced the initial Core/Services/App compilation failures. Offline fixture histories exercise files, decisions, numbers, instructions, Unicode/CRLF, plans, approvals, old reads/searches, command results/errors/web pages and complete recent turns. An independent leaf checker verifies every original detail is present in the summary or recoverable from the archived conversation, with a negative control for lost detail. Further tests check actual archive bytes and sizes, transcript copying, provider requests, failure rollback, quiescence, version/root mismatch and runtime journal recovery. Tests use Rule and Feature traits accepted by Traceability; no new Decision trait grammar, packages, project references or UI. No test contacts a real CLI, model or network. Linux build and test evidence is in porting/reports/codex-ma-4.md. This first-release feature is not an existing T-* parity packet and does not advance the parity/task ledger.

## ED-408

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][ENGINE][TEST] ED-408. MA-5, the multi-account Handshake engine, no UI (OD-0114; `porting/first-release/multi-account-NOTES.md`: Handshake, Handshake timing, Handshake defaults, Handshake point everywhere, Pills, Pills loop, When an earlier account resets, Remember scope, Rule for every choice, Q3 answered, Enable/disable per account; `multi-account-FEASIBILITY.md` read for the provider-terms risk, see (9)). Branch `cloud/ma-5` from `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` (7a4cfad3e). PORT-ONLY: no Swift twin; every rule below is the owner's text in the NOTES, every number or word not in the NOTES is marked ENGINEERING DECISION. All of it is pure and deterministic: an injected `TimeProvider`, scripted sessions, no CLI, model, network or file. (1) Layer and names. `src/Marrow.Core/Accounts` (Core depends on nothing); tests `tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Accounts` (Feature MA-5, Spec MA-T1 to MA-T75). Interfaces for the parallel units, each with an in-memory stand-in so the units join later: `IAccountStore` (MA-1: `Accounts` in global priority order, enabled or not; `AccountInfo` Id, Service, Name, Enabled, Plan, HandshakeAt), `IAccountLimits` (MA-2: `Usage` of the binding window, `SpendPercentPerMinute` per thread and `HandshakeCostPercent`, the usage-rate estimator), `IHandoffSummary` (MA-4: `BuildAsync` and `FindGaps`, the read-back check), `IDecisionStore` (Settings values and thread values, `InMemoryDecisionStore`), and `IThreadAccountHost` with `IStandbySession` (the thread runtime's side: `ActiveAccountId`, `Pill`, `StepIndex`, `Pinned`, `AtSafePoint`, `ReplyInFlight`, `StartStandbyAsync`, `RequestBriefingAsync`, `SwitchAsync`). Nothing in `ThreadRuntime.cs`, `AutoContinue.cs` or the Hydra runtime was changed and nothing binds the host yet: the production host is the join unit's. (2) The machine (`HandshakeMachine`, one per thread). Phases Idle, Standby, Linking, InSync, Switch, plus two PORT-ONLY phases the UI needs: Waiting (for a reset) and Asking (a card is open). `TickAsync` is the poller's beat; at the start point it starts the incoming account's session in the background (Standby), then Linking runs Marrow's summary, the outgoing account's briefing (only while it still has usage), and the incoming account's read-back; In sync has Marrow check the read-back against the summary (`FindGaps`) and send only the gaps; Switch happens only when `host.AtSafePoint` (between steps, never mid-edit), at a later beat if need be, on the same standby. A beat that finds a Handshake running returns at once. `LimitHitAsync` is the hard-stop fallback: it cancels the briefing in flight, keeps the standby and summary already prepared, skips the briefing (the outgoing account is out), still reads back and fills gaps, and switches at once (a turn that died on a limit is at a safe point). With the Handshake setting off: nothing starts near the limit, and a hard stop still moves, handing the summary over without a read-back. A failed standby, briefing or switch emits `Degraded`, falls back to Idle (a failed briefing still carries on) and is not retried on every beat: `failedFor` holds the account until its usage falls below the start point. (3) Start point (`HandshakeTiming`): step, else account, else general (null inherits, Smart is an explicit value); a set point is 80 to 99 (`HandshakePoint.At` refuses others); Smart with measurements starts at 100 minus (Handshake cost + spend rate x one step + margin), clamped to 80..99, with no measurements the plan-aware defaults the owner set ($20 plans 95, 5x/10x/20x 98). ENGINEERING DECISION: one step is 1 minute and the margin 1 percent (`HandshakeTimingOptions`), an Unknown plan takes the $20 default (the earlier start is the safer error). (4) Next account (`NextAccountChooser`). Outside a pill: enabled accounts of the same service in priority order, skipping those out (an account past its reported reset time counts as back), the next after the current one first, else the highest-ranked available (the wrap); with the whole service out and another service available it returns `OtherService` (never taken by the chooser); with none it returns `WaitFor(earliest reset)`; with no enabled account `NoAccounts`. In a pill: the next available step after the current one, crossing services without asking, then the loop to the highest-ranked available step, else `WaitFor` the earliest reset over the pill's enabled steps; a step on a disabled account is skipped; the step's model, effort, fast mode and Handshake point travel in `SwitchTarget`. `EarlierBack` gives the highest-ranked available account above the current one. (5) Decisions (`DecisionPolicy`). Five kinds: OnLimit (switch or wait), OtherService (switch or wait), MidReply (finish or stop), Bring (full, Marrow summary, AI summary), EarlierAccount (go back or stay); "Ask me" exists only for OnLimit, OtherService and EarlierAccount. Precedence thread, then the pill's own EarlierAccount value, then Settings, then ask; unset is the first-time ask, "Ask me" the not-first-time one. One card carries every unresolved kind the move needs, with one Remember line (Just this time stores nothing, This thread the thread value, All threads the Settings value) applied to all choices on the card. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: the pill's value sits between thread and Settings (the NOTES say only that a pill can carry its own); a card answered without a kind the switch still needs is not asked a second time but takes `DecisionValues.Fallback` (OnLimit switch, OtherService wait, MidReply finish, Bring Marrow summary, EarlierAccount stay); a card is refused if it answers a kind it did not ask or answers "Ask me". (6) When it asks. Nothing is prepared ahead of time unless OnLimit says switch and Bring is set (the card appears at the limit, as the approved limit card says "reached its limit"); at the hard stop the card asks OnLimit, Bring, MidReply (only if a reply was in flight) and OtherService (only when the move leaves the service) in one card. OtherService is asked outside a pill even when OnLimit says switch, and a remembered answer is honoured (the owner's text gives it the three Remember choices); inside a pill it is never asked. UNRESOLVED: the lead's brief said "always asked outside a pill"; the owner's verbatim answer gives a Remember line, so a remembered OtherService value is read; if the owner means always, drop the read in `HardLimitAsync`. (7) Earlier account back. Only at Idle, only when the thread is not pinned by hand; Stay (or a card's Stay) remembers the account so it is not offered again until the thread moves; Go back runs the normal Handshake (with briefing, the current account has usage) and switches at the next safe point; the first time asks (with Bring if that is unset too). (8) Waiting. A user-chosen wait ends, without a switch, when the current account is back (the host's own resume, e.g. `AutoContinue`, carries on). A wait because nothing was available (a pill or a whole service out) shows the earliest reset in `ResumesAt` and, when any account is back, moves there by the hard-stop pipeline (reason ResetReached). Events: `HandshakeEvent` carries kind (PhaseChanged, DecisionRequested, InSyncReady with "in sync" or "N gap(s) filled", Degraded with the cause), from and to phase, outgoing and incoming account, reason (NearLimit, HardLimit, EarlierAccountBack, ResetReached), time, `ResumesAt` and the `DecisionRequest`. (9) Provider terms. FEASIBILITY quotes terms against rotating accounts to avoid limits (Command Code one account per person; OpenCode prohibits it; others bar bypassing limits). This unit builds the mechanism only, nothing binds it to a real account, and nothing here turns it on: whether and for which services it may be enabled is the owner's decision to be taken with that risk (the lead raised it in OD-0114). (10) NOT DONE: the production `IThreadAccountHost` over `ThreadRuntime` (safe-point signal after a tool finishes, briefing request, session start, the resume message), the real stores and limits (MA-1, MA-2, MA-4), the Settings rows and cards, the capsule and animation, Pills editor and link-up, "@" opinions, persistence of the thread's pill step, one machine per live thread and the poller that beats it, the Handshake cost and spend-rate numbers themselves (MA-2 measures them), the owner's final design-page picks (OD-0114: the interface waits for them). (11) Tests: 75 test methods (MA-T1 to MA-T75), 82 cases, in `tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Accounts`: chooser 9 and pill chooser 7, decision policy 9, timing 5 (7 cases), machine 13, hard stop 7, cards 9, other service 4, earlier account 7, waiting 5. Written first against stubs (81 of 82 cases red, commit f3ae9c74), then the engine. Mutation spot checks, each caught by at least one test and restored: the switch without the safe-point wait; the briefing requested after a hard stop (caught by a hang in the cancelled-briefing test and by a failure); the earlier-account offer to a pinned thread; the near-limit start without the OnLimit setting; the failure guard removed. The full Core suite on Linux (`FullyQualifiedName!~Native`) fails 563 cases identically on the untouched base 7a4cfad3e (Linux culture and tool differences, none in Accounts; two flaky cases differ between the two runs); TraceabilityTests and LayeringTests pass. UNVERIFIED: nothing ran against a real thread runtime, CLI or clock, and no Windows run was made.

## ED-410

[PROVIDERS][MULTI-ACCOUNT][LOCAL] MA-3, 2026-10-05, commissioned against `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` at `7a4cfad3ef57459faf2f593368412fd44d54de06`, on the isolated branch `codex/ma-3`. Authority: OD-0114; OD-0049/OD-0060's port-only OpenRouter precedent; multi-account-NOTES.md's Local and no-cap items; multi-account-FEASIBILITY.md section 5. This is the commissioned Local foundation unit, not the differently named proposed MA-3 row in MA-0's build-order table. No new controls, account selection UI, Handshake, pills, link-up or model downloads.

1. Core model. ProviderKind.Local is appended after OpenRouter, raw value `local`, display name `Local`, no executable, login, key environment variable, key acceptance, hosted credits or subscription limits. It compacts through the existing native session. `Port/Local/LocalServer.cs` holds independently identified servers and their model/capability records. Normalize HTTP(S) host:port (including LAN, DNS, IPv6 and an optional base path) to an OpenAI `/v1/` base; reject credentials, queries, fragments and unsupported schemes. The server identity is SHA-256 of the normalized base URL. A model's opaque selection contains that identity plus its escaped original model ID, so identical model names on different servers cannot collide. Existing model/thread persistence stores that selection without schema changes. No server/model count cap. Loopback has the exact summary `No limit, stays on this PC`; private IP addresses say `No limit, stays on your network`; other hosts use their chosen host name without claiming local privacy. No hosted allowance is synthesized.
2. Discovery. `Port/Local/LocalDiscovery.cs` automatically probes only 127.0.0.1 on 11434, 1234, 8080 and 8000; arbitrary additional addresses are explicit user additions, never a LAN scan. A 1.5-second total deadline per server bounds listing and metadata; eight probes may run concurrently, with no limit on the total entries. Per-instance HTTP client, no authorization, cookies, redirects or inference. Read `/v1/models`; also read Ollama `/api/tags`, even when the compatibility list succeeds. HTTP failures, malformed bodies and absent usable models do not advertise ready entries. A listed server whose optional metadata times out retains honest fallback capabilities. Cancellation propagates, preserves the last completed snapshot and does not publish a partial discovery.
3. Capabilities. Store nullable tool support, a context window and whether it was reported, plus explicitly reported vision. Accept explicit boolean/array tool metadata; never infer tool ability from a model name or from OpenAI compatibility. Ollama `/api/show` supplies capabilities and configured `num_ctx`; theoretical `model_info.*.context_length` alone does not set effective context. LM Studio `/api/v0/models` supplies `loaded_context_length`; llama.cpp `/props` supplies single-model per-slot `default_generation_settings.n_ctx`; compatible listings may report `context_length` or vLLM `max_model_len`. Unknown context falls back to 4096 and the model detail says `4096 context fallback`. Unknown tools are labelled `Tool support unknown` and run text only; false support also omits tools/tool_choice. Unsolicited tool calls from those models cannot execute locally. No model is pulled, loaded or run by a capability check.
4. Session. `Port/Local/LocalSession.cs` subclasses the real OpenAICompatibleSession SSE/history/tool/approval path. New Config flags default to existing provider behavior; Local disables required keys, bearer auth, redirects and cookies, even if an unrelated key was supplied. URLRequest's port-only FollowRedirects/UseCookies hints enforce the Local privacy boundary without changing existing request defaults. Local maps selection IDs to the server's original model ID before prompt/image/request construction, rejects foreign selections, uses reported context for usage accounting, and sends max_tokens bounded to min(2048, context/4), at least one. Marrow native tools and approvals remain the existing implementation. HTTP/capacity failures are ordinary failed turns, never synthetic account exhaustion.
5. Registry/runtime. Local registry integration has separate entries, shared in-flight discovery, existing status/catalog observation and no secret store. Explicit addresses persist as a non-secret JSON array under `localServerAddresses`; malformed individual saved entries are isolated. Only discovered usable Local models make the provider available. Cached generic catalog rows cannot bypass fresh endpoint binding. The runtime resolves a specific selected model/server, never picks another server implicitly, and reuses a session only while both server identity and discovery revision match. Refreshing capabilities or changing server restarts the session and uses the existing API transcript replay. API keys from other providers are never read for Local. The existing exhaustive composer palette map assigns Local the existing purple no-provider palette, allowing current controls and preview fallback to render it without a new control, asset or style.
6. Offline tests and limits. New tests carry Rule R-TEST-10 and Feature MA-3, as Traceability accepts; no new source-parity Req claim. Tests use actual fake HTTP servers on loopback, manual deadline time, throwaway folders, in-memory defaults and existing actor/store seams. Both test assemblies install a fail-closed LocalDiscovery factory at module load so legacy registry refresh tests cannot probe a real installed server. Production's factory retains the four automatic candidates. Independent review covered tests and implementation; review fixes and exact Linux build/slice evidence are in `porting/first-release/ma-3-REPORT.md`. Real-model reliability, real Windows server smoke tests, token-aware input budgeting/automatic compaction, native metadata version expansion and authenticated Local servers remain outside this foundation's verified scope. The output cap and context metadata do not establish an input token budget or guaranteed fit.

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][API-KEYS][TEST] ED-411. MA-6, several API keys per service (OD-0114; `porting/first-release/multi-account-NOTES.md` "API providers", "Enable/disable per account"). Branch `cloud/ma-6` from `claude/verify-terminal-20261001` (bfbbea40). PORT-ONLY: no Swift twin; the rules are the owner's text in the NOTES, every number or word beyond it is marked ENGINEERING DECISION. Tests run a real `OpenAICompatibleSession` against a scripted server on 127.0.0.1 only; no real key, network or CLI. (1) Layer. Core `src/Marrow.Core/Accounts/Keys`: `ApiKeyEntry` (Id, Service, Nickname, Allowed, MonthlyCapUsd), `KeyOrderMode` (InOrder, MostCreditsFirst, SpreadEvenly), `KeyChoice`, `ApiKeyEvent` (Continued, AllKeysOut, PinnedKeyOut, CapReached), the interface MA-1's store can satisfy `IApiKeyStore` (`Keys(service)` in the user's order, `Order(service)`, `Secret(keyId)`), `IApiKeyCredits` (credits left where the service reports them), `IApiKeySpend` (month spend and `Add`), `IApiKeyRotation` (what a session calls per request: `Current`, `OnFailure(status, retryAfter)`, `RecordSpend`), in-memory fakes of the three stores, and `ApiKeyPool` (one per service; `ForThread`, `Pin`, `State`, event `Changed`). Services: `KeychainApiKeySecrets` (secrets over `APIKeychain`; the first key keeps the account older builds used, so one key looks exactly like today; each further key is "<that account> [<key id>]"; `APIKeychain.PrimaryAccount` exposes the private account table, internal), and in `OpenAICompatibleSession` the PORT-ONLY seams `KeyRotation`, `KeySpendEstimator` and `StreamRound.RetryAfter`. With `KeyRotation` null the session is byte-for-byte as before (a test pins a 402 with one key). (2) Choice. A key is usable when Allowed, a secret is stored, it is not out, and its month spend is under its cap. In order: the list order. Most credits first: highest `CreditsLeft`, unknown last, ties by list order. Spread evenly: fewest requests so far, ties by list order (a count of choices made by the pool; a key that was off owes no turns when it returns). (3) Continuation. A 402 (out of credits) or 429 (rate limited) on a request marks that key out and the session sends the same payload again on the next usable key, in the same turn, with no delay, before anything was shown (the refusal is not a stream); the session adds an Info notice "Continued on <name>" and the pool raises `Continued`. Any other status neither rotates nor marks a key out. A key is tried at most once per request (a Retry-After of zero cannot loop). Each tool round is a new request and starts from the current key. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: a 429 keeps the key out for its Retry-After in whole seconds, else 60 s; a 402 keeps it out until the service reports credits above zero again, else 30 minutes; the out state is shared by every thread, the tried set is the thread's own. (4) All keys out. With no usable key the pool raises `AllKeysOut` (with the earliest return time where one is known: an out time, or the start of next month for a capped key), `State()` says all out, the session adds a Warning notice "All <Title> API keys are out." and the turn ends in a failed turn, whatever the cause (all refused, all off, all capped). The wording of the notices is the unit's. (5) Cap and spend. The cap is per UTC calendar month (ENGINEERING DECISION). The pool records spend through `RecordSpend` against the key the request used and raises `CapReached` once per key per month. UNRESOLVED: no source gives a price for a token, so the session records spend only when the host gives `KeySpendEstimator`; with none (the default) no spend is recorded and a cap never trips. (6) Pin. `Pin(thread, key)` makes that thread use the key whatever the order; a pinned thread whose key is out, off, unstored or unknown gets no choice and never falls to another key (`PinnedKeyOut`); the pin is in memory (the join persists it on the thread). ENGINEERING DECISION: a pin does not look at the cap. (7) Enabled/disabled. An off key stays stored and is skipped by choice and by continuation. (8) NOT DONE: the Settings rows and cards (nickname editing, the Allowed switch, order picker, cap field), the popover with credits, fetching credits (OpenRouter's credits call is not bound to `IApiKeyCredits`), a price table for `KeySpendEstimator`, persisting pins and spend, MA-1's real `IApiKeyStore` over its store and `KeychainApiKeySecrets`, binding a thread's rotation when its session is created (`ThreadRuntime`/`AppSettings` do not set `KeyRotation`), DeepSeek, Z.ai and OpenRouter session subclasses were not re-run beyond the shared slice, and the OpenAI-compatible (custom endpoint) service has no `ProviderKind` and so no keychain account here. (9) Provider terms. Rotating keys of one person on 402 and 429 is the mechanism the FEASIBILITY study warns about for some services (terms against circumventing limits); this unit builds the mechanism and turns nothing on; whether it may be on per service is the owner's decision. (10) Tests: 38 methods (MA-T101 to MA-T138), 42 cases: Core `tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Accounts/Keys` 28 (order, failover, cap and pin), Services 14 (session over loopback 11, keychain secrets 3). Written first against a stub (27 of 27 red, commit ff09fc51). Mutation checks, each caught: the new key not used for the retry, retry on a 500 in the session, retry on a 500 in the pool, the tried set removed (found uncaught, then T138 added and the mutant caught). Slice `OpenAICompatible|APIKeychain|DeepSeek|Zai|OpenRouter|Meta|Traceability|Layering` in Services: 103 failures, the same 103 on the untouched base bfbbea40 (Linux), none new; Core Traceability and Layering pass. UNVERIFIED: no Windows run, no real service.

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][API-KEYS][TEST] ED-411, update of 2026-10-05 (lead decisions on the MA-6 choices; OD-0116). These supersede items (3), (5) and (6) of the entry above where they differ. (1) Local month. The monthly cap follows the user's LOCAL calendar month (`TimeProvider.LocalTimeZone`), not UTC: `IApiKeySpend` is now `SpendSince(keyId, since)` and the pool passes the first instant of the local month; a capped key returns at the first instant of the next local month; `CapReached` comes once per key per local month. Tests use a UTC-8 and a UTC+5:30 zone around the month turn (MA-T147 to MA-T150). (2) Pin and cap. A pin no longer ignores the cap. A pinned key at its cap stops the thread before it sends: no request goes out, the pool raises `PinnedKeyCapped`, `StopReason` and the session notice read "<name> reached its monthly cap. Unpin this thread or raise the cap." (the wording is the unit's); raising the cap or unpinning lets the thread send again. A pinned key that is out or off likewise stops with "<name> is out. Unpin this thread to use another key." / "<name> is off. ..." and never falls to another key. (3) Out times. The 60 s rate-limit and 30 min credits re-check stand as decided. (4) OD-0116. Automatic moving to another key is OFF by default and the first time it would happen the user is asked. `IKeyMovePolicy` (`Unset` default, `Allow`, `Deny`; `InMemoryKeyMovePolicy`) is the interface the join maps onto the remember scopes (just this time / this thread / all threads, MA-5's decision policy). A FORCED move is one the thread did not choose: its key answered 402 or 429, or ran out of credits, or reached its cap. With `Unset` the pool does not move: `OnFailure` returns null, the failure still marks the key out, the pool raises `MoveNeedsAnswer` (naming the key left and the key proposed), the session adds a Warning notice "<from> is out. Continue on <to>?" and ends the round as the error it was; the thread then waits on its key (its next `Current()` gives no key and repeats the question) until answered. `AllowMoveOnce()` is "yes, just this time": the next forced move is made (the same request if given before the refusal returns, else on the thread's next request, announced "Continued on <name>"); a remembered `Allow` moves silently from then on, which is the silent same-turn retry; `Deny` raises `MoveDeclined` and never moves except by `AllowMoveOnce`. Not forced moves, so never asked: starting a thread on the first usable key, spread-evenly or most-credits picks that change key from request to request, and a key the user turned off. The question is asked once per thread and service until answered (remembered answers are the join's). The session now says "Continued on <name>" also when a new request moves the thread (`IApiKeyRotation.ContinuedOn`). (5) Tests: 42 MA-6 cases in Core (28 before, 14 added in this update, T139 to T152) and 16 in Services (T153, T154 added); the update was written first (commit 997f62c5, 11 of 14 new Core cases and 2 of 2 new Services cases red against the old pool), then the pool; one mutation check (the policy answering yes unless declined) was caught. NOT DONE (unchanged, plus): the card that asks and the remember scopes, the Settings row for the policy, the UI for unpin and the cap field.

## ED-412

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][PILLS][STORE][TEST] ED-412. MA-7, pills as data (OD-0114; `porting/first-release/multi-account-NOTES.md` "Pills", "Pills loop", "Effort and fast mode", "Handshake point everywhere", "Pills get their own Settings category", "When an earlier account resets"). Branch `cloud/ma-7` from `cloud/ma-5` (22bff240). PORT-ONLY: no Swift twin; no UI, no network. This also closes MA-5's "not done" item "persistence of the thread's pill step". (1) Model. MA-5's `Pill` and `PillStep` grew trailing optional members (existing callers unchanged): `Pill.Id`, `Pill.HandshakeMode` (`PerStep` or `SameForEvery`), `Pill.SameHandshake`, `PillStep.KeyId` (an API key of the service instead of the account's own sign-in, MA-6). A step's null model, effort, fast mode or Handshake point is "same as the account". `Pill.Effective(i)` is the step as the Handshake sees it: in same-for-every mode the pill's one point replaces the step's own; `HandshakeMachine.CurrentStep` now reads it (the only edit to MA-5 code). (2) `PillStore` (`src/Marrow.Core/Accounts/Pills`): create, rename, duplicate, delete, add/remove/update/move step, the pill's earlier-account rule (go back, stay, ask, or null to follow Settings), Handshake mode, "Use for new threads", `NewThreadRelay`, and a `Changed` event per change. ENGINEERING DECISIONS: names are trimmed, non-empty and unique ignoring case (`NameProblem` for the editor, the mutators throw `ArgumentException`); a duplicate is "<name> copy", "<name> copy 2"... placed right after the original and is not made the new-thread pill; deleting the new-thread pill clears that choice; a step needs a non-blank account; moving a step onto itself is a no-op (no event, no write); switching to same-for-every without a point means Smart, switching back to per-step drops the pill's point and keeps every step's own; a new thread starts at the first step the caller finds usable. (3) Persistence. `PillStorage` keeps all pills as one JSON text under settings key `multiAccount.pills` (`ISettingsStore`, as `AppSettings` does): `{version, useForNewThreads?, pills: [{id, name, earlierAccount?, handshakeMode, handshakeAll?, steps: [{account, key?, model?, effort?, fast?, handshake?}]}]}`, a Handshake point written as `"smart"` or 80 to 99. Version 1 is the first shape, so no real migration exists yet; the mechanism is built and tested with a test-only chain: older text is migrated one version at a time in memory through `migrations[v]` and rewritten at the current version on the next change; a migration that throws leaves the text alone; text from a NEWER app loads what this version knows (unknown fields ignored) and is never written over (`SaveBlocked`); unreadable text loads empty and is never written over; both until `Save(overwrite: true)`; a pill or step that cannot be read (no id, blank name or account, repeated id) is skipped and counted, an unreadable fast mode or an out-of-range Handshake point becomes null (same as the account), an unknown earlier-account value becomes null, a new-thread id with no pill is dropped. Nothing is written until the first change. (4) The thread. `ChatThread` (Library.cs, ported file, PORT-ONLY block marked) gained `PillID`, `PillStepIndex`, `PillStepAccountID` (init-only, with `PillRelay` and `WithPillRelay`); written only when set and read leniently, so a thread with no pill writes the same JSON as before and an old thread reads as having none; a partial or unreadable set is no relay. The account id is stored beside the index so an edited pill is still understood. `PillRelayResolver.Resolve(pills, saved)`: the stored step if it still holds the stored account (Exact); else the same account at the nearest step, ties to the later one (Moved); else, the account having left the pill, the stored position clamped into it (Replaced); a deleted pill gives PillGone (the relay is cleared); a pill with no steps gives Empty. (5) NOT DONE: Settings category, pill editor and drawing; who calls `WithPillRelay` after a switch (the join reads `SwitchTarget.StepIndex` and the account); an `IThreadAccountHost` over `ThreadRuntime` that returns `Pill` and `StepIndex` from the thread; a real v2; the lock a multi-threaded caller would need (the store is single-threaded); the pill's "loop" is MA-5's chooser, not a stored setting. (6) Tests: 33 MA-7 cases (MA-T201 to MA-T233) in `tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Accounts/Pills`: store 13, storage 10, thread and resolver 7, restart with the MA-5 machine 3. Written first against stubs (32 of 33 red, commit 36851cf6; the thread-JSON code was real from the start, so its tests were green or failed on the stubs). Mutation checks, each caught: saving over blocked text, the resolver's tie rule, the machine ignoring same-for-every, delete not clearing the new-thread pill, the thread not writing its pill. Slice `MA-5|MA-7|Library|ChatThread|Traceability|Layering` in Core: 239 passed, 0 failed. UNVERIFIED: no Windows run, nothing ran against the real `AppSettings` file.

### ED-433: consent invariant test, and an earlier account must have come back

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][CONSENT][TEST] ENGINEERING DECISION: OD-0116 is also checked as an invariant, not only as listed cases. `HandshakeConsentModelTests` (Core) drives the real `HandshakeMachine` through 60,000 seeded random conversations (settings at thread and Settings level, answers with every Remember scope, partial and refused answers, revocations and pins and accounts turned off or out at any host call, repeated limits, safe points, clock moves) with a probe host and an independent oracle. At every call that carries the conversation to another account (receive, incoming light briefing, gap fill, switch) the oracle requires the user's current word: switching agreed (or going back agreed), another service agreed when the service changes, the Handshake on for a near-limit move, no pin, the destination on and not out, no resume after Stop, the package equal to the Bring choice. An answer governs the operation it was given for (as the machine does) and ends with it. 600,000 seeds were run once during development with no violation; the committed run uses 60,000. No bypass was found in the machine; the five bypasses T11 listed (recovery, incomplete answers, late mid-reply choice, revoked consent, healthy API-key re-ranking) were already closed by T11's later commits (see handoff claude-ma-engine.md for the test of each).

An account without a reading still counts as back (unchanged).

### ED-435: a key turned off under a live thread is a forced move (OD-0116)

### ED-436: CLI destinations without a verified standby get deferred delivery (OD-0116)

[MULTI-ACCOUNT][HANDSHAKE][SAFETY] ENGINEERING DECISION (lead decision 2026-10-06; supersedes the open UNRESOLVED CLI read-only standby notes of ED-403): only Claude, after its verified gate (version, effective policy, acknowledged tools-empty init), and the API and Local providers (final-report, no tools) are primed in a private standby. No other CLI (Codex and the rest) is ever started early, and there is never a prompt-only "please take no actions" mode. Such a destination, and a Claude whose gate does not pass (any failure of the gated start other than a cancel), takes one deferred path: `ThreadAccountHost.StartStandbyAsync` returns a `DeferredStandby` (no session, no process); `HandshakeMachine` (through `IDeferredDeliveryHost`) sends no read-back request, fills no gaps and never resumes a reply for it; a near-limit or earlier-account move waits for the source reply to end whatever the mid-reply choice; at the switch `ThreadRuntime.AdoptDeferredAccount` binds the thread to the destination with no session and keeps the context (Marrow summary, or the whole archive, or the AI briefing plus summary, built from the final archive at the switch under the same source/consent/pin/settings guards) until the destination's first real turn, which carries it in front of the user's message exactly once (like the forwarded continuation). No read-back means no "in sync" claim; the capsule must say handed over, not in sync (step 3). The outgoing briefing on an unverifiable source returns none (no private session on it); Bring "A summary by AI" for a destination without a verified light-model path still fails closed. The mid-reply card is still asked when a reply is in flight even though a deferred destination ignores the answer (known cosmetic gap). The held context lives in memory: an app restart before the first turn loses it (the thread then starts a new provider conversation, with the existing "no longer has this conversation" notice). Tests: Core `HandshakeDeferredDeliveryTests` (3), App `DeferredContextDeliveryTests` (2: a Codex destination never launched and delivered on the first turn only; a Claude with an old CLI gate takes the same path with no process started).

### ED-439: Codex waits for the switch with the context loaded as history, no model turn (OD-0116, OD-0120, OD-0121, OD-0122)

[MULTI-ACCOUNT] ENGINEERING DECISION: lead brief 2026-10-06 (research `claude-cli-standby-research.md`, section 1). The engine now knows three ways a prepared destination holds the context, `StandbyKind` on `IStandbySession` (default `Primed`, so every existing standby is unchanged): `Primed` (a text-only model turn that reads it back: Claude after its gate, API, Local), `Injected` (the history is loaded with no model turn at all) and `Deferred` (nothing is sent early; the context rides in front of the first real turn). For `Injected` the engine asks for no read-back, fills no gaps and shows the same in-sync tick as Claude once the history is loaded (OD-0122: `InSyncReady`, detail "in sync"); a reply may be continued exactly as for Claude. A standby that is discarded for safety drops to `Deferred` and the engine then treats it as deferred (no tick, no resumed reply).
Codex (`CodexSession`, new `IStandbyInjectionSession`): `StartInjectedStandby` connects the destination's own `codex app-server`, requires the `initialize` `userAgent` version to be at least 0.159.3 and the CLI's own generated schema (`codex app-server generate-json-schema`, cached per executable and version, offline seam `CodexHistoryInjection.SchemaProbe`) to list `thread/inject_items`; then `thread/start` read-only/untrusted (belt and braces only). `InjectStandbyHistory` is one `thread/inject_items` developer message with an `input_text` part. No `turn/start` exists before the handover: `Send` on a waiting thread throws. The handover is the runtime's first real turn, whose existing `turn/start` already carries the user's real approval policy, sandbox policy, model and effort. Fail-safe: any `turn/started`, `item/started`, `item/completed`, `hook/started` notification or any server request (approval, question) on the waiting thread is a violation: it is never forwarded, the thread is deleted (`thread/delete`, 3 second bound), the process stops and the standby becomes deferred; a refused inject, an exit or an old CLI do the same. Cancel (`DisposeAsync` before adoption) deletes the thread and stops the process; no turn is ever sent. `ResolveDeliversDeferredAsync` (new default member of `IDeferredDeliveryHost`) lets the host run the same cached check before the user is asked anything.
`InjectedStandbySession` holds the package; the first load is the whole recorded context (Full: the archive text, over 400,000 characters Marrow's summary instead; Marrow summary; AI summary: summary plus briefing); later loads (the host rebuilds the summary at the switch) inject only new or changed entries, the trailer/header changes and the new archive path, compared block by block against Marrow's own summary layout, and the whole text when it is not that layout. `IAdoptableStandby` now carries what the host needs, and `ThreadAccountHost.SwitchAsync` adopts a Primed or an Injected standby through the same path; a discarded injected standby falls back to the deferred switch with the package it already holds (no context lost).
Simplifications recorded: the research suggests user/assistant message pairs for the Full bring and a read-back of the rollout JSONL by SHA-256; this build loads one developer message per load (the context is one recorded document, not a replayed conversation) and does not read the rollout file back (its format is internal to Codex and is not pinned here), so "loaded" means every `thread/inject_items` returned `{}` and nothing happened on the thread. Unverified against a real CLI (owner OK needed, like R4): that `userAgent` is `client/version (...)`, that the generated schema file is `ClientRequest.json`, and that a real `thread/inject_items` makes no model call (the upstream test says so).
Test changes: `DeferredContextDeliveryTests.A_non_Claude_CLI_destination_is_never_started_in_standby_and_gets_the_context_with_its_first_turn` used Codex as its example of a destination that is never launched early; Codex is no longer that destination (OD-0116 refined by this brief, OD-0122), so it now uses Command Code, which has nothing to open early; its assertions are unchanged. The `FakeThreadHost` and the Codex stand-in (`emit-<method>.txt` replies for scripted notifications) gained test-only members. New tests: Core `HandshakeInjectedStandbyTests` (five of its six were red before the engine change), Services `CodexStandbyTests`, `InjectedStandbySessionTests`, App `InjectedStandbyHostTests`.

### ED-440: Pi waits for the switch with the context stored by the app's load extension, no model turn (OD-0116, OD-0122)

[MULTI-ACCOUNT] ENGINEERING DECISION: lead brief 2026-10-06 (research section 2). `PiSession` implements `IStandbyInjectionSession`. A standby launch loads a second, app-owned extension, `droppy-load.ts` (`PiCLI.LoadExtensionSource`, installed beside `droppy-gate.ts`), which registers `/droppy-load <file>` and stores the file's text with `pi.sendMessage({ customType: "droppy-handoff", content, display: false }, { triggerTurn: false })`; it is a separate file because the gate source is pinned byte for byte by existing tests. The standby runs behind the existing tool gate: its gate file says `finalReport: true`, which blocks every tool call, and `Send` on a waiting session throws; the handover (`EndStandby`) lets the next `Send` rewrite the gate for the user's real turn. Proof at run time, else fallback: the `get_commands` reply must list `droppy-load`; the `prompt` reply for `/droppy-load <file>` must be `success` with `disposition: "handled"`; `get_messages` must then hold a `droppy-handoff` custom message with exactly the loaded text. Any miss deletes the session file, stops Pi, marks that executable build as unavailable (`PiHistoryInjection`, so the host knows before asking the user anything) and falls back. Fail closed: `agent_start`, `turn_start`, an assistant `message_start`, `tool_execution_start` or `extension_ui_request` on the waiting session is a violation, never forwarded; the process is stopped and its session file deleted.
Unverified against a real Pi (not installed here, owner OK needed): the exact reply shapes above (`disposition`, `get_messages` fields), the `registerCommand` handler signature, and that `triggerTurn: false` on an idle session appends at once (open item in the research). The fake-stand-in tests prove the app side only. New tests: Services `PiStandbyTests`.

### ED-441: warm start for Copilot, Cursor, Grok, Devin, Antigravity (and the fallback of Pi and OpenCode); Command Code plain wait (OD-0116)

[MULTI-ACCOUNT] ENGINEERING DECISION: lead brief 2026-10-06 (research section 4): none of these CLIs can load history without a model turn. `ThreadAccountHost` now plans each service (`StandbyPlan`): Claude and the API/Local services Primed; Codex injected, falling back to deferred delivery; Pi injected, falling back to a warm start; Copilot, Cursor, Grok, Devin, Antigravity and OpenCode warm; Command Code (one process per turn) deferred with nothing opened early. A warm start (`WarmStandby`, `DeferredStandby.Warm`) opens the destination's process and session early through the same account-bound launch and sends nothing: no prompt exists, so nothing can act. Fail closed: any turn, message, reasoning, tool, plan, approval, question, head event or exit before the switch stops the session; the standby is then the plain deferred one. At the switch a healthy warm session becomes the conversation's session through `AdoptHandshakeSession(..., deferredContext)` (so it is the same session id, no second launch) and its first real turn carries the recorded context in front of the user's message, exactly like deferred delivery (no read-back, no resumed reply, no in-sync tick: the engine sees `StandbyKind.Deferred`). A start that fails, or is cancelled, is stopped and falls back to deferred delivery. Unverified against real CLIs: that `Start()` of each of these sessions sends no prompt and reports a session id without one (read from the code: ACP `session/new`, Copilot `session.create`, `agy` stream-json init); Antigravity's start waits up to its own 30 second timeout for the CLI's init line, in the background, and then falls back. New tests: Services `WarmStandbyTests`, App `WarmStandbyHostTests` (offline scripted sessions).

### ED-442: the two known gaps of deferred delivery closed (OD-0116, OD-0120)

[MULTI-ACCOUNT] ENGINEERING DECISION: (1) The "finish the reply?" (mid-reply) card was asked even when the destination is deferred and ignores the answer. `HandshakeMachine.HardLimitAsync` now adds that question only after the destination is known and only when it can continue a reply (`IDeferredDeliveryHost.DeliversDeferred` for services with no early standby, plus the cached run-time check `ResolveDeliversDeferredAsync`: a Codex or Pi build that cannot hold history, a standby already discarded); the question keeps its place in the card. When every account is out and there is no destination the card is asked as before. Residual: for the first limit on a Pi or Codex build whose capability is not yet known and cannot be known offline (Pi is learned by trying, then cached per executable build; a Claude whose gate later fails) the card can still be asked once and its answer is then ignored by the deferred fallback; no owner call needed, recorded only. (2) The held context survived only in memory, so an app restart before the first real turn lost it. It is now also written to `deferred-handoff.txt` in the thread's own folder (first line the account id, then the context; atomic temp-and-move like the other handoff files), read back on the first turn after a restart only when the thread is bound to that same account, and deleted when delivered or when another session is adopted. Tests: Core `HandshakeInjectedStandbyTests` (card), App `DeferredHandoffPersistenceTests`.

### ED-443: OpenCode waits with the context stored by a no-reply message on its own server, ACP session loads it at the switch (OD-0116, OD-0122)

[MULTI-ACCOUNT] ENGINEERING DECISION: lead brief 2026-10-06 (research section 3). The run-time check: `OpenCodeHistoryInjection.OpenApiSupportsNoReply` reads the running `opencode serve` OpenAPI document (`GET /doc`) and requires `noReply` on `POST /session/{id}/message`, in its request body or in a schema it refers to; the verdict is cached per executable build, and anything else (no server, no `noReply`, not that document) is false and the standby falls back to a warm start (ED-441). When it holds, `OpenCodeInjectionSession` (a `ProviderSession` that is only a waiting standby until the handover) creates a session on the server (`POST /session`), stores the context with a `noReply` text message, reads it back (`GET /session/{id}/message`) and requires the exact text; a miss deletes the session and falls back. The ACP session the conversation actually uses is opened only at the handover (`EndStandbyAsync`): the server stops (the stored session stays on disk) and the ACP session loads that id (`session/load` through `ResumeID`), whose reported id must be the same; a failure at that point is a handover failure and the host delivers the context the deferred way. `IStandbyInjectionSession.EndStandby` therefore became `EndStandbyAsync`, and `InjectedStandbySession.PrepareForAdoptionAsync` turns a failed handover into a deferred standby instead of an exception. No model turn can run on a standby: only a no-reply message is ever sent to the server.
UNVERIFIED and the weakest of the three injections: the research could not confirm that OpenCode v2.0.24's server accepts `noReply` or that a session created over HTTP is loadable by ACP `session/load` in another process; the real server launcher (`opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 0`, address read from its output) and the HTTP shapes are written from the documentation only and have no real run behind them. Every step is gated by the check and by read-back, and every miss falls back, so a wrong guess costs a warm start, not a turn. A real OpenCode run (owner OK, like R4) should confirm it before the owner relies on it. New tests: Services `OpenCodeStandbyTests`, App `OpenCodeStandbyHostTests` (fake server, fake ACP session).

No CLI/network/model, no existing test edits, no ledger byte normalization.


### ED-446: retire injected sessions that start after cancellation

[T19][MULTI-ACCOUNT][LIFECYCLE] OD-0116. Confirmed with a gated injection fake that ignores cancellation during startup: cancelling StartAsync released the still-unstarted session, but its later startup completion made it live again with no owner. Retain and observe the start task; after every failed/cancelled start, discard again when startup finishes and always stop the session even if deletion fails. The retained task is observed even if completion races the first release. InjectedStandbyCancellationReviewTests was red (late cleanup never occurred) before repair. Revised implementation: 20/20 injection, consent and traceability cases passed in the combined 36/36 run with OpenCode handover tests. No real CLI/network/model, existing tests unchanged, ledger prefix preserved.


### ED-447: a stopped OpenCode handover cannot publish a live session

[T19][MULTI-ACCOUNT][LIFECYCLE] OD-0116. Confirmed with a fake server and gated ACP startup: Stop during EndStandbyAsync did not reach the in-flight ACP object, and the completed start was then published as live; a cancelled token was ignored too. Keep the starting session owned, stop it on cancellation or Stop, recheck cancellation after startup, and guard publication against Stop with the existing lock. Discard also releases a pending ACP launch. OpenCodeStandbyHandoverReviewTests: both cases red before repair; afterward 2/2 plus all 14 unchanged OpenCodeStandbyTests cases pass (combined injection/OpenCode/traceability run 36/36). No real process/network/model, no existing test or ledger-byte edits.


### ED-448: standby guards cover compaction and the discard window

[T19][MULTI-ACCOUNT][SAFETY] OD-0116/OD-0122. Confirmed at sentinel transports (no process/pipe/network/model): Compact on a waiting Codex or Pi reached RPC/stdio instead of rejecting it. Those commands can run model compaction. Also, Codex clears standbyActive while thread deletion awaits acknowledgement; Send accepted a new turn during that discarding window. Guard Compact on both services and guard Codex Send while standbyDiscarding as well as standbyActive. StandbyControlReviewTests: all five cases red before repair, all five green afterward. Complete focused Services validation: 58/58 passed, including all 14 added review cases and unchanged injection, OpenCode, warm-start and traceability cases. Existing tests and assertions remain byte-identical; original mixed-line-ending ledger prefix retained.

### ED-454: link-up A engine behind ILinkPort (T17 MA-3b-E1)

ENGINEERING DECISION: LinkEngine serves the job-0 port, keeps ordered explicit per-thread links, checks completed primary answers through CheckAnswerAsync (stable answer id deduplicates), and streams independent text-only check results. It never selects/pins/moves an account. Active, disabled, disconnected and out/capped targets cannot link or dispatch. Revocation, unlink, source change and disposal cancel preparation and running heads; late text is ignored. The supplied IConversationHeadHost must give connected account identities, current cap/out availability, full recorded context, cross-service confirmation and a verified no-tools runner. UI binding/completed-answer forwarding remain job W as the original seam specifies. Conservative choice: an out or disabled primary source also suspends checks; no work is sent while the source is unavailable. This is a restriction against the page's unqualified each-answer language, pending final integration review.

### ED-455: one-message parallel opinions and one Combine

ENGINEERING DECISION: OpinionsEngine implements IOpinionsPort with the active Answer plus each selected other account's Opinion; deduplicates targets, includes all connected services and every Local entry in EveryoneWithRoom, and refuses an invalid target before any dispatch rather than silently sending to a subset. Each head streams independently. Selection lives only in its round; no account/pin/pill route is changed. Failed, empty, cancelled or unavailable heads prevent Combine. Combine is reserved once at a time, uses the captured original account, includes each actual response and posts the page's byline pattern (<name> U+00B7 combined <N> answers). Once append is attempted it cannot be retried because an external host error could follow a successful append. Cancellation/disposal and source changes cancel pending confirmations/heads; snapshots are immutable. Completion is a stable task published before the first stream callback (independent reviewer found and reproduced the initial publication race).

Evidence: tests-first CS0246 for missing OpinionsEngine; adversarial publication regression red with 30 passing / 1 failing, fixed without changing assertion. Scoped Services link/opinion/boundary/publication/Traceability 31/31. Broad baseline Services !~Native completed: 4141 passed, 1288 failed, 52 skipped, total 5481 (Linux Windows-native/ICU/process/file watcher constraints); these are not accepted or hidden. Full Windows verification still required. Concrete fresh text-only account runner and OD-0120 persistence/presentation are next.


### ED-456: default-off cross-service consent and verified private text heads

ENGINEERING DECISION: ConversationTransferConsent asks before a conversation goes to any different service (OD-0120), with an unchecked Don't ask again checkbox. Only explicit accepted-and-checked consent persists. Persistence is narrowly scoped to directed source/destination service pairs, shared across link/opinion requests; new services and reverse directions still ask. Refusal/cancellation save nothing, corrupt preferences fail closed without overwriting, AskAgain revokes a pair, and no automatic switching or Handshake setting is enabled (OD-0116). Avalonia's real modal presenter has no default Send action; ownerless, dismissed and cancelled prompts cannot grant permission. Proposed copy beyond the owner's literal checkbox: Send this conversation?, Send conversation, Cancel, and the service names in the question; the locked page has no confirmation copy. OD-0120's explicit checkbox takes precedence over a generic switch convention.

AccountConversationHeadHost uses AccountSessionFactory with fresh context/account binding, removes Hydra/skill launch state, and invokes the existing verified restricted Claude or API/Local IsFinalReport boundary. Every head is private, streams complete text-so-far and stops without adoption. Primed/Injected/Deferred standby capability does not prove a tool-safe model turn: Codex/Pi/OpenCode/Copilot/Cursor (and other unverified CLI services) fail explicitly before launch; @all never silently drops them. This is the safe choice required by item 4; enabling those providers needs a verified no-tools turn. Startup/inter-turn action events also fail closed. API heads require app.ApiKeys.BindPrivate via the host's bindKeys callback; absence of shared rotation fails before dispatch. A pinned identity wrapper refuses all account fallback/move consent, forwards cost and disposes the rotation. Job W still owns view binding/live state/full context/atomic timeline append and must supply MainActor callbacks.

Core accounts/job-0/consent/Traceability 351/351; Services E1/standby/context-consent/Traceability 69/69; App dialog/modal lifecycle/Traceability 7/7 on Linux headless. The fake API stream never reaches HTTP, writes no credentials and proves selected-key cost, cap stop with stale HasRoom and no fallback. App build succeeded with Windows targeting enabled. Broad Linux baseline remains non-green; no Windows release claim.


### ED-457: context epochs, last completed answers and live caps

ENGINEERING DECISION: The required host Revision is a monotonic context/ownership epoch (transcript edits/resume, source/model/effort/endpoint/launch settings/pin/pill changes), invalidated with AccountsChanged; capacity changes use current rows. Both engines and the concrete runner capture/recheck it through confirmation, context load, dispatch, progress, completion and synthesis. Link source service identity is captured too. CheckCompletedAnswerAsync is the canonical real completed-answer notification: an enabled unchanged author may have just exhausted its cap, but only eligible checker targets receive turns. This supersedes ED-454's each-answer restriction for the canonical callback; CheckAnswerAsync retains its stricter source-room guard. Linked exposes eligible live accounts only while retaining explicit tap intent internally; explicit unlink removes the intent even when hidden/out. OpinionAnswer.Error carries failure/cancellation reasons through IOpinionsPort.

API rows must include the configured MonthlyCapUsd. Private shared routing forwards reported USD, but the existing KeySpendEstimator is otherwise unset: capped token-only APIs without an authoritative estimator verified for their selected model now fail before send. OpenRouter uses reported charged USD; E1 invents no rates. Live cap/pricing permission is rechecked at dispatch. Job W must supply real cap metadata, key routing and verified estimators, revision notifications, full context and an atomic deduplicated timeline append; integration contract is porting/first-release/multi-account-E1-integration.md. ### ED-461: RR-50 authoritative pricing boundaries and durable conservative USD caps (2026-10-07)

ENGINEERING DECISION: RR-50 is missing on engine-review 7b910406. OpenAICompatibleSession.cs:232,538-547 records ReportedCostUsd or an optional KeySpendEstimator, with no production estimator assignment; AppApiKeyRouting.cs:40 binds only rotation; ApiKeyPool.cs:119-120,290-302 checks/records spend after the request. Token-only replies thus do not consume normal per-account dollar caps and no shared pre-dispatch ceiling exists. OD-0114/0115 require per-account limits in this release; OD-0116/0120 consent remains authoritative. This implements a stop before an unpriceable or unaffordable request, not a new automatic consent setting.

The user's explicit 2026-10-07 network clarification supersedes the withdrawn RR-37/design-source message: use authoritative pricing APIs at runtime; for page-only providers supply a Windows-runnable official-page generator, cited dated schema/data with an explicit unfilled state; unknown prices must stop or ask before exceeding a USD cap. No design branch was merged, no rate invented, no provider pricing page fetched through a workaround. Cloud host restrictions prevent filling DeepSeek/Meta/Z.ai rates here. RR-50 remains BLOCKED for that data and Windows live accounting proof even though the conservative engine/generator path is delivered.

AUTHORITATIVE API CONTRACT, inspected 2026-10-07: https://github.com/OpenRouterTeam/typescript-sdk/tree/3c88d7075ba91b7b7fbca33073126873823131ed/src/models ; model.ts (exact model/context/top-provider output limits), publicpricing.ts (USD per-token prompt/completion; optional per-request fee, discount and conditional/extra billing), providerpreferences.ts (max_price prompt/completion USD per MILLION, request USD per request). Runtime capped OpenRouter requests read https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models without account credentials/cookies/redirects, bind only their exact model and constrain provider.max_price plus output tokens. Auto, conditional overrides, invalid discounts, unhandled extra charges and non-text billing are refused. No real current API price was retrieved by these tests. Ignoring a valid positive discount and using maximum rates for incomplete cache/total-only breakdowns is intentionally conservative; malformed or inconsistent receipts retain their hold.

PAGE DATA: ModelPriceCatalog binds exact case-sensitive service/model, official HTTPS host, finite nonnegative rates, dated source and hash. Default ModelPriceData/model-prices.json are schemaVersion 1, state unfilled, prices empty. generate-model-prices.py runs under Windows Python 3: inspect official captures, review exact cell coordinates/model identifiers/USD-per-million and billing quotes, then re-fetch all mapped sources before emitting JSON and compiled C#. Source URLs currently point to https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing , https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing/ , https://docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing ; the lead must verify canonical pages and complete reviewed mappings locally. There are no numeric overrides/default provider token rates. Missing fee evidence, ambiguous/spanned/tiered cells, changed layout, malformed/nonfinite amounts, unfilled mappings or fetch failures preserve old outputs. Missing authoritative input/output limits cannot authorize a capped request. Rows expire after 24 hours (future dates refused); regenerate/review/commit both outputs and rebuild daily/on pricing changes. A future runtime page-price updater needs separate review; until then expiry stops capped traffic. Generator/schema/commands are documented in Providers/Pricing/README.md.

BUDGET: Every production rotation forwards its shared budget. Before HTTP, ApiKeyPool atomically reserves a conservative full authoritative model input window and maximum output plus request fee against actual spend AND every pending hold. AccountKeyStore persists the hold in existing metadata, preserving old document shape when no holds exist. The active reservation does not revoke its own permission, while each new reservation still counts all holds; lowered caps, disabled/removed accounts, retired ownership, price expiry and transfer consent are rechecked at dispatch. Proven unsent cancellation releases its hold. A completed response settles the captured original key and send-month once, even after ownership changes; reported USD wins, otherwise the request's exact price snapshot estimates its tokens. Empty/partial/inconsistent usage, interrupted requests and uncertain server failures retain holds across restart/month changes. Unpriced uncapped receipts also remain unknown so enabling a finite cap later cannot grant free allowance. BudgetSince carries uncertainty separately from displayed known SpendSince, preserving all original no-price assertions. No automatic expiry or receipt reconciliation UI is claimed. The full model-window reservation can stop a small request early; no tokenizer guess silently authorizes it.

OVERLAP: core key pool/store and OpenAICompatibleSession are the engine surface. AppApiKeyRotation has one necessary Budget forwarding property (job W); E1's PinnedConversationKeyRotation is carried with that same forwarder, so private heads retain shared accounting without permitting another account. Merge with E1/W's host and wrappers rather than dropping either budget binding. RR-49's collector/Pi files remain the separately committed row. No views, owner-law files, existing tests, assertions, tolerances, SDK/package/project pins or actual credentials changed.

4. Final sweep, real bug on the owner's PC: PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is an app execution alias in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps; Windows refuses PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST for it and for the packaged pwsh.exe (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, probe), so the terminal panel and run_command could not start. ProcessLauncher is unchanged (ADR-0002 / R-PROC-1: the child joins its job in the attribute list, never afterwards; a suspend-assign-resume variant was tried and withdrawn). LoginEnvironment.WhichLaunchable skips Store-packaged executables (\WindowsApps\ paths) and TerminalHost.WindowsShell and WindowsShellForCommands use it, so a non-Store pwsh or Windows PowerShell runs. Terminal, run_command and ProcessLauncher classes pass twice alone.

T44 retains the approved resting voice orb and composer light. The owner's latest instruction supersedes their previous always-running policy: decorative motion requests at most 60 frames per second on every display; it stops while the window is hidden, minimized, DWM-cloaked, fully covered, or not the foreground window. After 20 seconds without pointer/keyboard input in the foreground window, its speed eases to zero over 0.6 seconds. The next pointer movement or key starts a smooth 0.6-second ease-in from the preserved phase. Repeated input does not restart that ramp. The phase never replays time spent unavailable. Real UI transitions retain the display's full frame rate: orb state/spring/crossfade changes (.7-second settling window), composer CSS changes (.9-second settling window), wallpaper selection/theme transitions (.6-second settling window), and live non-rest voice state. Popover, slider and pill frame sources are unchanged.

One shared event-driven native availability/input source serves each window. WinEvents include foreground, minimize, show/hide, cloak, location and stacking-order changes. Fully covered means the window rectangle is covered by the union of visible opaque windows above it; transparent/layered windows are conservatively excluded. Routed pointer movement/press/wheel and key input refresh the activity deadline. There is no idle polling timer. One-shot wakes schedule the next ambient registration through the UI thread, where SendHandlerMessage is valid; the compositor does not request intervening frames merely to check a deadline. Detach synchronizes timer disposal with scheduling. The non-native renderer continues to support the existing injected frame-clock proofs; explicit host-policy tests cover unavailable/idle/resumed controls without changing reference fixtures or tolerances.

The application's glass is never explicitly invalidated by the ambient controllers.
