## ED-NEW-launch-fix

### Launch: program cache before the first link, kept across builds; hand-over not waiting for provider checks (lead's phase 2 brief, owner OD-0133, 2026-10-10)

Branch claude/launch-fix from 2eecff5ac (release base + T45 + T46 + T44, without f87ba24c9's awaited 8-variant warm-up). OD-0096, OD-0108's GPU and content readiness, OD-0113 (Boot B, its 1.8 s floor, the window shown only when ready) unchanged; no visual or shader-math change.

1. Install before the first link. GpuProgramCache.PrepareAtLaunch reads the adapter identity and every kept folder on a pool thread right after the storage paths are bound in Main (measured 20-26 ms, done at 60-740 ms, before Boot B's first frame). Marrow.UI.Port.AuroraBootGpu.ContextReady (set by Program, UI cannot name App) is called by AuroraBootHandler with each new GRContext, the context current, before Boot B draws with it, and installs the callbacks through GpuProgramCache.ForContext. Measured in every after-run: the first install is inside Boot B's first compositor draw (before: 1.4-6.3 s, after the hand-over on relaunch). A store not yet loaded reads a missing entry from its file (the only render-thread disk read, until Load ends); install reads the adapter itself when Prepare has not yet, so key.txt never lacks the machine. ENGINEERING DECISION: a hook object per context in the handler, never per frame.
2. Survives builds. The folder is KeyFolderName(GL_RENDERER, GL_VERSION): ANGLE names the adapter and driver in the renderer and its commit in the version, so a driver or ANGLE change still gets a new folder; the app build is no longer in the name. Each install rewrites key.txt naming the current build, and warm.txt still names the build whose warm-up completed, so IsWarm and the first-run screen after an update are unchanged (OD-0096). Entries are kept under a 16 MiB cap over all folders (Trim in Prepare, least recently used first; an entry read from disk and then found is touched on the pool once a process; about 0.7 MB a GPU today). MarkWarm's removal of other builds' folders is kept unchanged because EffortSliderJewelWarmupTests.A_completed_warm_up_keeps_only_this_builds_folders_made_on_this_machine pins it; with the build-free name the current GPU's folder is always the kept one, so it now removes only old-scheme folders and other adapters' folders last keyed by another build (reported to the lead, not changed). ANGLE and unloadable binaries, measured: all 131 kept binaries damaged (88 bytes-flipped, 43 cut to half); the launch ran, every entry handed back was rejected and compiled again (hits 9/20/34/41 against Puts 9/20/34/40 per phase), the next launch found them all (Puts 0-1), and Boot B's frames match the clean run (mean absolute difference 0.4/255, the same as clean against clean). A stale binary from another driver or ANGLE cannot be handed over: it lives in another folder.
3. OD-0133. AppModel.LaunchReady completes when Bootstrap reaches its provider refresh (recent documents, keychain, login environment and Hydra done); AppDelegate readies Boot B on whichever comes first, LaunchReady or the whole bootstrap, then still waits for the first-run preparation; a bootstrap that fails before it still never reveals the window; the bootstrap is awaited afterwards as before. The login environment read starts in Main (single-flight). No existing test pinned "Ready waits for the provider refresh": BootStageWindowTests.At_launch_the_main_window_waits_for_the_boot_sequence_which_waits_for_the_bootstrap scripts a bootstrap that never reaches the milestone and still passes unchanged; no test was retired. Added: AppModelLaunchReadyTests (ready while a provider's refresh is held, the refresh starting only after readiness, every provider's status arriving once it ends), BootLaunchReadyTests (B hands over at the milestone with the refresh never finishing). Soft status changes (OD-0076): the composer chip already crossfades its name and effort and the account capsule animates its states; ProviderStatusRow (the welcome checklist) cut, and now crossfades its status line and trailing control over 0.25 s (ease in-out; first build and reduce motion at once; the outgoing control takes no clicks), RootViewProviderRowTransitionTests.
4. No awaited 8-variant warm-up is brought back; nothing new runs on the critical path (Prepare is on the pool).
6. GpuWarmup.HoldIdle: while a hold answers true the idle fallback does not step, its 3 s cap included; Boot B holds from its start until Finish or its window closes (a hold whose stage is not visible holds nothing). WarmAsync (the first run's awaited preparation) is not held. GpuWarmupBootHoldTests.

Measured (owned Release publishes, copied T44 profile, --performance-profile; before = 2eecff5ac, two pairs): relaunch Ready 4787/4745 -> 844/891 ms, hand-over 4803/4748 -> 2316/2347 ms (the 1.8 s floor now decides it), hand-over WM_PAINT 1331/2381 -> 30/45 ms; cold after an update Ready 7006 -> 5203 ms with every program a hit before Ready. Remaining (fix 5, not done here): one to three programs miss the cache on every launch and compile on the render thread right after the hand-over (0.65, 0.82, 3.2 and 5.2 s in four runs), freezing B's grow and the UI thread's WM_PAINT; they are put again each launch, so their source changes between launches (UNRESOLVED which shader; the glass variant per shape count is the likely one). Cold launches vary 7.3-13.2 s to Ready in both builds, dominated by first-run compiles.

### ED-NEW-launch-fix (A), round 2: the programs linked after the hand-over

Finding (native, owned Release publishes, copied T44 profile, cache folders diffed launch by launch and every new entry decompressed to the HLSL ANGLE compiled): no shader text varies between launches; no literal, size, culture or seed is baked into one. The earlier "every launch" was the second launch of a fresh profile each time: on one profile the new entries were 4, 4, then 0 (after build) and 1, 2, 0, 0 (diagnostic build). Each new entry was the same effect linked by Skia into another program: the glass material whole or faded (a paint alpha below 255 wraps the effect in an alpha modulation), open or under the hand-over's content clip (BootStageWindow.Apply's rounded RectangleGeometry, applied by Skia as a coverage mask; a worker drawing under PushGeometryClip found exactly those programs, PushClip(RoundedRect) made an analytic one no window had), a lone rounded rectangle with its inside drawn apart; plus small gradient/image/fill programs under the same mask. Which a launch meets depends on where the fade and the clip stand when each piece first draws. Cost per link: six merged glass pieces 2.7-3.0 s, a lone piece 0.2 s, the rest 3-11 ms, all on the render thread.

Fix: GlassVariantPreparation draws every glass variant (1 to 8 pieces, whole/faded, open/clipped, a lone piece as a rounded rectangle and a capsule: 36) through the material's own Draw (GlassProgramVariants; GlassMaterial and its Backdrop become partial, no other change to GlassMaterial.cs) on GpuBootPreparation's independent context, started at the first GPU context's arrival, awaited by nothing and not in the first run's registry; a root marker (build, GPU folder, count) makes later launches of the build do nothing. Against a cache filled only by real launches every variant drawn so was a hit. GlassVariantPreparationTests. Item B (the shader rewrite) not done: after this no relaunch links a glass program on the render thread.

Measured (two fresh profiles, cold then two relaunches, app in the foreground): relaunch render-thread links after the hand-over 8/0 and 8/0 (3-9 ms each, gradient/image/fill programs under the clip mask; none glass) against a 2.7-2.9 s glass link in the first relaunch before; max Boot B draw gap 59/120 and 50/48 ms, not compiles: an early Boot B draw of 102 ms loading programs from the cache, 51-54 ms draws during the provider discovery, and the main window's WM_PAINT (46-53 ms) after the hand-over. Capture (content-based, 60 fps) between hand-over and finish: max still 34 ms on every relaunch (before: 2334 ms). Remaining: on a first launch with an empty cache the pass (54 s, all on the worker) reaches six pieces only after the hand-over has linked them on the render thread (2.4-2.6 s, twice per cold launch).

First opens (parked for later work, not on this branch): measured with the interaction recorder, the first effort-popover open of a session looks up 18 programs (27 ms of its first render frame from the disk cache; 119 ms of compiles after a cold launch that never opened it) and JIT takes 244-623 ms on the UI thread; GR-1's knob and liquid warm-up programs are not the ones the popover draws with (destination read, the card's round clip, gradient text), and SkiaSharp cannot load a Skia program by its cache key, so a warm-up has to draw the popover itself. A prototype that draws the real panel on its card once, offscreen, through the compositor's snapshot on the window's GPU context in an idle moment (8 headless tests) is kept at E:/Droppy/work/scratch/claude-launch/parked/first-open-warmup.patch, unmeasured natively.
## ED-NEW-native-fix
2026-10-10 - Native test repairs after the merged gate (claude/native-fix, base 2eecff5ac). Design wins (OD-0126): every replacement assertion is equal or stricter; no foreground or covered-target guard was removed or softened.
1. SETTINGS FIXTURE PLACEMENT (8 WindowManagerNativeTests). Since T45 (ED-NEW-T45 part 23) the Settings HWND is owned by Main and so always above it. The native fixture still placed Settings on Main's origin (96,96), covering Main's caption zones and bottom edge, so WindowManagerNativePointer.GuardStart ("covered or no longer the foreground test window") and the bottom-edge search correctly refused. The gate labelled these a foreground precondition; they failed deterministically on the merged head and passed on the pre-T45 base. WindowManagerNativeSubject now places Settings clear of Main (to its right, else below it, 24 px apart, inside the working area) and throws NATIVE_PRECONDITION when the working area cannot hold both. The pointer guard is unchanged; its message now names the target, foreground and covering HWND and the three rectangles.
2. CAPTION MENU MAXIMIZE (A_real_caption_right_click_opens_a_menu_with_each_windows_native_capabilities). T45 part 20 lets Settings maximize while it cannot be resized. The assertion that Maximize follows canResize is replaced by: Maximize is enabled in the native menu of both windows, both windows report CanMaximize, and CanResize is still true for Main only (SC_SIZE unchanged).
3. REOPENED DIFF POPOVER (DiffPopoverNativeTests). ED-196 reproduced upstream defect 67 (a reopen onto another anchor left the new show without its monitors, so Escape and an outside tap did not dismiss it). ED-NEW-T45 part 11 records that the owner's rule that every popover closes on Escape and on an outside press authorizes the shared lifecycle and that the old unusable state is not an acceptance target; DiffPopoverCoordinator no longer completes the stale close while the popup is open. The native step that asserted the stuck state is replaced by its inverse and extended: after a reopen while shown, the monitors are still set, Escape closes the popover and is swallowed, a second reopen is closed by an outside tap, a third by its flag, and a fresh show still has its monitors. The recording-presenter oracle of ED-196 is untouched.
4. EFFORT SLIDER CADENCE (Both_retained_slider_sources_keep_sixty_updates_per_second_without_refresh_drift). T44's ambient policy (AmbientWindowState) runs the track only while its window is the foreground one, uncovered; the test waited for IsActive only. It now brings its window to the front with WindowManagerNativeForeground.Acquire (which refuses with NATIVE_PRECONDITION) and checks the front again after the measured seconds. The 174-183 assertions are unchanged and the test still fails: with the front held the track measured 97 updates in 3 s on a 240 Hz display, because AmbientMotionController.Request waits out the rest of each 1/60 s interval on a timer whose resolution is a whole frame (32 a second). That is a production finding, not fixed here (the pinned AmbientTimelineTests cap the requests at 60 Hz, so the pacing has to move onto the refreshes, aligned with AnimationTimeline's counted refreshes); the knob's GPU-frame count is also phase-dependent (it failed on 4 of 8 runs of the pre-T44 base).
5. REVERT POPOVER ESCAPE (TimelineRowsNativePopoverTests). Intermittent on the merged head (the click lands on the scroller beside the revert disc; 0 of 8 failures on the base); no code cause was found. Only the failure message gained the scroller's viewport and extent.

## ED-NEW-frame-pacing

2026-10-10 - Decorative (ambient) motion paced on the display's refreshes, never on a timer (claude/native-fix). Amends ED-NEW-T44's 60 Hz cap in mechanism only: the cap, the unseen stop, the 20 s idle stop and the 0.6 s eases are unchanged, and no assertion, tolerance or reference was changed.

1. PROBLEM. AmbientMotionController.Request waited out the rest of each 1/60 s interval on a TimeProvider timer and a UI-thread hop. Windows timers fire on a whole-frame grid, so the wake often missed its slot and landed on the next one: EffortSliderNativeFrameTests measured 97 track updates in 3 s on this PC's 240 Hz display (expected 174-183). The new headless test AmbientPacedTimelineTests reproduced it (red at f8e73ece8): the track drew every 2nd refresh at 60 Hz, every 3rd at 120 Hz, every 5th at 240 Hz, and the knob on other refreshes than the track. That second fault also made the knob render twice per slot, once for each invalidation (the knob GPU-frame assertion failed 4 of 8 runs on the pre-T44 base).
2. DECISION. AmbientRefreshPacer (src/Marrow.UI/Port), one per compositor (AmbientRefreshPacer.For). Every ambient source of that compositor asks it at each refresh tick. The tick's identity is the compositor's CompositionNow, or the frame's time for the main-thread title drift, so every caller in one tick gets the same answer. Refreshes are counted relatively, on a grid locked to the ticks. A tick that comes earlier than the grid moves the grid at once; a later one moves it 1/32 of the way. DWM's vblank timestamp is not used as a clock: on this PC it was 64 s off the Stopwatch clock. A slot is every n-th refresh when 1/60 s is a whole number n of refreshes (AnimationTimeline.RefreshesPer: 4 at 240 Hz, 2 at 120 Hz, 1 at 60 Hz). Otherwise slot = floor(refresh / (refreshes per 1/60 s)), which gives gaps of 2 or 3 refreshes at 144 and 165 Hz and is balanced: any run of L slots spans the same number of refreshes as any other, to within one. A pause of more than 0.25 s, a clock that goes back, or a changed period (re-read at most once a second) starts the count again, and the first refresh after it is a slot.
3. CONTROLLER. The timer is gone. Request now only answers whether the motion has stopped (unavailable, or idle past the ease); a stopped source registers for no frame until AmbientWindowState.Changed wakes it, as before. Pace(tick, now, interaction) returns Go (advance now), Wait (register for the next refresh and draw nothing) or Stop. Interactions are not paced, but their refreshes are counted, so the slots go on from the count afterwards. RenderFrameSource's ticker, the composer light, the voice orb, the wallpaper and the title drift (MorphingTextBlock, on its own main-thread pacer) handle Wait by asking for the next refresh.
4. ONE RENDER PER REFRESH. The track, the knob, the orb, the light and the wallpaper of one compositor share one pacer, so they advance on the same refresh, and overlapping areas (the knob over the track) are drawn once. An ambient render AnimationTimeline with an interval of 1/60 s or less draws at every frame its paced source delivers (PacedBySource). Counting or timing the interval a second time skipped slots: at 144 Hz a slot is 2 or 3 refreshes, never 1/60 s.
5. SAFETY. With no known refresh period, slots are due on a 1/60 s grid, at most 1 ms early (ED-117 (2), ED-232). Four net early ticks show the period is not this display's (for example, a window on another monitor); for the rest of that run the period is not trusted and the same 1/60 s grid is used, so the rate never runs above 60 Hz.
6. COST. While the motion runs (foreground, uncovered, within 20.6 s of input), each ambient source handles one compositor tick per refresh. On a Wait refresh it does no drawing and allocates nothing. A stopped source asks for no frame, so idle CPU after the 20 s stop is unchanged. The title drift's Wait refreshes are main-thread frame requests (AvaloniaFrameSource), only while it drifts.
7. EVIDENCE. AmbientRefreshPacerTests checks 60/120/144/165/240 Hz with tick jitter of 0.2-1.9 ms: 180 slots in 3 s, gaps of floor or ceiling of rate/60, balanced runs, at most 60 slots in any second, and identical decisions for two callers in one tick. Further cases: 239.96 Hz for a minute (every gap 4), a source that joins later, a missed refresh, a pause, no period, a wrong period, and the controller (no timer; interaction; idle and unseen stop). AmbientPacedTimelineTests runs two timelines through the real compositor ticks at the five rates: the same refreshes, 180 updates per 3 s, balanced. EffortSliderNativeFrameTests.Both_retained_slider_sources_keep_sixty_updates_per_second_without_refresh_drift passed 8 of 8 runs at 240 Hz (period 4.166-4.167 ms), with track and knob counts of 179-183 in its 3 s window (180, 180, 181, 181, 183, 181, 179, 181), and the two counts equal in every run.
## ED-NEW-gate-fixes
### ED-NEW-gate-fixes-1: model list rows begin 78 down, not 38 (OD-0126, owner task T46 model search)
EffortSliderPanelTests.The_header_is_a_back_chevron_and_select_model_with_the_source_fonts_colours_and_spacing pinned the source layout in which the model rows begin 4 pt under the "Select model" header (y 38). Owner task T46 asked for a model/maker search field between the header and the rows (ModelListSearch.cs: a 28 pt capsule with margins 4 / 4 / 4 / 8), so the rows now begin at y 78. Design wins (OD-0126). The old single assertion on the scroll offset is replaced, in the same commit, by stricter assertions: the header assertions are unchanged, the search field's rectangle is exact (x 10, y 42, width list-20, height 28, 4 under the header), and the rows begin exactly 78, which is exactly the field's bottom plus its 8 pt bottom margin. No tolerance changed (0.5 as before).
### ED-NEW-gate-fixes-2: the Settings preview composer centres its contents as the real composer does (OD-0132)
ComposerPreviewPixelsTests.The_restated_ring_chip_end_and_send_ink_draw_as_the_real_controls_do and ComposerPreviewTests.At_472_the_preview_is_laid_out_as_a_real_composer_of_the_same_width compare the preview with the real composer and were red on the merged tree because T46 (owner decision OD-0132) centred every real composer control and the one-line text on the composer's vertical centre while ComposerPreview still bottom-aligned them: a REAL regression in production, not a stale pin. Fixed in src/Marrow.App/Port/Settings/ComposerPreview.cs; the comparison tests pass UNCHANGED (tolerances, expected values and pixel thresholds as before). The preview now: centres the attach button (real: y 9 in the 46 pt pill), the control row and each control (the ring is its natural 25 high, not stretched to 28); applies the real column's ink-centred placeholder shift (ComposerTextView.PlaceInk) to the placeholder, the typed words and the caret; draws the control row unrounded (ComposerView.ShowControls) with its trailing edge exact (a whole-pixel TrailingHost column, because the Grid rounds a fractional Auto column to the nearest pixel and the overflow moved the ring and send by that fraction); and keeps the paperclip's natural size unrounded (ComposerAttachButton). The one assertion that pinned the preview's own old rectangle, ComposerPreviewTests.cs:129 `new Rect(8, H - 36, 34, 28)`, is replaced by the stricter-equal exact value of the new design `new Rect(8, (H - 28) / 2, 34, 28)` (= 8, 9, 34, 28 in the 46 pt pill), with no tolerance, and it is still compared with the real attach button's X and Y exactly two lines later. Design wins (OD-0126, OD-0132).
### ED-NEW-gate-fixes-3: an outside press anywhere in the owner window dismisses a presented popover (T45 regression fixed in production)
CzControlsTests.Menu_popup_flips_at_the_window_edge_and_an_actual_outside_click_dismisses_it was red on the merged tree: T45 replaced Avalonia's light-dismiss overlay (a transparent layer over the whole window) with an owner-window pointer handler (PopoverHost.BeginPresentation / Follow) so that the close animation runs, but Avalonia routes a press to the element it hits and to no element when it hits none, so a press on a bare part of a window (here a template that draws no background, the click at the top right where no control is) never reached the handler and the popover stayed open. A real regression, so the PRODUCTION code is fixed and the test is UNCHANGED: while a dismissible popover is presented, PopoverDismissSurface (src/Marrow.UI/Port/PopoverDismissSurface.cs) sits in the owner's overlay layer, draws nothing, and is hit only where nothing else under the pointer is (ICustomHitTest, the hit test of everything but dismiss surfaces); the handler already there then sees the press and starts the popover's own close transition. A press on a control, the anchor or the card is hit as before, so the click-through the T45 handler allows is kept, and so are the close animation and Escape. It is removed when the popover closes, and a window without an overlay layer behaves as before. The fallback "change the fixture to a realistic background" was not needed.
### ED-NEW-gate-fixes-4: the voice rig delivers 60 Hz frames through a running transition (no assertion changed)
MountedVoiceCountdownTests (3), RenderedVoiceCountdownTests (8), MountedVoicePreparationTests (2) and MountedVoiceDownloadNoteTests (1) were red on the merged tree for one reason. T46 made the voice pill's motion keep its progress across stalled frames (VoicePill.cs:70 LookMotion(this, preserveFrameProgress: true); LookMotion.Step moves a transition's start when two frames are more than 50 ms apart), so that the pill never snaps after a stall; that is intended (the owner's no-snap bar) and VoicePill and LookMotion are unchanged. The rig, VoiceComposerRig.Elapse, jumped the clock and delivered ONE frame for the whole step (0.8 s, 269.99 s, 275 s, 280 s), which a running app never does, so the opening of the pill treated the whole step as one stalled frame and never progressed. Elapse now behaves as a display does: while a voice pill is in a transition (VoicePill.IsMoving, with a frame wanted) it advances the clock and delivers a frame every 1/60 s, for up to the first 2 s of the call (every transition of the voice surfaces ends within a second), and only then jumps the remaining steady time in one step; a call in which no pill moves is one jump exactly as before (a first version stepped whenever any frame was wanted and changed the timing of ComposerDictationWithdrawTests.A_cancel_keeps_the_caret_riding_and_fades_it_after_the_words_have_gone, so it is limited to the transitions the stall rule is about) (the exact total, in ticks, is unchanged, so the tests' tick-exact boundaries such as 269.99 / 270.01 and the 10 s boundary hold). No assertion, expected value or tolerance of the four test classes is changed.
### ED-NEW-gate-fixes-5: a field note never runs under the voice pill (OD-0130 F5, OD-0132)
The owner's F5 complaint (text running under the opening voice pill and through its label) was reproduced frame by frame at 60 Hz: the text is the voice note shown in the composer's field on first use (VoiceNotes.LocalPrivacy, "Voice typing runs on this computer ... recordings are never kept", 5 s), not the placeholder and not dictation. Production DID hold the text column in (its right edge 10 pt before the pill, the 24 pt fade, OD-0130 / V-12.6), but the note line (VoiceNoteLine) laid its words and link out in a horizontal StackPanel, which measures its children without a limit: the words took their full width, ignored the column's width (the TextBlock's CharacterEllipsis never applied) and drew past the column's right edge, where neither the layout nor the column's opacity mask clears them (376 to 1318 px of note text inside the pill's rectangle in frames 4 to 6, at 100/125/150/200 %). Fix: the line is now a NoteRow panel that gives the words only the width left after the mark and the link, so a long note ends in an ellipsis inside the column and the link keeps its width. The pill's own label is one label (Listening...), not a crossfade: the garbled "are nevergke" was the note drawn through it. Test first (red 7/7 before the fix, green after): ComposerPillClearsTextTests renders every frame at 60 Hz of the pill opening for 0.8 s and of its closing (Cancel) for 0.8 s at 100/125/150/200 %, light and dark, with the privacy note and with a draft that fills the line, and asserts for each frame (a) the text column ends no later than the pill's left edge and (b) the column, drawn and not drawn, differs in no pixel inside the pill's rectangle (the pill's own 2 device pixel rim excluded: its antialiasing shifts by one pixel with any sibling's layer, and a real overlap is hundreds of pixels).
The composer outline's 1 pt (ComposerView.PlaceInlineComposer, ED-NEW-T46-centre) is unchanged and is NOT a jump when voice turns on or off: voice is fixed when the composer is made (VoiceFeature.Enabled). The outline moves only when the composer changes between a single line and a wrapped or auxiliary-content state (the controls change between centre and bottom alignment at the same instant, so the orb stays on the approved window coordinates). Removing the shift keeps the outline still but moves the orb and pill 1 pt off the approved window coordinates, failing ComposerVoicePillT46Tests.Inline_placement_preserves_the_approved_pill_and_orb_window_coordinates and ComposerCentreT46Tests at 1.5 (text ink 320.5 against centre 319.5); that is an owner decision and was not taken here.
### ED-NEW-gate-fixes-6: the composer outline's 1 pt glides with the height instead of stepping when the text wraps or unwraps (OD-0132, owner no-snap bar)
CAUSE (measured frame by frame at 60 Hz, 100/125/150/200 %): ComposerView.PlaceInlineComposer (ED-NEW-T46-centre) put the single-line outline 1 pt down with a RenderTransform of 1 or 0 chosen in ArrangeOverride, so the outline's bottom edge (and top edge, on top of the height's own glide) stepped 1 pt in ONE frame when the text wrapped (the first frame, because the text view takes its height at once) and when it unwrapped (the last frame, when the clip reaches one line). At 125 % the unwrap never re-ran the arrange, so the pill came to rest 1 pt off the fresh single-line rest (236, not 237): a second, resting-state defect of the same cause. SOURCE FACT (ComposerView.swift:599-604): Swift animates only the clip's height, on .smooth(duration: 0.28) (not while the window is being dragged); it has no 1 pt placement, which is the port's own T46 centring.
FIX (ENGINEERING DECISION): the resting rectangles are exactly as before (single line: view and outline 1 pt down; wrapped: not; contents' window places and places in the view unchanged). The view keeps carrying the contents' point (`rest`, flipped with their alignment as before). The plate (the glass shape, ComposerView.Child) carries the rest of the outline's point on an AnimatedScalar driven toward where the text is going (ComposerTextColumn.WillBeSingleLine, true the moment the text view's height says one line) on Animation.Smooth(0.28), the same curve and length as ApplyHeight, and with no glide where the height does not glide (no live-resize state, window being dragged, Reduce Motion, no frame clock); the plate's glide is cancelled on the contents by a counter-translation of the same size on the body (`layers`), so no control or text moves. The first showing is the state as it is. Left as it was, by decision: the text's own ink-centring shift (ComposerTextView.PlaceInk, 0.44 pt at 100 %) changes with the text itself on the frame the second line appears, where the line also reflows.
Test first (red 4/4 before, green 4/4 after, twice): ComposerWrapTransitionT46Tests.The_outline_glides_when_the_text_wraps_and_unwraps_and_the_resting_rectangles_are_unchanged at 100/125/150/200 %, light and dark, wrap and unwrap, 40 frames each: the plate's bottom edge and its top edge net of the height never step more than 0.2 pt, never double back, the orb, send, attach and model chip never step more than half a device pixel and end where they began, and the resting plate bottoms are 1 pt apart and equal before and after a round trip. Unchanged and green: ComposerCentreT46Tests and ComposerVoicePillT46Tests (32 with the new test). ComposerVoiceCleanPillTests (173 of 470) fails with identical pixel coordinates on the tree without this change (checked on two cases), so it is not caused by it. Evidence: E:\Droppy\work\scratch\lead\composer-shots3\ (10-frame contact sheets, wrap and unwrap, 100 % dark and light).
## ED-NEW-stutter-fix
Steady-state stutter work (coordinator Phase 2, 2026-10-10, worktree wt/cl/stutter on 2eecff5ac). Scope: items 1, 2, 5 and 4 of the stutter analysis; item 3 (warm-up), item 6 (popover close teardown, PopoverHost) and items 7-8 are out of scope here. No visual change: glass pixels, layout and animation curves are those of 2eecff5ac; no assertion, tolerance or reference was edited.
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-1
Interaction recorder (PORT-ONLY, measurement). InteractionProbe (Marrow.UI) times named UI jobs (spans of 1 ms or more) and reports each drawn frame's merged dirty rect through the existing GlassMaterial debug-events proxy; it costs one static bool test when off. InteractionRecorder (Marrow.App) is on only when the Release performance profile root holds interaction-script.json: it then sets Avalonia's diagnostic switch before setup, listens to the Avalonia diagnostic meter, probes render ticks per TopLevel with a composition custom visual, runs a 2 ms UI-stall ping on a high-resolution waitable timer, and records per interaction the GPU program cache writes/misses, JIT-compiled-method and GC deltas, spans over 16 ms by name, ticks over 33 ms and dirty area (optional allocation sampling by type through the runtime's GCAllocationTick). The tour drives effort open/close, the model picker (open, scroll, search, close), Settings, Hydra and composer typing through the app's own controls and events; it never sends a message and restores the composer text. It writes interactions.json. Without the script nothing changes (the quiet-window measurement runs as before).
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-2
Model lists fill in over frames. Measured before: a ~480-row ModelList took 50-54 ms to build and 20-65 ms to lay out in the frame it opened (UI stalls up to 71 ms; OpenRouter profile 112-290 ms). DeferredRows puts in at once the rows of the first two 440-point screens and the rest in a 2 ms slice per frame, each the same control in the same place as before; until the last is in, one hit-test-invisible spacer of exactly the pending rows' height (with their spacing) stands for them, so the extent, the scrollbar and every realised row's place are final from the first frame. A search, an arrow or Return key, or a viewport reaching to within a screen of the spacer realises the rows first (so search folds, keyboard selection and scroll-into-view see every row). A list whose remainder is under one screen, or one with no frame clock bound, is built whole as before. The OpenRouter picker still makes every PickerRow with the picker (Rows, colours and selection unchanged) and only defers adding them to the list; its count labels (one per distinct count) are made when a count is first shown, inserted in count order, for lists of 100 models or more. Tests first: ModelListDeferredFillTests, OpenRouterPickerDeferredFillTests.
Not done, with evidence: keeping the effort popover's panel alive across opens. A warm effort open measured no UI stall and render ticks under 10 ms, with the panel's build at about 0.05 ms; its first-open cost is JIT and GPU program compilation (item 3). Keeping it would add stale hover and re-attach paths for no measurable gain.
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-3
The glass backdrop and blur surfaces are created budgeted on the GPU context (SKSurface.Create(gpu, true, info)), so a texture a popover's grow or shrink releases returns to Skia's scratch pool for the next surface instead of being freed and reallocated. Sizes, formats and pixels are unchanged; oversizing the surfaces to reuse them across sizes was rejected because it would move the clamp and blur edges.
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-4
Glass synchronisation on layout passes. Measured before: composer typing synchronised each of the main window's glass pieces on every layout pass, about 45 synchronisations per keystroke (1,936 for 43 keys). A lone piece (drawing its own material, in no container, in a window whose renderer step is installed) now skips a layout pass when what changes without an event is as it was at its last synchronisation: its render transform's value, its fill's colour, its tint as resolved (the accent), its having no container, and its material's copy of its composition visual (offset, size, opacity, visibility and the rest). Everything else it is drawn with raises its PropertyChanged or ActualThemeVariantChanged, which queue it as before; any difference queues it at that layout pass exactly as before, so computed glass state and its timing are unchanged. Containers, pieces drawn by a container and windows without the renderer step keep every layout pass. A first version that also watched the piece's own transform in place made the glass follow an in-place transform at once instead of at the next layout pass; GlassMaterialKeptBackdropReviewTests (a piece returning into a clipped viewport) then read a stale kept backdrop beside the clip, so that version was withdrawn rather than change when the glass moves. Not done: caching container piece lists (their regions follow every piece's place, so their layout-pass synchronisation stays). Test first: GlassMaterialSyncCoalesceTests.
### ED-NEW-stutter-fix measurements (Release, copied profile, 3 rounds, same machine)
Recorder: interactions.json from tour runs of the 2eecff5ac-based build (before) and 0b761d21a plus probe counters (after). Claude profile, rounds 1-3: model picker open UI stall 51/47/50 ms (modellist.build 50/39/52 ms) became 0/21/0 ms (build 6/2/1 ms), ticks under 33 ms; picker scroll and search unchanged in kind (search keeps a 20-57 ms stall from its fold pass); effort, Settings and Hydra warm opens unchanged (their round-1 costs are JIT and GPU program compilation, item 3). OpenRouter profile: picker open stall 112/127/290 ms became 41/58/62 ms. Composer typing under equal conditions: glass synchronisations 2,024 became 1,848 per 43 keys; about 90% of layout-pass synchronisations come from containers and pieces drawn by a container, which keep the layout pass.
Found while measuring, not changed here: HandshakeCapsuleHost.Advance rebuilds its ghost AccountCapsule whenever the ghost's style differs from the slot capsule's, and a ghost made for a plain account is always "plain", so while an incoming account is plain and the slot shows a pill the ghost is removed and remade on every Advance (641-752 glass attachments per 43 keys in the tours where it occurs). The OpenRouter profile's allocation storm (1-6 GB per interaction, gen2 collections) comes from ModelShades observing each cold model separately, each observe publishing a full palette snapshot and saving it.
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-5
Handshake ghost made once per incoming account (Round 3, item 1). HandshakeCapsuleHost.Advance compared the ghost's style with the slot capsule's, but a plain account's ghost is "plain" beside a pill (and a pill's ghost is style "1" beside a slot with no capsule), so the ghost AccountCapsule, glass and all, was removed and remade on every Advance of a running handshake: each frame and each composer keystroke. The host now remakes the ghost only when the incoming account or the slot's capsule style changes, or when the accounts were updated and the content's style differs. Test: HandshakeGhostOnceTests (30 Advance calls, one ghost, the content asked for no more). Composer typing in the Claude profile: max UI tick 62.8 ms before, 12.9 ms after.
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-6
Palette observations queued together publish once (Round 3, item 2). ModelShades.Resolve observes each cold model as its row is made; each observation was an actor job that published a whole snapshot and saved it (snapshot-v1.json): 487 snapshots, about 1 GB/s of allocation, while the OpenRouter picker opened. PaletteEngine.Observe now counts the observations queued; the last of them to run publishes once (one snapshot, one save, one Changed), with the same snapshot and the same saved bytes as one observation of them all; an observation on its own still publishes when it is done. ModelShades still observes at once per model (PaletteColdLookupTests pins one post per observe), so the coalescing is on the engine's actor. Test: PaletteObserveBatchTests (200 queued observes behind a held actor: 2 publishes, equal digest and equal saved bytes).
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-7
SwiftString.Split walks Characters in place (Round 3, item 3). The Settings and Hydra first-open allocations (0.4-1 GB, 24 UI ticks over 33 ms) were not made by Settings or Hydra: dotnet-stack snapshots during the tour showed the background TokenHistoryScanner splitting each session file's head and tail by "\n" through SwiftString.Split, which made one string for every Character of the text (about 2.5 GB in the first minutes), and the gen2 collections it caused landed under those opens. Split now steps through grapheme clusters with StringInfo.GetNextTextElementLength over the text, with an ASCII fast path for a one-unit ASCII separator, and compares each cluster with the separator as before (NFC equality: U+037E is ";", U+212A is "K"); the pieces, maxSplits and omittingEmptySubsequences are unchanged. Test: SwiftStringSplitCostTests (canonical-equivalence cases, CRLF as one Character, ZWJ and flag clusters; splitting 20,000 JSON lines allocates under 4 bytes per character).
### ED-NEW-stutterfix-8
Search folds only what the viewport can show (Round 3, item 5). A search in the model list (ModelListSearch) or the OpenRouter picker folded every row, so each frame of the 0.34 s fold measured and arranged all ~486 rows (20-57 ms frames). All folds of one search start together on one curve (TimingCurve .25,.1,.25,1, monotone in [0,1]), so a row's top at any frame lies between its tops before and after the fold, each row being laid out at least as tall as its folded height (layout rounds up). A row whose lesser top is past the tallest viewport (440) and two rows is never seen while the fold runs, the offset being 0 during a search: it is hidden at once and one spacer stands for its height at each frame (each held row's height rounded as layout rounds it, plus the model list's 1 px spacing), so the extent, the scrollbar and the edge fades are those of the full fold. Model list: a 0-to-1 progress scalar on the same curve drives the held rows' values, which equal AnimatedScalar's own formula; OpenRouter picker: the held items' own fold, opacity and scale scalars keep running and only their drawing is held. A held row takes its end state when the fold ends; a key press, a user scroll or a new search first gives every held row the value the plain fold has reached, and the fold goes on from there as before. Tests: ModelListSearchFoldTests and OpenRouterPickerFoldTests run two lists side by side, one with the plain fold, and assert at every frame the same rows in the viewport at the same places, heights, opacities and scales, the same extent, viewport and offset, and the same rendered pixels, through a narrowing search, a search changed mid-fold, keys and a scroll mid-fold and a cleared search; the held list resizes under a quarter as many rows. Mutations (a 200 px threshold, an unrounded spacer) fail them.
### ED-NEW-stutter-fix Round 3 measurements (Release, copied profile, same machine)
Build r3b (items 1-3 on 0b761d21a's line) against run-before2-claude and run-before-openrouter, round 1 unless stated. Claude profile: settings-open 1,010 MB allocated with 24 UI ticks over 33 ms became 406 MB (String/Byte[] on another thread) with no tick over 33 ms (max 16.6 ms); settings-close 566 MB to 0.9 MB; hydra-open 605 MB to 1.9 MB; hydra-close 317 MB to 1.4 MB; composer typing max tick 62.8 ms to 12.9 ms. Warm Settings and Hydra opens: 17-19 MB and 1.8 MB, no tick over 33 ms. OpenRouter profile: picker-open 1,145 MB with a 112 ms stall became 376 MB with a 35 ms stall (round 2: 1,675 MB to 66.9 MB, no gen2); picker-search 3,365 MB to 579 MB (round 2: 294 MB); composer typing 6,107 MB with 28 ticks over 33 ms to 127 MB with none. Item 5 (ED-NEW-stutterfix-8) is proved equal frame by frame in the headless tests above; it was not measured in a native tour within the time box. Item 4 (container piece-list caching: keep a container's pieces until one comes, goes or changes its glass, walk only the paths to them in subtree order, and let the container's own layout pass stand for its pieces' with one echo queue so it synchronises in the same frames) was written with a frame-by-frame equivalence test that passed with the UI Glass, Popover and Chrome suites, but is not committed: the coordinator time-boxed the round and the App suites were not run on it twice; the patch is kept outside the repository for later. Left for later: the OpenRouter model list build is still 34-41 ms (ModelPickerBinding runs Makers.Resolve twice per entry, with a Regex.Replace each, and PalettePickerColours re-resolves every row on each palette Changed); the round-1 Settings open still allocates about 400 MB on a background thread; SettingsViewFinishProvidersTests' order dependence was not investigated.
## ED-NEW-ignis-contract - Ignis shared contract, unit U0 (ENGINEERING DECISION)
Port-only feature Ignis (OD-0134; work/ignis/PLAN.md, design work/design/phoenix/phoenix-designs.html "Kindle (locked)"). U0 adds the contract every other unit codes against, in src/Marrow.Core/Port/Ignis: IgnisContract.cs (IgnisMode Off/KeepWarm/WarmAndTidy, IgnisSource, IgnisCacheState, IgnisNext, IgnisPause, IgnisTurnUsage with disjoint uncached/read/5m/1h/unknown-TTL buckets and Reported, IgnisEvent with timeline id prefixes "ignis:event:" and "ignis:ping:", IgnisChatStatus snapshot, IgnisLedgerEntry/IgnisDayTotals, and the interfaces IIgnisController, ISavingsLedger, IIgnisPoints, IIgnisRuntimePort), IgnisPointsSchema.cs (schema v1 records only; prices USD per million tokens), IgnisSettings.cs (one settings key "ignis", a compact JSON string; defaults Warm + tidy up, Auto on, heads on, helpers on, (i) on, pings hidden, keep 12 turns, auto-update on, notice unseen; each chat's own mode/Auto stored under "chats" only when it differs from the defaults; a bad value reads as the defaults), IgnisWords.cs (every design string; no keyboard shortcuts), IgnisSeams.cs (Ambient seams Controller, ComposerSlot, TimelineFilter, EventLine, HelperAgents; inert until Program.Main binds them; UI seams return object because Core does not reference Avalonia). Decisions taken here: Keep word for word choices 6/12/24 (the design shows only 12); the Codex Smart helpers (i) sentence; the Built-in tools estimate sentence; the 5-minute quick-memory tip variant; history row for a cold cache uses the design's mock wording "Quick memory went cold over a break". DEVIATION: ProviderEvent gains a 32nd, port-only case CacheUsage(IgnisTurnUsage), appended after the 31 Swift cases so their order is untouched; ProviderSessionTests (order and union coverage) and ThreadRuntimePartFourTests (rehearsal) list it explicitly as the deviation; ThreadRuntime ignores it until unit U3 forwards it. Tests: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Ignis/IgnisContractTests.cs (9 cases: defaults, round-trip bytes, bad values, words exact, event lines and ids, usage totals and report, fake controller through the seam; fakes FakeIgnisController, FakeIgnisPort, FakeIgnisLedger, FakeIgnisPoints, one per file).
## ED-NEW-ignis-engine - Ignis engine, unit U1 (ENGINEERING DECISION)
Port-only feature Ignis (OD-0134; work/ignis/PLAN.md unit U1), logic only, coded against the U0 contract with no contract change. src/Marrow.Core/Port/Ignis/Engine: IgnisPointsParser (schema v1; a file is taken whole or rejected with its first reason; unknown members ignored; ids and aliases match ordinal case-insensitive per provider; a Claude selector suffix such as "[1m]" is dropped when the whole id does not match), IgnisMoney (prices USD per million tokens; the highest price step the whole prompt is above prices the whole request and a step's missing write price keeps the base's; a write whose TTL the stream did not say pays the 5-minute premium, else the 1-hour one, else input; no write price means no premium, so Codex pays input; Reuse saving = cost without cache minus real cost, never below 0; cold loss = the held prefix paid at write (or input) price instead of cache read, only when the gap exceeds the TTL; unreported usage saves and loses nothing; on plans the same numbers are API-equivalent dollars), IgnisTidyPoints (tidyAt overrides; else floor(95 %) of the first step inside the window, so 100K gives 95K; else 75 % of the window; never below break-even C >= (S*out + K*(write + M*read)) / (read*(M - 1)) with K 20,000 kept tokens, S 4,000 summary tokens, M 10 messages), IgnisKeepWarm (skip when Off, Auto off, unknown model or keepWarm false, any pause, never sent or no TTL, already cold; wait until TTL minus a lead of a tenth of the TTL clamped to 15 s..2 min; ping when P x (rebuild - read) > ping cost, ping = 60 input + 5 output tokens plus the prefix read; not between tasks: ask again in 10 s while warm; with no reported prefix the price ratio decides; P = the chat's own gaps longer than the idle time that ended within the TTL, smoothed with 3 pseudo-gaps toward the global history (5 or more gaps) or the prior 0.8 / (1 + idle minutes / 30); draft text raises P to at least 0.9, on screen removes 40 % of the doubt; TTL from the stream's write buckets before the points), IgnisReportText (design Stage.report via IgnisWords.Report; plan line = week share plus the weekly-limit day part). src/Marrow.Services/Port/Ignis: IgnisPointsData (bundled points 2026.10.10 as a C# const string; every price as printed on platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing or its per-model overview pages, and on developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (platform.openai.com/docs/pricing redirects there), retrieved 2026-10-10, none estimated; Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 (step above 100K), Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5 with aliases opus/sonnet/haiku/fable, TTL main 1 h and sub-agents 5 min, keep-warm on, helper claude-haiku-5-5; Codex gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5.4-mini, steps above 272K where printed, keep-warm off, ttlMainSeconds 1800 for GPT-5.6 and later (OpenAI's 30-minute cache) and none for earlier; OpenAI's cache-write price for GPT-5.6 and later (1.25x input) has no field in schema v1 and is left out, harmless while Codex reports no write tokens; the gpt-5.6-sol prices are OpenAI's promotional prices "at least through November 21, 2026"), IgnisPointsFeed (raw.githubusercontent.com/Oak993/marrow-releases/main/ignis/model-points.json; only https GitHub hosts or a loopback test feed are asked, any other host is refused before a request; redirects not followed; 1 MB cap; 30 s bound; 404 = not published, so up to date), IgnisPointsStore (IIgnisPoints; Storage.Root/ignis/model-points.json used only when valid and newer than the bundled copy; a fetched file is installed only when valid and newer than the points in use, atomically), IgnisSavingsLedger (ISavingsLedger; Storage.Root/ignis/ledger-v1.json, compact JSON with sorted buckets by local day, chat, kind and source plus events with UTC tick times; written on every change; an unreadable file is moved to ledger-v1.corrupt-<stamp>.json, never deleted, and the ledger starts empty; an entry with an unknown value is skipped; events older than 60 days are dropped). Tests: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/Ignis/Engine (IgnisPointsParserTests, IgnisMoneyTests, IgnisTidyPointTests, IgnisKeepWarmTests) and tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Port/Ignis (IgnisPointsDataTests, IgnisPointsStoreTests with a loopback feed and a fail-closed wire proving no other host is called, IgnisSavingsLedgerTests, IgnisReportTextTests).

## ED-NEW-ignis-providers - Ignis providers, unit U2 (ENGINEERING DECISION)

Port-only feature Ignis (OD-0134; work/ignis/PLAN.md U2), coded against the U0 contract; every change from the Swift is marked // DEVIATION (OD-0134 Ignis). ClaudeSession: HandleResult emits ProviderEvent.CacheUsage after Usage/TokenSpend and before RequestResolved/TurnCompleted (CacheUsageOf: usage.iterations[] summed when present, else the top-level usage; cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens / ephemeral_1h_input_tokens fill the 5-minute and 1-hour write buckets, the rest of cache_creation_input_tokens goes to the unknown-TTL bucket; no cache_read/cache_creation field anywhere: Reported false); the native Hydra --agents JSON passes through WithIgnisHelperModel, which asks IgnisSeams.HelperAgents (ProviderKind.Claude, the session's model) and, when it answers a model, sets only the droppy-scout entry's model (worker and profile entries untouched; unbound or null: unchanged); Compact() now calls Compact(string? instructions), which writes "/compact <instructions>" (null or blank: the Swift's bare "/compact"), and KeepTurnsInstructions(n) is the keep-N request for a tidy-up (a request to the CLI, not a guarantee). CodexSession: thread/tokenUsage/updated emits CacheUsage for the lead (AgentID null) and for heads (AgentID the head thread) from tokenUsage.last: uncached = inputTokens - cachedInputTokens, read = cachedInputTokens, writes 0 (no write premium); no cachedInputTokens: Reported false. OpenAICompatibleSession: ReportUsage emits CacheUsage whenever the round carries token usage (uncached = prompt tokens - cached; writes 0; no cached_tokens / prompt_cache_hit_tokens: Reported false); the system prompt's date line is date only (UTC yyyy-MM-dd) and keeps the session's day, moving to a new day only once no request has gone out for an hour (the longest cache TTL), so two turns on one day send a byte-identical system prompt (Swift sent the full ISO 8601 time to the second, rebuilt every turn); TrimHistory still triggers past 60 messages but cuts the body to 40 (Swift: 50), so the history grows 20 messages on one stable prefix before the next cut; KeepWarm() sends, through the normal StreamOneRound path (key rotation, price reservation, retries), the payload the next turn would send plus one user message IgnisWords.PingText with max_tokens 1, adding nothing to history and raising no turn or notice events (spend and CacheUsage reported); Tidy(keepTurns) sends one summary request on the chat's own model whose messages are the system prompt, the history before the last keepTurns turns (the cached prefix) and a summary ask (tools listed, tool_choice none), then rebuilds the history as system + summary (user) + acknowledgement (assistant) + the kept turns word for word (a turn starts at a user message, so kept tool calls keep their results) with no notices; nothing to tidy, an error or an empty summary leaves the history exactly as it was. Both run only between turns (no turn running, none in flight, started, history beyond the system prompt) as main-actor tasks; a Send meanwhile waits for them. Expectations changed by this decision (not loosened): OpenAICompatibleSessionThirdTests' trim test now expects the 40-message body (renamed ..._up_to_40), and the 15 skills-native golden fixtures (tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Fixtures/skills-native/golden-*) now read "Today's date is 2026-09-22." instead of "2026-09-22T12:00:00Z."; nothing else in them changed. Contract additions: none (IgnisTurnUsage, ProviderEvent.CacheUsage, IgnisSeams.HelperAgents and IgnisWords.PingText from U0 suffice). UNRESOLVED: the exact shape of Codex's tokenUsage.last (field names inputTokens / cachedInputTokens / outputTokens, and whether inputTokens includes the cached part) is taken from the app-server's camelCase TokenUsageBreakdown and OpenAI's convention, not from a captured stream; Claude's iterations[] entries are assumed to carry cache_creation like the top-level usage. Tests (fixtures only, no request ever sent): tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Providers/ClaudeSessionIgnisTests.cs (7), CodexSessionIgnisTests.cs (3), OpenAICompatibleSessionIgnisTests.cs (9), with tests/Marrow.Services.Tests/Fixtures/IgnisApiSessionSeam.cs (records each payload at PerformStreamAttempt and answers a queued round).
## ED-NEW-ignis-runtime - Ignis runtime and controller, unit U3 (ENGINEERING DECISION)
Port-only feature Ignis (OD-0134; work/ignis/PLAN.md unit U3). ThreadRuntime.cs gets only hooks: an ignisPingTurn AsyncLocal beside skillsContinuationTurn; in StartTurn a ping turn's user item becomes an info notice with id "ignis:ping:" + the turn id (lowercase "D"; the view can hide the whole turn by TurnID and the mark survives restarts with no store of its own), and a ping skips GenerateTitle, the start checkpoint, the Hydra route/preamble, the sidebar UpdatedAt bump and ReopenIfSettled, counts as not user-authored for the Hydra budget, and is dropped (never queued as a follow-up) when the chat is busy or archived; Handle forwards ProviderEvent.CacheUsage to the controller and tells it about UsageLimit; Compact() keeps its notices while Compact(ignisKeepTurns) is the silent tidy-up origin (no "Compacting context."/"Nothing to compact yet.", the provider's "Context compacted." is swallowed and ends the tidy-up, else it ends after 5 minutes; a failure ends it silently). AppModel.TurnFinished returns early for a ping turn after settling LastStatus (no chime, notification, unread mark, AutoContinue, Hydra head report); every turn end reaches the controller. Program.cs binds IgnisRuntimeStartup (one line); the controller is made on first use once the U1 parts are bound, else Ignis stays inert. New: src/Marrow.App/Port/Ignis/Runtime/ (ThreadRuntimeIgnis.cs partial: IIgnisRuntimePort with "between tasks" = idle, no follow-ups or pending send, no approvals/questions, no Hydra reports/batches/waiting, no running heads, not reverting, not archived, not a Droppy-run head, no tidy-up running; AppModelIgnis.cs partial and AppIgnisEnvironment; IgnisController.cs; IgnisSessionHooks.cs; IgnisRuntimeStartup.cs). Contract additions, additive, in a new file src/Marrow.Core/Port/Ignis/IgnisRuntimeContract.cs: IIgnisEngine (TidyPoint, ShouldKeepWarm(IgnisKeepWarmQuestion), ReuseSaved, RebuildPremium, PingCost, TidySaved) for unit U1 to implement, IIgnisRuntimeTimeline (IsTidying, AppendEvent: an info notice with id "ignis:event:" + event id, appended once), IgnisRuntimeSeams (Engine, Points, Ledger factories, unbound = null). Decisions: keep-warm is considered a tenth of the cache lifetime before it goes cold, clamped to 15 s..5 min (30 s on a 5-minute cache, 5 min on a 1-hour cache); a busy chat is asked again every 15 s while something is due; at most 6 keep-warms per idle stretch; the TTL comes from the stream's writes (1 h wins over 5 min), else the points (main or sub-agent), else unknown; a model without keepWarm in the points is never pinged (Pause NotSupported); automatic work pauses when the PC is locked (input desktop cannot be opened), the chat is archived, the chat's provider has a plan window >= 95 %, or after a usage-limit error (until resetsAt, or until a request goes through when none was given); the cold line and its Lost entry (RebuildPremium of the chat size) are recorded once per warm spell when the lifetime runs out, never for an archived chat; a ping's own cache read is not a saving, its cost is a Spent KeptWarm entry, and its saving (RebuildPremium of the read) is credited when the user's next request reads the cache; a tidy-up's saving (TidySaved) is credited when the next request reports the shorter chat, and no second tidy-up starts before that; "Tidied up" shows 4 s; Hydra heads: provider sub-agents (CacheUsage with AgentID) are tracked as "Head n" with their own cache, lifetime and tidy point when Include Hydra heads is on, a head's model switch records HeadTidiedAfterSwitch with the new point; Droppy-run head chats are never pinged (their turns belong to the lead). Manual "Keep warm now"/"Tidy up now" work with Auto off and through every pause except a usage limit. AT MERGE (lead): bind IgnisRuntimeSeams.Engine/Points/Ledger to U1's classes, and point IgnisSessionHooks.KeepWarm (OpenAICompatibleSession.KeepWarm) and IgnisSessionHooks.Tidy (API Tidy(keepTurns); Claude Compact(instructions)) at U2's methods; until then a tidy-up is a plain silent compact and API sessions keep warm with hidden ping turns. Tests: tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Port/Ignis/IgnisControllerTests.cs (22, manual clock: Off does nothing, 1 h keep-warm timing and costing, silent API keep-warm, busy retry, cold line and loss, tidy waits for between tasks and keeps 12 turns, Keep warm never tidies, Auto off, pauses locked/archived/plan 95 %/usage limit, not-supported model, model switch moves the point, heads in and out, unreported numbers, ping cap, lead and TTL rules, report) and tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Runtime/ThreadRuntimeIgnisTests.cs (9, real StartTurn over the scripted session: ping notice turn ends silently with no unread/UpdatedAt/title change, follow-ups typed during a ping drain as an ordinary turn, not between tasks while busy, CacheUsage/turn end/usage limit forwarded, silent tidy-up and its timeout, the user's own compact still notices, event line appended once); fakes in tests/Marrow.App.Tests/Port/Ignis/IgnisRuntimeFakes.cs. The runtime tests turn the finish chime off: FinishChime caches its sound on first play, which belongs to AppModelTurnFinishedTests' collection.
## ED-NEW-ignis-views - Ignis views, unit U4: Kindle capsule, popover, event lines, ping filter (ENGINEERING DECISION)
Port-only feature Ignis (OD-0134; work/ignis/PLAN.md unit U4, design work/design/phoenix/phoenix-designs.html "Kindle (locked)", "Timeline event lines", "First-time notice"). New files only, in src/Marrow.App/Port/Ignis/Views; every word from IgnisWords; bound to IIgnisController / IgnisChatStatus; no contract members added.
- Binding point: IgnisViews.Bind(controller) sets the IgnisSeams process defaults (ComposerSlot, TimelineFilter, EventLine) and re-runs the timeline's pass when "Show keep-warm pings" changes; IgnisViews.Override(controller) scopes the same for tests. Unbound, every hook is a no-op (the ContextMeter, every entry, the NoticeRow).
- Hooks (three lines, PORT-ONLY comments): ComposerView hosts IgnisViews.ComposerOffer(thread, provider) where the ContextMeter sits and falls back to the ContextMeter when it returns null; ThreadTimeline.Draw passes runtime.Entries through IgnisViews.Visible (which returns the same list when nothing is filtered, so the block cache keeps its identity); NoticeRow.Build hands an "ignis:event:" item to IgnisEventLine.
- Supported providers (capsule shown): Claude, Codex, DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, OpenRouter, the providers PLAN.md gives a cache route; any other provider keeps the ContextMeter. Compact composers carry neither.
- The capsule is the app's chrome glass capsule (the existing material), not the page's CSS gradient; the popover is PlainControls.Popover with PlacementMode.TopEdgeAlignedRight through the popover host, so Escape closes it like every popover; no keyboard shortcuts (owner).
- The countdown re-reads the clock once a second while warm and attached (a warm cache whose time ran out reads Cold before the controller says so); only the changed characters roll.
- Continuous motion (breathing core, tidy-up spin, warm track head) is drawn on the render thread from a main-thread snapshot, on an Ambient AnimationTimeline at 1/60 s (AmbientRefreshPacer), and stops under Reduce Motion or when the frame clock is unbound; one-shot motion (spark, settle, heat, fill, drawer, rise, fold) uses AnimatedScalar with the design's curves, instant under Reduce Motion.
- The first-time notice card uses a popover-like glass fill and rim (PopoverCard carries a tip, so it is not reused). It shows once: above the first keep-warm line of a Claude Code or Codex chat while NoticeSeen is false, held by one line id per process (IgnisViewState.NoticeHolder); Got it sets NoticeSeen.
- The popover re-reads the Ignis preferences (Show (i) explanations, Smart helpers) on IgnisSettings.Changed, since they are not observable.

## ED-NEW-handoverfix-2
2026-10-10 - Test mechanics (claude/handover-fix): the two Boot B hand-over tests in GlassWindowNativeTests, Under_the_full_boot_sequence_the_hand_over_shows_the_main_window_blurred_and_never_as_scrim_over_sharp_stripes and With_reduce_motion_the_boot_hand_over_shows_the_main_window_blurred_and_never_as_scrim_over_sharp_stripes, are rewritten for Boot B as the earlier native sweep prescribed when it left them failing (ED-NEW-testing-lead-1 item 15 (b) and (c), left UNRESOLVED). CAUSE: not the launch, native or stutter merges. Both fail identically on the release base 2eecff5ac (built in a temporary worktree, run alone twice) and on 148f81f92: they still assumed Comet's hand-over. Boot B's locked design (OD-0113, loading-aurora.html :98, :622, :663) dims the desktop with an unblurred stage scrim (AuroraBootPainter: rgba(2,6,16,.5) dark) from the stage's start until after the hand-over, drawn above the main window, and shows the window inside one growing frame whose whole-window alpha fades in. A frame-by-frame log (stage frames and screen samples on one clock) showed the reduce-motion test's bare mean taken in the first 150 ms includes the scrim's fade-in (118 against 120-135), and the full test's samples after the hand-over are the stage scrim over the stripes (mean 66.4, contrast 19.4) until the growing frame reaches the sampled block. The product follows the locked design; no product change. MECHANICS: (1) the bare mean and contrast are read in 150 ms of samples before the stage opens. (2) Launch records, at every stage frame on the sampler's clock, the scrim strength and whether the sampled block lies wholly inside, wholly outside or across the main window's rounded content clip (BootHandOverRun.Place); the screen may show any frame of the last 50 ms. (3) Before the hand-over (reduce motion, as before), every sample must be the stripes under the stage scrim alone: mean within 1.5 and contrast no more than 3 below what that scrim makes of the bare stripes (the old rule with the design's scrim instead of none). (4) The P13 rule (no frame shows the window's tint over sharp stripes) is judged against the design: the stage scrim is undone with its known alpha, the sample's mean gives how much of the tinted window is seen (the test's black scrim, 66/255), and the contrast the uncovered stripes cannot explain, brought back to the screen, must stay under Blurred (3, unchanged). Samples whose frames put the clip's edge across the block (the stage's own growing edge) are not judged. STRENGTH: the control launch without the hand-over (reduce motion) must still show the P13 gap under the new rule, at least 20 samples over 80-600 ms (unchanged); in the logged run it showed 54 samples over 220 ms, with excesses of 4.7 to 14.6 against at most 1.5 in the logged honest launches. Every other assertion (bare mean 120-135, bare contrast, more than 100 samples, at least one blurred sample, the end blurred under the scrim) is unchanged. Evidence: both tests passed 5 runs of 5 alone under native.lock (with The_boot_outline_lies_on_the_main_windows_visible_frame_as_DWM_reports_it in 3 of them). BootHandOverRun.cs holds the judging; Traceability is unchanged.

## ED-NEW-handoverfix-4
2026-10-10 - The GPU warm-up's idle cap is read on the port's one clock (claude/handover-fix; ED-252, ED-068). CAUSE: EffortSliderJewelWarmupTests.The_idle_warm_up_counts_its_cap_from_its_start failed under load ("the last three steps took 486 ms: a cap each, not one a frame") because both sides measured the machine's wall time: GpuWarmup's Driver counted IdleCap with DateTime.UtcNow (against ED-068: every clock read and wait goes through SwiftClock's TimeProvider), and the test stamped each step with DateTime.UtcNow while it pumped frames every 10 ms, so a loaded machine stretched the frames between the forced steps past 450 ms. PRODUCT: the Driver takes SwiftClock.Provider.Current when it is made (as it already takes the frame source: the steps run in other flows), counts the cap with its timestamps (GetTimestamp / GetElapsedTime) and bounds the no-frame wait with the same clock (Task.WaitAsync(IdleCap, clock, token)). In the app the clock is TimeProvider.System, so the behaviour is unchanged; StepTimeout and the work steps' timeouts are untouched. TEST MECHANICS: the test installs a ManualTimeProvider on SwiftClock.Provider and drives frames with a new ClockedFrames helper (a render tick, the dispatcher's jobs, a 10 ms sleep for the warm-up's Task.Delay turn, then 16 ms of the manual clock), stamping each step with the manual clock. The assertions are the same, with the same numbers: all four steps done and asked, the first not before the 500 ms cap, the last three within 450 ms of it (less than one cap), all forced. Mutation check: resetting the cap at each step makes the test fail ("the last three steps took 4496 ms"). The other warm-up tests (wall-clock lower bounds only) are unchanged.
