## ED-NEW-ignis-data - Ignis points schema v2, the all-model price catalogue and the 2026-10-10 data refresh (ENGINEERING DECISION)

Branch claude/ignis-data (part A of the Ignis refinement; owner order 2026-10-10: Ignis fully up to date in this release, its update able to fetch every model's prices and cache facts for all providers by itself, cheaply, with no model calls).
1. SCHEMA v2 (src/Marrow.Core/Port/Ignis/IgnisPointsSchema.cs, Engine/IgnisPointsParser.cs): the parser reads v1 and v2 (any other schemaVersion is rejected); the bundled data and the feed are v2. New, read only from a v2 file: prices.cacheWrites and steps[].cacheWrites, a list of {ttlSeconds, price} for write lifetimes other than 5 minutes and 1 hour (OpenAI's 30-minute writes; 300 and 3600 keep their own fields and are refused in the list; one entry per lifetime); and a top-level providers list, one rule per ProviderKind raw value: billing perToken|flat|none, optional ttlMainSeconds/ttlSubagentSeconds, keepWarm (refused unless perToken with a known main lifetime), catalogue (the LiteLLM provider names that map to it, each mapping once), notes, sourceUrl, retrievedAt. The new members are additive: IgnisPrices/IgnisPriceStep keep their positional constructors and gain an init property CacheWrites (default empty) and WriteFor(ttl) (exact lifetime: the 5m/1h field, else the list; null when unknown); IgnisPrices.WriteFor(ttl, promptTokens) applies the step in force as IgnisMoney.Tier does; IgnisPointsFile gains Providers and Rule(provider). IgnisMoney is not changed (part B owns the engine); it can call WriteFor. IgnisPointsParser.ParsePrices reads one prices object (the catalogue's stored copy uses it).
2. PRICE CATALOGUE (src/Marrow.Services/Port/Ignis/IgnisPriceCatalogue.cs; IIgnisPriceCatalogue in Core/Port/Ignis/IgnisPricesContract.cs, implemented by IgnisPointsStore): LiteLLM's public model_prices_and_context_window.json on raw.githubusercontent.com (BerriAI/litellm main), fetched through the points feed's GitHub-only rule (any other host refused before a request, no redirects, the URLSession.Transport seam), with its own 8 MB cap (declared or streamed, counted unpacked) and 60 s limit. Both fetches now ask for gzip (the transport does not decompress; the catalogue packs 2.7 MB into about 130 KB) and the catalogue sends If-None-Match with the stored ETag, so an unchanged file costs one 304. Only the providers the rules map are read (2026-10-10: anthropic, openai, deepseek, xai, zai, gemini, meta, meta_llama, openrouter; LiteLLM has no openrouter entries today, kept for when it does), only modes chat and responses, only the standard prices (the _batches, _flex, _priority, _ultrafast and regional fields are never read); a "provider/" key prefix is dropped and the bare key wins a duplicate; a model without max_input_tokens is skipped. Per-token costs become per-MTok decimals from the number's text (decimal.Parse, x 1,000,000, rounded to 9 places, trailing zeros dropped), never through double. Steps come from the *_above_<N>k_tokens fields (N x 1000, inside the window, input and output required). DECISIONS: cache_creation_input_token_cost is the 5-minute write for anthropic and ..._above_1hr the 1-hour write (LiteLLM's naming); for any other provider it is the write at the rule's ttlMainSeconds (OpenAI 1800 -> cacheWrites) and is left out when the rule names no lifetime; a write of 0 is no premium; a missing cache-read price is the input price (no cache saving claimed). GUARDRAILS: any price below 0, or a cache read above the input, sets the model aside with a warning; a write below the cache read is dropped. For a model the curated points list, a catalogue price more than 4x (either way, any of input, output, cache read, 5m, 1h) from the curated one keeps the curated prices and records a warning; otherwise the catalogue's prices replace the curated ones only when the curated entry's retrievedAt is more than 30 days old; curated rules (context window, lifetimes, keep-warm, tidyAt, helperModel, display name, source) are never replaced. A model only the catalogue knows becomes points under its provider's rule (cache lifetimes and keep-warm from the rule, display name = id, source = the LiteLLM URL, retrievedAt = the catalogue day), so a new model is covered at once. The trimmed catalogue (about 44 KB, 244 models from the 2026-10-10 file) is kept at Storage.Root/ignis/prices.json with fetchedAt, checkedAt, the ETag and the warnings, loaded at start-up (a damaged copy is ignored); Find asks the curated points first, then the catalogue. Checked against the real 2026-10-10 file (scratch copy, not committed): no warning, and every curated id LiteLLM lists has identical prices.
3. UPDATES ROW (src/Marrow.App/Port/Updates/IgnisPointsUpdateItem.cs): one action updates the curated feed (unchanged) and the catalogue. Versions read IgnisWords.UpdatesRowVersion: "2026.10.10 · prices 2026-10-10" (the version alone before any catalogue; the day is the UTC day the catalogue was last confirmed current). With "Update automatically" on, the check asks the points feed only when its last successful check is a day old or more and the catalogue at most once a day (the store skips a fresher one); a feed 404 is still up to date and the catalogue still runs; a catalogue error makes the check throw (row "Checks when updated" with the message) and Update fail, as a feed error always did (a points feed error keeps priority). With it off, a check asks the small points feed only and Update refreshes both (forced, so the ETag check runs). An update that only changed prices counts as a change. The item reaches the catalogue through IIgnisPriceCatalogue on the points object, so IIgnisPoints and every fake are unchanged. Known limit (lead to decide): VersionText.Same compares the first dotted number, so with updating automatically off a catalogue-only change never shows "Update available"; and the Updates page columns show VersionText.Number (the curated version only) while the pill shows the full text (ellipsis-trimmed).
4. DATA (src/Marrow.Services/Port/Ignis/IgnisPointsData.cs, version 2026.10.10, schema v2; the same JSON is work/ignis-feed/ignis/model-points.json for the owner to publish) from work/ignis-research/claude.md, openai.md and others.md (retrieved 2026-10-10). Claude: all existing prices confirmed; added Fable 5 (claude-fable-5, read 1.00), Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6 (200K) and "claude-sonnet-4-6[1m]" (1M, same prices, so the selector finds the right window); Opus 4.7/4.6 left out (ids UNCONFIRMED), Mythos left out (not public); Haiku 4.5 keeps the 200K window from its overview page (the research left the window UNCONFIRMED). OpenAI: all prices confirmed; GPT-5.6 and later gain the 30-minute write at 1.25x input (base and the >272K step at 2x); gpt-5.6 is an alias of gpt-5.6-sol; sources are now each model's page. Providers: a rule for all 16 ProviderKind values with its official page; keepWarm only for claude (per token, 1 h / 5 min, write premium); codex keeps keep-warm off (PLAN lead decision) with ttlMainSeconds 1800; no lifetime where the research found none (grok, deepseek, meta, zai, cursor, copilot, devin, commandcode, opencode, opencodeGo, pi, openrouter, antigravity, local). Billing DECISIONS (lead may revise): claude, codex, cursor, opencode, grok, deepseek, meta, zai, copilot, commandcode, pi, openrouter perToken (an API key, credits or a pool priced per token; plan use is API-equivalent); opencodeGo, devin, antigravity flat; local none.
5. TESTS: Core IgnisPointsSchemaV2Tests (v2 reading, WriteFor, v1 ignores v2 members, 18 rejection cases, ParsePrices); Services IgnisPriceCatalogueTests over a trimmed fixture (IgnisCatalogueFixture: a few real LiteLLM entries plus "*-test-*" guardrail entries) and IgnisPricesStoreTests (loopback stand-ins, fail-closed wire, manual clock: install, disk, restart, daily cadence, 304, errors, 8 MB cap declared and streamed, gzip, host refusal), IgnisPointsDataTests gains three tests (every ProviderKind has a sourced rule, the new Claude models, OpenAI 30-minute writes); App IgnisPricesUpdateRowTests (versions, daily cadence, unpublished feed, errors). REPLACED (deliberate v2 change, equal or stricter): IgnisPointsParserTests' case "schemaVersion 2 is not supported" now names 3 and 0. AMENDED: IgnisIntegrationTests.The_model_points_update_row_reads_and_installs_from_the_loopback_feed_only gives the store a loopback catalogue address, answers its request and asserts NewVersion "2026.10.20 · prices <day>" and the catalogue model (stricter; the wire stays fail-closed).

## ED-NEW-ignis-data-2 - The Ignis update row sees a changed price catalogue and compares the newer data date (ENGINEERING DECISION)

Branch claude/ignis-data (amends ED-NEW-ignis-data; found while checking the "Update everything" row; data only, GitHub only, no model provider contact).
1. PROBLEM: the orchestrator compares installed and latest with VersionText.Same, which counts only the first dotted number. The row text "2026.10.10 · prices 2026-10-10" had the points version first and the price day dashed, so (a) with "Update automatically" off the latest only came from the curated feed, a price-only change never read "Update available" and the overall update never refreshed prices, and (b) the price day never took part.
2. TEXT (IgnisWords.UpdatesRowVersion, unchanged signature, the catalogue day still "yyyy-MM-dd"): "2026.10.11 · rules 2026.10.10 · prices 2026.10.11" - the first dotted number is the newer of the points version and the catalogue day in dotted form (ordinal on "yyyy.MM.dd"), then both dates named; the version alone while no catalogue is held.
3. DRY RUN: IIgnisPriceCatalogue.ProbePricesAsync(ct), implemented in IgnisPointsStore beside CheckPricesAsync (same lock, same GitHub-only fetch): a conditional GET with the held ETag, not asked more than once per check, installing and storing nothing and raising no Changed. 304: unchanged (the held day). 200 with a catalogue that builds: changed, day = today (SwiftDate.Now, UTC). None held: no ETag, so changed. A missing, failing or malformed file is the same error text as CheckPricesAsync (the row's "Checks when updated"). A 200 downloads the file (about 2.7 MB) once per manual check; an automatic check is unchanged (it installs at most once a day).
4. ROW (IgnisPointsUpdateItem): with "Update automatically" off, LatestVersion asks the points feed and then the dry run; its latest text names the feed's version and the catalogue's day (today when changed, else the held day). With it on, nothing changed (the catalogue was just refreshed, so its day is current). GUARD: when "changed" would not move the first number past the installed one (the catalogue changed the same day it was confirmed, or the points version is later than today), the latest day is the day after the installed first number, so the change still shows; that day exists only in the pending "latest" text, and after Update the installed text names the real day. Update is unchanged (it refreshes both with force) and its outcome version uses the new text.
5. TESTS: App IgnisPricesUpdateRowTests (manual clock, the fake catalogue): auto off + catalogue changed shows Update available and one update makes it the same; auto off + 304 is up to date with no catalogue check; changed the day it was confirmed still shows; a newer points file alone shows and is the same after Update; a dry-run error keeps the row's error behaviour; Words/VersionText pins. Services IgnisPricesStoreTests: the dry run sends the held ETag, 304/200/none held/500/malformed answers, nothing stored (file and memory), no Changed, no request to any host but the loopback stand-in. STRICTER pins replacing the old text: the "2026.10.10 · prices 2026-09-22" assertions in IgnisPricesUpdateRowTests now read "2026.10.10 · rules 2026.10.10 · prices 2026.09.22" (and the VersionText.Same pair gains two negative assertions); IgnisIntegrationTests.The_model_points_update_row_reads_and_installs_from_the_loopback_feed_only now also answers the dry run's catalogue request, asserts the latest text and that nothing was stored, and the final NewVersion in the new text.
## ED-NEW-ignis-runtime (part B): cache lifetimes, gap learning and helper accounting, 2026-10-10
2026-10-10 - Ignis refinement part B (branch claude/ignis-runtime, from claude/release-integration 39b9dd99d; lead research E:/Droppy/work/ignis-research/claude.md, openai.md, others.md). ENGINEERING DECISION unless a line says SOURCE FACT or UNRESOLVED. Test traits cite Decision OD-0134.
1. QUALITY GUARD: nothing here changes what the model sees. No prompt, message, tool, instruction or context is edited, trimmed or added. Part B only chooses how long a provider keeps the same prefix (cache lifetimes, retention hints, cache markers) and how Ignis counts money. Keep-warm pings and tidy-ups are unchanged from U3.
2. GAP LEARNING (IIgnisGapHistory; IgnisGapStore at Storage.Root/ignis/gaps-v1.json, atomic write on each change, a corrupt file moved aside, never deleted): per provider and bucket (main, helpers) the last 200 requests' idle gap, prefix before the gap, writes by lifetime (5 min, 1 h, unlabelled), model, and whether nth had lengthened the bucket. No message content and no chat ids. The chat's gap runs from the end of its last user turn to the start of the next one (IIgnisRuntimePort.TurnStartedAt; the usage's own time when unknown). Keep-warm pings, the tidy-up's own request, unreported usage and chats in Off mode add nothing. Helpers are learned whenever Ignis is on; their list, lines and money still follow "Include Hydra heads".
3. EVERY HELPER AT EVERY DEPTH: each helper is its own head, keyed by the agent id its usage carries, so nothing is missed or counted twice. Claude: an assistant message with parent_tool_use_id is one helper request (a subagent of a subagent names its own spawning Task call, so each depth is a separate agent); a message repeated once per content block is counted once by message.id (the last 4096 ids per session); the "<synthetic>" model is skipped; the main chat is counted only through its result usage, which excludes subagents (SOURCE FACT, claude.md). Codex: a sub-thread with an agent nickname or role was already a head; a sub-thread without one whose parent is a head or such a nested thread now reports its thread/tokenUsage/updated usage as its own agent, and nothing else of it reaches the chat. Tests: a two-level Claude fixture (ClaudeSessionIgnisRuntimeTests) and a three-level Codex fixture (CodexSessionIgnisTests).
4. TTL CHOICE AT CLAUDE LAUNCH (IgnisCacheLifetime.Decide, pure). SOURCE FACT (code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching and settings, claude.md): main bucket 1 h on a subscription within plan, 5 min on credits, an API key or a cloud provider; everything else (subagents at every depth, workflows, forks, compaction, titles) 5 min; CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL take "5m" or "1h" from Claude Code 2.1.242; precedence FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M > the bucket's variable > promptCacheTtl / subagentPromptCacheTtl > frontmatter cacheTtl (ignored on credits) > ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H > default. RULE: benefit = sum over gaps with 5 min < g <= 1 h of prefix x (w5m - read); cost = sum of the writes 1 h would raise (5-minute, unlabelled, and 1-hour writes nth itself caused) x (w1h - w5m); prices from each request's own model points at its price step. Ask for 1 h when benefit > cost x 1.1 and at least 12 gaps were seen; otherwise set nothing. Checks in order: not Claude; Ignis Off; helpers with "Include Hydra heads" off; the user's own choice; CLI version unknown or below 2.1.242; main bucket already 1 h (no API key or cloud-provider marker in the inherited environment and the newest own main writes are not 5-minute only); helpers already writing more 1 h than 5 min without nth (issue anthropics/claude-code#84289: the observed bucket wins); too few gaps; no write prices.
5. USER CHOICE, READ ONLY: any of FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M, the bucket's variable or ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H in the inherited environment (any letter case), or the bucket's setting or one of those variables in the "env" block of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (else home/.claude)/settings.json, the project's .claude/settings.json and settings.local.json, or ProgramFiles/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json. nth reads these files and never writes them; in Off mode it does not read them. The CLI version is ProviderRegistry.Status(provider).Version, already read by the provider check: no process is started for it.
6. ONCE PER PROCESS: ClaudeSession.StartCore asks IgnisSeams.CacheLifetimes once, before the spawn, and adds the chosen variables to the CLI process environment (never over a variable already present). Every request of that process inherits them, nested helpers included; heads never ask again. Test: Start_sets_the_lifetimes_on_the_process_environment_once_and_helpers_never_ask_again. The verdicts and their reasons are kept on the chat (IgnisChatStatus.CacheLifetimes) and written in the report ("Helpers' quick memory: 1 hour, chosen by Ignis (saves about $X over N breaks)", one line per reason).
7. PLAN VS PAID CREDITS: the main chat's lifetime follows its observed writes, and a read-only turn keeps the last one. 5-minute writes where the points promise 1 hour mark the chat "Paid credits: 5-minute cache" and the keep-warm timer runs on 5 minutes at once; 1-hour writes switch back. An API key or cloud provider is 5 minutes by default, not credits. When nth itself set the main bucket to 1 h, the env var holds on credits (SOURCE FACT, claude.md), so neither the hint nor 5-minute writes turn the chat to credits. A rate_limit_event whose rateLimitType / rate_limit_type is "overage" or whose isUsingOverage is true is a credits hint (ProviderEvent.CacheBilling, ThreadRuntime to IIgnisController.CreditsHint): it drops the stale 1-hour reading at once, and the next writes still decide. UNRESOLVED: no single documented "billed to credits" flag; these fields are the closest (claude.md section 4). A rejected event stays the existing usage-limit path. prompt_cache.ttl / expires_at are statusline-only (SOURCE FACT, statusline docs), not in the stream, so ping timing uses the observed bucket.
8. ACCOUNTING (ledger and history). New kind Missed: a helper's write after a gap longer than its lifetime, priced at that lifetime's rebuild premium on the part it rewrote (the part it still read was alive and is not counted). It is kept apart from the chat's Lost. New source LongerMemory ("Longer quick memory"). Saved: a read after more than 5 minutes and within nth's 1-hour lifetime, priced as the 5-minute rebuild it avoided; on the main chat only when no keep-warm ping ran since the user's last turn, so a break is credited to Kept warm or to Longer quick memory, never both. Spent: the extra (w1h - w5m) of the 1-hour writes nth caused, inside Spent and also LongerMemorySpent. Ledger raw names "missed" and "longerMemory" (existing files read unchanged). The settings history, the Kindle popover and the report show the fifth source only when it saved something, plus "Helpers rebuilt their quick memory: $X". Contract test replacement (equal or stricter): IgnisContractTests.Words_are_the_designs_exactly asserted the four source names; it now asserts the five names in order and, separately, that the first four are still the design's four in order. Likewise ProviderSessionTests.ProviderEvent_declares_exactly_31_cases_in_source_order_with_tokenSpend_directly_after_usage asserted the port-only CacheUsage as the last case; it now asserts CacheUsage and then CacheBilling in that exact order, and the ProviderEvent union-coverage samples (ProviderSessionTests, ThreadRuntimePartFourTests) add a CacheBilling sample.
9. CODEX: CodexSession.CacheUsageOf reads cache_write_input_tokens (SOURCE FACT: codex-rs exec_events.rs Usage) and the app-server spelling cacheWriteInputTokens (UNRESOLVED: exact camelCase name) into the unlabelled write bucket; uncached = input - read - written. Older CLIs omit it and writes stay 0. Keep-warm for Codex stays off (PLAN lead decision kept): nth has no way to touch the same thread's cache without adding a turn to its history, which would change what the model sees; GPT-5.6+ caches 30 minutes and every read refreshes it (SOURCE FACT, openai.md). Its 1800-second lifetimes arrive with part A's points data.
10. KEEP-WARM PROVIDERS (IgnisController.KeepWarmAllowed): Claude, OpenRouter and OpenCode Zen only, and the points still decide per model. Off for Codex, antigravity, the Z.ai coding plan and API, local servers, request-billed Copilot, DeepSeek, Grok, Cursor, Devin, Command Code, OpenCode Go, Meta and pi; those keep the savings report (others.md section 4).
11. HELPER TIDY-UP: no documented control compacts or tunes compaction for subagents only. /compact and auto-compact act on the main conversation; subagents compact inside the CLI. The process-wide auto-compact setting would also move the main chat's compaction and changes the context the model reads, so it is not used. What does apply: compaction requests are in the helpers bucket, so the helpers lifetime choice covers them.
12. REQUEST LEVERS (only while Ignis is on for the chat; IgnisSeams.IsOn). OpenRouter: a top-level cache_control {"type":"ephemeral"} for "anthropic/..." models only (SOURCE FACT: openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching; Anthropic upstreams cache only when marked; other upstreams cache on their own). ProviderToolBillingGuard restricts payload keys only for Meta and Z.ai, so the key passes. pi: PI_CACHE_RETENTION=long unless the user set it (SOURCE FACT, pi-coding-agent README: "Anthropic: 1h, OpenAI: 24h"). RISK: on an Anthropic upstream this pays 2x writes on every request; issue #74318 measured a blanket 1-hour subagent setting at 8.6% more expensive. Not sent: Meta prompt_cache_retention (Responses API only; nth's API sessions use Chat Completions); Meta prompt_cache_key (documented for the Responses API, UNRESOLVED on Chat Completions). Not applicable: Grok's x-grok-conv-id (nth drives Grok as a CLI, not an OpenAICompatibleSession). DeepSeek and Z.ai cache automatically with no key. No unknown field is sent anywhere.
13. FILES: Core Port/Ignis/Engine/IgnisCacheLifetime.cs, Port/Ignis/IgnisGapHistory.cs (new); IgnisContract, IgnisRuntimeContract, IgnisSeams, IgnisWords, IgnisEngine, IgnisReportText. Services Port/Ignis/IgnisGapStore.cs, IgnisClaudeSettings.cs (new); IgnisSavingsLedger; Providers ClaudeSession, CodexSession, PiSession, OpenRouterSession, ProviderSession. App IgnisController, AppModelIgnis, IgnisRuntimeStartup, ThreadRuntime (IgnisThreadID, CacheBilling), IgnisSavingsHistory(View), KindlePopover. Part A's points files were not touched.

## ED-NEW-ignis-integration - exact-lifetime write prices in the money maths, and pi's long retention gated by the gap rule (ENGINEERING DECISION)

Branch claude/release-integration, 2026-10-10 (integrates Ignis part A, points schema v2 and catalogue, with part B, runtime and TTL choice). ENGINEERING DECISION unless a line says SOURCE FACT. Test traits cite Decision OD-0134. Nothing here changes what a model reads: it only prices a cache lifetime exactly and chooses whether pi asks its provider for the longer one.
1. WRITE PRICE BY EXACT LIFETIME: IgnisPriceTier.CacheWriteFor(ttl) now returns the points' price for a lifetime they list in cacheWrites (OpenAI GPT-5.6+ and GPT-6: ttlSeconds 1800 at 1.25x input; SOURCE FACT, openai.md, ED-NEW-ignis-data). IgnisMoney.Tier carries the base cacheWrites into the tier and a price step replaces them per lifetime (a step that names no 30-minute write keeps the base's, as it keeps the 5-minute and 1-hour ones); the tier's lookup agrees with IgnisPrices.WriteFor(ttl, promptTokens). Every other case is unchanged: 5 minutes and 1 hour still use their own fields, 1 h or longer without one uses the 5-minute price, a shorter or unknown lifetime uses the 5-minute price, a model with no write fields pays plain input. A lifetime with no listed write on a model that has none (a 25-minute observed lifetime on GPT-6.1) pays plain input as before. IgnisPriceTier gained an init property CacheWrites (default empty, so the five-field constructor and value equality stay).
2. CALLERS: IgnisKeepWarm.Worth (ping worth), IgnisMoney.RebuildPremium (rebuild premium, ping/rebuild decisions, Kept warm and Lost money) and IgnisTidyPoints.BreakEven (tidy point) all price through CacheWriteFor and already receive the lifetime: IgnisEngine and IgnisKeepWarm.TtlFromPoints take it from the points' ttlMainSeconds (1800 for GPT-5.6+), IgnisController.Ttl() takes a Codex or any other chat's lifetime from the stream's write buckets when it wrote (1 h over 5 min), else the points' ttlMainSeconds (sub-agent: ttlSubagentSeconds), so a 30-minute model is a 30-minute chat. Two controller sites passed no lifetime and so used the points' even when the writes had shown another: the Kept warm credit (a read after a ping) and the cache-went-cold Lost line now pass the chat's own lifetime (chat.Ttl), so a plan chat that fell to 5-minute writes (paid credits) loses the 5-minute write, not the 1-hour one. The Claude 1-hour decision (IgnisCacheLifetime.Worth, which prices the 5-minute and 1-hour fields by design) is untouched.
3. PI LEARNS ITS GAPS: pi gave Ignis no cache numbers, so provider "pi" had no history. PiSession.HandleMessageEnd now reports each finished assistant message's usage as ProviderEvent.CacheUsage (PiSession.CacheUsageOf): input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite (the *Tokens spellings the usage panel already reads too), the model as the message's provider and model ("anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"), else the session's. pi names no write lifetime, so its writes go in the unlabelled bucket (priced at the 5-minute premium, the premium a 1-hour retention would raise). A message with no cache fields, no tokens, or a role other than assistant reports nothing. The controller already records the gap of the first request after an idle spell for any reporting provider; pi has no model points, so no money is claimed for it.
4. PI RETENTION GATE (IgnisPiRetention.Decide in Core, pure, seam IgnisSeams.PiRetention, answered by IgnisController.ChoosePiRetention, bound in IgnisRuntimeStartup): PiSession.WithIgnisCacheRetention(environment, thread, model) sets PI_CACHE_RETENTION=long only when Ignis is on for the chat, the variable is absent (any letter case; a user value is never replaced and the rule is not even asked) and the verdict says so. The rule, by the upstream in pi's "provider/id" launch model (else the newest request pi was seen to make): openai and openai-codex, the 24-hour retention carries no write premium (SOURCE FACT, pi-coding-agent README "Anthropic: 1h, OpenAI: 24h" and openai.md), so it always pays: long. anthropic, the same gap rule as Claude's 1-hour choice, the same function and constants (IgnisCacheLifetime.Worth, MinimumGaps 12, Margin 1.1) over pi's Anthropic requests only, priced on the points of the model id without pi's prefix (the launch model's for a request with none): long when benefit > cost x 1.1 and at least 12 gaps were seen; otherwise nothing is set (TooFewGaps, NotWorthIt, NoPrices). Any other or unknown upstream (google, openrouter, no model named and none seen): pi's setting does nothing there, so nothing is set. RISK, accepted: with no model named and no history the first launch sets nothing and a later launch decides; the variable is read at launch, so a model switched mid-chat keeps the launch decision until the chat restarts.
5. FILES: Core Port/Ignis/Engine/IgnisMoney.cs, IgnisPiRetention.cs (new), Port/Ignis/IgnisSeams.cs. Services Providers/PiSession.cs. App IgnisController, IgnisRuntimeStartup. Tests: Core IgnisThirtyMinuteWriteTests (exact decimals for GPT-6.1 Sol: tier and step writes, rebuild premium 0.24 / 1.44 / 0.19, ping worth 0.12 against 0.01017, keep-warm decision at 28 minutes, tidy break-even 122223 against 111112) and IgnisPiRetentionTests (every reason, the margin edge at 134265 and 134266 written tokens); Services IgnisRequestLeverTests (the gated Pi behaviour: unbound, no rule, long, user value kept in any case, free OpenAI, five not-paying reasons, Ignis off, and the real rule), PiSessionTests (cache numbers reported; Start sets the variable only with the rule's yes), fixtures/pi-cli/PiStandIn.cs also records PI_CACHE_RETENTION; App IgnisIntegrationControllerTests (30-minute Codex chat and its Lost 0.0984, plan chat on 5-minute writes losing 0.242075, pi gaps learned, ChoosePiRetention on a manual clock).
## ED-NEW-ignis-guards: keep-warm guards, the sidebar keep-warm mark, the switch-cost notice and the never-reused check, 2026-10-10
2026-10-10 - Ignis refinement unit C (branch claude/ignis-guards, from claude/release-integration). ENGINEERING DECISION unless a line says SOURCE FACT or OWNER. Test traits cite Decision OD-0134. IgnisMoney.cs and PiSession.cs were not touched (another unit's files; IgnisMoney is only read).
1. OWNER (the question): "Not every chat stays active; I have lots of old chats. If Ignis was on, will it keep sending messages in old chats to keep the cache warm? If that's an issue, how do we solve it?" Ignis must launch complete: the most savings, never lower work quality. Answer: keep-warm now stops by itself; nothing here changes what the model sees (no prompt, message, tool or context is edited), the guards only decide whether a keep-warm ping is sent.
2. OWNER (guard changes, relayed by the lead): no lock or away pause ("the owner often starts work and locks the PC"; never wake the PC, no lock seam): IgnisPause.Locked is no longer produced and a locked PC is still kept warm (test A_locked_pc_is_still_kept_warm replaces the old "locked" row of the pause theory). The "6 consecutive pings" rule is replaced by the idle limit (test Pings_stop_at_the_idle_limit replaces Pings_stop_after_the_idle_stretch_limit; the stricter rule now stops at the limit, not after a ping count). Kept: at most 3 chats warm (the most recently used) and a daily spend cap.
3. IDLE LIMIT (IgnisKeepWarmGuards.IdleLimit, Settings › Ignis). OWNER: "Cool idle chats after" (1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24 hours, Never; default 12 hours) and "Learn when to cool" (default on). Both on: the sooner of the learned time and the fixed limit; learning off: the fixed limit only; Never with learning: the learned time capped at 24 hours; both off: no idle limit (the three-chat and daily caps still apply). The learned time is the 90th percentile of the chat's own breaks (at least 5), else of every chat's breaks for the provider (IgnisGapHistory), else 3 hours; never under one cache lifetime, so the first keep-warm of a break stays possible. A draft in the composer sets the learned part aside (the user is coming back): the fixed limit, or 24 hours with Never. The idle clock starts at the chat's last real turn. Settings persist in the one "ignis" key (coolAfterHours: a number or null, written only when not 12; learnCooling written only when off); an older file reads the defaults; a value outside the menu (1-168) is shown in its place.
4. THREE CHATS (IgnisKeepWarmGuards.WarmSlots): of the chats Ignis would keep warm, the three most recently used, a chat on screen or with a draft first. Turning one off frees its place.
5. DAILY ALLOWANCE (IgnisKeepWarmGuards.DailyAllowance): $0.50 plus what keep-warm saved over the 7 days ending today, less what pings cost on the 6 days before today, never below $0.50 (so learning never deadlocks). Ping cost = a day's Spent minus its longer-lifetime writes. Once today's pings reach it, keep-warm rests until tomorrow.
6. HISTORY, NOT THE TIMELINE: a held keep-warm writes one History row per reason and idle stretch (KeepWarmHeld with the reason: IdleLimit, DailyLimit, OtherChats); the user's Turn off (LetCool) and Turn on (KeepWarmOn) and the never-reused flag (CacheNotReused with the cause) are History rows too. None is a timeline line. A chat the user turned off records no Lost amount when it goes cold (the user was done with it). The report adds today's ping count and cost, the hold reason and the never-reused line.
7. THE SIDEBAR MARK. OWNER: the control lives only in the left sidebar chat list ("Do NOT add anything new at the top of the chat"; the Kindle capsule and popover stay as they were, but for item 9). The owner picked variant B of the review mock (work/design/nth-brand/ignis-sidebar-review.html) with two changes. A warm chat: a thin ember line (2.5 pt wide, 2 pt corner, 7 pt in from the top and bottom, 2 pt from the leading edge), the ember gradient (#ffd57e to #ff6a1f) with a soft glow, breathing (opacity .8 to 1 over 2.6 s on the paced ambient clock, never waking main; Reduce Motion: still). No flame at rest. A completely invisible hover zone (the row's full height, 32 pt wide; with the pill one hover region, 120 ms of grace) fades in the flame at +14 % brightness and slides a glass pill out to its left (0.2 s ease-out, 6 pt), masking the title's end. Lit, the pill reads "Turn off": the flame douses (0.42 s: squashes toward its base and settles, glow out, colour to the cold grey) and the line turns dim cold grey (.5 opacity, no glow, no breath). OWNER: "the pill must then change to turn on, to provide the user an option to turn Ignis back on for that chat": cooled, hovering shows the dim flame and "Turn on", which lights it again and resumes keep-warm. OWNER: "tooltip looks bad, remove it": no tooltip at all. Clicking the flame never cools it (it selects the row). The row's context menu offers the same "Turn off" / "Turn on" (keyboard access). Rows Ignis never kept warm show nothing. Reduce Motion: every change is instant. The pixel test proves the zone draws nothing outside the flame and the pill.
8. MARK PLACEMENT: the zone's right edge sits where the title's room ends (the row's padding plus its trailing clearance, as that clearance glides on hover), so it never covers the time, the status or the hover buttons; the title keeps its full width at rest. The look is one view (IgnisSidebarMark) over a per-row state (IgnisRowWarmth: lit / cooled / none, until when it stays warm, saved today) kept by IgnisRowWarmthSource, so another look can replace it without touching the rules (lead). The mark is lit while Ignis would keep the chat warm now (on, Auto, warm, not paused, not past its idle limit, within today's allowance and among the three); cooled once it was lit and is not; a restart forgets which chats were lit.
9. TURN ON (IIgnisController.KeepWarmAgain): only on a cooled chat. Keep-warm resumes as if the chat had just been used (its idle limit starts again and it ranks first among the three). A warm cache is kept warm from here; a cold one is never rebuilt by this (that would spend a cache write the user did not ask for): the mark stays lit until its new idle limit and keep-warm starts with the next message.
10. BOTH PLACES FOR THE SETTINGS. OWNER: the two idle-limit settings appear in Settings › Ignis and in the Kindle popover (a compact section, the existing row, switch and menu parts), one source of truth (IgnisSettings), both views updating live (IgnisCoolingControls). Words in IgnisSettingsWords.
11. SWITCH-COST NOTICE: when a chat whose cache is warm and at least 50K tokens changes model, one timeline line (and History row) before the next send: "Switching to Opus 5.5 rebuilds 300K tokens: about $1.50." (the prefix at the new model's write price for the lifetime the chat writes, in the tier of the prefix's size; IgnisModelPoints, IgnisMoney.Tier read only). Never blocks, never changes the conversation; once per target model; switching back clears it. "Start fresh with a summary" is not offered: nth has no new-chat-from-summary facility (HandoffSummary is for account switches, and /compact on the new model would read the whole chat cold), so the notice is shown alone.
12. CACHE NEVER REUSED (IgnisKeepWarmGuards.NotReused, report only): the last 4 main-chat turns each read at most 2 % of a prompt of at least 4,096 tokens (the largest provider minimum). Likely cause, in order: the model changed between them, the effort changed, nothing was written either (no caching), every turn wrote it again (the start of the chat changes: tools or instructions), else unknown. Flagged once per streak in History and the report; a real read clears it.
13. FILES: Core IgnisContract, IgnisRuntimeContract, IgnisSettings, IgnisSettingsWords, IgnisWords, Engine/IgnisEngine, Engine/IgnisReportText, Engine/IgnisKeepWarmGuards (new). Services IgnisSavingsLedger (event names and the reason field). App IgnisController, ThreadRuntimeIgnis (effort), AppModelIgnis and AppModel (model changes), IgnisEventLine, KindlePopover, Settings/IgnisSettingsPage, Settings/IgnisCoolingControls (new), Views/IgnisSidebarMark (new), Views/Sidebar/SidebarView (SidebarThreadRow's mark, context menu item and ThreadRowFace's clearance hook). Screenshots: work/design/nth-brand/built/ignis-*.png.

## ED-NEW-warmupsplit-1
2026-10-11 - The GPU warm-up draws one GPU draw a step, so a step fits a 60 Hz frame on a cached launch (claude/native-fixes; GR-1, ED-252, ED-288, OD-0090, OD-0105, OD-0108; the owner's zero-stutter bar). ENGINEERING DECISION.
1. CAUSE: EffortSliderNativeFrameTests.On_a_second_launch_the_knob_programs_come_from_the_cache bounds every step of a cached launch under 1000/60 ms, and several steps made several programs and drew whole frames. Measured on an independent ANGLE D3D11 context drawing the registered programs as GpuBootPreparation does (this PC, scaling 1.5, programs from the cache): noise 19-21 ms, light-rotate 44, liquid 41, strike 352 (its 42 Mix frames, a fresh lightning frame being about 475 anti-aliased strokes, 11-18 ms of CPU each time). The bound is kept as it is.
2. SITES (Marrow.UI.Port.GpuWarmSites): the drawing code numbers its GPU draws with GpuWarmSites.Draw(): ComposerLightRenderer's rounded-rectangle bake, its beam shader, the blob bake's passes and the aura; LiquidLayers' passes, palette ink, palette loading, bubbles, Mix rings, light composite, rings, Mix raster, resolved strike, legacy painter and glass. Inside a warm-up part (GpuWarmSites.Only, thread-static, opened by the step on its own thread) only the part's site draws; every other site still makes its surfaces, snapshots and paints as a real frame does, so the drawn site makes the program a whole frame makes. The family's last part also draws every later site, so a site added later is never left out. Outside a part every site draws (one thread-static read).
3. PARTS: GpuProgram.Family names what a part belongs to; the registry holds the knob's four programs, light-rotate[0..4], light-moving[0..2], light-aura[0..2], liquid[0..7], strike[legacy 0..7] and, for each brand (Claude, Silver, Copilot) and Mix strike (36862, 36863, 36870, 36875, 36887, 36898, 36918), strike[<brand> <strike> a|b|c]: the fresh lightning (35 ms in) with its even masks, with its odd masks, and the settled frame (1.3 s in), each on a fresh LiquidLayers. 92 steps (was 9). The site counts are pinned by a test that counts them (5, 3, 3, 8, 8); the same counts were read on ANGLE. StrikeWarmup.DrawMix keeps its whole-frame behaviour for its tests.
4. NO COVERAGE LOSS: on ANGLE the whole frames (as drawn before) and the parts make the identical set of 43 cache entries (the same file names); a test pins that the Mix parts draw every ink, light and wash pass the whole Mix draws and that the two halves stroke every mask once.
5. COUNTS: IsWarm and the warm marker count families (9), not parts, so a machine needs the same entries as before; GpuWarmup.Families. Done keeps the last 256 steps (was 64: a pass is 92).
6. PACE: once two calm frames came, the idle fallback steps a part a frame while nothing animates (calm frames are counted from step to step in a pass); anything that animates, a hold or input waits for two calm frames again. After the cap, one a frame as before.
7. MEASURED per step on that context after the worker pass (ED-NEW-warmupsplit-2), program load and flush included: noise 4-5 ms, fluid 3-4, orb 3-4, page 5, the light parts at most 7.4 (light-rotate[0]: the blur bake's 8 programs), the liquid parts at most 2.5, the legacy strike parts at most 2.8, the Mix parts at most 11 (a brand's first part loads its 5 to 7 programs); about 260 ms over the 92 steps. UNVERIFIED in the app's own window until the native run.

## ED-NEW-warmupsplit-2
2026-10-11 - No warm-up phase holds the UI thread for long, and no compile sits between a key and its handling (claude/native-fixes; ED-252, ED-NEW-launch-fix, OD-0108). ENGINEERING DECISION.
1. WHAT BLOCKS: Avalonia 12.1.2 (decompiled) makes the UI thread wait for the render thread: CompositingRenderer.Paint (WM_PAINT) goes through MediaContext.ImmediateRenderRequested to SyncCommit and batch.Rendered.Wait(), and a popup or window closing (Dispose) through SyncDisposeCompositionTarget to batch.Processed.Wait(). A warm-up step runs on the render thread (the Primer), so a popover that opens or closes while a step draws waits for the whole step. In the lead's run B (StepsDone 0 before and after, the Escape handled about 500 ms after its key down) the UI thread was in such a wait while the render thread was busy for about 500 ms. UNRESOLVED which work: StepsDone counts finished steps only, so a step in flight (the noise program compiled cold) and the popover's own first frame compiling its programs (none warmed yet) both fit; the second is more likely for 500 ms. Logging StepsAsked and the AuroraBootTrace spans in the native run would tell.
2. WORKER PASS: before an idle pass's first step, once a process and scaling, GpuBootPreparation.Run draws every program of the pass on its own ANGLE D3D11 context on its worker thread (Boot B's independent context, its own EGL display; only program binaries cross, through GpuProgramCache). On an uncached launch the compiles happen there (about 1.3 s on this PC) and the render thread's steps only load; on a cached launch it pays the drawing code's first run there (about 350 ms), so a step is its GPU draw. The cap counts from the pass's start, the worker pass inside it. A failure (no ANGLE, no cache folder) only leaves the steps doing it all as before. The first-run screen's WarmAsync is unchanged (it compiles on purpose, with its progress shown), and Boot B keeps GpuBootPreparation as it was.
3. NO CPU PREPARATION: drawing the warm-up frames on the CPU first (tried, to pay the code's first run off the render thread) changed what 10 of the 43 programs compile to (the next process missed them and made them again: Skia's caches serve both). No part of the warm-up is drawn on the CPU; the worker draws on the GPU as the steps do.
4. INPUT QUIET: class handlers on every TopLevel (key down and up, text, pointer pressed and released, wheel; every route, handled events too) note the time of the user's last input on the port's clock; the idle fallback asks no step for InputQuiet (300 ms) after it, the cap included, so a step is not drawn just as a key opens or closes a popover. A pointer that only moves does not hold it. A frame wait that times out while held or after input takes a timer's turn before it waits again.
5. Each step is frame-sized when cached (ED-NEW-warmupsplit-1), so a sync wait that meets one waits about a frame at most.

## ED-NEW-warmupsplit-3
2026-10-11 - A warm-up step is labelled forced only when something animates as the cap lets it through (claude/native-fixes; ED-252; EffortSliderNativeFrameTests.The_knob_warm_up_waits_until_the_animation_stops). ENGINEERING DECISION.
1. Before: Forced was true whenever the cap ran out before two calm frames, even when the animation had stopped (a step at the cap in a calm moment was called forced). Now the cap's answer is Animating(frames) read at that moment, on both of its paths (the cap reached, or no frame within the cap). A hold never lets the cap through, so held || Animating reduces to Animating. When the cap lets a step through is unchanged.
2. Consumers checked: GpuWarmupStep.Forced is read by no product code; the native records print it; EffortSliderNativeFrameTests asserts every step unforced when the track stopped and every step forced when it animated throughout (both hold); EffortSliderJewelWarmupTests asserts the steps after the cap forced while frames animate throughout, and WarmAsync's reports unforced.

## ED-NEW-glassslots-1
2026-10-11 - Every glass container of 2 to 8 pieces draws with one merged program, so a piece coming or going never links a program on the render thread (claude/native-fixes; PR-WIN-180, PR-CHAT-110; the owner's zero-stutter bar; TimelineRowsNativeReviewKeysTests.REVIEW_Escape_and_Return_reach_the_rename_and_archive_popovers_once_each). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (Skia programs; no Swift counterpart).
1. CAUSE (measured with temporary probes, not committed): the test failed about half its runs with "Escape did not close the rename popover". In the native session the program cache is off, so programs link cold on the render thread, and the UI thread waits on the render thread. As the test opened the popover, the seeded thread's git state arrived and two of the main window's glass containers changed piece count: the ChatChromeRow container from 6 to 7 pieces (the branch menu appeared) and the ComposerArea container from 1 to 2 (the changes tab appeared). GlassMaterial made one SKRuntimeEffect per count, so each was a new program: count 7 (cache entry 63924181..., 336 KB binary) linked in about 3.1 s and count 2 (767f5231...) in about 0.47 s (from a warm cache they still cost 64 to 237 ms on the window device). The 3.1 s link held the test's UI calls; the Escape was pressed just after it, the count-2 link began 12 to 18 ms after the press and delayed the close to 506 to 683 ms after it, past the 460 ms the test reads at. A real user meets the same thing: the first popover after a thread's state arrives froze the window for seconds.
2. FIX (Marrow.UI.Port.GlassMaterial): a lone piece keeps its program (its source is byte-identical). Every container of 2 to 8 pieces (WarmShapes) draws with one program of 8 slots and a "pieces" uniform: the smooth union and the nearest-piece choice are loops over the slots that stop at "pieces", reading each slot's uniforms through generated accessors; the slots past the container's pieces are set to zero. Containers above 8 pieces keep a program of their own count, as before. WarmupPrograms() now names the lone program and the merged one, and GlassVariantPreparation's variants of 2 to 8 pieces are that one program each way.
3. A FIRST TRY THAT FAILED: the merged program unrolled for 8 slots made the cold first frame link for more than 4 s, so the window opened at about 5.96 s (about 4.2 s before) and Rig.Open's 4 s bound ran out. The looped form opens it at about 3.8 to 3.9 s.
4. MEASURED with the fix (probes): cold, the thread's change linked no heavy program, the popover closed 190 to 193 ms after the Escape and no gap after the press exceeded 25 ms; from a warm cache it closed at 190 to 195 ms with no gap over 20 ms.
5. TESTS: GlassMaterialSlotsTests (new) pins that 2 to 8 pieces draw with the same program, distinct from the lone piece's, that it has 8 slots and the "pieces" uniform, and that a container of every count from 2 to 8, in a row and overlapping, draws exactly the same pixels with the merged program as with the program of its own count (GlassMaterial.CountProgramsForTests draws with the latter; zero differing pixels). A guard shifted by one slot fails it with 560 to 1225 differing pixels. The native test's 800 ms and 460 ms are unchanged.

## ED-NEW-warmupsplit-4
2026-10-11 - Each brand's first Mix strike frame is warmed one GPU draw a step, and the Mix raster's paint is six sites (claude/native-fixes; ED-NEW-warmupsplit-1; EffortSliderNativeFrameTests.On_a_second_launch_the_knob_programs_come_from_the_cache). ENGINEERING DECISION.
1. CAUSE (cached launch, this PC, per-step programs loaded counted with a temporary probe on GpuProgramCache's hits): strike[Claude 36862 a] loaded 7 programs in 20.8 to 21.6 ms and strike[Silver 36862 a] 4 in 19.9 to 20.0 ms, one step each; inside them the Mix raster's paint, one site, loaded 6 (Claude) and 4 (Silver) in 14.1 to 20.8 ms.
2. SPLIT: StrikeWarmup draws each brand's first strike's first part (the fresh lightning with its even masks) in MixSites (14) parts, strike[<brand> 36862 a0] to a13, one site each, the last every later one too; its b and c parts and the brand's later strikes link nothing new and stay whole. StrikeRaster.Paint numbers six sites on every paint, in order: the masks' strokes, the soft ink layer's fill, its blur, the sharp ink layer, the light, and the bursts with the light's screen; LiquidLayers no longer gates the paint as one site. Outside a warm-up part every site draws, so a real frame paints as before. The registry's 94 programs become 133 (the strike step's 71 parts become 110 in FirstRunPreparation's plan).
3. NO COVERAGE LOSS: on the second launch the cache found 89 entries and missed none, as before the split; a test pins that each new part draws exactly one of its frame's 14 sites, that the sites together draw the ink, light and wash passes the whole part drew, and the parts' names.
4. MEASURED after (cached launch, native, two runs): every strike part at most 10.1 ms (strike[Silver 36862 a9], the soft ink's blur, 2 programs; strike[Claude 36862 a7], the strokes, 3 programs, 8.5 ms; one 12.2 ms step that loaded nothing was CPU time in the drawing code, 0.9 ms in the other run).
5. UNRESOLVED: four steps stay over 1000/60 ms and the native test still fails on them; each is a single Skia draw on the window's D3D11 device whose time is in the flush, with the program loaded from the cache: light-rotate[0] 16.3 to 17.5 ms (the blurred rounded rectangle's bake, 8 programs made inside one DrawRoundRect), light-rotate[4] 25.4 to 26.3 ms, light-moving[2] 21.4 to 22.2 ms and light-aura[2] 31.3 to 35.5 ms (one program each). A program cannot be split into sites; what the window's device spends on a cached binary (the driver compiling it on each launch, as the worker devices do not) is unexplained. The bound is kept.
6. HEADLESS TEST: EffortSliderJewelWarmupTests.Warm_async_hurries_an_idle_warm_up_already_running bounded the hurried warm-up's two passes (one part a frame, run one after the other: the idle run in the same window, then the first run's own pass) by 5 s of wall time (pinned so in c90421293). A headless frame there costs 16 to 25 ms of timer and sleep, and a step is now and then answered a frame late, so the bound held the 186 parts of then at about 1.26 frames a part and failed once the parts grew (5.9 s for 234 parts at 9 sites; the parts' own drawing about 1 s of it). It now counts frames, at the same strictness a part: at most 5 frames for every 4 parts of the two passes and 10 more (342 for 266 parts; measured 306 to 316, about 1.14 to 1.18 a part), where a run still waiting for idle frames would need the 60 s cap (about 2800 frames). Warm_async_hurries_the_idle_warm_ups_going_in_its_window keeps its 5 s (its two runs step side by side; it passes with the 133 parts).

## ED-NEW-ignisadvisor-1
2026-10-11 - The Claude advisor is a model choice in the chat's model picker, "Sonnet 5.5 + Opus advisor": the chat runs on Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Code's own advisor tool asks Opus only when Sonnet is stuck; Ignis only accounts for it honestly (claude/ignis-advisor; ClaudeAdvisorModels, AdvisorPicker, ClaudeSession, IgnisController). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (no Swift counterpart).
1. OWNER: on 2026-10-11 the owner approved the advisor for this release, off by default (nothing changes until a chat picks the entry), with the main model dropping from Opus to Sonnet for that choice. The same day the owner moved it out of the Ignis settings into the model picker (entry "Sonnet 5.5 + Opus advisor", subtitle "Opus steps in only when Sonnet is stuck · about half the cost"), and gave cross-provider advice to Hydra (the hosted ask_advisor tool, built by the other helper). There is no Ignis setting, row or popover section for it, and Ignis books no saving for it.
2. THE OWNER'S TOO-OLD REQUEST (translated): when Claude Code is too old, the app must tell the user plainly and give a way to fix it. While the installed Claude Code cannot use the advisor, the entry still shows, its second line reads "Your Claude Code is too old for this. Update it to use it." (or, when the version could not be read, "Claude Code’s version is unknown. Update it to use it."), and an accent "Update" action (accessible name "Update Claude Code") opens Settings on the Updates page (WindowManager.ShowSettings(SettingsPage.Updates)), where the "cli:claude" row runs nth's existing "claude update". Choosing the entry while too old still works: the chat runs on Sonnet without the flag. While nth’s provider check has found no Claude Code executable the entry is not offered (there is no Claude Code to run the flag or to update; the picker then lists exactly what it listed before), and a list without Claude models never gets it. LAYOUT: the subtitle and the notes do not fit the 330-point list on one line, so the entry’s row lets its words wrap to two lines and is 15 points taller (61, the other rows keep 46); the Update action follows the words’ last word on their baseline, so the name and the words keep the row’s full width and nothing is cut short (pinned by AdvisorPickerTests: no collapsed line, no scrolling). ModelListSearch folds each row from its own height (ModelListRow.RowSlot, rowHeight for every other row), so search behaves as before.
3. LAUNCH (SOURCE FACT, code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor and the changelog): `claude --advisor opus` (a launch flag not listed by --help; the advisorModel setting is the other way). ClaudeSession passes `--model claude-sonnet-5-5 --advisor opus` for the entry, and only when all hold: `claude --version` (probed only for the entry) reads 2.1.284 or later (Sonnet 5.5 arrived in 2.1.284; the advisor itself in 2.1.117); CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL is not set (empty, "0" and "false" count as not set); none of CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY is set (the tool is Anthropic-API only). Otherwise the launch is plain Sonnet. The picker id (claude-sonnet-5-5+advisor-opus) never reaches the CLI: --model, set_model and the Ignis pricing model read its main model. Moving a chat onto or off the entry stops its session so the next message resumes with the right flags. Every other model launches with exactly the arguments it had, and starts no version probe (pinned by ClaudeSessionAdvisorTests).
4. WHY THE FLAG and its risk: the owner and the lead asked for --advisor. The docs say the CLI exits at launch when the main model cannot take the advisor, the advisor is invalid, an availableModels allowlist excludes it, or a consent is missing. The version gate removes the first two for the shipped pairing; an organisation allowlist that excludes Opus would still make the launch exit (UNRESOLVED: not detected before launch).
5. USAGE AND PRICE (SOURCE FACT, platform advisor tool docs, "Usage and billing"): the result's usage.iterations[] holds the executor's requests (type "message") and the advisor's (type "advisor_message", with its model), and the top-level usage is the executor's only. ClaudeSession.CacheUsageOf keeps advisor iterations out of the chat's buckets (so the chat's cache reuse is not credited with them) and hands each on as IgnisTurnUsage.AdvisorCalls with its model; the chat's context size is the last executor request. IgnisController prices each call with IgnisMoney.Cost at the advising model's own points (Opus's rates, not Sonnet's), books it as IgnisLedgerKind.Advice (a cost the user chose: not in Saved, not in keep-warm's Spent; IgnisDayTotals.Advice and AdviceCalls), whatever the chat's Ignis mode, and adds the chat line "Asked <model> for advice · $x" (IgnisEventKind.AdvisorAsked, stored as "advisorAsked"); the report adds "Advice: N calls cost $x" when there was any. A model without points books the call with no amount.
6. SHARED CONTRACT (src/Marrow.Core/Port/Advisor/AdvisorContract.cs, byte-identical with the Hydra helper's): AdvisorSeams.Asked is set at Ignis start-up and books hosted advice (Hydra heads asking an advisor) the same way, at the reported dollars when finite and not negative, else its tokens at the advising model's points (cached tokens taken as inside the input); no chat, nothing booked. AdvisorSeams.Choice is left at its null default here (the app does not set it in this branch); both doc comments read "Set by the app.".
7. TESTS (Decision ED-NEW-ignisadvisor-1): ClaudeSessionAdvisorTests (flag at 2.1.284 and later; none when too old, unknown, the probe fails, turned off or on a cloud provider; other models unchanged with no probe; the usage split on the docs' example), IgnisAdvisorControllerTests (price at the advisor's rates, Advice not a saving, the line, Off mode, unknown model, hosted advice), AdvisorPickerTests (placement after Sonnet, none without Claude Code found or without Claude models, the subtitle when new enough, the note and Update only when too old or unknown, not on a locked row, Update opens SettingsPage.Updates without choosing the model, choosing while too old).
8. UNRESOLVED: (a) whether Claude Code's stream-json result usage actually carries the advisor_message iterations (the API does; the CLI's pass-through is not verified offline, and no request was sent to a provider); if it does not, advice is unbilled in Ignis, never mispriced. (b) Advisor calls made by Hydra heads and subagents inside a Claude session are not split (HeadCacheUsageOf is unchanged). (c) The hosted AdvisorAdvice's InputTokens is taken to include its cached tokens. (d) The allowlist exit in 4. (e) "about half the cost" is the owner's wording, not measured here.
## ED-NEW-ignisadvisor-2
2026-10-11 - A Hydra head that nth runs as its own chat asks its lead's model for advice through ask_advisor, a tool nth hosts, whatever providers the head and the lead run (claude/advisor-host; ED-NEW-ignisadvisor-1; AdvisorHostedRouteTests). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (no Swift counterpart).
1. OWNER REQUEST (2026-10-11, translated): "multi-provider support, mix and match, e.g. Astra advises while Sonnet works", in this release; then the owner's decision the same day: "it should go inside Hydra, because Hydra runs the agents and delegates the work". So Hydra heads ask their lead: a stuck head asks the lead side of its running pair (a Sol head asks Astra 6, a Sonnet head asks Opus), on another provider or the same one. A Claude head with a Claude lead is hosted too (heads are separate sessions).
2. WHO HAS AN ADVISOR: AdvisorSeams.Choice (the shared contract, Marrow.Core.Port.Advisor.AdvisorContract) is bound by the app (AdvisorRuntimeStartup): for a Droppy head's chat it is the lead chat's provider and model (else the pair's lead model, else the provider's default); null for every other chat, a native head included (it runs inside the lead's own session). Choice is read once when a session launches.
3. HOW THE TOOL REACHES THE HEAD: only a session whose chat has an advisor gets it. Claude: the advisor server is merged into the session's one --mcp-config (the connected servers plus the advisor, in a file of the chat's own; --strict-mcp-config only when there were connected servers, as before), and the session lets its own ask_advisor run without a card, as the skills relay's tools do on ACP; a session with no advisor launches byte for byte as before (pinned against the frozen launch). Codex: the server joins the thread's config.mcp_servers. Cursor, OpenCode, OpenCode Go, Grok and Devin (ACP): appended to session/new's mcpServers. Copilot: the session.create parameters' mcpServers. The API providers (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, OpenRouter, Local): a native function tool in their own loop (NativeSkillTools). The server is nth's own executable as a stdio relay (--marrow-advisor-mcp) into one process-wide named pipe (current user only); each advised session registers a token, so the pipe knows the chat and its advisor. Not reached: Antigravity and Command Code (their MCP servers come from one shared settings file, not per session) and Pi (no MCP).
4. HOW THE ADVICE RUNS: one headless turn of a provider session made the way a chat's is (the provider's first enabled account, its login or API key; no chat id, so it never gets the tool itself): plan mode, a final-report turn, any approval declined. The prompt is a short system line (advising another AI coding model that is stuck; a concise, concrete recommendation), then the question and the context (capped at 8,000 and 40,000 characters). The reply is capped at 12,000 characters. A timeout (3 minutes), a missing account or a provider error is a short "Error: ..." tool result and the head carries on; nothing throws to the head.
5. WHAT IT COST: the turn's own cache-aware usage (else its token spend) is priced with IgnisMoney.Cost on the Ignis points' entry for the advisor model (null when the model is unknown), and AdvisorSeams.Asked gets the advice, the tokens and the dollars; each answer also leaves a one-line note in the lead's transcript.

## ED-NEW-bootpop-1

2026-10-11 - The nth boot mark without the shine (OD-0142; branch claude/boot-logo-pop). ENGINEERING DECISIONS unless noted.
1. The shadow's lift scales its offset (0.2 to 1 of the box-shadow's) and blur (0.3 to 1) with one mask filter, drawn in a frame scaled by the blur's share (the blur follows the canvas matrix). The trim's leading end is a round head clipped at the feet's line, so it lands flush on the finished glyph's butt foot (the glyph itself keeps its butt caps, as the icon). ## ED-NEW-lean-6
Lean pass unit L6 (E:/Droppy/work/lean-pass/RELEASE_PLAN.md): idle when unseen. PORT-ONLY, no visible change: same look, motion and timings.
1. WINDOW EVENTS. AmbientWindowState no longer installs SetWinEventHook(3, 0x801B) per window (32,793 event ids each, including 0x800B, the location change every caret and cursor move on the desktop raises). The process has one hook set, AmbientWindowState.Events, shared by every window's ambient state and presence and removed with its last listener: 3 (foreground), 0x0B (move/size end), 0x16-0x17 (minimise start/end), 0x8002-0x8004 (show, hide, reorder), 0x8017-0x8018 (cloak, uncloak); only OBJID_WINDOW/CHILDID_SELF events reach the listeners, and each listener posts one refresh (one walk of the windows above) per batch. Accepted risk: a window dragged over the app counts once the drag ends (0x0B), not at every move.
2. WINDOW PRESENCE. New Marrow.UI/Port/WindowPresence.cs: a window is seen when shown, not minimised, not cloaked (DWMWA_CLOAKED, which covers other virtual desktops), not fully covered, the session not locked (WTSRegisterSessionNotification, WM_WTSSESSION_CHANGE) and the display on (RegisterPowerSettingNotification GUID_CONSOLE_DISPLAY_STATE, WM_POWERBROADCAST; dimmed counts as on). The messages are observed through NativeWindowHooks, never handled. The first presence asked for tracks every window of the app (open ones and, through Window.WindowOpenedEvent, later ones) and sets HangWatchdog.Quiet: quiet while no tracked window is seen. A non-Win32 window has no presence and counts as always seen (headless tests use WindowPresence.TestFactory).
3. CONSUMERS. NthMotionHandler asks for no animation frame while its window is unseen; seen again it invalidates and asks, so its next frame is the painter at the current time (painters are pure functions of the frame and the time: every loop resumes in phase). NthElapsedTime (the working line's clock) sets no timer while unseen and, seen again, shows the current time at once (SetTextInstantly, so no roll from the stale time) and ticks on the same one-second grid. HangWatchdog's thread neither pings nor checks main while quiet (its 0.5 s sleep stays; main is not woken); the first beat after a quiet spell restarts the wait for main's answer (State.Resume), so the spell is never a stall. HangWatchdog.Quiet is a public static field, so the type's public methods stay Start alone (HangWatchdogTests). RenderFrameSource reads DWM's timing (RefreshSource) once per refresh and shares it among every source ticking in it (keyed by the compositor's tick time, as AmbientRefreshPacer).
4. BUDGETS (Debug, headless, manual clocks; first limit about 1.5x the measured base, then about 1.3x the new value, never above the old): NthUnseenFrameBudgetTests, frame requests in one simulated second at 240 Hz while unseen: 240 before, 0 after (limit 360, now 0). HangWatchdogQuietBudgetTests, pings in 10 simulated seconds while quiet: 20 before, 0 after (limit 30, now 0). AmbientWinEventHookBudgetTests, event ids hooked with two windows' ambient states: 65,586 before, 9 after (limit 98,379, now 11). RenderFrameSourceSharedTimingTests, DWM timing reads per refresh with two sources: 2.0 before, 1.0 after (limit 3.0, now 1.3). NthElapsedTimeUnseenTests, clock text changes in 10 simulated seconds while unseen: 10 before, 0 after (limit 15, now 0).
5. GUARDS. Restore: After_hidden_then_seen_the_first_frame_is_the_painter_at_the_current_time (the restored window draws on the next refresh, at the clock's current time, with an unchanged frame, and its pixels equal a window that was never hidden). The hook test asserts the five ranges installed once for two windows, 0x800B never heard, and the hooks removed with the last listener. The watchdog test asserts no stall report after the quiet spell and pings resuming. The clock test asserts the current time shown at once (no previous word) and the next tick a second later. No test was replaced or loosened; test seams added: AmbientWindowState.SetHook/Unhook/Events, NthMotionControl.FrameRequests/LastDrawnAt, HangWatchdog.Runner's optional quiet.
6. REVIEW FIXES (ED-NEW-lean-6, follow-up commit; no visible change, no budget limit moved). (a) A hang that begins while the app is unseen: the stuck main thread cannot refresh the presence, so WindowPresence.Quiet is false while any tracked window's thread has stopped answering (IsHungAppWindow, asked from the watchdog's thread, never waking main; WindowPresence.Hung is the test seam). HangWatchdog.Quiet became a nested type (Use, and an internal Now read with Volatile), so HangWatchdog's own public methods stay Start alone. Accepted cost: Windows calls a window hung after 5 s without taking messages, and the watchdog's 4 s wait starts when the quiet ends, so such a hang is reported about 9 s after it began, with the stall counted from the quiet's end. (b) A stuck pause: with 0x800B dropped, a covering window restored from maximised, snapped, or moved with Win+Shift+Arrow raises only a location change, so the app stayed unseen until it took the foreground. The hub (AmbientWindowState.EventHub, one per process; tests swap in their own) now hears the location changes of the processes covering a fully covered app window (one 0x800B hook per covering process, top-level windows only, removed when nothing of the app is covered or the last listener goes), and pointer input over an unseen window looks again. Every window is looked at once per flush however many listeners ask. The process-wide hooks are unchanged: 9 event ids for two windows (limit 11). (c) Tests: WindowPresenceTests (the Quiet aggregate and the hung escape; each window counted once, a closed one leaving the counts; a live presence through cloak, cover, the covering process's location change, child and non-window events ignored, pointer recovery, minimise, hide; WM_WTSSESSION_CHANGE and WM_POWERBROADCAST parsing with off, dimmed, on, wrong GUID, short payload, other events and lock with the display off; the covering arithmetic in physical pixels through the new pure AmbientWindowState.Covers, which stops walking once nothing shows). HangWatchdogQuietBudgetTests.A_hang_that_begins_while_quiet_is_reported_once_the_quiet_ends. (d) AmbientWinEventHookBudgetTests now records through a hub of its own instead of the static SetHook seam, so no listener left by another test can make the result depend on order; the check is stricter (also every process-wide hook for process 0, nothing removed while a window listens, every installed hook removed at the end). (e) Process: the before numbers in point 4 were measured on the unchanged base in the builder's working tree before the fix, but were committed together with the fix in one commit, so history cannot reproduce them (no amend or force push to split it). Runs (Debug, headless, heavy slot): Marrow.UI.Tests WindowPresence/Ambient/Nth/RenderFrameSource 204 passed; Marrow.Core.Tests HangWatchdog 13 passed; Marrow.App.Tests NthElapsed/NthWorkingLine/AmbientTrack 2 passed.

## ED-NEW-lean-7
Lean pass unit L7 (E:/Droppy/work/lean-pass/RELEASE_PLAN.md): FrameClock's slow draw loops wake only when due; draw loops get no frames while no window can be seen. PORT-ONLY, no visible change: the same draws at the same instants by the same maths. src/Marrow.UI/Port/FrameClock.cs only. Amends ED-117 (1) ("frames are the only wake-ups") in how a frame is asked for, never in what decides a draw.
1. WAKE WHEN DUE. IWakeFrameSource (WakePeriod, RequestFrameAt(instant or null, frame)) is the frame source for draw loops: DisplayLink and AnimationTimeline ask through it, every other caller keeps RequestFrame. A DisplayLink with a preferred rate and an AnimationTimeline with a minimum interval (the timed ED-232 path) compute the instant their next draw is due (FrameClock.DueAt: the first instant IsComplete holds, 1 ms early) and, when that is more than 2.5 refreshes away, hold the request back until 1.5 refreshes before it (FrameClock.WakeFor); from there they ask at every frame as before, so the draw lands on the same refresh. Every frame skipped comes before the due instant, where the maths would not have drawn. A changed rate or schedule withdraws a held request and asks at the next frame, as every request did. The refresh-counting path (ED-248 review 2) and every-frame schedules are unchanged.
2. PRODUCTION SOURCE. AvaloniaFrameSource asks the platform through IFrameHost (production Win32FrameHost; tests a fake). On a Win32 window (HWND) it holds requests back with one one-shot high-resolution waitable timer (CREATE_WAITABLE_TIMER_HIGH_RESOLUTION; the system timer resolution is untouched, R-VIEW-10); a background thread waits on it and posts the wake-up to main at Normal priority, above Render and UiThreadRender, so a render job already queued for the next frame runs after it and the request it asks for is in that frame. The timer is armed for the earliest instant anything waits for; armed earlier already, it stays (a wake-up with nothing due re-arms; a withdrawn request's wake-up asks nothing). WakePeriod is DWM's refresh period (read again after a second); null without HWND, DWM or the high-resolution timer: nothing is held back.
3. UNSEEN. While every shown window of the app is minimised (IsIconic) or cloaked (DWMWA_CLOAKED, other virtual desktops), AvaloniaFrameSource asks for no frames for draw loops: their requests are parked (still counted in Pending, ED-252, and withdrawn by CancelFrame) and asked for when a window can be seen again. All windows, not the host TopLevel alone: the process has one frame source and one MediaContext (Program.cs). No shown window, or a non-Win32 one, counts as seen (AvaloniaFrameSource.NoWindowSeen). The look is cached 100 ms and redone at once on WindowState, IsActive or IsVisible changes (the hooks post a re-look at Normal); parked requests look again every 100 ms on the high-resolution timer, or, without it, on a waitable timer of the system's resolution (15.6 ms), so a window back from another virtual desktop without an activation change resumes within about 100 ms either way (within 116 ms on the coarse timer); a request parked later never puts the next look off.
4. NOT PARKED (review 2026-10-11). RequestFrame is never parked: transitions and their completions (OpacityTransition, LinkFlyMark, OpinionArrival, SkillsMotion, HydraPanel and others), ComposerCapsuleSeams.FinishTick, DeferredRows, GettingReadySheet and every FrameClock.TrySleep loop get frames while minimised as before (on the Mac those are timers and CA completions, which do not stop with the window). Only the draw loops park. Their callers, checked: every TimelineView/AnimationTimeline update (HydraProgressBar bar and title, TimelineRows shimmer, EffortSlider, KindleArt) draws a function of the time (SwiftUI does not update a TimelineView that is not drawn); the DisplayLinks of StreamVeil and LinkTextVeil set the veil's time and paint, and stop or settle when the fade is over (on return, at the first frame); VoiceGlowLayer, VoiceOrbSlot, VoicePill and VoicePillSlot step what they draw; DictationLayer moves the dictated words and publishes the live draft (V-8.2) from its tick, and hands over or withdraws when its motion ends: while minimised those wait for the window, and the landed text is the session's one edit (TranscriptUpdateKind.Landing, editor.LiveText), not the tick's, and HandOverNow (a send, the composer leaving, a new dictation) still ends it at once. Accepted: a dictation's live draft and its hand-over wait while no window can be seen.
5. LIMIT. Frames on the compositor's render thread (RenderFrameSource, given by AvaloniaFrameSource.RenderFrames: ambient and onRenderThread timelines, the most frequent loops) are neither held back nor parked by this unit; gating them needs RenderFrameSource.cs, outside L7's files (reported to the lead). "No frames while unseen" holds for main-thread draw loops only.
6. MARGIN. A held request is asked for 1.5 refreshes before its draw is due (6.25 ms at 240 Hz, 10.4 ms at 144, 25 ms at 60). The draw lands on the same refresh as before when the timer's lateness plus the time until the UI thread runs the posted wake-up stays inside that margin; a UI thread busy past it (or a wake-up later than it) makes that one draw land a refresh later than the every-frame path, whose callback waited in the frame queue. Measured, real kernel timer, Debug test host under the full Marrow.UI.Tests run (FrameClockWin32HostTests, 40 armings of 4 ms): lateness min 0.027 ms, median 0.499 ms, 90th percentile 0.623 ms, max 4.400 ms (one outlier under the 6.25 ms margin); guarded at median under 2 ms and 90th percentile under 4 ms. The UI thread's part is not measured here (it needs a native run); the wake-up runs at Normal, ahead of the queued render job and of input.
7. BUDGETS (Debug, headless, ManualFrameSource at 240 Hz with ManualTimeProvider; first limit about 1.5x the measured base, then about 1.3x the new value): FrameClockPacingBudgetTests, frame requests a second: 30 Hz display link 240 before, 60 after (limit 360, now 78); 24 Hz timeline 240 before, 48 after (limit 360, now 62). FrameClockHiddenHostBudgetTests, frames delivered to a display link in 240 refreshes while no window can be seen: 240 before (window minimised), 0 after (limit 360, now 0).
8. GUARDS. FrameClockPacingEquivalenceTests: the draw instants of 30/24/20 Hz links and timelines (also paused, resumed and re-timed) on 240, 144 and 60 Hz displays, with and without jitter, recorded as digests on the unchanged base (1fdf47b43), hold both for a source that holds nothing back and for one whose requests sleep. FrameClockWakeTests: ManualFrameSource's held requests, withdrawal, and rates changed while a request sleeps draw exactly where a non-holding source draws.
