## ED-NEW-lean-1
2026-10-11 - SwiftString takes ASCII fast paths and keeps the Character-walking code for everything else (claude/lean-l1; src/Marrow.Core/Port/SwiftString.cs; SwiftStringOracleTests, SwiftStringLeanBudgetTests). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (no Swift counterpart; Swift's own String has the same ASCII fast paths).
1. RULE: in ASCII text every UTF-16 unit is one Character except "\r\n" (GB3); no other grapheme rule joins two ASCII units, and an ASCII string is its own NFC form. Only a non-ASCII unit can join an ASCII unit into a longer Character (Prepend before it, Extend/ZWJ/SpacingMark after it) or be canonically equal to ASCII (U+212A KELVIN SIGN, U+037E GREEK QUESTION MARK, U+1FEF), so each fast path checks that every unit that can decide the answer is ASCII and otherwise falls back to the unchanged slow path.
2. FAST PATHS: Equal is ordinal when both strings are ASCII. Contains (both ASCII) is ordinal when the needle neither starts with "\n" nor ends with "\r"; otherwise an IndexOf loop keeps only matches whose two ends are Character boundaries. HasPrefix/HasSuffix look only at the prefix or suffix plus prefix.Length + 1 units at that end of the text (the old code needed the whole text ASCII). Split with a one-unit ASCII separator over ASCII text is an IndexOf loop that skips a "\r" or "\n" belonging to a "\r\n" (the brief allowed only texts without "\r"; the CRLF check makes CRLF texts safe too). Count is Length minus the "\r\n" pairs. Suffix/DropLast walk back from the end while the units are ASCII (the unit before the stop must be ASCII too, so a Prepend cannot sit across it) and otherwise count Characters forward without listing their starts.
3. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (crash fix, no visible change): the old Suffix(text, 0) and DropLast(text, 0) on a non-empty text threw ArgumentOutOfRangeException (they indexed one past their list of Character starts). They now give Swift's suffix(0) == "" and dropLast(0) == text. Call sites can pass 0 (HydraMergePopover trailingCount, QuestionTab Count(suffix) for an empty suffix). The oracle asserts both the old throw and the new value.
4. ORACLE: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/SwiftStringFrozen.cs is a frozen copy of the pre-change code (claude/release-integration 1fdf47b43). SwiftStringOracleTests runs 10,000 fixed-seed random cases per method (Equal, Contains, HasPrefix, HasSuffix, Split with maxSplits and omitting variants, Count, Suffix, DropLast, and SwiftStringComparer equality, hash and order plus 50 sorts of 200 items) over ASCII with CR, LF and CRLF, Latin-1, bare and attached combining marks, NFC/NFD pairs, KELVIN SIGN, GREEK QUESTION MARK, OHM/ANGSTROM singletons, emoji with ZWJ, skin tones and flags, a Prepend character and Hangul jamo; results compared by value and exceptions by type.
5. BUDGETS (Debug, AllocationProbe after warm-up, heavy slot): Contains over 500 thread titles (3 needles, one title in ten with an em dash so the slow path stays in the mix): 1,434 bytes per call before (limit 2,150), 158 after, limit tightened to 210. Split of a 10,000-character ASCII text by "\n" (247 pieces): 29,984 bytes before (limit 45,000), 29,920 after (the pieces themselves; the win there is the grapheme walk, not memory), limit tightened to 39,000. Budget tests landed green on the unchanged code first (0fee17211).
6. TESTS (Decision ED-NEW-lean-1): SwiftStringOracleTests (9), SwiftStringLeanBudgetTests (2); guards SwiftStringTests (17) and SwiftStringSplitCostTests unchanged and green. No test was loosened or removed.
## ED-NEW-lean-2
2026-10-11 - SwiftDate converts without BigInteger on the per-frame paths (claude/lean-l2; src/Marrow.Core/Port/SwiftDate.cs; SwiftDateLeanEquivalenceTests, SwiftDateLeanBudgetTests). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (Foundation's Date is a Double, so Swift has no conversion at all; ED-073 keeps DateTimeOffset as the model type).
1. RULE: ReferenceSeconds must be the Double nearest to (ticks - reference) / 10^7, ties to even, and NearestTicks the tick nearest to m x 2^e x 10^7, half to even (ED-073). Both were done in BigInteger, and the per-frame callers (StreamVeil, HydraShimmer, HangWatchdog, HydraIdleSeconds, SwiftFormatters) paid for it every frame.
2. ReferenceSeconds: when the tick offset lies within +-2^53 (mid-1972 to mid-2029) the offset and 10^7 are both exact Doubles and IEEE division is correctly rounded with ties to even, so offset / 10^7 is already the nearest Double. Outside that window the unchanged BigInteger neighbour comparison (NearestDouble) runs. Dates after mid-2029 or before mid-1972 therefore still allocate; the brief kept the old path there.
3. NearestTicks: the mantissa is below 2^53, so m x 10^7 < 2^77 is exact in UInt128; the half-to-even division by 2^shift is done in UInt128 (from a shift of 78 the value is under half a tick and rounds to 0, which also keeps every shift inside 128 bits). A non-negative exponent means at least 2^52 s (over 4 x 10^22 ticks), which the old checked BigInteger-to-Int64 conversion always rejected; it now throws the same OverflowException type directly. The final Int128-to-Int64 conversion is checked, so out-of-range values throw OverflowException as before; values that fit Int64 but not DateTimeOffset still throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the constructor. Non-finite input still traps (SwiftTrapException).
4. ORACLE: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Port/SwiftDateFrozen.cs is a frozen copy of the pre-change conversions (claude/release-integration 0a946c558). SwiftDateLeanEquivalenceTests runs 1,000,000 fixed-seed cases each way plus listed edge values. FromReferenceSeconds: uniform values across and past the DateTimeOffset range, random 53-bit mantissas with exponents -100..10 (sub-tick, the 77/78 shift cut-off, overflow), exact half-tick ties (odd/256 s), other binary fractions of a tick, raw random bit patterns (NaN, infinities, subnormals, negative zero) and present-day tick values nudged a few ulps; ticks compared exactly and exceptions by type. ReferenceSeconds: offsets inside +-2^53, at that edge, whole seconds, small offsets and the whole DateTimeOffset range; Double bits compared. No difference.
5. BUDGETS (Debug, AllocationProbe after warm-up, 1,000 present-day calls, heavy slot): ReferenceSeconds 2,464 bytes per call before (limit 3,700), 0 after; FromReferenceSeconds/NearestTicks 119 bytes per call before (limit 180), 0 after. Both limits tightened to 0 with bytes per call rounded up, so any allocation fails. Budget tests landed green on the unchanged code first (b23b285b0).
6. TESTS (Decision ED-NEW-lean-2): SwiftDateLeanEquivalenceTests (2), SwiftDateLeanBudgetTests (2); guards SwiftDateTests, TimingShapeTests and ISO8601Tests (36 with the lean tests' SwiftDate filter), Marrow.Core.Tests as a whole (5,139 of 5,140; the one failure is the open GAP acceptance test GAP_The_embedded_catalogue_has_every_required_release_pin_and_passes_the_strict_gate, missing release pins in the embedded skills catalogue, no date code), and StreamVeil/TimingShape/HydraShimmer/SwiftFormatters tests in Marrow.UI.Tests (46) unchanged and green. No test was loosened or removed.
## ED-NEW-lean-3
2026-10-12 - StripANSI and WithoutEmDashes return nothing-to-do text before any work (claude/lean-l3; src/Marrow.Core/Support/Text.cs; TextCleanupLeanBudgetTests, TextCleanupLeanEquivalenceTests). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (Swift runs its Regex and its string scans natively; the cost is the port's grapheme walk and UTF-8 copy).
1. RULE: StripANSI (26 callers, every process-exit LastLines among them) walked every grapheme of its input, NFC-normalising each, even when the text holds no escape; WithoutEmDashes copied the whole text to UTF-8 (Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes) on every streamed delta before its byte prescan. Same look, same answers.
2. StripANSI: every match of the Swift pattern \x1B\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~] starts with an ESC grapheme, and NFC never composes or decomposes anything into U+001B, so text without U+001B has nothing to strip and is now returned as is (the same string reference) before the walk. Text with an escape takes the unchanged walk.
3. WithoutEmDashes: MayContainEmDash is true exactly when the UTF-8 holds E2 80 94/95 or E2 B8 BA/BB, which only the four long dashes IsEmDash matches (U+2014, U+2015, U+2E3A, U+2E3B) encode to (a lone surrogate becomes EF BF BD). A UTF-16 IndexOfAny over those four characters now runs first and returns the input as is when none is present; otherwise the unchanged prescan and walk run. MayContainEmDash stays public for the packet's truncated-byte fixtures.
4. ORACLE: tests/Marrow.Core.Tests/Support/TextCleanupFrozen.cs is a frozen copy of the pre-change code (claude/release-integration 0a946c558). TextCleanupLeanEquivalenceTests compares 200,000 fixed-seed texts per method by value, by identity (input returned as is) and by exception type, from an alphabet built around both patterns (ESC and every CSI class edge, canonical equivalents NFC turns into pattern characters such as GREEK QUESTION MARK and KELVIN SIGN, combining marks on ESC, '[', digits and dashes, the four long dashes and their neighbours, CRLF, emoji and ZWJ sequences, Hangul jamo). No difference. One accepted difference, pinned by its own test: an escape-free text holding a lone surrogate made the old StripANSI throw from .NET's NFC normaliser (a Swift String can never hold one, so Swift has no such input); it is now returned as is. With an escape present such text still matches the frozen code exactly.
5. BUDGETS (Debug, AllocationProbe after warm-up, fixed seeds, heavy slot): StripANSI over 1 MB of escape-free CLI text 48,072,688 bytes before (limit 72,000,000), 0 after; WithoutEmDashes 96 bytes per dash-free streamed delta before (limit 144), 0 after (bytes per delta rounded up). Both limits tightened to 0, so any allocation fails. The budget tests and the oracle landed green on the unchanged code first (456599303).
6. TESTS (Decision ED-NEW-lean-3): TextCleanupLeanBudgetTests (2), TextCleanupLeanEquivalenceTests (3); guards TextCleanupTests, TextCleanupUnicodeTests and TextCleanupTrapTests (44 with the TextCleanup filter) and the whole Marrow.Core.Tests.Support namespace (767) green. No test was loosened or removed.
## ED-NEW-lean-4

2026-10-11 - Lean pass unit L4 (branch claude/lean-l4): provider streams append in place, and search_text runs off the main actor reading line by line. ENGINEERING DECISIONS; no visible change and no change to any text a provider, the timeline or the model sees.
1. STREAM BUFFERS: StreamedTextTracker (src/Marrow.Services/Providers/SessionSupport.cs, Pi and Command Code) keeps the message and thinking text in StringBuilders; MessageText and ThinkingText flatten once when read (cached until the next delta), so they are still the plain concatenation (a random 5,000-step script of starts, resets and deltas compares every read). OpenAICompatibleSession.PerformStream's content, reasoning and per-index tool-call arguments (:612-617, :675-688) moved into OpenAICompatibleSession.StreamRoundText with StringBuilders, flattened once at message end (round content, MessageCompleted, ReasoningCompleted, PendingToolCall arguments, in the same index order); the transport-error branch flattens the content only when it fires.
2. BUDGETS (StreamedTextTrackerBudgetTests, StreamRoundTextBudgetTests; AllocationProbe, 400 deltas of 40 characters, Debug): bytes per delta at 10k / 100k streamed characters. Before (string +=): message 36,064 / 216,070, thinking 36,064 / 216,064, text 36,064 / 216,072, reasoning 36,064 / 216,075, tool arguments 36,075 / 216,075 (linear in the reply). After: 80 / 80 for all five. Asserted: the 100k cost within 2x of the 10k cost, and at most 104 B (1.3x of 80).
3. SEARCH OFF MAIN: SearchText awaits Task.Run(SearchWalk) like NativeFileTools' reads (R-ISO-2); before, the whole walk ran inline on the main actor (ExecuteReadBatch hops ExecuteTool there). SearchTextOffMainTests holds the walk mid-file through the SearchFileProbeForTests seam: before, the probe ran on the main actor (test failed); after, it runs on a pool thread and the main loop still runs posted work while the search stays open.
4. LINE BY LINE: SearchFile reads 64 KB pieces through a strict UTF-8 decoder and matches each line as a span (Regex.IsMatch(span) / Contains Ordinal), building a string only for a matching line, instead of File.ReadAllBytes + SwiftText.DecodeUtf8OrNil + SwiftString.Split. Same output: a line ends at a "\n" not after "\r" (SwiftString.Split's "\n" Character; "\r\n" is one grapheme cluster and LF otherwise always stands alone, UAX #29 GB3-GB5), the piece after the last "\n" is a line even when empty, a BOM stays U+FEFF, invalid or cut-off UTF-8 anywhere drops the file's matches (skipped whole, as before), a file File.ReadAllBytes refused (open failure, longer than Array.MaxLength) is skipped. Decision kept: no new exclusions and no size cap. Only difference: a file between about 1 GB and 2 GB of text, whose whole-file decode could not fit one string and failed the search, is now searched.
5. GOLDEN (SearchTextGoldenTests): fixed goldens for CRLF, mixed endings, no final newline, a final newline, lone CR, a combining mark after LF, empty lines (regex ^$, including the piece after the last newline), BOM, invalid UTF-8 early and late; pieces straddling 1, 4, 16, 64 and 80 KB buffer edges; 150 random files (fixed seed) with 3 searches each against a frozen copy of the whole-file search. All passed on the unchanged code first.
## ED-NEW-lean-5

Lean pass unit L5 (2026-10-11): a streamed reply and tool output without whole-string copies. Files: src/Marrow.App/Runtime/ThreadRuntime.cs, src/Marrow.Core/Models/Timeline.cs. No visible change: every row's text, every flush delay tier and every tool Output is the same string as before.
1. PENDING TEXT. PendingDelta becomes a class: later deltas of a flush window are appended to a StringBuilder and Text flattens once when read (PendingFlushLength at the start of the window, FlushDeltas at its end). Text still reads as one flat string (the reflection tests of ThreadRuntimePart7Tests read and set it unchanged). Before, every delta copied the whole pending text (`pending with { Text = pending.Text + delta }`), quadratic for a tool-output burst.
2. FLUSH DELAY TIER. PendingFlushLength keeps the exact Swift `count` (Characters, row and pending text counted apart, as ThreadRuntime.swift:3101-3138) instead of the brief's `.Length`: `.Length` would move the 4,096 and 32,768 tiers for text with surrogate pairs or combining marks, and the owner rule is "same timings". The counts are taken with StringInfo.GetNextTextElementLength over spans (the walk SwiftString.Characters does) without a string per Character, and each row's count is carried in a ConditionalWeakTable keyed by its TimelineEntry: text that extends the counted text is walked again only from the start of its last Character. Every earlier boundary is decided by scalars wholly inside the counted text, so an append cannot move it; a counted text ending in a high surrogate, or text that does not extend the counted one (a completion, a replaced row), is counted afresh.
3. ROW TEXT. AppendStreamed still joins the row text once per flush (the item records are immutable and the views' previous.Text == message.Text checks see a flat string); that one copy is the floor the per-flush budget is measured above.
4. TOOL OUTPUT. ToolCall.AppendOutput gives TrimOutput(Output + text) without joining first: the UTF-8 count of the joined text is the sum of the two counts (a high surrogate ending Output meeting a low one starting text takes the old path, since two replacement characters become one scalar). Under 60,000 bytes the joined string is the result; over it both parts are joined in an ArrayPool buffer and only "…" + the last 30,000 Characters becomes a string. The suffix walks the Characters twice (count, then skip) instead of building a list of every Character start; SetOutput's TrimOutput uses the same walk. The UTF-8 guard and the Character suffix (the unit mismatch of PR-RUNTIME-150) are unchanged.
5. BUDGETS (Debug, headless, manual clock and main loop; first limit about 1.5x the unchanged code, then about 1.3x the new value, never above the old). ThreadRuntimeStreamBudgetTests: bytes per queued delta 282.7 B at 10k and at 100k characters before, 173.3 B after (limit 424, now 225); bytes per flush beyond the one flat copy of the reply 349,088 B at 10k and 2,482,912 B at 100k before, 592.0 B and 592.0 to 609.9 B after (two runs) (limits 524,000 and 3,725,000, now 770 and 795); 1 MB of tool output queued in 4 KB deltas within one window 288,557,112 B before, 8,485,592 B after (limit 433,000,000, now 11,040,000); new after the fix: per-delta and per-flush cost beyond the flat copy within 2x from 10k to 100k characters (7.1x before). ToolCallOutputBudgetTests: ToolCall.AppendOutput of 1 MB in 4 KB chunks with trimming 48,723,112 B before, 20,270,040 to 20,276,112 B after (two runs) (limit 73,100,000, now 26,360,000; the floor is one flat Output per append).
6. GUARDS. ThreadRuntimeStreamEquivalenceTests: six random delta scripts (fixed seeds, 1,500 steps, all four row kinds, pieces that split CR LF, combining marks, ZWJ sequences, regional indicators, Indic conjuncts and surrogate halves across delta and flush seams) give byte-identical rows and the identical PendingFlushLength at every step as a frozen copy of the old code; a replaced, shortened or half-surrogate row is counted as before. ToolCallOutputEquivalenceTests: eight random AppendOutput/SetOutput scripts, appends at 59,999, 60,000 and 60,001 bytes across surrogate and Character seams, Output stored over the ceiling and an empty append (same string instance) match the frozen old TrimOutput. The flush timing tests (ThreadRuntimePart7Tests), ThreadRuntimePart11Tests, ThreadRuntimePartFourTests and TimelineTests pass unchanged. No test was replaced or loosened.
7. REVIEW FIX (2026-10-12). The count memo kept `Text`, a strong reference to the row string as last counted; the final flush and the completion put other strings in the row, so every streamed assistant, reasoning or plan row kept a second near-complete copy of its text for the thread's lifetime (about 200 KB at 100k characters), which the old code never did. And its extension check `text.AsSpan().StartsWith(memo.Text.AsSpan())` compared the whole counted prefix on every flush, so CPU per flush stayed O(row length) though it allocated nothing. Now the memo holds the row text only through a WeakReference<string> (one per row, retargeted with SetTarget, so nothing per flush) plus the counted length, the Character count and the last Character's start, and it is trusted only for the very string it was handed on to: AppendStreamed (now an instance method) passes it from the previous row text to the joined one (CarryStreamedCount), whose first Length chars are by construction the counted ones. The check is one reference compare; any other text (a completion, a replaced row, a writer outside AppendStreamed) is counted afresh as before. Per flush the count now walks only the newest Characters; the one flat join of the row text in AppendStreamed (item 3) is still O(row length) in CPU and bytes, and that copy remains the floor the per-flush budgets are measured above, so per-flush cost is constant in reply length only beyond that copy. Budgets unchanged by the fix (two runs): 173.3 B per delta and 592.0 B per flush beyond the flat copy at 10k and 100k characters, 8,485,592 B for the 1 MB tool window; limits kept (225, 770, 795, 11,040,000). New guard in ThreadRuntimeStreamEquivalenceTests, The_count_memo_keeps_no_row_text_alive_and_resumes_on_the_flushed_text: the memo type has no string field, the streamed row text is collected once a completion replaces it, every flush hands the memo on to the new row text (it covers exactly the text counted before the flush) and every count matches the frozen old Characters count. It fails on the code before this fix. No test was replaced or loosened.

## ED-NEW-lean-10

Lean pass unit L10 (2026-10-12): the terminal frame snapshot shares unchanged rows. File: src/Marrow.App/Views/Terminal/Port/TerminalScreenBuffer.cs (TerminalHost.cs needed no change: ApplyOutput still takes one Snapshot per output frame). No visible change: every snapshot holds exactly the cells, wrapped flags, history count, size and cursor it held before.
1. COPY-ON-WRITE ROWS. Before, Snapshot deep-copied every scrollback and screen row on every frame (about 3.5 MB at 200 columns, 50 rows and 500 scrollback lines). Now the buffer keeps a per-row flag `owned` beside `lines` (and `savedNormalOwned` beside the saved normal screen while the alternate screen is up). Snapshot copies only the outer row and wrapped arrays, shares the row arrays and clears the flags; every write to a screen row goes through OwnRow, which copies the row first when a snapshot holds it. Scroll moves carry the flag with the row; a new blank row, a row created by Resize and the fresh alternate screen are owned. Scrollback rows are never written after they leave the screen, so every snapshot shares them.
2. SNAPSHOT API. Unchanged: TerminalFrame(TerminalCell[][] Lines, bool[] Wrapped, ...) as TerminalSurface and TerminalSelection read it. Neither writes a frame's rows (they only read), which is what makes sharing safe; the guard below fails if either side ever writes a handed-out row.
3. BUDGETS (Debug, headless, AllocationProbe; first limit about 1.5x the unchanged code, then about 1.3x the new value, never above the old). TerminalSnapshotBudgetTests at 200 columns, 50 rows, 500 scrollback lines: bytes per frame (one output read that rewrites one line, then the snapshot) 3,540,048 B before, 13,032 B after (limit 5,310,000, now 16,950); bytes per idle snapshot 3,538,496 B before, 5,056 B after (limit 5,310,000, now 6,580).
4. GUARDS. New: Random_escape_sequence_scripts_snapshot_exactly_like_the_deep_copying_buffer (four seeds and sizes, 4,000 steps each: text, wide, combining, ZWJ and regional-indicator glyphs, cursor moves, erases, SGR, scroll regions, insert and delete of cells and lines, save and restore, alternate screens 47 and 1049, OSC titles, sequences split across reads, resizes and rare scrollback clears; the scrollback reaches 500 lines) compares every snapshot cell by cell with a frozen copy of the deep-copying buffer (tests/.../Terminal/LegacyTerminalScreenBuffer.cs) and re-checks the last 24 snapshots against their own deep copies so none changes after it is handed out; Consecutive_snapshots_share_every_unchanged_row_and_copy_the_written_one pins the sharing. Existing guards unchanged and green: TerminalScreenBufferTests, TerminalHostFrameSyncTests, TerminalSelectionTests (41), every Views.Terminal class (278), AppModelTerminalTests. No test was replaced or loosened.

## ED-NEW-lean-18

2026-10-12 - Lean pass unit L18a (E:/Droppy/work/lean-pass/RELEASE_PLAN.md): background processes stay in the background. PORT-ONLY, ENGINEERING DECISIONS, no visible change: same look, motion and timings.
1. PRIORITY GROUPS (src/Marrow.Core/Port/ProcessLauncher.cs). New ProcessPriorityGroup: a launcher takes ProcessPriorityGroup.Current (an AsyncLocal, set by group.Enter() for a scope) when it is made. While its group is in the background the child runs below normal priority through the job it already runs in (JobObjectBasicLimitInformation, JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PRIORITY_CLASS with BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS, set before CreateProcessW so the child starts low and its tree follows; a launcher with no job uses the BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS creation flag) and with EcoQoS on the child (SetProcessInformation ProcessPowerThrottling, PROCESS_POWER_THROTTLING_EXECUTION_SPEED). Setting the group's IsBackground to false puts every live child at NORMAL and then lifts the limit (flags 0, the limitless job of ED-194 again) and hands EcoQoS back to Windows (control mask 0). A child leaves its group when it exits; a group made for one folder takes only children launched in that folder (normalised, case and trailing separator ignored). No group: the launch is byte-for-byte the old one. Priority failures are ignored; they never fail a launch.
2. USES. ProcessPriorityGroup.Background (always in the background) wraps git's working-tree captures: WorkingTreeWatch.CurrentTree's capture task and its no-watch fallback, and AppModel+Hydra's HydraTreeCache capture of a head's starting point. A Droppy head's session starts inside its own group (AppModel+Hydra StartDroppyHead and the launch-failure retry), made for the head's workplace folder (its own copy, or the shared checkout), so a shared MCP server started from the head's turn in the home folder never joins it and the lead's own processes, started outside any head scope, never do. The group is in the background while the head is not on screen and in the foreground when it is (ObservationTracking on SelectedThreadID and the lead runtime's IsHydraPanelHidden), and it is let go in the foreground when the head finishes (FinishHydraHead). On screen: the head's own chat is selected, or its lead's chat is selected with the Hydra panel shown; every head of that lead counts then (the panel's strip, stage and popped panels show them), and an unknown lead counts as on screen, so a head is never lowered by doubt. Native heads (subagents inside the lead's own CLI) have no process of their own and are untouched.
3. FILE EVENTS. bin, obj and node_modules events are not dropped: WorkingTreeWatch has never ignored them (a tracked file may live in a folder of that name, and dropping its event would leave a stale captured tree), so the brief's "cheap prefix checks before normalising" became an ordinal fast path for every path the stream reports. WorkingTreeWatch.NoteBatch: a path that starts with the resolved root prefix exactly, holds no forward slash and whose root is drive rooted with an ASCII git directory name under it is answered with no normalisation: the cookie test is the same OrdinalIgnoreCase test; the git test compares ASCII with ASCII and gives up on any other character (falling back to the old code, unchanged, as every other shape does); the folder string is made once per batch for the last four folders seen. git's own writes (the events NoteBatch passes over with no effect) are dropped by the stream itself: FileWatcher.WatchTree gained an optional skip(root, name), asked before the path is joined or the file system asked whether it is a directory; WorkingTreeWatch passes SkipsName, which answers exactly NoteBatch's git-internal case and never a cookie. FileWatcher's tree delivery notes one path with no array and holds its pending batch under a plain Lock (Mutex<T>.WithLock took a closure per event); delivery order, batching and the Everything flag are unchanged.
4. BUDGETS (Debug, headless, GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread after a warm-up; first limit about 1.5x the unchanged base 0a946c558, then about 1.3x the new value, never above the old): WorkingTreeWatchNoteBudgetTests bytes per bin/obj/node_modules event through NoteBatch 4,960.7 before, 52.5 after (limit 7440, now 70); per git-internal event 2,862.2 before, 0.1 after (limit 4290, now 0.5, target 0). FileWatcherEventBudgetTests bytes per bin/obj/node_modules event through the watch's handler 558.2 before, 418.8 after, mostly the delivered path itself (limit 840, now 545); per git-internal event 590.5 before, 0.0 after (limit 890, now 0.5, target 0).
5. GUARDS. WorkingTreeWatchNoteBudgetTests.Every_batch_leaves_the_watch_exactly_where_the_pre_lean_note_left_it (400 random batches over every path shape: case, separators, \\?\ forms, the roots themselves, cookies well formed, malformed and in other case, non-ASCII names, paths outside the root; generation, cookie and changed folders equal a frozen copy of the pre-lean NoteBatch, Fixtures/WorkingTreeNoteOracle.cs) and The_stream_drops_only_names_the_pre_lean_note_passes_over_without_effect; FileWatcherEventBudgetTests.The_watch_ends_where_the_pre_lean_note_of_every_raised_path_ends (same events delivered, end to end through the real stream). ProcessLauncherPriorityTests (the seam: a background launch carries the job limit, BELOW_NORMAL and EcoQoS; outside a group nothing changes; foreground and back on a live child; the folder rule; a Shell.Run inside the background group, the path git takes, reads its own priority as BelowNormal and outside it as Normal). 2026-10-12 - Lean pass unit L18b, background services hygiene (work/lean-pass/RELEASE_PLAN.md). No visible change: no pixels, motion or timings move; only background threads, retry pacing and a registry's lifetime change.
1. EcoQoS (SetThreadInformation ThreadPowerThrottling, execution speed) on the threads that already ran BelowNormal: the palette engine's PaletteExecutor thread (for its life), the palette ink worker thread (PaletteInkWorker.Run; Marrow.Services keeps its helper internal, so Marrow.App has its own private copy), and SkillGenerations' spare build, which borrows a pool thread and hands both priority and EcoQoS back (EcoQoS(false): Windows decides again) before it returns. When the last relay connection of a token closes (the CLI ended and its relay with it), the registration is dropped 30 s later (Grace, on an internal TimeProvider Clock); a relay reconnecting with the token inside the grace keeps it. A token whose relay never connects is still kept (no session-end signal reaches this file; the session classes are outside this unit). The pipe's listen retry after an IOException backs off 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 2 s, then 4 s (RetryDelay), capped under the relay's 5 s connect window so a relay never times out waiting for a listener; a connection resets it.

## ED-NEW-lean-23 (review fixes)

2026-10-12 - Follow-up to ED-NEW-lean-23 after its review. No visible change; the ink worker change below restores the base exactly.
1. Advisor registrations reused by a session: ACPSession and CopilotSession cache the relay entry (advisorServer ??= ...) and put the same token into every MCP session they open, so dropping a registration 30 s after its last relay closed broke ask_advisor in a chat whose new MCP session (a reset, a resume fallback) came later. Fixed inside AdvisorMcpBridge, no session class touched: each returned relay entry carries a holder (ConditionalWeakTable value with a finalizer), and a registration is dropped only when the entry is no longer held, no relay is connected and no grace is running. ACP and Copilot sessions hold it for their life, ClaudeSession until its next launch replaces it; CodexSession builds one per thread start and holds nothing, so its registrations still end 30 s after their relay.
2. Tokens no relay ever reaches (a CLI that failed to start, a relaunch that never reached its relay) were kept forever; now, once their entry is not held, they are dropped 5 min after registering (Unclaimed), which leaves a slow CLI start ample time to connect its relay.
3. Attach/Drop race: a relay that looked up an entry just before its drop now re-adds it under the entry lock (Removed flag), so that relay and later reconnects with the token keep the registration. A grace timer that fires after being replaced is ignored (Generation).
4. The serve loop runs through an internal seam, Serve<T>(listen, serve, wait, stop); production passes the real pipe listen, Task.Run(ServeClient) and Task.Delay. Listen now also disposes and rethrows when creating the pipe instance fails, so a creation IOException is retried with the same backoff instead of ending the serve task for good.
5. PaletteInkWorker: the EcoQoS added by ED-NEW-lean-23 item 1 is removed; the file is byte-identical to the base again. Its thread computes every on-screen frame of the palette ink (up to 4 fluid steps and the 480x20 density paint per frame), and on hybrid CPUs EcoQoS may move it to efficiency cores at a low clock; with no N1/N3 frame-rate evidence and no native runs allowed, the owner's zero-stutter bar wins. PaletteExecutor and SkillGenerations keep EcoQoS (no on-screen frames).
6. PaletteEngine: only automatic offline failures count toward the backoff; a manual refresh (or a check before Start) keeps the pace it found and reschedules at it.
7. Budgets, measured before and after this follow-up (Debug, headless, through the heavy slot):
   AdvisorPipeRetryBudgetTests: listen retries in one simulated minute of a persistent pipe error, now driven through the real serve loop: before 240 (measured through the seam on the base's flat 250 ms wait; limit about 1.5x: 360), after 18 (limit 23). The earlier version summed RetryDelay alone and stayed green with a flat wait; replaced by this stricter one.
   AdvisorRegistrationBudgetTests: registrations left after 100 launches whose relay never connects: before 100 (measured on commit 41475c14a; limit about 1.5x: 150), after 0 (limit 0). The 100-session budget is unchanged at 0 and now also collects the entries before the relays connect, so each token must survive its unclaimed window.
8. Guards added: AdvisorPipeRetryBudgetTests.The_serve_loop_backs_off_on_errors_in_a_row_and_a_connection_resets_it (250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 4000, then 250 again after a connection), AdvisorRegistrationBudgetTests.A_held_entry_keeps_its_registration_for_a_new_relay_long_after_the_first_ended (failed on 41475c14a with a null registration), PaletteOfflineBackoffTests.A_manual_refresh_while_offline_does_not_lengthen_the_automatic_retry (failed on 41475c14a: the first automatic retry was 240 s). The reconnect-within-grace guard is kept, now registering after the manual clock is set.

The line split works on the UTF-16 text (0x0A and 0x0D are never inside a longer UTF-8 sequence, and on well-formed UTF-16 the decoded piece is the piece), counting each line's UTF-8 length to keep Restart in bytes; Utf8StartsWith is an ordinal StartsWith and SubstringFromUtf8Offset walks the byte offset to a character offset. Each of the three keeps the old byte path for text with a lone surrogate (UTF-8 turns it into U+FFFD). TrimmedLine and IsRule read the first/last characters instead of encoding the line (a byte in the accepted ASCII range is exactly that ASCII character). ListMarkerAt reads offsets into the line when the body's first Character is one ASCII character (a letter or other non-digit is no marker at once: no ASCII Character but 0-9 is isNumber); any other first Character keeps the old Character-list reading (ListMarkerAtCharacters, unchanged). Indentation, CountLeadingHashes, HeadingLevel and IsTableDelimiter work on Character lengths and characters. Prefix checks against one ASCII character (">", " ", "\t") answer directly when the text's Character there is one ASCII character and hand every other Character to SwiftString.HasPrefix itself; FenceMarker, the closing fence and the task-box check skip SwiftString.HasPrefix (and the lowercased copy) only when the first characters are two different ASCII characters, where the canonical compare is false and throws nothing. The fence markers are one static array.
2. MENTION SCAN (src/Marrow.UI/Markdown/MentionScanner.cs). The text's Characters are kept as one array of boundary offsets (the old SortedSet, its per-step enumerator, the per-Character strings and the linear previous/next searches are gone); each name is split into Characters once, with each Character's NFC form. HasPrefix(text[cursor..], name) becomes a Character-by-Character compare at the cursor with SwiftString.Equal's rule: ordinal first; a text Character that is one ASCII character is its own NFC form and is compared with the name Character's NFC form; every other text Character goes through SwiftString.Equal itself (so a lone surrogate reaching NFC throws the same ArgumentException). The Characters beside a match are still made as strings for SwiftCharacter (only on a prefix match).

2. FIX. (a) StreamVeil.Advance keeps the string its Characters were cut from: a tick feeds the same text again, and an ordinally equal text skips cutting and comparing (a different string still goes the old way, canonical comparison included). (b) VeiledText reads its source's text once (AttributedText.PlainText built a new string on every read) and keeps a VeilPieces: where each Character of the joined text starts, and for each attributed run where its own Characters start and which joined Character each overlaps first, found by binary search; this replaces AlphaForRange's linear scan over every Character for every Character (O(n^2) time). Between two chunk bounds every Character has the same alpha (StreamVeil.swift:314-320), so a run is split only where a bound falls; the pieces no chunk touches are kept from one tick to the next (two generations, so a piece unused for a tick is dropped) and only the dissolving tail is rebuilt. The runs come out exactly as before, the empty Text each concatenation started from included. (c) Avalonia 12.1.2's SelectableTextBlock rebuilds its whole text twice for every inline added or removed (the selection coercion reads Inlines.Text), so swapping every inline on every tick cost the whole paragraph each time. StyledText.Render(host, Painted) (VeiledText's own text block only) and LinkTextVeil.Paint now give the dissolving pieces their new brush in place when the host still holds exactly the inlines the last paint made and only the colour moved (a Foreground change invalidates the text layout but not the collection); anything else renders afresh as before. The host ends up with the same inline properties either way. (d) LinkTextVeil keeps the joined text and its Character starts while every text block still holds exactly the inlines (and run texts) it set, computes the alpha ranges from the chunk bounds, keeps the slices of a run between ticks (the piece before the tail is most of a long paragraph), and PaintRun builds no list for a run no range touches. (e) StyledText.Render's line box is one pass with no arrays (the same Enumerable.Max semantics: a missing box skipped, a NaN gives way to the next).

2026-10-12 - A thread event touches only what changed (claude/lean-l16; src/Marrow.App/AppModel.cs; AppModelLeanBudgetTests, AppModelLeanThreadEventTests). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY (the Swift setter re-syncs the same way; the cost is the port's allocation per pass over the library).
1. RULE: every UpdateThread (each runtime status, unread and timestamp change), MarkRead and the sort reorder (UpdateThreads) assigned Threads, whose setter (AppModel.swift:33-45) re-synced every thread cell (a HashSet and a key array of the whole library), rebuilt the child cells (a dictionary of every parent, a copy of every child cell) and rebuilt ThreadIndex (two dictionaries copied into ValueMaps), and SetItem copied the list twice: about 500 B per thread in the library per event. Same look, same answers, same notifications.
2. FIX: AssignThreadsInPlace. When the new list differs from the held one only at known indices, and every changed thread keeps its id, project and parent, and no id repeats (threadCells.Count == threads.Count), the cells, the child cells and the index are already right but for the changed threads' own cells: those are written exactly as Sync would (only a cell whose value differs, collected before any write), then Threads notifies (SetAlways: the lists differ by construction). Any other change (added, removed, moved to another project or parent, repeated id) takes the unchanged setter. UpdateThreadValue builds the new list with one copy (OneReplaced, an ICollection the ValueList constructor copies once). The stray child cells the setter's SyncChildCells drops at the next event (AppModel.swift:203-207: a cell asked for a parent that is neither a thread nor anyone's parent) are now remembered when ChildIDs makes them and dropped by the in-place event too, so an observer of such a cell sees what it saw before.
3. LEFT: the new list itself, one 8-byte reference per thread. Threads is a ValueList (Marrow.Core/Port/ValueCollections.cs, outside this unit) that the sidebar and RootView read on every change, so a list per event stays. The plan's "500 vs 50 threads within 2x" is therefore not met: 4,752 B against 1,152 B (4.1x); everything but that copy is flat (the growth budget below). Meeting it needs a persistent list in Marrow.Core; reported, not done here.
4. GUARD: AppModelLeanThreadEventTests runs 1,500 fixed-seed events over 60 threads in two projects (timestamps, statuses, unread, titles, pins, archive and panel flags, no-op changes, project moves, reparenting, MarkRead with unknown ids) and after each checks Thread, Children and ThreadsIn against the list and that exactly the observers of changed cells fire (each thread cell, each Children read including its children's cells, Threads); two more pin the stray child cell's drop and its control. All three landed green on the unchanged code first (bad4ced7f).
5. BUDGETS (Debug, bytes per UpdateThread after 20 warm-up events, 200 measured, every row's child and selection cells made, heavy slot): 500 threads 251,544 before (limit 377,000), 4,752 after, limit tightened to 6,200; 50 threads 26,616 before (limit 39,900), 1,152 after, limit tightened to 1,500; new growth budget, bytes each library thread adds to an event: 499.8 before, 8.0 after, limit 10.4.
6. TESTS (Decision ED-NEW-lean-16): AppModelLeanBudgetTests (3), AppModelLeanThreadEventTests (3); guards, all non-native: every AppModel* class (554), Sidebar/Selection/Selected/AppCommands/CommandPalette (1004), ThreadRuntime/RootView/LiveThread (763), green. No test was loosened or removed.

Version-pinned to Avalonia 12.1.2 like the formatter adapter in ComposerParagraphLayout.Install: a renamed field fails visibly (MissingFieldException), never silently.
2. FIX (src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/ComposerParagraphLayout.cs): the paragraph walk (each paragraph's start and natural base) depends only on the text and the fallback base, and one keystroke rebuilds layouts of the same text several times (the presenter at each text, caret, selection and measure change; ComposerTextView.CreateComposerLayout's height and ink probes). ComposerParagraphSource keeps the last 4 walks per thread ([ThreadStatic], each an immutable array) and reuses one for an ordinal-equal text and the same fallback. The walk reads each paragraph through a span (ComposerParagraphLayout.Direction gained a ReadOnlySpan<char> overload; the string overload delegates) instead of a substring per paragraph; zero or one style span is copied without LINQ sorting (two or more are still sorted by start, stable, as before). The brief's key "(text, width)": the walk does not depend on the width, so its key is the text and the fallback; the TextLayout itself is not cached across rebuilds because TextPresenter disposes its layout at every invalidation.

MANIFEST (src/Marrow.App/app.manifest, ApplicationManifest in Marrow.App.csproj): before, the SDK embedded its default manifest (assemblyIdentity 1.0.0.0 "MyApplication.app" and trustInfo asInvoker, uiAccess false; read from the built Marrow.App.exe at 0a946c558). The new manifest keeps those two byte-for-byte in meaning and adds only compatibility/supportedOS {8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a} (Windows 10 and 11) and windowsSettings/heapType SegmentHeap (namespace http://schemas.microsoft.com/SMI/2020/WindowsSettings; honoured from Windows 10 2004, build 19041, the target's floor). asInvoker is kept so nothing about elevation changes; no dpiAware, dpiAwareness, longPathAware or any other setting (Avalonia sets the DPI awareness itself). The segment heap covers the process's native heaps (Skia, HarfBuzz, ANGLE/D3D, the CRT); the GC heap is unaffected.
2. COMPOSITE READYTORUN: PublishReadyToRunComposite is set only when the publish passes -p:MarrowReadyToRunComposite=true; the shipped publish (scripts/package-windows.ps1, unchanged) stays plain ReadyToRun. Measured headless on 2026-10-12 (dotnet publish -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained, this branch): plain R2R publish folder 402,934,346 bytes (deflate-6 per file 144,357,640); composite 466,927,506 bytes (deflate 167,010,157; one Marrow.App.r2r.dll composite image), +15.9 % raw and +15.7 % compressed, inside the 30 % installer-growth gate. The boot half of the gate (10 % or better) needs the native N4 run.
3. BUDGET: no headless budget fits this unit (RELEASE_PLAN: "the verdict comes from native N4"). Before and after numbers for working set and boot are N4's to record; this entry gets them as an addendum. Keep rule: the segment heap stays only if N4 shows a lower working set and no boot regression; composite R2R is switched on by default only if N4 shows boot 10 % faster or better. If N4 says no, delete app.manifest and the ApplicationManifest line (and AppManifestTests with them, by a later ED entry), or leave the composite switch off.

## ED-NEW-lean-9 (pacing)
2026-10-12 - Lead decision D1 (claude/lean-r1): the composer's working dots draw on the 60 Hz slots of the shared ambient pacer (item 2 of ED-NEW-lean-9, the unit's central goal, was open). ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY. No visible change: every drawn picture is the unpaced field's picture at the same instant; the field draws 60 times a second, as every other ambient source does (ED-NEW-frame-pacing, T44).
1. SEAM (src/Marrow.UI/Port/AmbientRefreshPacer.cs): a small public static class AmbientRefreshPacing with one method, For(compositor), which returns AmbientRefreshPacer.For(compositor).Beat: the same per-compositor pacer every ambient source of that compositor asks, never a private copy. Chosen over [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("Marrow.App")] because that would open every internal of Marrow.UI to Marrow.App (name and overload clashes between the two assemblies' internals); the seam opens one call.
2. GATE (src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/DotFieldCompositionHandler.cs, ComposerWorkingDots.cs): the handler takes the pacer when it is made (ComposerWorkingDots builds it with AmbientRefreshPacing.For(host.Compositor)). OnAnimationFrameUpdate copies NthMotionHandler's gate: when the tick (CompositionNow.Ticks, used as the tick's identity only) is not a slot at the clock's seconds (the frame's ClockNow, SwiftClock: timestamp over frequency, the same base as NthFrame.Seconds), it asks for the next update and draws nothing, leaving `drawn` as it is so the stop-when-not-drawn guard holds. A message (a new frame) still draws at once, as before. The draw's time is still the clock's.
3. NUMBERS (ComposerWorkingDotsLeanBudgetTests, Debug, headless, 240 Hz, one simulated second after 60 warm ticks, a 700 x 24 field of 3 x 89 dots): draws 240 before, 60 after (limit 312 tightened to 61, the brief's target); clock reads 240 before, 300 after (each of the 240 frame updates reads the clock for the pacer, and each of the 60 draws reads it again; limit 312 kept, never raised); the dots' own share of a drawing tick 0 B (limit 0); new: a paced tick (an update that draws nothing) allocates 0 B (limit 0, A_paced_compositor_tick_with_the_dots_allocates_within_the_budget).
4. REPLACED CHECKS (each equal or stricter). (a) ComposerWorkingDotsCompositorTests.The_animation_path_has_no_UI_frame_timer_or_Avalonia_animation_clock asserted DoesNotContain("CompositionNow", handler + frame); now the frame never names it, and the handler names it exactly once, only in pacer(CompositionNow.Ticks, paced.ClockNow().Ticks / (double)TimeSpan.TicksPerSecond) (the tick's identity, with the clock's seconds as the pacer's time). (b) The two own-share tests asserted Assert.Equal(240, draws) and Assert.Equal(60, draws) (a draw at every tick, as the reference). Paced, the own share is the median of the drawing ticks only, compared with the reference's median, and EverySlotDrew asserts a draw on every 60 Hz slot (every 4th tick, one phase) and at most one draw more (a frame sent from main draws at once; a test running beside this one can change the theme). The blend's measured ticks start after the new frame's own first draw (it lands one or two ticks after the UI sends it, when headless applies the commit); all 60 are still inside the 0.32 s blend. (c) ComposerWorkingDotsStopGuardTests run on a 60 Hz display (RenderFrameSource.PeriodSource 1/60 s, ticks 1/60 s apart), where every refresh is a slot, with every assertion as before but one: Blending at the first refresh back inside with a new frame is now checked at the next refresh, together with the new frame's Target (the new colour). The first refresh draws the old frame (headless, the new one reaches the render server a tick later); at 240 Hz the earlier blend was still running there, so the old check passed on the wrong blend; the new check fails if the new frame never blends. The stop guard at 240 Hz, paced, is new: ComposerWorkingDotsPacedStopGuardTests (one update per refresh, one draw per slot at the clock's time, the updates stop within one slot outside the window and start again inside, twice).
5. GUARD: ComposerWorkingDotsPacedPixelGuardTests, 24 refreshes 1/240 s apart after 10 warm ones (well inside the pacer's 0.25 s reset, so a dropped or doubled slot shows). The hashes of the unpaced field at every refresh were recorded on claude/lean-r1 d723dd5f8 (twice alone and once in a mixed run: identical); the paced field shows at every refresh exactly the unpaced picture of the last slot, in one phase of four. The existing pixel guard (20 times 0.37 s apart, hashes from before L9) passes unchanged.
6. KNOWN FLAKY, not this change: EffortSliderJewelWarmupTests.Warm_async_hurries_an_idle_warm_up_already_running failed alone here, as it did in the L9 review round before this change (item 7 above); it makes no dot field.

## ED-NEW-lean-7 (render-thread frames)
2026-10-12 - Lead decision D7: of the five findings of the last L7 review, four were fixed; the fifth (render-thread frames while no window can be seen, item 5 above) is not a defect. ENGINEERING DECISION.
1. WHY: frames on the compositor's render thread (RenderFrameSource) are not held back or parked by L7, but RenderFrameSource stops them itself while their window cannot be seen: at a frame update its handler returns with no new request while the ambient source's AmbientMotionController.Available is false (src/Marrow.UI/Port/RenderFrameSource.cs, OnAnimationFrameUpdate; Available is AmbientWindowState's: visible, active, not minimised, in front, not cloaked, not fully covered). Every render-thread timeline is ambient: the only one in the tree is EffortSlider's track (src/Marrow.App/Views/Composer/EffortSlider.cs, AnimationTimelineSchedule(..., Ambient: true) with onRenderThread: true). So no render-thread timeline runs while every window is minimised or cloaked. Nth motion is gated by WindowPresence (ED-NEW-lean-6); the other render-thread handlers (the dot field, composer light, wallpaper, voice glow and orb, interaction recorder) belong to their own units.
2. COMMENT: AvaloniaFrameSource's summary in src/Marrow.UI/Port/FrameClock.cs said render-thread frames are "neither held back nor parked here", accurate but misleading; it now says they stop by RenderFrameSource's own ambient gate. Comment only; no code or test changed.
3. STILL OWED before merge (unchanged): the native wake-from-idle proof, FrameClockWakeNativeTests (native, not run here).
## ED-NEW-lean-16 (follow-up)
2026-10-12 - Lead decision D2: one more fix round toward the plan's "a thread event at 500 threads within 2x of 50 threads". ENGINEERING DECISION. PORT-ONLY. No visible change.
1. FIX (src/Marrow.App/AppModel.cs): the two events that change several threads at once copied the library twice (threads.ToList(), then the new ValueList's array) and compared the whole lists (ChangedIndices): UpdateThreads (the activity reorder MoveInActivity, the sort reorder and the settled children's update) and MarkRead(ids). Both now keep only the replaced threads (a dictionary by place) and lay them over the held list in the new list's one copy (SomeReplaced, an ICollection the ValueList constructor copies once, as UpdateThread's OneReplaced); the changed places are the replaced ones whose thread differs from the held one, ascending. The same list, the same changed places in the same order, the same cells written, the same notifications (a repeated id still sees its own earlier change; changes that cancel out still take the setter).
2. NUMBERS (AppModelLeanMultiEventBudgetTests, new, Debug, the bytes each library thread adds to one event, 500 against 50 threads, 200 events after 20 warm, every row's child and selection cells made): MarkRead of two threads 16.0 B before (d723dd5f8), 8.0 B after, limit 10.4; an activity reorder of two threads 16.0 B before, 8.0 B after, limit 10.4. UpdateThread is unchanged: 4,752 B at 500 threads, 1,152 B at 50 (8.0 B per thread; AppModelLeanBudgetTests unchanged).
3. ACCEPTED GAP: the plan's 2x target for UpdateThread at 500 against 50 threads is not met (4.1x: 4,752 B against 1,152 B) and cannot be within L16's files or without a visible change. The rest of the event is flat (752 B at any size); what grows is the new list itself, one 8-byte reference per thread, which ValueList's constructor copies (src/Marrow.Core/Port/ValueCollections.cs: base(items.ToArray())). Threads is a Swift array value that the sidebar and RootView read on every change, and the held list may not be changed in place (the event's snapshots `held` and `before`, and every reader's earlier list, must keep their contents). Meeting 2x needs a persistent or chunked list in Marrow.Core (outside L16), or Threads no longer a flat list. Recorded as an accepted gap by the lead's decision; no budget was loosened.
## ED-NEW-lean-11 (check review)
2026-10-12 - Lead decision D4: the replaced assertion of item 6 (TimelineRowsPrRecordsTests.A_reply_is_rebuilt_only_when_its_text_or_streaming_flag_moves_and_its_hover_line_shows_only_on_hover_of_a_finished_reply; on claude/release-integration: Assert.NotSame(before, row!.Child) after a flush of a reply that streams on) was compared with the original and is kept. ENGINEERING DECISION.
1. WHY: the original checked only that the row's child object changed, a stand-in for "the reply's body follows its new text" (SwiftUI has no view identity; the source re-evaluates the body). It passed for any new child, also one still showing the old text. The replacement checks what the reader sees: the row's one MarkdownView holds "more words", and the drawn runs contain "more words" and no longer "first words". It fails whenever the body does not follow the text, which is the claim of the test's name; it accepts a kept body that shows the new text, which is L11's change (MarkdownView.Stream). Equal or stricter on the requirement. Restoring the identity check would mean rebuilding the body at every flush, which L11 exists to remove. The test's other checks are unchanged.
